cells.C2: When should one stop the most exciting game? Sequential Inference for win-martingales
cells.D2: Derives an optimal-stopping / free-boundary theory for deciding when to act on a live win-probability process before a fixed-horizon outcome is revealed.
cells.E2: Models market-implied win probability as a diffusion (win-martingale) and solves a Bayes-risk optimal stopping problem with explicit boundary characterization.
cells.F2: Directly touches GSE's pick lifecycle (proposed->locked) and live odds-derived win probabilities; gives rigorous theory for when a pick's probability estimate is 'good enough' to lock/publish.
cells.G2: Use the stopping-boundary math to auto-determine the optimal moment to lock a pick's odds/confidence before kickoff, rather than a fixed T-minus-X cutoff, potentially improving closing-line value capture.

cells.C3: Gap distributions between successive personal bests in cricket: Data and Models
cells.D3: Shows cricket players' personal-best gaps follow a truncated power law, not the i.i.d. record-theory prediction, revealing path-dependent career effects.
cells.E3: Fits truncated power-law models to inter-record gaps and compares against shuffled-career bootstrap baselines to isolate temporal-ordering effects.
cells.F3: A methodological example of testing whether observed sports performance sequences deviate from naive stochastic baselines -- directly analogous to GSE's own backtest failing to beat a naive baseline.
cells.G3: Adapt the bootstrap-shuffle test as a diagnostic tool to check whether GSE's own historical pick/performance data shows genuine skill signal versus record-statistics artifacts before trusting calibration windows.

cells.C4: Vector field theory in motion: Revealing latent potentials in soccer dynamics
cells.D4: Introduces a physics-based vector-field/potential-function framework that extracts stable, team-specific tactical fingerprints from player and ball tracking data.
cells.E4: Reconstructs velocity vector fields over the pitch and derives scalar potentials whose gradients correlate with ball progression and possession control.
cells.F4: A novel feature-engineering approach for tracking-data-driven sports analytics that could feed GSE's prediction-engine with richer spatial features beyond box-score stats, particularly for soccer/MLS.
cells.G4: Use team-potential 'fingerprints' as a new predictor class in the ensemble, potentially explaining variance the current MAE-losing model misses, especially for live/in-play prediction updates.

cells.C5: Topological Data Analysis and Graph-Theoretic Approaches for Tennis Match Prediction
cells.D5: Applies persistent homology and Katz similarity on player competitive networks to predict ATP tennis outcomes, reaching 66.2% accuracy, competitive with ranking-based baselines.
cells.E5: Builds player networks from historical match results, extracts topological/graph features via lower-star filtration and Modified Band Depth, then feeds a Random Forest.
cells.F5: Directly relevant as an alternative feature-engineering approach for match prediction that could supplement GSE's core model, which currently loses to a naive baseline on MAE.
cells.G5: Use TDA-derived topological features as an independent 'sub-model' in the ensemble specifically for lower-data sports/matchups where box-score features are sparse, feeding into bootstrap-mode confidence weighting.

cells.C6: Stochastic generator of trajectories from record data: application to glacier fluctuations
cells.D6: Proposes a Brownian-motion-based simulator with neural-based-inference-style hyperparameter tuning to reconstruct full time series from only record (peak) observations.
cells.E6: Uses a stochastic simulator plus simulation-based inference to fit hyperparameters when only extreme/record values of a non-stationary process are observed.
cells.F6: Tangential: the record-value-from-sparse-data problem is structurally similar to reconstructing performance trajectories from sparse historical sports data, relevant to bootstrap-mode confidence handling.
cells.G6: Apply a similar simulator-based inference technique to reconstruct plausible full-season performance trajectories for new or thinly-tracked teams/players, improving bootstrap-mode's sparse-data confidence caps.

cells.C7: X-Stream: Exploring MLLMs as Multiplexers for Multi-Stream Understanding
cells.D7: Introduces a benchmark and framework testing whether multimodal LLMs can jointly reason over multiple concurrent video streams, such as live sports broadcasts, finding current models struggle (~50% accuracy).
cells.E7: Constructs a multi-stream QA benchmark and evaluates MLLMs as 'signal multiplexers' handling multi-window/multi-view/multi-device video understanding.
cells.F7: Relevant to GSE's longer-horizon content-automation and Intelligence Graph ambitions if they ever ingest live broadcast video for real-time event extraction across multiple games simultaneously.
cells.G7: Use the multiplexer framing to design an internal agent (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable-style) that monitors multiple live game streams at once for anomaly/event detection feeding the data pipeline in real time.

cells.C8: Matrix concentration inequalities for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains
cells.D8: Derives Chernoff-type concentration bounds for eigenvalues of matrix sums from non-stationary Markov chains, applying the theory to analyze the Elo rating system under a dynamic Bradley-Terry-Luce model.
cells.E8: Uses Wasserstein contractivity (Ollivier-Ricci curvature) and spectral-gap conditions to bound deviation of matrix-valued statistics generated by time-varying Markov kernels.
cells.F8: Directly relevant to GSE's rating/probability models: provides rigorous finite-sample guarantees for Elo-like dynamic rating systems, which underlie sport-specific probability models feeding the calibration gate.
cells.G8: Use these concentration bounds to derive theoretically-justified confidence intervals on team/player Elo ratings for bootstrap mode, replacing ad hoc confidence caps with statistically grounded uncertainty bands.

cells.C9: An Axiomatic Theory of Tie-Breaking: Impossibility, Characterization, and Decomposition
cells.D9: Develops an axiomatic framework proving no anonymous tie-breaking rule can produce a strict ranking, and characterizes the unique fair partition-based alternative.
cells.E9: Formalizes tie-breaking as symmetric-group action on standings plus auxiliary info, proving impossibility and decomposition theorems for ranking rules.
cells.F9: Niche but relevant to GSE's pick-grading/settlement logic and any league-standings or tournament features (e.g., Galaxy Dynasty game), where fair, defensible tie-breaking rules matter for trust/compliance.
cells.G9: Formalize GSE's own tie-breaking rules (e.g., for pick grading edge cases, leaderboard ties in Galaxy Dynasty) using this axiomatic framework to produce a defensible, published fairness spec for the trust/compliance toolkit.

cells.C10: Novel neighborhood structures for incomplete round robin sports tournaments
cells.D10: Proposes new local-search neighborhood structures for scheduling incomplete round-robin tournaments, achieving new best-known solutions via hill-climbing metaheuristics.
cells.E10: Defines graph-theoretic neighborhood moves (single-game-plus-repair-chain and single-round multi-game swaps) embedded in adaptive late acceptance hill climbing.
cells.F10: Operationally adjacent: relevant only if GSE ever builds scheduling/simulation features for leagues or its own Galaxy Dynasty persistent game requiring tournament formats.
cells.G10: Reuse the neighborhood-search scheduling algorithm inside Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR to generate balanced incomplete-round-robin brackets for the persistent web game's competitive seasons.

cells.C11: SoccerRef-Agents: Multi-Agent System for Automated Soccer Refereeing
cells.D11: Builds a multi-agent framework combining video perception with a rule-knowledge RAG base to make explainable soccer foul/refereeing decisions, outperforming general MLLMs.
cells.E11: Uses cross-modal retrieval-augmented generation across a multi-agent architecture, grounding foul classification in a vector database of official rules and precedent cases.
cells.F11: Directly relevant to GSE's internal agentic tooling (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) and trust/compliance ambitions: a concrete multi-agent RAG architecture for explainable, rule-grounded sports decision-making.
cells.G11: Adapt the rule-grounded multi-agent RAG design to build an explainability agent that justifies GSE pick grading/settlement decisions by citing the specific rules/data points involved, reinforcing the trust/compliance toolkit.

cells.C12: Iterative Semantic Reasoning from Individual to Group Interests for Generative Recommendation with LLMs
cells.D12: Proposes an iterative LLM-based reasoning framework that bridges individual and group user interests for generative recommendation, outperforming baselines on Sports and other e-commerce datasets.
cells.E12: Uses LLMs to build semantic item/user interaction graphs and iteratively refines individual explicit interests against group implicit interests via batch optimization.
cells.F12: Tangential: a recommendation-system technique validated partly on a 'Sports' product dataset, relevant to GSE only if it builds personalized pick/content recommendation features for users.
cells.G12: Apply the individual-to-group iterative reasoning framework to personalize which picks or content GSE surfaces to each user by reasoning about both their individual betting history and similar-user group patterns.

cells.D13: An expository, visually-illustrated review of graph colouring theory and algorithms, including applications to sports scheduling.
cells.E13: Surveys node/edge/face colouring algorithms and theoretical results with pedagogical figures rather than new results.
cells.F13: Weak/background relevance: graph colouring underlies sports-scheduling constraint problems, tangential to GSE's core prediction stack but could inform future scheduling-aware features.
cells.G13: Use as a teaching reference for onboarding new data-eng hires on constraint-based scheduling concepts if GSE ever tackles fixture-conflict detection in its data-ingestion pipeline.

cells.C14: Detecting Parameter Instabilities in Functional Concurrent Linear Regression
cells.D14: Develops CUSUM-based structural break tests for functional linear regression on functional time series, applied to detect fatigue-induced changes in runners' joint-angle trajectories.
cells.E14: Builds L2- and sup-norm CUSUM statistics with functional strong invariance principles to detect breakpoints in a time-varying slope function.
cells.F14: Directly relevant as a rigorous change-point detection technique applicable to GSE's time-series sports data pipeline (e.g., detecting regime shifts in team/player performance or line movement).
cells.G14: Adapt the CUSUM functional break test to flag mid-season 'regime changes' in a team's performance curve (injury, coaching change) that should trigger a model re-weighting or confidence downgrade in bootstrap mode.

cells.C15: A two-player version of the assignment problem
cells.D15: Introduces and analyzes computational complexity of a competitive draft-style assignment game where two players alternately pick agents to maximize/minimize a resulting score gap.
cells.E15: Formalizes turn-based agent drafting followed by optimal bipartite assignment, proving PSPACE-completeness and tractable special cases.
cells.F15: Directly models sports drafts; relevant if GSE's Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR game includes draft mechanics, and offers complexity-theoretic grounding for fair draft design.
cells.G15: Use the game's tractable special cases to design and balance the draft mechanic in Galaxy Dynasty, ensuring the draft order/algorithm cannot be trivially exploited by dominant strategies.

cells.C16: Muscle Synergy Patterns During Running: Coordinative Mechanisms From a Neuromechanical Perspective
cells.D16: Reviews EMG-based muscle synergy decomposition methods (PCA, ICA, NMF, autoencoders) and how running conditions and pathology modulate coordination patterns.
cells.E16: Surveys neuromechanical decomposition techniques for lower-limb muscle synergies during running across populations and conditions.
cells.F16: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's prediction/calibration stack; a biomechanics domain review with no statistical modeling GSE would reuse.
cells.G16: Only a stretch: if GSE ever ingests wearable/biomechanical data feeds for athlete-level injury-risk signals, this survey could inform which synergy features to track as leading indicators.

cells.C17: Non-invasive load measurement in the human tibia via spectral analysis of flexural waves
cells.D17: Introduces a wearable sensor technique using flexural wave spectra to non-invasively measure tibial compressive force during walking, validated with strong correlation in 9 participants.
cells.E17: Models the tibia as an axially-compressed beam and infers load from load-dependent shifts in flexural-wave frequency spectra measured by skin-mounted accelerometer/transducer.
cells.F17: Not relevant to GSE's core calibration/prediction stack; pure biomechanical sensing hardware research.
cells.G17: Only a distant stretch: could inspire a future 'injury-risk overlay' data feed if GSE partners with wearable-data providers for player-load monitoring features.

cells.C18: Annotate Rhetorical Relations with INCEpTION: A Comparison with Automatic Approaches
cells.D18: Compares manual annotation to BERT/DistilBERT/Logistic Regression classifiers for identifying rhetorical relations (elaboration, contrast, cause-effect) in cricket news reports.
cells.E18: Fine-tunes transformer and classical NLP classifiers to predict discourse relation labels in sports-news text, benchmarked against human annotation.
cells.F18: Relevant to GSE's brand-language/NLP style-control needs: discourse-relation classification could help enforce consistent, non-'AI-powered' framing in auto-generated content copy.
cells.G18: Use rhetorical-relation classifiers to audit auto-generated social/media content for consistent causal/explanatory phrasing ('math you can read'), flagging copy that reads too speculative or AI-hype-like.

cells.C19: Signals in the Noise: Decoding Unexpected Engagement Patterns on Twitter
cells.D19: Analyzes 600k+ tweets to show sports/games content generates unexpectedly high likes/comments relative to predicted engagement, driven by emotional investment versus informational sharing.
cells.E19: Defines an 'unexpectedness quotient' comparing observed vs. predicted engagement by content type using Signaling and Attention Economy theory.
cells.F19: Directly useful for GSE's automated social/media content generation component -- informs what content framing (emotional vs. informational) drives sports-audience engagement.
cells.G19: Build an 'unexpectedness quotient' scorer into GSE's content pipeline to predict which auto-generated picks/posts will overperform on likes vs. shares, and tune posting strategy per pick type accordingly.

cells.C20: Inference in a generalized Bradley-Terry model for paired comparisons with covariates and a growing number of subjects
cells.D20: Establishes asymptotic consistency and normality of MLE estimators in a Bradley-Terry model with covariates (e.g., home-field advantage) as the number of teams grows.
cells.E20: Derives high-dimensional asymptotic theory for merit parameters and covariate coefficients in paired-comparison models, extended to sparse comparison graphs.
cells.F20: Directly relevant to GSE's core rating/probability model: Bradley-Terry with covariates is a natural per-sport probability model candidate to replace or complement the current global calibrator.
cells.G20: Use this covariate-augmented Bradley-Terry framework as one leg of the per-sport ensemble the founder suspects is needed to fix calibration, explicitly encoding home-field advantage and other structural covariates with proven asymptotic guarantees.

cells.C21: Mallows Model with Learned Distance Metrics: Sampling and Maximum Likelihood Estimation
cells.D21: Generalizes the Mallows ranking model to learn the distance metric from data (not just fixed Kendall tau), with an FPTAS sampler and consistent joint MLE, validated on sports ranking data.
cells.E21: Develops Lα-distance Mallows models with a polynomial-time approximate sampling scheme and joint estimation of central ranking, dispersion, and metric exponent.
cells.F21: Relevant to GSE's ranking/upset modeling: learns how 'surprising' rankings are per-sport (frequency of upsets), which maps to sport-specific variance structure needed for the failing calibration gate.
cells.G21: Fit a per-sport Mallows distance metric to characterize how upset-prone each league is, then use the learned dispersion parameter as an input feature to bootstrap-mode confidence capping and per-sport calibration models.

cells.C22: Temporal Dynamics of Emotions in Italian Online Soccer Fandoms
cells.D22: Finds that fan-comment sentiment burstiness (especially anger) on Instagram correlates significantly with final league standings, improving explanatory power by 32% in statistical models.
cells.E22: Applies sentiment analysis and complex-systems burstiness metrics to fan comments across 83 teams over a season, correlating with performance outcomes.
cells.F22: A stretch for the core prediction engine but interesting: fan sentiment burstiness as an alternative-data signal could be an auxiliary feature for team performance/morale proxies.
cells.G22: Incorporate a social-media sentiment-burstiness feature (scraped alongside odds data) as an experimental weak signal in the ensemble, especially for soft factors like team morale not captured by box scores.

cells.C23: Automated Meta Prompt Engineering for Alignment with the Theory of Mind
cells.D23: Deploys an LLM-as-judge meta-prompting system at the US Open 2024 that iteratively aligns AI-generated tennis articles with human editor expectations via in-context learning.
cells.E23: Uses agentic reinforcement learning where an LLM judge teaches a generator LLM to match human-edit patterns across content traits (factualness, novelty, relevancy) in a Hilbert vector space.
cells.F23: Directly relevant to GSE's automated social/media content generation ambitions and its NLP brand-language enforcement (avoiding 'AI-powered' framing while producing polished, human-approved copy).
cells.G23: Adapt the LLM-as-judge alignment loop specifically to enforce GSE's 'math you can read' brand voice, training a content-generation judge to reject any phrasing that implies AI authorship or overhypes predictions.

cells.C24: Simultaneous All-Pay Auctions with Budget Constraints
cells.D24: Characterizes Nash equilibria for two-player all-pay auctions across multiple items under budget constraints, showing equilibria may not always exist unlike the unconstrained case.
cells.E24: Constructs joint-distribution Nash equilibria for one-, two-, and three-item budget-constrained all-pay auction games via game-theoretic analysis.
cells.F24: Tangential: all-pay auctions are a classic model for competitive effort in sports, loosely relevant to GSE's understanding of competitive incentive structures but not to its core forecasting stack.
cells.G24: Could inform modeling of playoff-race 'effort' incentives (e.g., tanking vs. competing) as a covariate for in-season prediction adjustments when teams have asymmetric stakes/budgets remaining.

cells.C25: Investigating Cultural Dimensions and Technological Acceptance: EPTS Adoption in Qatar's Football Sector
cells.D25: Uses Hofstede's cultural dimensions and TAM survey analysis to find perceived usefulness and low power distance drive adoption of player-tracking tech among Qatari football stakeholders.
cells.E25: Applies multiple regression on survey data (perceived usefulness, ease of use, power distance, innovation receptiveness) to explain technology adoption.
cells.F25: Weak relevance: a social-science technology-adoption study, not a modeling or data technique GSE could reuse for calibration or forecasting.
cells.G25: Only a stretch: could inform GSE's B2B go-to-market messaging/design when pitching embeddable widgets or trust/compliance tooling to non-US sports organizations with different tech-adoption cultures.

cells.C26: Solving Football by Exploiting Equilibrium Structure of 2p0s Differential Games with One-Sided Information
cells.D26: Proves equilibrium strategies in asymmetric-information two-player zero-sum games concentrate on few action prototypes, collapsing game-tree complexity and enabling solution of a 22-player continuous football simulation.
cells.E26: Combines model-free multiagent RL and model predictive control exploiting proven equilibrium sparsity in imperfect-information extensive-form games.
cells.F26: Relevant as advanced game-theoretic/RL methodology; more applicable to in-play strategic simulation than GSE's current statistical scoring engine, but shows techniques for handling asymmetric information which parallels market/bettor information asymmetry.
cells.G26: Apply the one-sided-information equilibrium framework to model how sharp bettors (informed) versus the market maker (uninformed) interact, informing GSE's closing-line-value benchmark and its own confidence-concealment strategy in pick timing.

cells.C27: Adaptive Manipulation for Coalitions in Knockout Tournaments
cells.D27: Studies computational complexity of coalitions strategically throwing games round-by-round in knockout tournaments to boost a designated player's win probability, proving hardness results and fixed-parameter tractability.
cells.E27: Formalizes 'adaptive constructive coalition manipulation' in probabilistic knockout brackets and analyzes complexity across the polynomial hierarchy.
cells.F27: Relevant to GSE's trust/compliance toolkit and integrity monitoring: formal complexity results on tournament manipulability could inform detection of match-fixing/tanking patterns in bracket-based competitions.
cells.G27: Build an integrity-monitoring module using this manipulation-detection theory to flag statistically anomalous bracket outcomes suggestive of coalition manipulation, feeding GSE's trust/compliance product.

cells.C28: sEMG-based Gesture-Free Hand Intention Recognition: System, Dataset, Toolbox, and Benchmark Results
cells.D28: Builds a wearable sEMG system and dataset for recognizing covert hand intentions without visible gestures, benchmarked across single-day, cross-day, and cross-subject settings including sports scenarios.
cells.E28: Uses surface electromyography and isometric contraction theory with a myoelectric watch to classify 6-12 class hand intentions.
cells.F28: Not relevant to GSE's software/prediction stack; a wearable biosensing HCI paper.
cells.G28: No meaningful application; at most a far-fetched idea for a future athlete-wearable-data partnership feeding alternative signals into the data pipeline.

cells.C29: Esports Training, Periodization, and Software -- a Scoping Review
cells.D29: A scoping review finding esports performance research is fragmented across psychology, nutrition, and informatics, lacking an integrated training-periodization theory or software tooling.
cells.E29: Systematic scoping-review methodology surveying existing esports training/performance literature and software systems.
cells.F29: Relevant only if GSE expands prediction coverage into esports markets; otherwise a background survey with no modeling technique to reuse.
cells.G29: If GSE considers adding esports betting markets, this review flags the data/feature gaps (no standardized performance metrics) that would need custom data-ingestion work before modeling is viable.

cells.C30: Hierarchical Clustering using Reversible Binary Cellular Automata for High-Dimensional Data
cells.D30: Proposes a novel hierarchical clustering algorithm using cyclic structure of reversible cellular automata, competitive with existing methods on benchmark datasets including sports applications.
cells.E30: Encodes data via frequency-based encoding preserving Hamming distance, then clusters using CA cycle relationships and median-based inter-cycle linking.
cells.F30: A general-purpose clustering technique with minor tangential relevance -- could be used for segmenting teams/players/bet-types in GSE's data pipeline, but not directly tied to calibration or forecasting problems.
cells.G30: Use as an alternative clustering backend for automatically grouping similar prop-bet markets or player archetypes when building per-sport sub-models, as a lightweight alternative to k-means/hierarchical clustering.

cells.C31: Sequential Manipulation Against Rank Aggregation: Theory and Algorithm
cells.D31: Formulates online adversarial manipulation of pairwise-comparison data collection as a distributionally robust game, proposing sequential attack policies with proven asymptotic optimality against rank aggregation systems.
cells.E31: Models attacker-vs-ranker as a distributionally robust game, deriving Bayesian sequential manipulation policies and a distributionally robust MLE defense.
cells.F31: Relevant to GSE's trust/compliance and data-integrity concerns: pairwise-comparison rank aggregation underlies rating systems (e.g., Elo-like inputs), and this shows how such systems can be adversarially gamed via manipulated data feeds.
cells.G31: Use the distributionally-robust MLE defense technique to harden GSE's rating models against manipulated or noisy scraped data sources (e.g., compromised or bot-inflated stat feeds) in the ingestion pipeline.

cells.C32: Modeling cyclicality and intransitivity in paired comparisons data
cells.D32: Develops a framework decomposing paired-comparison preference profiles into transitive and cyclic components, using sparse dictionary selection to detect rock-paper-scissors-like intransitivities.
cells.E32: Orthogonally decomposes comparison data into transitive merit-based and cyclic components via an overcomplete cycle dictionary, with large-sample recovery guarantees.
cells.F32: Directly relevant to GSE's core rating models: sports matchups often exhibit stylistic intransitivity (Team A beats B, B beats C, C beats A) that standard Bradley-Terry/Elo ignore, a plausible contributor to the calibration failure.
cells.G32: Add a cyclic-structure diagnostic to the calibration pipeline to detect which sports/matchups have significant intransitivity, then route those to a matchup-specific model component instead of forcing a single global transitive rating.

cells.C33: Online Learning in Betting Markets: Profit versus Prediction
cells.D33: Proves bookmaker profit-maximization and information-eliciting price-setting are fundamentally incompatible goals, and introduces online learning algorithms for dynamic odds-pricing with regret guarantees.
cells.E33: Analyzes the belief-vs-price interplay in binary betting markets and derives O(sqrt(T)) regret online pricing algorithms updating after each bet.
cells.F33: Highly relevant: directly addresses the tension between GSE's stated 'math you can read' calibration/prediction goal and any monetization, plus gives online-learning tools applicable to real-time confidence/line updates.
cells.G33: Use the online-pricing regret-bound framework to design GSE's own live-updating confidence scores as bets/data arrive, explicitly separating a 'pure prediction' calibrated probability from any monetized product feature to keep the brand's non-AI, math-transparent claim defensible.

cells.C34: Structural and Algorithmic Results for Stable Cycles and Partitions in the Roommates Problem
cells.D34: Establishes structural and algorithmic results for stable partitions in the Stable Roommates problem, including efficient enumeration and fairness/optimality criteria, with applications to sports scheduling and time-sharing.
cells.E34: Extends stable-matching theory to stable partitions/half-matchings, giving complexity results for fair and optimal partition computation.
cells.F34: Tangential: stable-matching theory could apply to future GSE features like fair scheduling or resource-time-sharing in B2B widget deployments, but not to core prediction/calibration.
cells.G34: Could inform algorithmic design for fairly allocating widget/API rate-limits or matchmaking users to leagues/products in the B2B embeddable widget product line.

cells.C35: Motor Imagery Task Alters Dynamics of Human Body Posture
cells.D35: Shows kinesthetic motor imagery measurably and directionally alters center-of-pressure postural dynamics, supporting psycho-neuromuscular theory in a controlled lab study.
cells.E35: Uses a nonlinear dynamical model of center-of-pressure sway to quantify path length and long-range correlation changes under different imagery conditions.
cells.F35: Not relevant to GSE's software/data stack; a neuroscience/rehabilitation biomechanics study.
cells.G35: No practical application beyond a very distant idea for athlete-wearable data if GSE ever expands into biomechanical performance feeds.

cells.D36: Proposes a supervised algorithm to group high-dimensional predictors into networks based on association with a response, with consistency guarantees and a fast bootstrap for uncertainty, validated on sports analytics data.
cells.E36: Constructs an implicit weighted predictor network and clusters predictors via network-wide metrics, using model-assisted bootstrap for computationally efficient uncertainty quantification.
cells.F36: Directly relevant to GSE's feature-engineering pipeline: offers a principled way to group correlated predictors (many stat features per sport) and quantify their uncertainty, useful for building leaner per-sport models.
cells.G36: Use the network-grouping method to prune GSE's large multi-source feature set per sport into interpretable predictor groups, directly supporting the 'math you can read' transparency claim while reducing overfitting behind the failing MAE backtest.

cells.C37: Capturing Momentum: Tennis Match Analysis Using Machine Learning and Time Series Theory
cells.D37: Uses Hidden Markov Models to define player 'momentum' as a latent performance state, then validates its predictive significance with XGBoost/LightGBM and SHAP feature analysis on tennis matches.
cells.E37: Combines HMM-based latent momentum estimation with gradient-boosted trees and SHAP importance ranking to explain and predict in-match performance shifts.
cells.F37: Directly relevant to GSE's in-play/live prediction ambitions: a concrete latent-state approach to model 'momentum,' a concept often invoked in sports betting narratives that GSE could formalize mathematically.
cells.G37: Build an HMM-based 'momentum state' layer feeding into live win-probability updates, giving GSE a defensible, transparent mathematical basis (not 'AI hype') for in-play confidence adjustments during a game.

cells.C38: PureLottery: Fair and Bias-Resistant Leader Election with a Novel Single-Elimination Tournament Algorithm
cells.D38: Introduces a blockchain leader-election protocol modeled on single-elimination sports tournaments, proving game-theoretic fairness and bias-resistance without decentralized RNG.
cells.E38: Uses pairwise elimination matches with game-theoretic incentive analysis to guarantee each honest participant at least 1/n win probability under adversarial manipulation.
cells.F38: Tangential: relevant only if GSE's Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR game needs provably fair random selection mechanisms (e.g., for prize draws or matchmaking) without a trusted centralized RNG.
cells.G38: Adopt the PureLottery tournament-based fairness protocol for any randomized prize/reward draws or matchmaking in Galaxy Dynasty, giving a publicly verifiable fairness guarantee as part of the trust/compliance toolkit.

cells.C39: They were robbed! Scoring by the middlemost to attenuate biased judging in boxing
cells.D39: Proposes majority-rule round-by-round scoring in boxing (rather than aggregate judge totals) to reduce the influence of biased judges, using social choice theory.
cells.E39: Applies majority rule and middlemost aggregation functions across judges' round scores to create a coordination problem that dilutes partisan bias.
cells.F39: Tangential but conceptually relevant to GSE's grading/settlement fairness and market-efficiency framing (closing-line value benchmarks against potentially biased official outcomes in judged sports).
cells.G39: Apply the middlemost-aggregation concept to GSE's own multi-model ensemble voting (combine per-sport sub-models via 'majority round wins' rather than simple averaging) to reduce the influence of any single miscalibrated sub-model.

cells.D40: Adapts the kinematic theory of rapid human movements (Sigma-lognormal model, from handwriting) to reconstruct speech motor kinematics and infer age/pathology from formant data.
cells.E40: Applies Sigma-lognormal neuromuscular impulse-response modeling to formant-derived speech kinematics, validated on English and German voice databases.
cells.F40: No direct relevance to GSE's prediction/calibration stack; a speech/handwriting biomechanics modeling paper mentioning sports only as a general application domain.
cells.G40: No credible application beyond a very distant idea for voice-based content generation quality checks in GSE's automated media pipeline.

cells.C41: Optimal strategy for trail running with nutrition and fatigue factors
cells.D41: Extends Keller's classical running model with nutrition and fatigue dynamics, using Pontryagin's Maximum Principle to derive optimal pacing strategies validated against real trail-race data.
cells.E41: Applies optimal control theory (Pontryagin Maximum Principle) to a fatigue/nutrition-augmented running dynamics model, predicting race time within a few percent error.
cells.F41: Tangential: an athlete-performance optimization model unrelated to GSE's market-prediction/calibration engine, though methodologically adjacent (optimal control vs. optimal stopping used elsewhere in the batch).
cells.G41: Could inspire a niche B2B or content feature: a 'pacing strategy' calculator widget for endurance-sports fans/athletes as a side product leveraging GSE's math-transparency brand.

cells.C42: The Fallacy of Borda Count Method -- Why it is Useless with Group Intelligence and Shouldn't be Used with Big Data
cells.D42: Argues that Borda Count voting/rating methods break down under Poisson/Pareto-distributed rating behavior common on large online platforms, using prior theory on predictable individualistic voting.
cells.E42: Applies a Poisson/Pareto behavioral theory of online rating platforms to critique range/Borda voting aggregation methods.
cells.F42: Weak relevance: a critique of a specific voting/aggregation method sometimes used in sports awards, not directly applicable to GSE's probabilistic scoring engine.
cells.G42: Only a minor caution: avoid using naive Borda-style aggregation if GSE ever builds fan-voting or leaderboard features in Galaxy Dynasty, since this paper argues it misrepresents true preference distributions at scale.

cells.C43: Game-Theoretic Analysis of Adversarial Decision Making in a Complex Sociophysical System
cells.D43: Combines Kuramoto synchronization dynamics with Lotka-Volterra resource competition on scale-free networks to model two adversarial teams, finding periphery-resource concentration often wins unless decision-cycle asymmetries dominate.
cells.E43: Uses coupled physics-based models (Kuramoto oscillators for decision synchrony, Lotka-Volterra for resource competition) with Nash Dominant Game Pruning for equilibrium search on complex networks.
cells.F43: Conceptually adjacent to GSE's founder's e-process/ensemble theory (CEPT) in spirit -- a worst-case adversarial dynamical-systems framing -- but not directly reusable for calibration; more a sports/military strategy modeling paper.
cells.G43: Could inspire modeling team-vs-team strategic resource allocation (e.g., bullpen usage, rotation management) as a Kuramoto-Lotka-Volterra adversarial system, feeding a novel strategic-context feature into game predictions.

cells.C44: Game Theory Solutions in Sensor-Based Human Activity Recognition: A Review
cells.D44: Surveys how game-theoretic concepts (e.g., Shapley values, adversarial games) can improve accuracy and robustness of sensor-based human activity recognition, including sports applications.
cells.E44: Literature review connecting game theory techniques to HAR model design, feature selection, and robustness.
cells.F44: Weak relevance: a survey of game theory applied to wearable-sensor activity recognition, not directly tied to GSE's odds/probability modeling.
cells.G44: Minor idea: use Shapley-value feature attribution (a game-theory concept highlighted here) to explain per-sport model predictions to users, supporting the 'math you can read' transparency positioning.

cells.C45: How Hard Is Squash? -- Towards Information Theoretic Analysis of Motor Behavior in Squash
cells.D45: Adapts Fitts' Law (an HCI difficulty model) to quantify shot difficulty and effort in squash based on speed, movement time, and distance data collected from players.
cells.E45: Formulates a modified Fitts' Law information-theoretic model correlating shot parameters with task difficulty/effort in a racquet sport.
cells.F45: Weak/tangential: a niche biomechanics-HCI crossover study with no direct connection to GSE's statistical forecasting or calibration problems.
cells.G45: Could be a very narrow content/product idea: a 'shot difficulty index' stat feature for racquet-sport coverage if GSE expands beyond its current NFL/MLB/MLS focus.

cells.C46: Analysis of ELO Rating Scheme in MOBA Games
cells.D46: Critiques Elo's fairness properties in online video-game matchmaking and proposes an alternative effort-based rating scheme, compared via simulation.
cells.E46: Analyzes Elo's advantages/drawbacks in competitive matchmaking and simulates an effort-based rating alternative.
cells.F46: Directly relevant: Elo-style rating systems are foundational building blocks for sport-specific probability models GSE needs; this paper's critique and alternative design are germane to fixing the failing calibration gate.
cells.G46: Evaluate the proposed effort-based rating variant as an alternative or complement to standard Elo in GSE's per-sport models, particularly for sports where simple win/loss Elo may misrepresent true team strength (e.g., blowout-prone leagues).

cells.D47: Derives a fluid-dynamics theory for wave-driven propulsion of floating bodies, validated against a robotic 'SurferBot,' with discussion of applications to competitive water sports.
cells.E47: Couples body equations of motion to a quasi-potential flow model to predict drift speed and propulsive thrust, verified by momentum conservation and experiment.
cells.F47: Not relevant to GSE's software/statistical stack; a fluid dynamics/robotics physics paper.
cells.G47: No credible application; at most a far-fetched idea for future water-sports (e.g., surfing/rowing) analytics content if GSE ever expands sport coverage.

cells.C48: How to Make Knockout Tournaments More Popular?
cells.D48: Introduces the problem of seeding knockout tournaments to maximize a 'popularity/profit' score over matches rather than to favor a specific player, with computational complexity results.
cells.E48: Formalizes tournament seeding as score-maximization over an ordered-strength player set and analyzes complexity of optimal seeding.
cells.F48: Relevant to GSE's Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR persistent game and any B2B bracket-style products: gives an algorithmic basis for designing more engaging/profitable tournament brackets.
cells.G48: Use the popularity-maximizing seeding algorithm to design Galaxy Dynasty's tournament brackets so that high-profile 'dream matchups' are more likely to occur later, boosting engagement and content-generation opportunities.

cells.C49: Optimal Estimation under a Semiparametric Density Ratio Model
cells.D49: Shows that pooling data across related populations via a semiparametric density ratio model achieves near-parametric efficiency for the smaller-sample population, illustrated with U.S. collegiate sports revenue data.
cells.E49: Uses the density ratio model (DRM) to combine samples from multiple related distributions, proving asymptotic efficiency gains for underrepresented groups' estimates.
cells.F49: Directly relevant to GSE's calibration problem: DRM-style pooling could help improve per-sport probability estimates for sparse-data sports (bootstrap mode) by borrowing strength from data-rich sports/leagues.
cells.G49: Apply a density-ratio-model approach to pool historical data across related sports/leagues (e.g., minor leagues borrowing from majors) so smaller-sample sports achieve near-full-data calibration accuracy in bootstrap mode.

cells.C50: Static and Dynamic BART for Rank-Order Data
cells.D50: Develops nonparametric Bayesian Additive Regression Tree models (ROBART, ARROBART) for rank-order data with time dependence, outperforming linear competitors on weekly NCAA football pollster rankings.
cells.E50: Uses BART to model nonlinear latent scores underlying observed ranks, with closed-form filtering/smoothing for dynamic autoregressive score evolution and Gibbs-sampler inference.
cells.F50: Directly relevant: a proven Bayesian nonparametric method for dynamic team-ranking/score estimation with full posterior uncertainty, applicable to GSE's calibration and ensemble-model redesign for sport-specific probability estimation.
cells.G50: Replace or augment GSE's global calibrator with an ARROBART-style dynamic Bayesian tree model per sport, directly using its closed-form posterior/smoothing machinery to generate calibrated, time-varying confidence intervals for picks.

cells.C51: Generalized Bradley-Terry Models for Score Estimation from Paired Comparisons
cells.D51: Introduces a broad exponential-family generalization of Bradley-Terry models with guaranteed strict convexity, and proves MAP estimates are monotonic and Lipschitz-resilient to new comparisons.
cells.E51: Defines the Generalized Bradley-Terry (GBT) family within the exponential family and proves convexity/robustness properties for Gaussian-prior MAP score estimation.
cells.F51: Directly relevant to GSE's core rating engine: provides theoretically robust, provably well-behaved scoring updates for team/player ratings, addressing stability concerns in an ensemble/calibration redesign.
cells.G51: Adopt the GBT family's Lipschitz-resilience guarantee to bound how much any single new game result can swing a team's rating, giving GSE a formally provable stability property to cite in its 'math you can read' brand claims.

cells.C52: Comparison of Visual Trackers for Biomechanical Analysis of Running
cells.D52: Benchmarks six pose-tracking models against expert manual annotation on 5,870+ sprint frames, showing joint-based trackers with post-processing achieve strong accuracy for biomechanical angle analysis.
cells.E52: Compares point- and joint-based pose estimators on trunk/hip/knee angle accuracy, with an outlier-detection and fusion post-processing module reducing RMSE substantially.
cells.F52: Tangential: relevant only if GSE ingests video/pose-tracking data for athlete performance features; not connected to its current stats/odds-based prediction-engine data sources.
cells.G52: If GSE later ingests broadcast video for automated highlight/event extraction, this benchmark helps choose a reliable pose-tracker for biomechanical features feeding player-performance sub-models.

cells.C53: Deep Learning for Sports Video Event Detection: Tasks, Datasets, Methods, and Challenges
cells.D53: Surveys and taxonomizes deep-learning approaches for temporal action localization, action spotting, and precise event spotting in sports video, critiquing existing benchmarks and evaluation metrics.
cells.E53: Provides a structured taxonomy of temporal modeling strategies and multimodal frameworks for detecting/timing events in sports broadcast video.
cells.F53: Relevant to GSE's data-ingestion and future automated content-generation pipeline if it processes broadcast video, e.g., for real-time event extraction to feed picks or highlight clips.
cells.G53: Use precise event-spotting techniques from this survey to auto-detect scoring plays/turnovers from broadcast feeds, generating structured event data that speeds up GSE's data pipeline versus manual scraping alone.

cells.C54: Polar Coordinate-Based 2D Pose Prior with Neural Distance Field
cells.D54: Proposes a polar-coordinate pose representation and neural distance field to refine noisy 2D human pose estimates for sports biomechanics, validated on long-jump video.
cells.E54: Uses a non-geodesic polar-distance metric and gradient-based augmentation to correct erroneous joint estimates via a neural distance field pose prior.
cells.F54: Not directly relevant to GSE's core prediction-engine work; a computer-vision pose-refinement technique for biomechanics rather than probabilistic forecasting.
cells.G54: Only relevant if GSE builds video-based player-tracking features later; could improve pose-estimation robustness for any future motion-derived performance metrics.

cells.C55: From Players to Champions: A Generalizable ML Approach for Match Outcome Prediction with Insights from the FIFA World Cup
cells.D55: Combines team-level historical data with player-specific stats (goals, assists, passing accuracy) in a classification framework to predict FIFA World Cup outcomes, outperforming aggregate-only baselines.
cells.E55: Builds year-specific team profiles integrating individual player metrics, applies dimensionality reduction and hyperparameter-tuned classifiers for match-outcome prediction.
cells.F55: Directly relevant to GSE's core prediction model: a concrete example of feature engineering (player-level plus team-level) improving match prediction accuracy, applicable to the failing MAE backtest.
cells.G55: Adopt the year-specific player-roster profiling approach to better handle roster turnover in GSE's models, directly targeting one likely source of the current model's underperformance versus the naive baseline.

cells.C56: Iterative Tool Usage Exploration for Multimodal Agents via Step-wise Preference Tuning
cells.D56: Introduces SPoRt, a self-exploration framework letting multimodal LLM agents learn effective tool-usage strategies without human-annotated data, via step-wise preference tuning and AI feedback verification.
cells.E56: Uses synthesized tasks, sampled tool-use trajectories, and preference-tuning (informed by an AI verifier) to iteratively improve an agent's tool-calling policy.
cells.F56: Relevant to GSE's internal autonomous coding/research agents (Jarvis, Hermes, Fable): a concrete method for improving agentic tool-use without costly human annotation.
cells.G56: Apply the step-wise preference-tuning loop to train GSE's internal agents to better use data-pipeline/ETL tools (scraping, odds ingestion) autonomously, reducing manual annotation needed to improve agent reliability.

cells.C57: X-Cross: Dynamic Integration of Language Models for Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation
cells.D57: Presents a cross-domain recommendation model that dynamically integrates multiple domain-specific LoRA-adapted LLMs layer-by-layer, achieving strong performance with far less fine-tuning data, including transfers into a Sports domain.
cells.E57: Refines each domain LLM's per-layer representations using activations from other domain adapters, propagating merged representations through the network for cross-domain transfer.
cells.F57: Relevant to GSE's need for genuinely better, data-efficient per-sport modeling: demonstrates how to transfer knowledge across domains (sports) with limited fine-tuning data, directly analogous to needing per-sport models without full independent retraining.
cells.G57: Adapt the layer-wise cross-domain adapter-fusion technique to build GSE's suspected 'independent per-sport probability models,' sharing structure across sports (NFL/MLB/MLS) while preserving sport-specific nuance, cutting the data needed per sport.

cells.C58: Integrating Learning-Based Manipulation and Physics-Based Locomotion for Whole-Body Badminton Robot Control
cells.D58: Builds a hybrid imitation+reinforcement learning and model-based control system enabling a badminton robot to achieve 94.5%/90.7% success rates against a serving machine and human players.
cells.E58: Combines model-based chassis locomotion with a physics-informed IL+RL arm-control policy, using privileged-information guidance and critic pretraining to stabilize the IL-to-RL transition.
cells.F58: Not relevant to GSE's software/statistical prediction stack; a robotics control paper.
cells.G58: No credible direct application; only a very distant idea if GSE ever explores robotics-adjacent sports-tech demos for marketing purposes.

cells.C59: Bridging Data Gaps and Building Knowledge Networks in Indian Football Analytics
cells.D59: An ethnographic HCI study of informal, decentralized analyst communities in Indian football overcoming data scarcity via peer mentorship, proposing frugal AI-assisted data tooling interventions.
cells.E59: Uses digital ethnography and participant observation to characterize grassroots analytics communities, then proposes low-cost decentralized-knowledge-platform interventions.
cells.F59: Relevant background context for GSE's multi-source, free/scraped sports data ingestion strategy (e.g., Pro-Football-Reference-style scraping) in data-scarce markets or leagues.
cells.G59: Use the paper's frugal-innovation framing to design GSE's own low-cost data-ingestion strategy for under-covered leagues (lower MLS tiers, international soccer), tapping community-sourced data the way these informal analyst networks do.

cells.C60: pix2pockets: Shot Suggestions in 8-Ball Pool from a Single Image in the Wild
cells.D60: Builds an RL-based pool-shot recommender from a single table image, with a new annotated dataset and standardized RL environment, showing standard RL algorithms struggle to clear the table without fouls.
cells.E60: Combines object detection (table/ball localization) with a custom RL environment and baseline algorithms to suggest optimal pool shots.
cells.F60: Not directly relevant to GSE's core forecasting/calibration problem; a niche computer-vision/RL application in a different sport category (billiards) than GSE's current NFL/MLB/MLS focus.
cells.G60: Only a stretch: could illustrate RL environment-design patterns useful if GSE ever builds a skill-based mini-game inside Galaxy Dynasty requiring physics-based shot simulation.

cells.C61: Traffic Adaptive Moving-window Service Patrolling for Real-time Incident Management during High-impact Events
cells.D61: Introduces TAMPA, a dynamic-programming patrol-routing algorithm for traffic incident management around major events (sports tournaments, concerts), showing large improvements over stationary/random patrol strategies.
cells.E61: Integrates predictive traffic modeling with real-time complaint-pattern shift detection (via Dvoretzky-Kiefer-Wolfowitz inequality bounds) to dynamically reoptimize patrol routes.
cells.F61: Not relevant to GSE's prediction-engine/calibration work; an urban traffic-management operations research paper only tangentially about sporting events as a traffic driver.
cells.G61: No credible direct application; at most a distant idea for a future 'game-day logistics' B2B product unrelated to GSE's current core business.

cells.C62: GridMind: A Multi-Agent NLP Framework for Unified, Cross-Modal NFL Data Insights
cells.D62: Introduces a multi-agent RAG+LLM framework that unifies structured, semi-structured, and unstructured NFL data sources to answer complex natural-language queries via a conversational interface.
cells.E62: Distributed specialized agents handle prompt interpretation, retrieval-augmented generation across multimodal NFL data, and response synthesis in a modular architecture.
cells.F62: Highly relevant: directly analogous to GSE's data-ingestion pipeline (multi-source NFL data) and its internal agent tooling (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable), demonstrating a working multi-agent RAG architecture for exactly its domain.
cells.G62: Adapt GridMind's multi-agent RAG architecture as the backbone of GSE's Intelligence Graph query layer, letting internal teams or eventually B2B customers ask natural-language questions across structured stats, odds, and scraped text sources.

cells.C63: Towards Unconstrained 2D Pose Estimation of the Human Spine
cells.D63: Introduces SpineTrack, a large dataset with detailed spinal keypoints, and SpinePose, a distillation-based pose model jointly predicting body and spine keypoints for sports biomechanics.
cells.E63: Combines synthetic (Unreal Engine/OpenSim) and real annotated data with knowledge distillation and anatomical regularization to extend pose estimators to spine articulation.
cells.F63: Not directly relevant to GSE's statistical prediction stack; a computer-vision biomechanics dataset/model paper.
cells.G63: Only relevant as a future video-analytics building block if GSE adds detailed biomechanical player-tracking features to its data pipeline.

cells.C64: SPoRt -- Safe Policy Ratio: Certified Training and Deployment of Task Policies in Model-Free RL
cells.D64: Provides theoretical bounds on safety-property violation probability for RL policies based on a maximum policy ratio to a safe base policy, with a data-driven scenario-approach method (SPoRt) for certifying deployment.
cells.E64: Derives probabilistic safety bounds via policy-ratio analysis and introduces Projected PPO to train task policies under a user-specified violation-rate constraint.
cells.F64: Relevant to GSE's internal autonomous agents (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) if any use RL: offers certified safety guarantees for deploying learned policies, useful for any RL-driven pipeline automation or trading-style decision components.
cells.G64: Use SPoRt's certified safety-bound framework to give provable guarantees on GSE's autonomous coding/research agents' worst-case behavior before granting them broader production access to the data pipeline or model deployment.

cells.C65: From Broadcast to Minimap: Achieving State-of-the-Art SoccerNet Game State Reconstruction
cells.D65: Presents a first-place SoccerNet Game State Reconstruction pipeline combining detection, camera-parameter estimation, and re-identification tracking to localize all players/referees from a single broadcast camera.
cells.E65: Integrates fine-tuned YOLOv5m detection, SegFormer-based camera calibration, and DeepSORT tracking with re-ID, orientation, and jersey-number recognition for real-world-coordinate player tracking.
cells.F65: Relevant to GSE's data-ingestion ambitions if it ever moves beyond box-score/odds data to broadcast-video-derived tracking data for MLS/soccer markets, providing a proven state-of-the-art pipeline design.
cells.G65: License or replicate this single-camera tracking pipeline to generate proprietary tracking-derived features (formations, spacing) for soccer/MLS predictions, differentiating GSE's data beyond free box-score scraping.

cells.C66: End-to-End Deep Learning for Real-Time Neuroimaging-Based Assessment of Bimanual Motor Skills
cells.D66: Presents an end-to-end deep learning model processing raw fNIRS brain-imaging signals to classify bimanual surgical/motor skill level with over 92% generalization accuracy, eliminating manual preprocessing.
cells.E66: Trains a deep network directly on raw functional near-infrared spectroscopy signals to classify motor-skill performance across suturing, cutting, and intubation tasks.
cells.F66: Not relevant to GSE's software/statistical prediction stack; a medical neuroimaging/motor-skill assessment paper.
cells.G66: No credible application; at most a very distant idea if GSE explores athlete neuro-performance data partnerships.

cells.C67: Nonparametric function-on-scalar regression using deep neural networks
cells.D67: Proposes a deep-neural-network estimator for function-on-scalar regression that adaptively handles anisotropic smoothness, with proven convergence rates and application to sports-medicine ground reaction force data.
cells.E67: Uses deep networks to approximate nonlinear scalar-to-function mappings, deriving minimax convergence rates over anisotropic Besov spaces that mitigate the curse of dimensionality.
cells.F67: Relevant methodologically: a theoretically grounded nonparametric regression technique for functional/time-series sports data that could improve GSE's forecasting model beyond linear/basis-function approaches contributing to its MAE underperformance.
cells.G67: Apply this deep function-on-scalar regression to model entire in-game probability trajectories (not just final win probability) as a function of pre-game scalar features, giving smoother, better-calibrated live win-probability curves.

cells.C68: FineCausal: A Causal-Based Framework for Interpretable Fine-Grained Action Quality Assessment
cells.D68: Introduces a causal-intervention framework using graph attention and temporal causal attention to disentangle genuine performance cues from background confounders in fine-grained sports action scoring.
cells.E68: Uses a causal-intervention module (graph attention) and temporal causal attention to produce interpretable, spurious-correlation-resistant action quality scores, state-of-the-art on FineDiving-HM.
cells.F68: Directly relevant to GSE's calibration/trust problem: a causal-inference technique explicitly designed to prevent spurious-correlation-driven miscalibration, aligning with the founder's CEPT causal e-process interests and the need for interpretable, trustworthy scoring.
cells.G68: Borrow the causal-intervention-plus-attention design pattern to build an interpretable causal layer into GSE's prediction engine, explicitly disentangling genuine predictive signal from confounded correlations to help pass the Brier/ECE calibration gate with defensible interpretability.

cells.C69: ForcePose: A Deep Learning Approach for Force Calculation Based on Action Recognition Using MediaPipe Pose Estimation Combined with Object Detection
cells.D69: Combines pose estimation and object detection to estimate applied physical force in human-object interactions without sensors, achieving 5.83N mean error, applicable to sports science.
cells.E69: Fuses MediaPipe skeletal tracking with SSD MobileNet object detection into a neural network predicting force magnitude/direction from video alone.
cells.F69: Not directly relevant to GSE's statistical/calibration stack; a computer-vision biomechanics tool for sensor-free force estimation.
cells.G69: Only relevant as a future video-analytics feature if GSE builds athletic-performance content (e.g., estimating pitch/swing force from broadcast video) for engagement-focused content generation.

cells.C70: ST-VLM: Kinematic Instruction Tuning for Spatio-Temporal Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
cells.D70: Builds a spatio-temporal kinematic instruction-tuning dataset and model (ST-VLM) enabling vision-language models to reason about object speed, distance, and motion direction, including sports analytics applications.
cells.E70: Uses 4D-reconstruction-derived pseudo-labels to instruction-tune a VLM on kinematic quantities (speed, distance, direction), improving generalization across spatio-temporal benchmarks.
cells.F70: Relevant if GSE processes video for automated commentary/insight generation: a concrete method for teaching a vision-language model to reason quantitatively about game motion, aligning with its 'math you can read' brand for video-derived stats.
cells.G70: Use ST-VLM-style kinematic instruction tuning to build a video-QA agent that can answer natural-language questions about play speed/distance for automated highlight captions, keeping the underlying reasoning quantitatively grounded rather than vague AI narration.

cells.C71: Leveraging Audio Representations for Vibration-Based Crowd Monitoring in Stadiums
cells.D71: Presents ViLA, a floor-vibration-based stadium crowd-monitoring method pre-trained on public audio data and fine-tuned with minimal vibration data, achieving up to 5.8x error reduction over non-pretrained models.
cells.E71: Uses cross-modal (audio-to-vibration) self-supervised pretraining to reduce labeled-data requirements for vibration-sensor-based crowd behavior prediction.
cells.F71: Not directly relevant to GSE's statistical prediction/calibration engine; a physical sensing/crowd-monitoring infrastructure paper.
cells.G71: Only a distant stretch: could inform a future stadium-safety/fan-engagement B2B product line if GSE expands beyond prediction into venue analytics.

cells.C72: Reproducing Human Individual Motor Signatures: A Data-Driven Approach for Repetitive Motion
cells.D72: Uses LSTM neural networks trained on individual motion data to generate synthetic one-dimensional motion that captures a specific person's unique velocity signature and amplitude envelope.
cells.E72: Trains person-specific LSTM generative models on oscillatory motion data, validated via statistical comparison of velocity distributions and amplitude envelopes.
cells.F72: Weak/tangential relevance: an individual-motor-signature generative modeling technique for avatars/robots, not connected to GSE's statistical forecasting engine.
cells.G72: Only a distant idea: could generate individualized avatar motion for Galaxy Dynasty's persistent game characters if player-specific movement realism becomes a feature.

cells.C73: Inferring Events from Time Series using Language Models
cells.D73: Tests whether LLMs can infer unobserved natural-language events (e.g., game events) from time series data, built on sports data, showing surprising success and that RL-distillation lets small models approach large-model performance.
cells.E73: Introduces an automated benchmark generation method pairing time series segments with event-inference tasks, then evaluates 18 LLMs and applies distillation+RL to improve small-model performance.
cells.F73: Highly relevant to GSE: directly demonstrates LLMs inferring real-world sports events from time-series data, applicable to automated commentary/content generation and to enriching structured data from time-series feeds.
cells.G73: Use this event-inference-from-time-series capability to auto-generate plain-language explanations of why a pick's probability moved (e.g., inferring 'injury' or 'momentum shift' from line/stat time series), reinforcing the 'math you can read' brand with grounded narrative explanations.

cells.C74: PassAI: explainable AI algorithm for soccer pass analysis using multimodal information resources
cells.D74: Develops PassAI, an explainable pass-success classifier combining tracking data and passer season stats, outperforming SOTA by 5%+ while visualizing the relative contribution of each data modality.
cells.E74: Uses two parallel processing streams (tracking imagery, passer stats) with contribution-decomposition analysis to classify and explain soccer pass outcomes.
cells.F74: Directly relevant as a template for explainable multimodal sports-event modeling, exemplifying the 'math you can read' interpretability GSE needs for its own pick explanations and calibration transparency.
cells.G74: Adapt PassAI's cross-modality contribution-decomposition technique as a template for explaining GSE's own pick probabilities in plain terms ('X% driven by team stats, Y% by market odds movement'), directly supporting the brand's transparency claim.

cells.C75: Imitation Learning of Correlated Policies in Stackelberg Games
cells.D75: Introduces LSDN, a latent-variable imitation-learning method for asymmetric leader-follower (Stackelberg) game dynamics, validated on turn-based sports like badminton and multi-agent environments.
cells.E75: Models two-agent interactions as shared latent-state trajectories via multi-output Geometric Brownian Motion, disentangling environment and agent-driven dynamics without adversarial GAIL-style training.
cells.F75: Relevant to GSE's in-play strategic modeling ambitions: gives a stable, non-adversarial imitation-learning approach for asymmetric sequential sports interactions (e.g., server vs. returner, pitcher vs. batter).
cells.G75: Apply the Stackelberg imitation-learning framework to model pitcher-batter or serve-return sequences as leader-follower dynamics, adding a new class of sequential, interaction-aware features to GSE's in-play prediction models.

cells.C76: Predicting Volleyball Season Performance Using Pre-Season Wearable Data and Machine Learning
cells.D76: Uses passively collected smartwatch and ecological momentary assessment data to predict collegiate volleyball players' season performance before the season starts, achieving F1=0.75.
cells.E76: Integrates wearable sensor features with subjective psycho-physiological survey data, validated via leave-one-subject-out cross-validation for pre-season performance classification.
cells.F76: Tangential to GSE's current odds/stats-driven model but conceptually relevant to bootstrap mode: shows how sparse pre-season data can still yield reasonably predictive signal via targeted feature engineering.
cells.G76: Use the pre-season wearable/psychometric feature-engineering approach as inspiration for a 'cold-start' feature set specifically for bootstrap-mode predictions, when a season has too little in-season data to trust the main model.

cells.C77: Artificial intelligence for objective assessment of acrobatic movements in cheer sports
cells.D77: Uses a single wearable IMU and machine learning to identify and objectively assess tumbling elements in cheerleading routines, demonstrating high classification accuracy across 1,102 recorded elements.
cells.E77: Applies ML classifiers to triaxial acceleration/rotation data from a single pelvis-mounted IMU to classify and score tumbling maneuvers.
cells.F77: Weak relevance: a niche wearable-sensor sports-scoring application outside GSE's current sport coverage (NFL/MLB/MLS) and unrelated to its statistical calibration problem.
cells.G77: Only a distant idea: illustrates single-sensor objective-scoring feasibility that could inform a future niche-sport (gymnastics/cheer) analytics expansion if GSE broadens its market coverage.

cells.C78: Machine Learning in Biomechanics: Key Applications and Limitations in Walking, Running, and Sports Movements
cells.D78: A book-chapter overview of ML applications (pose estimation, event detection, clustering, classification) in gait and sports biomechanics, highlighting data/annotation scarcity and explainability as key limitations.
cells.E78: Surveys ML methodology categories applied to biomechanical movement analysis, discussing cross-cutting limitations rather than presenting new results.
cells.F78: Weak/background relevance: a biomechanics-ML survey outside GSE's core statistical/odds-based domain, though its explainability-limitation discussion echoes GSE's own transparency requirements.
cells.G78: Cite its explainability-limitation framing as supporting rationale when designing GSE's model documentation standards for the trust/compliance toolkit, even though the biomechanics content itself isn't directly usable.

cells.C79: Using Machine Learning for move sequence visualization and generation in climbing
cells.D79: Explores Transformer models for predicting climbing move sequences from hold-sequence information, presenting inconclusive but foundational early results plus a visualization tool.
cells.E79: Trains three Transformer variants to predict move sequences from simplified climbing-hold data, alongside a move-sequence visualization tool.
cells.F79: Weak relevance: an early-stage, inconclusive sequence-prediction study in a sport outside GSE's current coverage, offering little transferable modeling insight.
cells.G79: Minimal application; at most illustrates Transformer sequence-prediction as a class of technique GSE could consider for modeling sequential in-game event chains (e.g., drive sequences) in its own sports.

cells.D80: An opinion/reflection column on active-learning pedagogy in undergraduate mathematics teaching, using the phrase 'math is not a spectator sport' as a rhetorical device, unrelated to sports analytics.
cells.E80: A non-technical essay reflecting on math-teaching philosophy and classroom practice, not a research methodology paper.
cells.F80: Not relevant: this is a pedagogy opinion piece that only superficially references 'sport' as a metaphor; no technical content applies to GSE.
cells.G80: No genuine product application; at most the title's 'math you can read/do' framing loosely echoes GSE's own brand tagline as a coincidental rhetorical parallel.

cells.C81: A dataset of high-resolution plantar pressures for gait analysis across varying footwear and walking speeds
cells.D81: Introduces UNB StepUP-P150, a large public dataset of high-resolution plantar pressure data from 150 individuals across varying footwear and walking speeds, for gait biometrics research.
cells.E81: Collects and releases footstep-level plantar pressure sensor data via a large pressure-sensing walkway, supporting gait recognition and biomechanics research.
cells.F81: Not directly relevant to GSE's statistical prediction/calibration stack; a biomechanics/biometrics dataset paper.
cells.G81: No credible direct application; only a distant idea for future athlete-movement-data partnerships if GSE pursues biomechanical performance features.

cells.C82: Beyond Performance Scores: Directed Functional Connectivity as a Brain-Based Biomarker for Motor Skill Learning and Retention
cells.D82: Introduces EEG-derived directed functional connectivity as a biomarker tracking stages of motor skill learning/retention, validated over a six-week retention period in a surgical training context.
cells.E82: Computes directed functional connectivity from EEG to map stages of the Fitts and Posner motor learning model, showing stability over time as a retention indicator.
cells.F82: Not relevant to GSE's software/statistical stack; a neuroscience biomarker study for motor skill training (surgical/robotics context, sports mentioned only in passing).
cells.G82: No credible application; a very distant idea for future athlete-training-adjacent content if GSE diversifies beyond prediction into training/coaching products.

cells.C83: LayeredSense: Hierarchical Recognition of Complex Daily Activities Using Wearable Sensors
cells.D83: Introduces a hierarchical framework decomposing complex daily activities (including playing sports) into unit-pattern building blocks recognized via wearable IMU data and Gaussian Mixture Models.
cells.E83: Uses a Myo armband IMU with Gaussian Mixture Models for novel-pattern detection and Random Forests for hierarchical activity classification, aggregating unit actions into complex activities.
cells.F83: Weak relevance: a wearable-sensor human-activity-recognition system unrelated to GSE's odds/stats-driven forecasting engine.
cells.G83: Only a distant idea for a future fan-engagement wearable feature (e.g., tracking user's own casual sports activity) within the Galaxy Dynasty ecosystem.

cells.D84: Presents a hybrid ARIMA-LSTM time series forecasting framework with embedding/PCA feature engineering, SHAP-based interpretability, and KNN-based prediction intervals, applied to sports time series data.
cells.E84: Combines linear (ARIMA) and nonlinear (LSTM) components with PCA dimensionality reduction, SHAP importance, and KNN-derived prediction intervals for sports time series forecasting.
cells.F84: Directly relevant: a hybrid statistical/deep-learning forecasting architecture with explicit interpretability (SHAP) and uncertainty intervals, closely matching GSE's need for genuinely better, explainable forecasting methods to beat its naive baseline.
cells.G84: Pilot the ARIMA+LSTM hybrid with SHAP-based feature attribution as a candidate replacement for GSE's underperforming core model, using the KNN-interval method to directly generate calibrated uncertainty bands feeding the Brier/ECE gate.

cells.C85: Behavioral Homophily in Social Media via Inverse Reinforcement Learning: A Reddit Case Study
cells.D85: Uses Inverse Reinforcement Learning to infer users' implicit behavioral policies on Reddit, finding behavioral similarity (e.g., soccer vs. esports users) can be high even when topical content differs.
cells.E85: Infers user policies via IRL from interaction sequences, then uses policy similarity as a behavioral-homophily measure, validated against traditional content-based homophily across 5.9M interactions.
cells.F85: Tangential but useful for GSE's social/content-automation strategy: IRL-derived behavioral clustering could identify audience segments across sports for targeted content distribution.
cells.G85: Apply IRL-based behavioral homophily analysis to GSE's own social audience data to identify cross-sport fan segments (e.g., NFL bettors who behave like MLB bettors) for smarter targeted content and cross-sell strategies.

cells.C86: OpenSTARLab: Open Approach for Spatio-Temporal Agent Data Analysis in Soccer
cells.D86: Introduces an open-source framework standardizing soccer event/tracking data formats and providing deep-learning event prediction plus reinforcement-learning packages for spatio-temporal soccer analytics.
cells.E86: Provides a Unified Event/State-Action-Reward data pipeline, an event-prediction deep learning module, and an RLearn package for training RL agents on soccer sequences.
cells.F86: Highly relevant to GSE's data-ingestion pipeline for MLS/soccer: a ready-made open-source standardization and modeling framework directly applicable to structuring scraped/ingested soccer event data for the prediction engine.
cells.G86: Adopt OpenSTARLab's standardized event/tracking data schema as the backbone for GSE's MLS data-ingestion pipeline, reducing custom ETL work and enabling direct reuse of its pretrained event-prediction models as an ensemble component.

cells.C87: VolleyBots: A Testbed for Multi-Drone Volleyball Game Combining Motion Control and Strategic Play
cells.D87: Introduces a multi-drone volleyball RL/MARL testbed combining low-level flight control with high-level strategic play, showing a hierarchical policy beats strong baselines and transfers zero-shot to real drones.
cells.E87: Provides a simulated volleyball environment for benchmarking RL, MARL, and game-theoretic algorithms, with a hierarchical policy separating motion control from strategic decision-making.
cells.F87: Tangential: a robotics/RL benchmark for embodied sports agents, not directly applicable to GSE's statistical forecasting engine, though the hierarchical strategy/control separation is a reusable design pattern.
cells.G87: Borrow the hierarchical policy design (separate low-level execution from high-level strategy) as an architectural pattern for GSE's own multi-agent research agents (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) handling complex, multi-step data-pipeline tasks.

cells.C88: STGCN-LSTM for Olympic Medal Prediction: Dynamic Power Modeling and Causal Policy Optimization
cells.D88: Combines Spatial-Temporal Graph Convolution and LSTM with a Zero-Inflated Compound Poisson framework to forecast Olympic medal counts, incorporating causal inference checks and policy-shock simulation.
cells.E88: Fuses graph-based country-interaction modeling with LSTM historical trends and a zero-inflated Poisson output layer to separate structural from random zero-medal outcomes, validated via causal backtesting.
cells.F88: Directly relevant to GSE's calibration and ensemble redesign: a zero-inflated, causally-validated hybrid forecasting architecture is a strong template for handling sparse/rare-event sports outcomes (e.g., upsets, longshot bets).
cells.G88: Adapt the Zero-Inflated Compound Poisson framework to model rare-event outcomes (e.g., blowouts, specific prop bets with near-zero base rates) separately from the main win-probability model, improving calibration on the tails that likely drive ECE failures.

cells.C89: Automated Detection of Sport Highlights from Audio and Video Sources
cells.D89: Presents a lightweight deep-learning method detecting sports highlights from audio Mel-spectrograms and video frames using small training datasets, achieving 89%/83% accuracy with an ensemble improving robustness.
cells.E89: Trains small CNN-based models on audio and video modalities separately then ensembles them for highlight detection, emphasizing practicality with limited data.
cells.F89: Relevant to GSE's automated social/media content generation: a practical, low-data-requirement method for auto-detecting highlight-worthy moments to fuel content pipelines.
cells.G89: Deploy this lightweight audio/video highlight detector as an automated triage layer feeding GSE's social content pipeline, flagging clip-worthy moments for auto-generated recap posts without heavy annotation investment.

cells.C90: Optimizing Human Pose Estimation Through Focused Human and Joint Regions
cells.D90: Proposes a bilayer masking and deformable cross-attention Transformer architecture that focuses pose estimation on the target person/joints, achieving state-of-the-art results including on PoseTrack2017.
cells.E90: Uses coarse-to-fine visual token masking plus deformable cross-attention constrained to target-person regions to improve video pose estimation accuracy and robustness to background clutter.
cells.F90: Not directly relevant to GSE's statistical prediction stack; a computer-vision pose-estimation architecture paper, relevant only if GSE processes broadcast video.
cells.G90: If GSE later adds video-derived player-tracking features, this focused pose-estimation architecture would improve robustness against crowded/cluttered broadcast footage compared to generic pose estimators.

cells.C91: SMART-Vision: Survey of Modern Action Recognition Techniques in Vision
cells.D91: Presents a comprehensive taxonomy of deep-learning human action recognition approaches spanning architectures and modalities, including sports motion analysis, and surveys open-set/Open-HAR challenges.
cells.E91: Surveys and taxonomizes hybrid HAR architectures and benchmarking datasets, highlighting emerging directions like Open-HAR for unknown-class detection at test time.
cells.F91: Relevant background for GSE's potential video-based data-ingestion expansion; the Open-HAR concept (detecting novel/unknown activity classes) is conceptually adjacent to anomaly detection in structured sports data pipelines.
cells.G91: Borrow the Open-HAR 'unknown class at test time' framing as inspiration for an anomaly-detection layer in GSE's data pipeline that flags novel, unclassified play types or data patterns the model hasn't seen before, rather than silently misclassifying them.

cells.C92: Exploring the Use of Contrastive Language-Image Pre-Training for Human Posture Classification: Insights from Yoga Pose Analysis
cells.D92: Fine-tunes CLIP on yoga pose images, reaching 85%+ accuracy and beating YOLOv8-based baselines with far less training time.
cells.E92: Transfer learning on a vision-language contrastive model (CLIP) for fine-grained posture/pose classification.
cells.F92: Not core to GSE's pick-grading pipeline, but the fine-tuning-with-few-labels recipe is a stretch analogue for low-data sports (bootstrap mode) where GSE has sparse per-sport labeled data.
cells.G92: Use the same low-shot CLIP fine-tuning recipe to auto-classify broadcast/scraped images (e.g. injury reports, bench posture) as a cheap new feature source for the data pipeline.
