cells.D93: Forecasts soccer outcomes by modeling shot quantity/quality distributions with ELO ratings plus ML, beating market odds in a betting challenge.
cells.E93: Combines ELO ratings with ML-estimated shot distributions to derive match outcome probabilities.
cells.F93: Directly on-target: a distributional (not point-estimate) forecasting approach that beats market odds, exactly the closing-line-value benchmark and MAE-vs-baseline problem GSE is failing.
cells.G93: Replace GSE's point predictions with shot/event-count distributions per sport, then derive calibrated win probabilities from the distribution rather than a single regression head.

cells.C94: Action Quality Assessment via Hierarchical Pose-guided Multi-stage Contrastive Regression
cells.D94: Proposes a pose-guided, multi-stage contrastive regression model for scoring athletic performance (diving) with sub-action segmentation.
cells.E94: Fuses skeletal pose and visual features via contrastive regression across segmented sub-actions to predict a quality score.
cells.F94: Tangential — its multi-stage contrastive regression architecture for score prediction is a distant methodological parallel to GSE's pick-scoring/confidence pipeline, but the video-vision domain doesn't map to GSE's tabular data.
cells.G94: Borrow the 'multi-stage contrastive regression' idea to structure the prediction-engine into sub-stage scores (matchup, form, situational) combined contrastively rather than one flat model.

cells.C95: Estimation of partial rankings from sparse, noisy comparisons
cells.D95: Develops a nonparametric Bayesian method that infers partial rankings (with ties) from pairwise comparisons only when evidence in the data supports distinguishing items.
cells.E95: Bayesian MAP inference via an agglomerative algorithm built on top of any pairwise-comparison model like Bradley-Terry.
cells.F95: Strongly relevant — a principled way to avoid overconfident rankings/probabilities under sparse data, directly addressing GSE's 'bootstrap mode' confidence-capping problem and overconfidence driving poor ECE.
cells.G95: Apply partial-ranking inference to team/player power ratings so GSE can honestly display 'statistically tied' teams instead of forcing false precision that hurts calibration.

cells.C96: Large Language Models for Market Research: A Data-augmentation Approach
cells.D96: Proposes a statistical framework to combine LLM-generated synthetic survey data with real data in conjoint analysis, yielding consistent, asymptotically normal estimators with lower bias than naive substitution.
cells.E96: Data-augmentation estimator that statistically blends LLM-simulated and real preference data with a proven finite-sample error bound.
cells.F96: Relevant as a rigorous template for safely blending synthetic/LLM-augmented data with real settled-pick data to fight data sparsity without corrupting calibration — directly useful for bootstrap mode.
cells.G96: Use this framework to safely augment thin early-season per-sport datasets with LLM-simulated matchup scenarios, bounding how much synthetic data can bias the probability model.

cells.C97: Optimizing Fantasy Sports Team Selection with Deep Reinforcement Learning
cells.D97: Frames fantasy cricket team selection as a sequential decision problem and trains RL agents on historical player data to optimize team composition.
cells.E97: Reinforcement learning treats roster construction as sequential action selection to maximize expected fantasy points.
cells.F97: Directly relevant to GSE's longer-horizon fantasy/B2B ambitions and illustrates an RL alternative to their currently-losing regression-based prediction model.
cells.G97: Repurpose the RL sequential-selection framing not for fantasy rosters but for sequencing which picks to publish/lock given a bankroll-like confidence budget.

cells.C98: An Interaction Design Toolkit for Physical Task Guidance with Artificial Intelligence and Mixed Reality
cells.D98: Presents a design toolkit (patterns, considerations, canvas) for building AI+mixed-reality systems that coach users through physical skills, drawn from student PTG prototypes.
cells.E98: Qualitative design-pattern toolkit synthesized from analyzing multiple human-AI-MR prototype systems.
cells.F98: Weak/stretch fit — GSE has no MR component; the only thread is general human-AI interaction design guidance potentially useful for their B2B widget UX.
cells.G98: Mine the 'design considerations' catalog as a checklist when designing GSE's trust/compliance toolkit UI for explaining AI-adjacent confidence scores to end users.

cells.C99: Learning Group Interactions and Semantic Intentions for Multi-Object Trajectory Prediction
cells.D99: A diffusion-based trajectory prediction model uses cooperative-game (Banzhaf) interaction modeling to predict NBA player trajectories conditioned on team-level tactics.
cells.E99: Conditional diffusion model over player trajectories, with group interaction captured via game-theoretic (Banzhaf) attribution.
cells.F99: Adjacent — trajectory prediction isn't GSE's core need, but the Banzhaf cooperative-game interaction concept is a legitimate ensemble-weighting idea relevant to CEPT's multiplicative-weight ensemble.
cells.G99: Apply Banzhaf-value style attribution to score how much each sub-model in GSE's ensemble contributes to a correct pick, informing ensemble reweighting beyond simple multiplicative weights.

cells.C100: RefHCM: A Unified Model for Referring Perceptions in Human-Centric Scenarios
cells.D100: Introduces a unified sequence-to-sequence transformer that handles multiple human-centric referring tasks (e.g., 'find the player wearing red') across vision-language modalities.
cells.E100: Converts multimodal inputs (image, text, coordinates) into unified semantic tokens processed by one encoder-decoder transformer.
cells.F100: Minimal direct relevance — it's a computer-vision referring-expression model; only loosely touches GSE's sports-analytics/chatbot ambitions mentioned in its intro.
cells.G100: Could inspire a natural-language query interface over GSE's Intelligence Graph ('show me the pick where the away QB was injured') using referring-style grounding.

cells.C101: Future Aspects in Human Action Recognition: Exploring Emerging Techniques and Ethical Influences
cells.D101: A review of emerging trends (synthetic video generation, RL, next-gen sensors) and ethical concerns in human action recognition across surveillance, sports, and robotics.
cells.E101: Survey/position paper synthesizing techniques and ethics rather than a novel method.
cells.F101: Peripheral — general vision survey; only the 'synthetic video data generation to fight dataset scarcity' theme lightly echoes GSE's own data-scarcity/bootstrap problem.
cells.G101: Reference its synthetic-data generation arguments when justifying GSE's own use of simulated/backtested seasons to pad calibration windows faster.

cells.C102: Challenges and Opportunities Associated with Technology Driven Biomechanical Simulations
cells.D102: Surveys challenges in computational biomechanics simulation (cost, standardization, ML integration) with applications to sports injury prevention.
cells.E102: Position paper discussing model-order-reduction and ML tooling for biomechanical simulations.
cells.F102: Minimal — GSE doesn't do biomechanical simulation; only a generic 'sports data is high-volume and hard to standardize' parallel to their data pipeline challenges.
cells.G102: None strong beyond citing its data-standardization pain points as validation for investing in GSE's own ETL normalization layer.

cells.C103: Buzz to Broadcast: Predicting Sports Viewership Using Social Media Engagement
cells.D103: A regression model predicts sports TV viewership from Reddit engagement/sentiment metrics, achieving R²=0.99 for ad-revenue forecasting.
cells.E103: Feature-engineered regression (post counts, sentiment scores) predicting viewership numbers per sport/event.
cells.F103: Relevant to GSE's social/media content-automation ambitions and as a signal source (buzz-based demand) that could feed the data pipeline or B2B interest targeting.
cells.G103: Use predicted 'buzz' as a leading indicator to flag which upcoming games need earlier/more confident picks published for maximum engagement timing.

cells.C104: Understanding the Impact of News Articles on the Movement of Market Index: A Case on Nifty 50
cells.D104: Shows that sentiment scores from news on varied topics (including sports) significantly move a stock market index, not just stock-specific news.
cells.E104: Topic-segmented sentiment analysis correlated with index movement via regression.
cells.F104: Tangential — its core insight (topic-segmented sentiment affects markets) has only a weak analogy to GSE's line-movement/odds-efficiency benchmarking.
cells.G104: Adapt topic-segmented sentiment scoring to sports news (injury reports, coach interviews) as an auxiliary input feature for GSE's ensemble, separate from raw odds.

cells.C105: Enhanced Multi-Object Tracking Using Pose-based Virtual Markers in 3x3 Basketball
cells.D105: Introduces pose-based virtual markers with active learning to improve multi-object player tracking in 3x3 basketball, cutting manual annotation cost.
cells.E105: Overlays synthetic pose-derived markers on video, then converts to bounding boxes for standard MOT evaluation.
cells.F105: Peripheral — relevant only if GSE ever ingests video-based tracking data; mainly a computer-vision/data-labeling efficiency technique.
cells.G105: Adapt the active-learning-to-cut-annotation-cost idea to reduce human labeling effort when building GSE's own settled-pick grading/QA datasets.

cells.C106: Real-Time Prediction for Athletes' Psychological States Using BERT-XGBoost: Enhancing Human-Computer Interaction
cells.D106: Combines BERT text embeddings with XGBoost to predict athletes' psychological states (stress, emotion) from structured and unstructured data at 94% accuracy.
cells.E106: Hybrid NLP+gradient-boosting model fusing self-report text and tagged observational data.
cells.F106: Weakly relevant — a BERT+XGBoost hybrid ensemble pattern is architecturally similar to combining text signals (injury reports, news) with GSE's structured stats ensemble.
cells.G106: Apply the same BERT+XGBoost fusion to blend scraped injury/beat-writer text sentiment with GSE's structured per-sport model as an extra calibration input.

cells.C107: CigTime: Corrective Instruction Generation Through Inverse Motion Editing
cells.D107: Generates natural-language corrective coaching instructions by comparing a user's motion to a target motion, using LLM-assisted triplet dataset creation.
cells.E107: Inverse motion-editing model paired with an LLM to translate motion deltas into text coaching cues.
cells.F107: Stretch — the underlying idea of using an LLM to translate a quantitative delta (actual vs. target) into human-readable text maps onto GSE's brand-language-constrained content generation.
cells.G107: Use the same 'delta-to-text' generation pattern to auto-write GSE pick rationales that explain the gap between model probability and market-implied probability, in non-AI brand voice.

cells.C108: A Graph Neural Network deep-dive into successful counterattacks
cells.D108: Trains gender-specific GNNs on soccer tracking data to predict counterattack success and identify which spatial features (speed, angles) matter most.
cells.E108: Graph neural network over player/ball spatiotemporal graphs with permutation feature importance for interpretability.
cells.F108: Relevant methodologically — GNNs over event/tracking data plus feature-importance analysis is a legitimate architecture GSE could evaluate for its underperforming core prediction model.
cells.G108: Use GNN-based feature-importance outputs as an interpretable 'why we picked this' explanation layer, satisfying GSE's brand need for math-you-can-read transparency.

cells.C109: Performance Benchmarking of Psychomotor Skills Using Wearable Devices: An Application in Sport
cells.D109: Uses wearable IMU data to build a performance-space benchmark cluster (via table tennis) that lets athletes see how their motion deviates from optimal technique.
cells.E109: Clusters reference performance metrics from IMU trajectories, then maps deviations back to specific motion corrections.
cells.F109: Minimal — wearable biomechanics benchmarking has no direct link to GSE's statistical prediction stack.
cells.G109: None strong; at best inspiration for a future wearable-data ingestion source if GSE expands into player-level performance products.

cells.C110: Research on Effectiveness Evaluation and Optimization of Baseball Teaching Method Based on Machine Learning
cells.D110: Compares regression models (KNN, Gradient Boosting) to predict student baseball performance scores from training statistics, identifying key predictive features.
cells.E110: Feature-importance-driven regression benchmarking across several ML models on training-outcome data.
cells.F110: Tangential — a small-scale model comparison exercise; only generically relevant as another data point on gradient-boosting vs. other regressors for sports metrics.
cells.G110: Could inform GSE's own baseline-vs-ensemble bake-off methodology when justifying which regressor family beats their current losing baseline.

cells.C111: Introducing IHARDS-CNN: A Cutting-Edge Deep Learning Method for Human Activity Recognition Using Wearable Sensors
cells.D111: Merges three wearable-sensor HAR datasets and trains a 1D CNN achieving near-100% accuracy classifying five daily activity classes.
cells.E111: Dataset fusion plus a lightweight 1D convolutional network for sensor-based activity classification.
cells.F111: Minimal — HAR from wearables isn't part of GSE's product surface today.
cells.G111: None substantive beyond noting dataset-fusion techniques as a template if GSE ever merges disparate free data sources into one training corpus.

cells.C112: GTA: Global Tracklet Association for Multi-Object Tracking in Sports
cells.D112: A plug-and-play appearance-based algorithm that fixes ID switches in sports player tracking, achieving state-of-the-art HOTA on SportsMOT and SoccerNet.
cells.E112: Post-hoc global tracklet splitting/merging using appearance embeddings to refine any base tracker's output.
cells.F112: Peripheral to GSE's core statistical stack; relevant only if GSE ingests broadcast video tracking data for advanced stats, which isn't currently core.
cells.G112: If GSE later scrapes broadcast video for event data, this 'refinement layer on top of any tracker' pattern maps to adding a data-cleaning pass on top of noisy scraped datasets.

cells.C113: Eagle Pass, TX: The First American City on the Path of Totality: Organizing Eclipse Party on the Stadium
cells.D113: A first-person account of NSO scientists organizing a solar eclipse viewing event at a stadium, with community outreach lessons learned.
cells.E113: Descriptive outreach/event-organizing report, not a technical method.
cells.F113: Not relevant — this is a public-outreach case study with only incidental stadium/sports venue setting.
cells.G113: No legitimate technical angle; at most a reminder that stadiums are community engagement venues, irrelevant to GSE's prediction product.

cells.C114: Real-time Monitoring and Analysis of Track and Field Athletes Based on Edge Computing and Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
cells.D114: Proposes an IoT/edge-computing system using an SAC-optimized deep RL model for low-latency motion recognition of track and field athletes.
cells.E114: Edge-deployed deep RL (Soft Actor-Critic) model performing real-time motion classification from sensor streams.
cells.F114: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's cloud-based prediction pipeline; the RL/edge-latency optimization angle is a stretch.
cells.G114: None compelling beyond general inspiration for low-latency inference patterns if GSE ever needs real-time in-game pick updates.

cells.C115: Proposal of a Contact Detection System using Micro-phones for a Chambara-based Augmented Sports
cells.D115: Builds a microphone-based ML system to detect and locate sword-hit events for a novel augmented combat sport with 93% accuracy.
cells.E115: Multi-microphone sound classification via machine learning to detect and localize physical contact events.
cells.F115: Not relevant to GSE's product; a niche sensor-engineering paper for a fictional sport.
cells.G115: No credible application; at most a novelty reference for GSE's own 'Galaxy Dynasty' game world-building around invented sports.

cells.C116: A Comprehensive Review of Multimodal XR Applications, Risks, and Ethical Challenges in the Metaverse
cells.D116: A scoping review of XR/AR/VR/MR applications across sectors (including sports) and their privacy, security, and ethical risks.
cells.E116: Literature review synthesizing XR application domains and governance concerns.
cells.F116: Weak — GSE has no XR component; only tangential relevance via its ethics/governance framing which parallels GSE's trust/compliance toolkit ambitions.
cells.G116: Borrow its ethical-risk taxonomy structure as a template for GSE's own trust/compliance documentation, even though the underlying tech (XR) is unrelated.

cells.C117: IMUDiffusion: A Diffusion Model for Multivariate Time Series Synthetisation for Inertial Motion Capturing Systems
cells.D117: A diffusion model generates synthetic multivariate IMU time series that, when added to training data, boosts activity classifier macro-F1 by up to 30%.
cells.E117: Probabilistic diffusion model trained to synthesize realistic multivariate sensor time series for data augmentation.
cells.F117: Methodologically relevant — a proven pattern for synthetic time-series data augmentation directly applicable to GSE's sparse per-sport data problem underlying bootstrap mode.
cells.G117: Adapt diffusion-based time-series synthesis to generate plausible synthetic game/event sequences for thin-data sports/leagues, expanding calibration-window sample size faster.

cells.C118: Straintronic magnetic tunnel junctions for analog computation: A perspective
cells.D118: A physics perspective piece on using strain-controlled magnetic tunnel junctions for analog computing and neural-network synapse implementation.
cells.E118: Hardware physics review of magnetoresistive device behavior for analog matrix-multiplication circuits.
cells.F118: Not relevant — solid-state device physics paper; 'sports' appears only as an incidental word choice ('sports a linear region'), no domain connection.
cells.G118: No legitimate application to GSE; excluded from consideration beyond noting the false-positive keyword match.

cells.C119: Boulder2Vec: Modeling Climber Performances in Professional Bouldering Competitions
cells.D119: Applies Probabilistic Matrix Factorization to bouldering competition results to learn multidimensional climber/problem skill vectors, beating plain logistic regression.
cells.E119: Latent-factor (matrix factorization) model representing athletes and challenges as vectors whose dot product predicts performance.
cells.F119: Directly relevant — PMF-style latent factor modeling on sparse sports outcome data is a strong candidate technique for GSE's per-sport probability models and handles the sparse-attempt problem similar to bootstrap mode.
cells.G119: Use PMF-style latent vectors to represent team 'style' dimensions (pace, matchup tendencies) rather than a single power rating, feeding a richer, better-calibrated ensemble input.

cells.D120: Compares Transformer, LSTM, RL and Markov models predicting which item a person consumes next in an ordered content bundle, using Spotify data; a decoder-only Transformer wins.
cells.E120: Benchmarks sequence models for next-item prediction, analyzing attention weights for interpretability.
cells.F120: Tangential — sequential-choice modeling of consumption isn't GSE's forecasting problem, but the model-comparison methodology (Transformer vs LSTM vs Markov vs RL) mirrors GSE's own model bake-off needs.
cells.G120: Apply the decoder-only Transformer architecture (shown here to beat LSTM/Markov baselines) as a candidate replacement for GSE's current core model that's losing to a naive baseline.

cells.C121: A Systematic Review of Machine Learning in Sports Betting: Techniques, Challenges, and Future Directions
cells.D121: A systematic review surveying ML techniques (SVM, random forests, neural nets) used across sports betting for odds-setting, value-bet identification, and fraud detection.
cells.E121: Literature survey categorizing ML applications and open challenges in sports betting analytics.
cells.F121: Directly on-target — surveys exactly GSE's problem space (odds-setting accuracy, value bets, data quality challenges) and can benchmark GSE's approach against the field.
cells.G121: Mine its 'future directions' section (adaptive multimodal risk-management models) as a roadmap input for GSE's next-gen ensemble and portfolio-style confidence management.

cells.C122: YourSkatingCoach: A Figure Skating Video Benchmark for Fine-Grained Element Analysis
cells.D122: Introduces a figure-skating video dataset and a Transformer-based model that detects jump 'air time' as a sequential labeling task, generalizing to other sports.
cells.E122: Casts fine-grained motion event detection as sequence labeling solved with a Transformer over skeleton features.
cells.F122: Peripheral — video-based fine-grained motion analysis doesn't map to GSE's tabular prediction stack.
cells.G122: None strong beyond noting the general 'coarse label to fine-grained sequential task' reframing technique as inspiration for refining GSE's pick-grading granularity.

cells.C123: Real-time Monitoring of Lower Limb Movement Resistance Based on Deep Learning
cells.D123: A mobile multi-task CNN (MMTL-Net) simultaneously predicts resistance levels and recognizes activities from wearable sensor data with low latency.
cells.E123: Multi-task learning network sharing a MobileNetV3 backbone for joint regression and classification.
cells.F123: Minimal — wearable rehab/sports-resistance monitoring is unrelated to GSE's prediction pipeline.
cells.G123: The multi-task-head pattern (shared backbone, multiple prediction heads) is a reusable architectural idea for jointly predicting win probability and spread/total from one shared model.

cells.C124: STAR: A Simple Training-free Approach for Recommendations using Large Language Models
cells.D124: Proposes a training-free recommendation framework combining LLM semantic embeddings with collaborative signals and LLM pairwise re-ranking, competitive with fine-tuned supervised models.
cells.E124: Retrieval via LLM embeddings + collaborative filtering, followed by LLM-based pairwise ranking refinement, no fine-tuning required.
cells.F124: Relevant to GSE's B2B/content ambitions (personalized pick or content recommendation) and demonstrates a low-cost way to get strong ranking performance without a heavy training pipeline.
cells.G124: Use the training-free LLM re-ranking pattern to power a 'similar picks/insights' recommendation feature on the platform without building a dedicated recommender model.

cells.C125: Mechanistic Unlearning: Robust Knowledge Unlearning and Editing via Mechanistic Localization
cells.D125: Shows that localizing edits/unlearning to mechanistic circuits (e.g., factual lookup tables) in LLMs, tested partly on a sports-facts dataset, yields more robust knowledge removal than output-based localization.
cells.E125: Mechanistic interpretability used to identify and edit specific model components responsible for factual recall, improving robustness of unlearning.
cells.F125: Relevant to GSE's internal agentic tooling (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) — mechanistic editing techniques could help scrub stale or incorrect factual associations (e.g., outdated team rosters) from any LLM components they use.
cells.G125: Use mechanistic-localization techniques to audit and patch factual drift in GSE's internal LLM-based content/agent tools (e.g., correcting an out-of-date player-team association) without full retraining.

cells.C126: Incorporating Metabolic Information into LLMs for Anomaly Detection in Clinical Time-Series
cells.D126: Introduces Metabolism Pathway-driven Prompting to help LLMs detect anomalous biological samples for doping detection in athletes, improving on generic anomaly detection.
cells.E126: Domain-knowledge-conditioned LLM prompting integrated with time-series anomaly detection for structured biological data.
cells.F126: Adjacent — the core technique (domain-knowledge-conditioned prompting for anomaly detection in time-series) is directly transferable to GSE's anomaly-detection needs, e.g., detecting suspicious betting-line moves or scraped-data corruption.
cells.G126: Adapt domain-conditioned LLM prompting to flag anomalous odds movements or scraped stat outliers (e.g., a nonsensical Pro-Football-Reference row) before they corrupt the prediction engine.

cells.C127: EITNet: An IoT-Enhanced Framework for Real-Time Basketball Action Recognition
cells.D127: Combines EfficientDet, I3D, and TimeSformer with IoT integration to recognize basketball actions in real time at 92% accuracy, up from an 87% baseline.
cells.E127: Multi-model deep learning pipeline (detection + spatiotemporal + temporal transformer) fused with IoT data collection.
cells.F127: Peripheral — real-time video action recognition doesn't intersect GSE's statistical/tabular prediction engine.
cells.G127: None compelling beyond general inspiration for combining multiple specialized models into one pipeline, echoing GSE's own multi-model ensemble structure.

cells.C128: SPORTU: A Comprehensive Sports Understanding Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models
cells.D128: Introduces a large text+video sports-reasoning benchmark; even top MLLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) score poorly on hard rule-application and foul-detection tasks.
cells.E128: Curated multiple-choice and QA benchmark testing rule comprehension and multi-level reasoning in MLLMs.
cells.F128: Directly relevant — reveals current LLM limitations in sports rule reasoning, a caution for GSE's internal agents (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) if they're used for rule-sensitive tasks like grading or explaining picks.

cells.C130: Samba: Synchronized Set-of-Sequences Modeling for Multiple Object Tracking

cells.D141: Adapts general-purpose pose trackers (MoveNet, CoTracker) for sprint biomechanics analysis, finding MoveNet-based tracking usable but not yet precise enough for demanding applications.

cells.C181: Expected Possession Value of Control and Duel Actions for Soccer Player's Skills Estimation
cells.D181: Extends the Expected Possession Value (EPV) model with decay-weighted event timing, possession risk, and duel-win ability to better estimate individual soccer player skill and predict future performance against specific opponents.

cells.C182: Beyond Isolated Frames: Enhancing Sensor-Based Human Activity Recognition through Intra- and Inter-Frame Attention
cells.D182: Proposes an intra- and inter-frame attention model plus a time-sequential batch training strategy for sensor-based human activity recognition from wearables.

cells.C183: Early Detection of Critical Urban Events using Mobile Phone Network Data
cells.D183: Uses unsupervised anomaly-detection algorithms on multivariate mobile-network time series to detect and localize urban events like accidents or sports gatherings in real time.
cells.E183: Applies multiple state-of-the-art unsupervised time-series anomaly detectors to spatio-temporal telecom signalling data, benchmarked against a labeled event ground truth.

cells.D186: Uses transformer-based embeddings of 40 years of world events (including sports) to improve e-commerce demand forecasting during anomalous periods.

cells.C187: Counterfactual Explanation-Based Badminton Motion Guidance Generation Using Wearable Sensors
cells.D187: Generates personalized counterfactual motion guides from wearable sensor data to help badminton players improve stroke quality toward expert-level performance.

cells.C190: Lasso Ridge based XGBoost and DeepLSTM Help Tennis Players Perform better
cells.D190: Predicts tennis match outcomes and quantifies in-match momentum/fluctuation using a Lasso-Ridge XGBoost model and a DeepLSTM, achieving 94% accuracy on Wimbledon data.

cells.D191: Forecasts English Premier League Fantasy player scores using CNNs, outperforming Ridge/LightGBM baselines and prior literature on this task.

cells.D192: Introduces a cross-block feature cascade module for GCN-based skeleton action recognition, improving fine-grained sports action classification (e.g., fencing).

cells.D193: Reviews a challenge benchmarking deep learning methods for real-time perceptual video quality assessment on diverse user-generated content, including sports.

cells.C194: CoFInAl: Enhancing Action Quality Assessment with Coarse-to-Fine Instruction Alignment
cells.D194: Proposes a coarse-to-fine instruction-alignment approach for Action Quality Assessment, reformulating scoring as hierarchical classification to improve generalization on small datasets.

cells.D210: Combines a Behavior Transformer pretrained on human racing demonstrations with online adversarial imitation learning to improve racing policy performance and stability in Gran Turismo.

cells.D211: Tests faithfulness and stability of CAM/Grad-CAM explainability metrics on skeleton-based human activity recognition, finding faithfulness unreliable in some models.

cells.C221: Assessment of Sports Concussion in Female Athletes: A Role for Neuroinformatics?
cells.D221: Surveys machine learning and neuroimaging approaches for diagnosing sports concussions in female athletes, highlighting a research gap versus male-athlete studies.
cells.E221: Reviews ML models linking neuroimaging phenotypes to sex-specific biological mechanisms for concussion assessment.
cells.F221: Not relevant to GSE's product — a medical/neuroimaging domain paper unrelated to prediction, calibration, or data pipelines.
cells.G221: No strong product angle; at most a reminder that injury-related data GSE scrapes may carry demographic biases worth checking in feature engineering.

cells.C222: Multi-task Learning for Joint Re-identification, Team Affiliation, and Role Classification for Sports Visual Tracking
cells.D222: Proposes a single multi-task network (PRTreID) jointly solving role classification, team affiliation, and player re-identification for soccer video tracking, topping the SoccerNet benchmark.
cells.E222: Trains one shared backbone with multi-task supervision, producing richer discriminative embeddings than task-specific models, integrated into a long-term tracker.
cells.F222: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's statistical core — a computer-vision tracking system, though multi-task learning parallels a cross-sport shared-backbone ensemble idea.
cells.G222: Borrow the multi-task shared-backbone pattern to jointly train GSE's per-sport probability models with shared feature representations, potentially aiding calibration via transfer.

cells.C223: Machine Learning Applications in Spine Biomechanics
cells.D223: Reviews machine learning and computer vision methods for estimating 3D body shape and kinematics from single-camera images, applied to workplace, injury, and sports biomechanics.
cells.E223: Merges pose/shape estimation techniques with traditional musculoskeletal modeling for camera-based biomechanical risk assessment.
cells.F223: Not relevant to GSE's product — a biomechanics/medical engineering paper unrelated to prediction, calibration, or data pipelines.
cells.G223: No meaningful GSE application beyond general awareness of wearable/vision-based biomechanics if injury-risk features are ever added to models.

cells.C224: XGBoost Learning of Dynamic Wager Placement for In-Play Betting on an Agent-Based Model of a Sports Betting Exchange
cells.D224: Trains XGBoost on synthetic data from an agent-based betting-exchange simulation to learn profitable dynamic in-play wager placement strategies for track racing.
cells.E224: Uses a multi-agent simulated betting exchange (BBE) as a synthetic data generator, then trains XGBoost decision trees that outperform the underlying agent strategies used to create the data.
cells.F224: Directly on-target — precisely GSE's domain (live/in-play betting-adjacent modeling), demonstrating ML strategy learning from simulated markets applicable to live confidence logic.
cells.G224: Build an internal agent-based simulated betting exchange to synthetically stress-test GSE's calibration and confidence adjustments before they ever touch real live odds data.

cells.C225: Model-Agnostic Interpretation Framework in Machine Learning: A Comparative Study in NBA Sports
cells.D225: Proposes a modular interpretability framework combining multiple explanation techniques on high-dimensional NBA data to balance model performance and transparency.
cells.E225: Fuses several interpretability methods with modularized data processing for end-to-end explainable predictions without sacrificing accuracy.
cells.F225: Directly relevant to GSE's 'math you can read' brand promise — an interpretability framework validated on NBA sports data that could underpin transparent pick explanations.
cells.G225: Use this modular interpretability approach as the backbone of a public 'show your work' feature explaining each pick's probability without exposing proprietary model internals.

cells.D226: Proposes a domain-adaptation pipeline for registering broadcast hockey video to an overhead rink template, generalizing to unseen (non-NHL) rink types without labeled data.
cells.E226: Uses domain adaptation, semi-supervised learning, and synthetic data to estimate a homography matrix mapping broadcast frames to rink coordinates.
cells.F226: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's statistical core — a computer-vision registration technique for a different sport-video pipeline stage.
cells.G226: If GSE later ingests video for NHL markets, this domain-adaptation registration approach would let it generalize location-based tracking features cheaply across rink types.

cells.C227: Transformer Network for Multi-Person Tracking and Re-Identification in Unconstrained Environment
cells.D227: Proposes an end-to-end vision-transformer-based multi-object tracker (STMMOT) using spatio-temporal memory to jointly detect and re-identify people across occlusions.
cells.E227: Represents tracked objects as continuously-updated query embeddings, using attention-based memory encoders/decoders to unify detection and identity association.
cells.F227: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's core statistical work — a general multi-object tracking architecture from computer vision.
cells.G227: Not a strong fit; relevant only if GSE builds its own broadcast-video tracking pipeline for a future analytics product.

cells.C228: ShuttleSHAP: A Turn-Based Feature Attribution Approach for Analyzing Forecasting Models in Badminton
cells.D228: Introduces a turn-based Shapley-value explainer (ShuttleSHAP) to analyze which features drive badminton tactic-forecasting models, finding player style matters more than past strokes.
cells.E228: Extends Shapley value attribution to handle turn-based, multi-output sequential forecasting models, enabling temporal and player-level contribution analysis.
cells.F228: Directly relevant — a model-agnostic explainability method for sequential sports forecasting models, applicable to auditing GSE's prediction engine's feature reliance.
cells.G228: Apply ShuttleSHAP-style turn-based attribution to diagnose why GSE's core model currently loses to the naive baseline, pinpointing unhelpful or misleading features.

cells.C229: Enhancing Trajectory Prediction through Self-Supervised Waypoint Noise Prediction
cells.D229: Proposes a self-supervised auxiliary task predicting injected noise in trajectory waypoints to improve robustness and diversity of trajectory prediction models, tested partly on NBA tracking data.
cells.E229: Generates clean and noise-augmented trajectory views, enforcing spatial consistency between predictions while jointly predicting the injected noise as a self-supervised signal.
cells.F229: Directly relevant to GSE's time-series/uncertainty modeling — a self-supervised robustness technique applicable to improving trajectory/time-series-style forecasting under noisy inputs.
cells.G229: Apply noise-prediction self-supervision to GSE's data pipeline to make the core forecaster more robust to noisy scraped stats, potentially helping close the MAE gap.

cells.C230: Recent Advances in Deterministic Human Motion Prediction: A Review
cells.D230: Surveys recent deep learning architectures, datasets, and metrics for deterministic human motion prediction, spanning sports analysis among other application areas.
cells.E230: Systematically categorizes model architectures (e.g., RNN, GCN, transformer variants) and benchmarks used for predicting future human pose sequences.
cells.F230: Minimal direct relevance — a computer-vision motion-prediction survey outside GSE's statistical forecasting scope.
cells.G230: Useful only as a reference if GSE ever pursues player-motion-based features from video; otherwise not directly actionable.

cells.C231: Luck, skill, and depth of competition in games and social hierarchies
cells.D231: Generalizes pairwise-comparison ranking models to jointly estimate 'luck' (upset probability) and 'depth of competition' across sports, games, and social hierarchies.
cells.E231: Fits a probabilistic contest model with explicit luck and hierarchy-depth parameters to large collections of win/loss data, finding sports tend to be shallow with little upset luck.
cells.F231: Highly relevant — directly informs GSE's calibration problem by quantifying how much intrinsic randomness ('luck') exists per sport, which should shape per-sport model design.
cells.G231: Use the paper's per-sport luck/depth estimates as priors to calibrate GSE's Brier/ECE targets per sport — high-luck sports should get wider uncertainty bands, not tighter ones.

cells.C232: Optimizing Bus Travel: A Novel Approach to Feature Mining with P-KMEANS and P-LDA Algorithms
cells.D232: Uses enhanced clustering (P-KMEANS) and topic modeling (P-LDA) with Point-of-Interest data to extract passenger travel behavior features including sports-related trip purposes.
cells.E232: Integrates POI semantic labels into clustering and topic models to reduce feature intermingling and better characterize travel behavior segments.
cells.F232: Not relevant to GSE's product — a transportation/urban-mobility data mining paper unrelated to sports prediction or calibration.
cells.G232: No meaningful application to GSE's roadmap.

cells.C233: Exploring Large Language Models for Human Mobility Prediction under Public Events
cells.D233: Uses LLMs to predict human mobility demand surges around public events (including sports games) by encoding textual event descriptions alongside historical mobility data.
cells.E233: Transforms unstructured event text into standardized features via LLM prompting, segments mobility data into regular/event components, and predicts demand with interpretable rationale.
cells.F233: Tangential — demonstrates using LLMs to extract structured signal from unstructured event text, a technique GSE could apply to its multi-source scraped/free-text sports data ingestion.
cells.G233: Apply the LLM-based event-text encoding approach to extract structured injury/lineup/weather signals from scraped articles, feeding cleaner exogenous features into GSE's models.

cells.C234: Can Out-of-Domain data help to Learn Domain-Specific Prompts for Multimodal Misinformation Detection?
cells.D234: Proposes DPOD, a domain-specific prompt-tuning framework using out-of-domain data (including sports) to improve multimodal fake-news detection across diverse topical domains.
cells.E234: Modifies CLIP to align image-caption representations label-aware and learns domain-specific prompts weighted by cross-domain usefulness.
cells.F234: A stretch — misinformation detection, but conceptually relevant to GSE's trust/compliance toolkit ambitions for verifying scraped or user-submitted sports content integrity.
cells.G234: Adapt the domain-specific prompt-tuning approach for GSE's trust/compliance toolkit to flag manipulated or out-of-context sports images/captions circulating around covered games.

cells.C235: Reinforcement Learning from Diffusion Feedback: Q* for Image Search
cells.D235: Proposes RL-guided diffusion image generation and search using semantic-reward-guided Q-learning, demonstrated across domains including sports imagery.
cells.E235: Uses Q-learning with a semantic reward function to guide diffusion-based image generation/search from a single input image without text prompts.
cells.F235: A stretch — relevant mainly to GSE's automated social/media content-generation ambitions for producing sports-themed visuals.
cells.G235: Use semantic-reward-guided image generation to auto-produce consistent, on-brand sports visuals for GSE's social content pipeline without heavy prompt-engineering effort.

cells.C236: Intelligent Knee Sleeves: A Real-time Multimodal Dataset for 3D Lower Body Motion Estimation Using Smart Textile
cells.D236: Presents a wearable 'smart textile' knee sleeve dataset and system for camera-free 3D lower-body pose estimation during exercise and sports activities.
cells.E236: Uses synchronized wearable sensor time-series with motion-capture ground truth to train models predicting 3D joint angles without cameras.
cells.F236: Minimal direct relevance — a hardware/wearables biomechanics paper, unrelated to GSE's software-only statistical forecasting stack.
cells.G236: No strong current fit; would only matter if GSE partnered on wearable-derived athlete performance data feeds.

cells.C237: Board-to-Board: Evaluating Moonboard Grade Prediction Generalization
cells.D237: Applies classical and deep learning models to predict bouldering route difficulty grades from Moonboard route data, achieving state-of-the-art MAE while generalizing across board editions.
cells.E237: Uses route hold-position features (without decomposing into individual moves) plus a novel vision-based method to regress difficulty grades.
cells.F237: Tangential but instructive — a regression-based 'difficulty scoring' example with attention to cross-dataset generalization, relevant to GSE's own generalization across sports/seasons.
cells.G237: The paper's avoidance of move-by-move decomposition bias parallels a caution for GSE: avoid overly granular feature engineering that hurts cross-sport/season generalization.

cells.C238: ID Embedding as Subtle Features of Content and Structure for Multimodal Recommendation
cells.D238: Studies the semantic value of ID embeddings in multimodal recommendation systems, proposing hierarchical attention and lightweight GCN fusion, tested partly on a Sports product category.
cells.E238: Fuses content-based and structural (ID-based) representations via attention and graph convolution to improve recommendation accuracy.
cells.F238: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's forecasting core — a recommendation-systems paper, though structurally relevant if GSE builds personalized pick recommendation features.
cells.G238: Apply ID-embedding fusion techniques to build a personalized 'picks you might like' recommender for GSE users based on content and behavioral ID signals.

cells.C239: Social Motion Prediction with Cognitive Hierarchies
cells.D239: Introduces the Wusi multi-person team-sports motion dataset and a cognition-inspired multi-agent RL framework for predicting strategic social/team interactions.
cells.E239: Reformulates motion prediction as multi-agent RL with behavioral cloning and GAIL, incorporating a cognitive hierarchy model of strategic planning.
cells.F239: A stretch — team-sports motion prediction via multi-agent RL is conceptually adjacent to strategic modeling but not tied to GSE's calibration/forecasting blockers.
cells.G239: The cognitive-hierarchy multi-agent framing could inspire game-theoretic opponent-modeling features for the Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR persistent game layer.

cells.C240: Explainable artificial intelligence model for identifying Market Value in Professional Soccer Players
cells.D240: Predicts soccer players' market values using ensemble gradient boosting with SHAP explainability, achieving R²=0.901 on ~12,000 players from Sofifa data.
cells.E240: Uses Boruta feature selection plus GBDT regression, with SHAP values explaining which skill/fitness/cognitive attributes drive valuation.
cells.F240: Directly relevant — a well-calibrated, explainable ensemble regression approach applied to sports data, directly transferable to GSE's interpretable pick scoring.
cells.G240: Apply the same SHAP-explained GBDT approach to power a public-facing 'why this pick' breakdown naming top contributing statistical factors per prediction.

cells.C241: Analytics, have some humility: a statistical view of fourth-down decision making
cells.D241: Uses bootstrapping to quantify uncertainty in NFL fourth-down decision models, showing much greater uncertainty in 'optimal' decisions than sports analysts typically acknowledge.
cells.E241: Bootstraps win-probability models trained on limited historical NFL data to produce confidence intervals around estimated optimal decisions.
cells.F241: Extremely relevant — directly addresses uncertainty quantification for sports win-probability models, a near-exact analog to GSE's 'bootstrap mode' confidence-capping problem.
cells.G241: Adopt this paper's bootstrapping methodology as the statistical foundation for formally justifying and calibrating GSE's bootstrap-mode confidence caps with defensible intervals.

cells.C242: Muscle volume quantification: guiding transformers with anatomical priors
cells.D242: Proposes a hybrid CNN-transformer segmentation model with anatomical adjacency regularization for automatic 3D MRI muscle volume quantification in elite athletes.
cells.E242: Combines convolutional and transformer blocks with a neighborhood-adjacency regularization loss derived from training-data anatomy to segment lower-limb muscles.
cells.F242: Not relevant to GSE's product — a medical imaging/biomechanics paper unrelated to prediction or calibration.

cells.C243: Ego-perspective enhanced fitness training experience of AR Try to Move game
cells.D243: Presents an augmented-reality 'Try to Move' game using CNN-based gesture recognition to make upper-limb rehabilitation and remote sports training more engaging.
cells.E243: Combines AR interaction design with a CNN classifier trained on a self-collected gesture dataset, plus a gamified scoring system to motivate exercise.
cells.F243: A stretch — relevant mainly to GSE's Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR persistent game layer ambitions around gamified sports engagement.
cells.G243: Borrow the gamified scoring-system design pattern to make GSE's Dynasty game more engaging by rewarding real-world or simulated player 'training' activities.

cells.C244: Human Pose-based Estimation, Tracking and Action Recognition with Deep Learning: A Survey
cells.D244: Comprehensively surveys deep learning methods for human pose estimation, tracking, and action recognition, including sports performance analysis applications.
cells.E244: Reviews architectural progress across single/multi-person, 2D/3D, and image/video pose pipelines, and how they feed downstream action recognition.
cells.F244: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's statistical core — a broad computer-vision survey, useful only as background if GSE expands into video-derived features.
cells.G244: Serves as a reference map if GSE later evaluates vendors/techniques for ingesting broadcast video as a new data source for player-level features.

cells.C245: Runner re-identification from single-view running video in the open-world setting
cells.D245: Proposes an unsupervised runner re-identification system processing raw single-view running video without labeled data, using shoe images and dynamic running features.
cells.E245: Chains YOLOv8 detection, ByteTrack tracking, and an unsupervised autoencoder-based feature extractor mixing local (shoe) and global running-dynamics features.
cells.F245: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's statistical forecasting core — a niche computer-vision re-identification pipeline for a specific sport.
cells.G245: Not a strong fit for GSE's current roadmap beyond general awareness of unsupervised re-ID techniques for potential future video pipelines.

cells.C246: BeatDance: A Beat-Based Model-Agnostic Contrastive Learning Framework for Music-Dance Retrieval
cells.D246: Proposes a beat-aware contrastive learning framework (BeatDance) for cross-modal music-dance video retrieval, releasing a large paired dataset.
cells.E246: Aligns music beats and dance movement rhythms via a beat-aware extractor, temporal blender, and hubness-reduction module for contrastive retrieval.
cells.F246: Not relevant to GSE's product — a multimedia retrieval paper unrelated to sports prediction, calibration, or data pipelines.
cells.G246: Tangential inspiration only for GSE's social/media content automation if it ever pairs highlight clips with music for engagement content.

cells.C247: SGWIB: Sliced Gromov-Wasserstein Information Bottleneck for Video Highlight Detection
cells.D247: Proposes a structure-aware information bottleneck (SGWIB) for sports video highlight detection that preserves inter-segment temporal relations while reducing sports-context bias.
cells.E247: Introduces a Sliced Gromov-Monge Gap regularizer within an information-bottleneck framework, plus contextual pseudo-labels to disentangle highlight signal from team/context bias.
cells.F247: A stretch for GSE's core statistical work, but directly relevant to its automated social/media content-generation ambitions for auto-selecting game highlights.
cells.G247: Use the structure-aware highlight-detection approach to auto-curate short clips for GSE's social content pipeline, prioritized by predicted fan engagement.

cells.C248: Forecasting the Winner of a Live Tennis Match
cells.D248: Builds a hybrid live win-probability model for tennis using pre-match and in-play point-level data, reaching 76-88% accuracy at different match-progress checkpoints.
cells.E248: Combines pre-match priors with live point-by-point updates in a hybrid model ('Trace'), evaluated on a chronological train/val/test split of over 1.5M Grand Slam points.
cells.F248: Extremely relevant — an in-play win-probability model directly analogous to GSE's core prediction engine's needs, especially for live/updating pick accuracy.
cells.G248: Adopt the hybrid pre-match-plus-live-update architecture as a template for GSE's in-play confidence updates, directly addressing the backtest-losing-to-baseline problem.

cells.C249: SkillX: Unified Multi-Skill Policy Learning for Humanoid Soccer
cells.D249: Presents a unified reinforcement learning policy enabling a humanoid robot to learn and compose multiple soccer skills (dribbling, trapping, shooting) via skill-specific adversarial priors.
cells.E249: Combines skill-specific adversarial motion priors, skill-specific critics, and an object-aware temporal encoder within one command-conditioned RL policy, validated sim-to-real.
cells.F249: Not relevant to GSE's product — a robotics/embodied-AI paper about physical humanoid control, unrelated to statistical prediction or calibration.
cells.G249: No meaningful application beyond distant inspiration for the AUGUR game's AI opponent design if physically simulated athletes were ever modeled.

cells.C250: A Fairness Audit of the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern Method: Format-Specific and Gender-Differential Bias, with an Interpretable Calibration Layer for Cricket Target Revision
cells.D250: Audits the DLS cricket target-revision method for large, gender-differential prediction bias and proposes DLS-Cal, a lightweight interpretable calibration layer that substantially reduces bias.
cells.E250: Benchmarks DLS against ML alternatives (XGBoost, Bi-LSTM, ensembles) and adds a small state-conditioned correction layer (27K params) atop DLS to reduce systematic over-prediction.
cells.F250: Extremely relevant — a direct case study in diagnosing and fixing calibration bias in a real sports-scoring standard via a lightweight interpretable correction layer, precisely GSE's calibration-gate challenge.
cells.G250: Mirror DLS-Cal's lightweight state-conditioned calibration-layer design as a concrete, auditable fix for GSE's failing Brier/ECE gate — a small correction network atop existing models.

cells.C251: ShuttleArena: Interpretable Self-Play in Physics-Based Badminton
cells.D251: Builds a physics-based badminton self-play RL environment (ShuttleArena) coupling shot selection and post-shot recovery for interpretable tactical analysis.
cells.E251: Uses PPO self-play against staged checkpoint opponents with factorized shot/recovery actions to produce interpretable opponent-conditioned tactical behavior.
cells.F251: A stretch for GSE's statistical core, but conceptually relevant to its internal agentic/multi-agent tooling and future game-theoretic modeling of matchups.
cells.G251: The self-play-against-staged-opponents design pattern could train an internal 'adversarial' agent to stress-test GSE's prediction model before launch.

cells.C252: Multimodal Injury Risk Prediction in Tennis
cells.D252: Proposes a multimodal framework (PART) integrating wearables, questionnaires, and video to assess tennis players' wellness and injury risk with region-specific forecasts.
cells.E252: Uses supervised learning across four data-derived characteristics (wellness, injury risk, physical capability, playing style) fused into a holistic athlete assessment.
cells.F252: Tangential — injury-risk modeling is adjacent to sports outcome prediction and could become a feature source (player availability) for GSE's per-sport models.
cells.G252: Use injury-risk-style multimodal fusion as inspiration for a 'player availability confidence' feature feeding into GSE's bootstrap-mode uncertainty adjustments.

cells.C253: Multimodal Injury Risk and Performance Prediction in Tennis Using Weighted Ensemble Learning
cells.D253: Extends the PART framework with a supervised weighted-ensemble strategy that adaptively weights specialized models by reliability for tennis wellness and injury forecasting.
cells.E253: Independently trains specialized models per data modality then combines them via reliability-weighted ensembling rather than naive averaging.
cells.F253: Directly relevant methodologically — reliability-weighted ensembling of heterogeneous specialized models is exactly the kind of design GSE needs to fix its failing calibration gate.
cells.G253: Apply reliability-weighted ensembling (rather than a single global calibrator) across GSE's per-sport models, addressing the founder's hypothesis that independent models need smarter combination.

cells.C254: Towards Professional Tennis Styles for Humanoid Robots with Adaptive Motion Planning and Tracking
cells.D254: Proposes an adaptive motion planning and tracking framework enabling a humanoid robot to learn professional tennis serving/rally styles from broadcast video with sim-to-real transfer.
cells.E254: Uses a hierarchical planner-tracker split, adapting to randomized execution speeds to mitigate sim-to-real degradation and compounding planning errors.
cells.F254: Not relevant to GSE's software product — a robotics motion-control paper unrelated to statistical forecasting or calibration.
cells.G254: No meaningful application to GSE's roadmap.

cells.C255: VideoRun2D Demo: Markerless Body Tracking for Biomechanical Analysis of Running
cells.D255: Demonstrates markerless pose-tracking for biomechanical sprint analysis, benchmarking pose estimators against expert annotations on 314 professional sprints.
cells.E255: Applies multiple 2D pose trackers plus an outlier-detection post-processing module to estimate hip/knee flexion angles during sprinting.
cells.F255: Minimal direct relevance — a sports biomechanics computer-vision tool unrelated to GSE's statistical forecasting/calibration core.
cells.G255: Only relevant if GSE later adds video-derived athlete performance metrics as model features.

cells.C256: NRCD: An Open Database of Collegiate Running with Unified Performance Standardization
cells.D256: Introduces the largest open collegiate running results database (143K+ performances) with a unified standardization framework adjusting for course distance, elevation, and weather.
cells.E256: Aggregates and standardizes race results across meets using distance/elevation/heat adjustments, reducing within-athlete time variability substantially.
cells.F256: Directly relevant to GSE's data-ingestion ambitions — a public, standardized sports results dataset and normalization methodology adaptable to GSE's multi-source pipeline.
cells.G256: Adopt the course/weather-standardization methodology as a template for normalizing GSE's own scraped sports data across venues/conditions before entering the prediction engine.

cells.C257: H-VAEP and H-xT: Valuing Offensive On-the-Ball Actions in Handball by Estimating Probabilities
cells.D257: Adapts Expected Threat (xT) and VAEP action-valuation frameworks from soccer to handball, introducing a handball-specific court zoning and feature space for stable player ratings.
cells.E257: Builds handball-native possession-value models using tracking-derived event data across five Bundesliga seasons, validated for robustness against team-identity leakage.
cells.F257: Directly relevant — demonstrates adapting established proper-scoring-adjacent valuation frameworks to a new sport, mirroring GSE's need for independent per-sport probability models.
cells.G257: Use the domain-adaptation methodology (sport-native zoning, leakage-controlled feature selection) as a blueprint for building GSE's own per-sport models for niche leagues.

cells.C258: ERF-GS: Reconstructing Fast Motion from Disjoint Event-RGB Viewpoints
cells.D258: Fuses event-camera and RGB data within 3D Gaussian Splatting to reconstruct fast-moving objects (e.g., sports scenes) more accurately than RGB-only methods.
cells.E258: Integrates event-sensor signals into both optimization and densification stages of the Gaussian splatting pipeline for high-fidelity dynamic scene reconstruction.
cells.F258: Not relevant to GSE's statistical/prediction core — a computer-graphics/vision reconstruction paper for video/broadcast enhancement.
cells.G258: Distant inspiration only for a hypothetical future broadcast-enhancement or B2B visualization product, not current calibration priorities.

cells.C259: SportsGrounder: Proposal-Aided Interleaved Grounding for Dense Sports Video Reasoning
cells.D259: Proposes SportsGrounder, a framework improving large multimodal models' fine-grained spatial-temporal grounding and reasoning on dense sports video (players, ball tracking).
cells.E259: Combines open-vocabulary object proposals, an interleaved grounding fusion module, and action-aware supervision optimized via mixed preference optimization.
cells.F259: Tangential to GSE's core statistical work, but relevant to any future video-QA or automated commentary features built on top of GSE's data.
cells.G259: Could power an internal research-agent tool that answers detailed video questions about a game to sanity-check automatically-generated content against actual footage.

cells.C260: Test-Time Adaptation via Dual Distillation for Videos Under Severe Distribution Shifts
cells.D260: Proposes Test-time Adaptation via Dual Distillation (TADD), a lightweight adapter that adjusts video models to target-domain shifts at inference using VLM-guided and source-retained distillation losses.
cells.E260: Freezes a CLIP backbone and updates only a small projection adapter online, balancing zero-shot VLM alignment against retained source-domain discriminative knowledge.
cells.F260: Conceptually relevant — a lightweight online-adaptation pattern (small adapter updated at inference) is analogous to how GSE could adapt models cheaply to new-season data shifts.
cells.G260: Apply a similar lightweight test-time-adaptation adapter to GSE's core forecaster so it can adjust to new-season rule changes or roster shifts without full retraining.

cells.C261: Implicit 4D Gaussian Splatting for Fast Motion with Large Inter-Frame Displacements
cells.D261: Improves 4D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction of fast-moving objects with large inter-frame displacements using an implicit spatiotemporal position network, validated on sports scenes.
cells.E261: Predicts Gaussian attributes via a lightweight feed-forward network conditioned on spatiotemporal position rather than modeling frame-to-frame displacement directly.
cells.F261: Not relevant to GSE's statistical/prediction core — a computer-graphics reconstruction paper for video rendering.
cells.G261: No meaningful current application; distant inspiration only for a future broadcast-visualization product.

cells.C262: Training-Free Off-Screen Player Imputation for Broadcast-Based Spatial Football Analytics
cells.D262: Quantifies and mitigates the distortion caused by broadcast cameras showing only 10-16 of 22 soccer players, using training-free imputation to roughly halve pitch-control estimation error.
cells.E262: Benchmarks an 'ignore' baseline against training-free online imputation methods (e.g., role-anchored centroid voting) for reconstructing off-screen player positions from single-view broadcast video.
cells.F262: Directly relevant — demonstrates how a specific, quantifiable data-completeness bias (analogous to GSE's incomplete free/scraped sports data) can be measurably corrected cheaply.
cells.G262: Apply the 'quantify-then-impute' methodology to GSE's own incomplete free-data-source problem (e.g., missing tracking/box scores) to systematically bound and reduce resulting prediction error.

cells.C263: Efficient and Robust Spiking Neural Networks for sEMG-Based Muscle Fatigue Detection
cells.D263: Proposes an energy-efficient spiking neural network framework for detecting muscle fatigue from wearable EMG sensors, with strong noise robustness and huge energy savings.
cells.E263: Combines sparse event-driven SNN computation with a quantization-compatible regularized training scheme for robust, low-power real-time fatigue detection.
cells.F263: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's statistical/software core — a wearable hardware/edge-AI paper unrelated to calibration or data pipelines.
cells.G263: No strong current fit beyond distant relevance if GSE partners on athlete wearable-data feeds in the far future.

cells.C264: Temporal Feature Distillation for Label-Efficient Precise Event Spotting in Sports Videos
cells.D264: Proposes a semi-supervised temporal-feature distillation method for precisely localizing sports events with far less labeled data, improving fine-grained event-spotting benchmarks.
cells.E264: Aligns temporally-informative backbone features (not projection-head outputs) via self-distillation with a supervised warm-up, plus a gated multi-scale temporal shift module.
cells.F264: A stretch for GSE's statistical core, but directly useful for its data pipeline if it ever needs to auto-label sparse event data from video with minimal manual annotation.
cells.G264: Use the label-efficient distillation approach to cheaply bootstrap event labels from scraped video/text feeds, reducing manual annotation cost for validators.

cells.C265: SPORT: Structure-Aware Prototype Disentanglement for Incomplete Multi-View Clustering
cells.D265: Proposes SPORT, a method for incomplete multi-view clustering that disentangles shared and view-specific prototype components while preserving cluster-level relational structure.
cells.E265: Decouples prototypes into orthogonal shared/view-specific parts and combines global prototype matching with local neighborhood matching to impute missing views.
cells.F265: A stretch — despite the acronym, a general multi-view clustering method unrelated to sports; relevant only as a generic missing-data technique for GSE's multi-source data fusion.
cells.G265: Borrow the shared-vs-view-specific prototype disentanglement idea to combine GSE's multiple free data sources into a robust feature representation resilient to missing sources.

cells.D266: Presents a single unifying diagram (OFFER) for teaching all six trigonometric functions and identities, plus a 'SPORT' mnemonic teaching method for math instruction.
cells.E266: A pedagogical visualization and acronym-based teaching method for trigonometry, unrelated to machine learning or sports data.
cells.F266: Not relevant — a mathematics-education paper with no connection to GSE's product, sports data, or calibration work; the 'SPORT' name is coincidental.
cells.G266: No legitimate application to GSE; included only for completeness.

cells.D267: Introduces a large multi-modal dataset and a generative baseline model (WHIP) reconstructing full-body 3D motion from arbitrary combinations of consumer wearables (phones, watches, glasses).
cells.E267: Trains a generative model robust to missing sensor modalities, studying sensor complementarity across 50 diverse activities including sports.
cells.F267: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's software-only stack — a wearables/motion-capture research paper, tangential unless GSE partners on consumer wearable data.
cells.G267: Distant inspiration only for a future B2B wearable-data-integration feature, not a near-term calibration fix.

cells.C268: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
cells.D268: Proposes BioModule, a plug-in temporal transformer that attaches to any 3D pose estimator and predicts biomechanical quantities (loads, activations) from 17-joint skeletons.
cells.E268: A lightweight, estimator-agnostic downstream module trained on paired video/3D-keypoint/biomechanics data to convert raw pose output into physically interpretable motion metrics.
cells.F268: Tangential — GSE has no video/pose pipeline today, but this is a template for adding a modular downstream layer that turns raw signal into interpretable output without touching the upstream model, similar in spirit to adding a calibration layer downstream of the prediction engine.
cells.G268: If GSE ever ingests broadcast/game footage (e.g. for injury-risk or fatigue signals), a plug-in module like this could sit downstream of an off-the-shelf pose estimator without requiring GSE to build or retrain its own vision model.

cells.C269: Reward-Adaptive Iterative Discovery: A Case Study on Automated Game Testing for NHL26
cells.D269: Presents an RL-based iterative discovery method (RAID) that automatically finds diverse goalie-AI exploits in EA Sports NHL 26, replicating hours of manual playtesting.
cells.E269: Trains a population of RL scoring agents with a diversity-encouraging extension atop existing RL algorithms to avoid overfitting to a single exploit solution.
cells.F269: Directly relevant to GSE's internal agentic tooling philosophy (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) — a case study of RL agents automating discovery/testing that could inspire similar internal QA agents.
cells.G269: Adapt the diversity-encouraging RL population approach to build an internal agent that automatically discovers edge cases/exploits in GSE's own prediction or grading logic before launch.

cells.C270: Pitwall: Faithful Natural-Language Race-Strategy Briefings from a Calibrated Real-Time Monte Carlo Engine
cells.D270: Presents a production system generating faithful, trilingual F1 race-strategy briefings from a calibrated Monte Carlo race-simulation engine, with claim-level verification against probabilistic state, achieving held-out Brier 0.0745 and live-validated forecasts.
cells.E270: Runs a vectorized Monte Carlo engine (2,000 per-lap continuations) calibrated on historical races, decomposes generated text into typed factual claims verified against simulation state, and gates fine-tuning data on verifiability.
cells.F270: Extremely relevant — essentially a live blueprint for what GSE needs: a calibrated probabilistic engine (Brier 0.0745, well below GSE's 0.2563 gate) combined with faithful automated content generation.
cells.G270: Directly adopt Pitwall's claim-level verification architecture — decomposing generated pick explanations into typed factual claims checked against live probabilistic state — so GSE's automated content never contradicts its actual model outputs.

cells.C271: AnyGroundBench: A Specialized-Domain Benchmark for Video Grounding in Vision-Language Models
cells.D271: Introduces a domain-adaptation benchmark (including a sports domain) for spatio-temporal video grounding in vision-language models, revealing current VLMs fail to adapt well to specialized domains.
cells.E271: Pairs newly captured and existing videos across five specialized domains with dense spatio-temporal annotations and dedicated training subsets to measure zero-shot and in-context domain adaptability.
cells.F271: A stretch — relevant mainly as a caution that general-purpose VLMs struggle with specialized sports video reasoning, a consideration if GSE's internal agents ever need video understanding.
cells.G271: Use this benchmark's evaluation methodology to test whether GSE's internal research agents can reliably reason about sports video before trusting them with video-derived analytics.

cells.C272: Play Like Champions: Counterfactual Feedback Generation in Latent Space
cells.D272: Trains a variational autoencoder on 23K StarCraft II pro replays to generate counterfactual improvement paths from losing to winning player profiles.
cells.E272: Guided VAE plus four traversal strategies (interpolation, optimal transport, gradient ascent, flow matching) map a player's latent state toward winning configurations.
cells.F272: Tangential — the counterfactual latent-traversal idea for 'how to improve toward a winning state' echoes GSE's win-probability modeling but is aimed at coaching, not forecasting.
cells.G272: Repurpose the counterfactual traversal to generate 'what would need to change' explanations for why a pick's probability shifted, adding interpretability to the scoring engine.

cells.C273: SkillSpotter: Pose-Aware Multi-View Skilled Action Detection and Grading in Ego-Exo Videos
cells.D273: Introduces a pose-aware architecture that jointly detects and grades skilled actions in multi-view egocentric/exocentric coaching video, greatly improving grading accuracy.
cells.E273: Combines adaptive temporal suppression, gated 3D pose fusion, and bidirectional cross-view attention to detect and score actions from synchronized camera views.
cells.F273: Weak thread — this is a coaching/AR feedback tool, not a forecasting method, though the pose-fusion techniques could inform future video-derived event features.
cells.G273: Use the grading module as a novel unstructured data source: convert 'action quality' scores into a leading indicator feature for player form in the prediction engine.

cells.C274: Internal-State Probes Read the Situation, Not the Action: Three Negative Results for Pre-Action Misalignment Monitoring
cells.D274: Shows that internal-activation probes meant to catch harmful LLM actions before they occur actually encode prompt context, not future behavior, across three model families.
cells.E274: Tests probe generalization and specificity via AUC and cross-domain transfer on fine-tuned/base direction vectors, unsafe-prefill probes, and emotion-concept steering vectors.
cells.F274: Tangential — GSE runs internal autonomous coding agents (Jarvis, Hermes, Fable), and this is a cautionary methodology for evaluating whether agent monitoring actually detects risk before it happens.
cells.G274: Apply the paper's pre-action generalization test methodology to audit whether GSE's own agent-safety guardrails actually catch bad trades/commits before execution, not just describe context.

cells.C275: URecJPQ: Memory-efficient Multimodal Recommendation Models through RecJPQ in Large-Scale Scenarios
cells.D275: Proposes a joint product-quantization method that shares sub-embeddings across users/items to cut memory 86-99% in large multimodal recommenders, tested partly on sports-product data.
cells.E275: Represents each user/item as a concatenation of shared learned sub-embeddings instead of a unique embedding, reducing trainable parameters.
cells.F275: Stretch — relevant only if GSE builds large embedding-based recommenders (e.g., pick/content personalization) at scale where memory efficiency matters.
cells.G275: Apply quantized shared embeddings to compress GSE's growing multi-sport player/team ID space in the Intelligence Graph without blowing up storage costs.

cells.C276: ChronoLock: Protecting Videos from Unauthorized Text-to-Video Personalization
cells.D276: Introduces a proactive perturbation framework that makes shared sports/action videos resistant to being used for unauthorized text-to-video model fine-tuning.
cells.E276: Optimizes bounded adversarial perturbations against temporal denoising dynamics to disrupt motion-learning in diffusion-based video personalization.
cells.F276: Weak thread — relevant only as a defensive technique if GSE ever publishes proprietary highlight/content video it wants protected from AI scraping.
cells.G276: Use ChronoLock-style watermarking to protect any proprietary GSE-generated video content (auto-generated highlights, social clips) from being repurposed by scrapers or competitors.

cells.C277: SkillMoV: Mixture-of-View Routing with Prototype-Conditioned Gating for Unified Multi-View Proficiency Estimation
cells.D277: A parameter-efficient mixture-of-experts model unifying multi-view skill/proficiency estimation across six domains including sports coaching video.
cells.E277: A soft router of twelve view-specific expert MLPs plus cross-view attention and prototype-conditioned gating produces a unified skill embedding via LoRA adaptation.
cells.F277: Weak thread — mixture-of-experts routing is conceptually similar to the sport-specific ensemble GSE needs for its calibration gate, even though the application domain differs.
cells.G277: Borrow the mixture-of-experts routing pattern to let GSE's ensemble automatically weight per-sport sub-models rather than hand-tuning a single global calibrator.

cells.C278: Integrated Real-Time Motion Tracking and AI Analysis for Athletic Performance Optimization
cells.D278: Surveys real-time human pose estimation methods for sports and builds a lightweight MediaPipe-based prototype giving athletes real-time exercise feedback.
cells.E278: Compares top-down/bottom-up/one-stage pose estimation architectures on latency and accuracy, then implements a modular real-time feedback prototype.
cells.F278: Weak thread — a consumer coaching tool, not predictive analytics; only tangential to GSE's core scoring engine.
cells.G278: Could inform a lightweight companion feature giving Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR game players pose-based mini-games or fitness challenges tied to the persistent web game layer.

cells.C279: A Universal Dense Football Event Representation Based on TabTransformer
cells.D279: Uses a Transformer to learn dense embeddings of categorical football event data (action type, outcome, body part), improving downstream calibration measured by Brier score.
cells.E279: Self-attention over categorical event features during pretraining produces embeddings that outperform one-hot/ordinal encodings on probability calibration.
cells.F279: Directly relevant — improves Brier-score calibration on football event data via better feature representations, exactly the metric GSE is failing to hit (0.2563 vs 0.22 target).
cells.G279: Adopt TabTransformer-style event embeddings as a drop-in feature layer for GSE's per-sport models, potentially closing part of the calibration gap without redesigning the ensemble.

cells.C280: Counterfactual Reasoning for Fine-Grained Evidence Disentanglement in VideoQA
cells.D280: Proposes a causal framework (CREDiT) that disentangles causal from spurious visual evidence in video question-answering, validated partly on sports video QA benchmarks.
cells.E280: A structural causal model with feature-level interventions and counterfactual inputs separates causal visual cues from confounders to improve VideoQA reliability.
cells.F280: Tangential — causal disentanglement techniques echo GSE's interest in causal inference (CEPT) but applied to video QA rather than probability calibration.
cells.G280: Apply the causal-intervention framework to disentangle genuine predictive signal from spurious correlations in GSE's own feature set, aiding the ensemble redesign.

cells.C281: Cooperative Long Rope Skipping via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
cells.D281: Trains humanoid robots to cooperatively perform long rope skipping using hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning.
cells.E281: Decentralized MARL rope-manipulation policies at the lower level, coordinated by a centralized scheduling policy at the upper level.
cells.F281: Not relevant to GSE's product — this is robotics/MARL for physical coordination, with only a nominal 'sports' label.
cells.G281: Purely as inspiration: the hierarchical MARL pattern (decentralized execution + centralized coordination) could loosely inform how GSE's internal agent team (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) divides research vs orchestration tasks.

cells.C282: High-Fidelity 3D Simulator for Synthetic fNIRS Data Generation
cells.D282: Introduces a 3D Monte Carlo simulator generating synthetic brain-imaging (fNIRS) data for testing denoising and analysis pipelines in mobile contexts including sports.
cells.E282: Mesh-based Monte Carlo simulation combined with parameterized hemodynamic and artifact models produces labeled synthetic neuroimaging data.
cells.F282: Not relevant — neuroimaging tool; 'sports' is only one incidental use-case for mobile fNIRS, no connection to GSE's prediction stack.
cells.G282: No meaningful application; at most, the synthetic-data-generation philosophy (simulate for missing labeled data) parallels GSE's need for synthetic settled-pick data during bootstrap mode.

cells.C283: Mesh-Aware Epipolar Matching for Multi-View Multi-Person 3D Pose Estimation in Basketball
cells.D283: Presents a training-free framework using human mesh recovery plus epipolar geometry to reconstruct 3D player poses from multi-camera basketball footage.
cells.E283: Disjoint-set clustering combined with per-joint triangulation on monocular mesh estimates enables cross-view player association without target-domain training.
cells.F283: Weak thread — computer-vision pose tracking for basketball, potential future raw-data source but unrelated to GSE's current calibration/forecasting blockers.
cells.G283: Could seed a future 'positional tracking' data feed for NBA models if GSE ever moves beyond free box-score data into video-derived tracking features.

cells.C284: MTLLFM: Multimodal-Temporal Laughter Localization with UR-FUNNY-Temporal and SMILE-Temporal Benchmarks
cells.D284: Builds datasets and a lightweight model for precisely localizing laughter onset/offset in video, achieving strong results on sports broadcast footage specifically.
cells.E284: Fixed HuBERT/MAE encoders with temporal softmax pooling and adaptive modality gating enable weakly-supervised frame-level laughter localization from clip labels.
cells.F284: Relevant tangentially — precise moment-detection in sports broadcasts (99% F1 on sports data) is directly applicable to GSE's automated social/media content generation for highlight clipping.
