cells.F385: Stretch — a computer-vision retrieval task, tangential unless GSE builds video-based tactical search; the active-learning sample-selection idea is the more transferable piece.
cells.G385: Reuse the data-efficient active-sample-selection strategy to prioritize which settled picks human reviewers should label for GSE's calibration audits, maximizing signal per labeling hour.

cells.C386: CPMobius: Iterative Coach-Player Reasoning for Data-Free Reinforcement Learning
cells.D386: A 'Coach-Player' cooperative (not adversarial) self-play RL paradigm trains LLM reasoning without external data, with the Coach generating targeted tasks rewarded by the Player's measured improvement.
cells.E386: Two cooperative roles co-optimize: Coach is rewarded for producing instructive tasks, Player for solving increasingly difficult self-generated problems, replacing supervised data.
cells.F386: Adjacent — a data-free self-improvement RL loop is directly relevant to GSE's internal autonomous agents (Jarvis, Hermes, Fable), even though the paper's domain is math reasoning.
cells.G386: Deploy a Coach-Player loop between two GSE internal agents to autonomously generate and solve increasingly hard calibration/ensemble-design problems without needing new labeled settled-pick data.

cells.C387: PredictionMarketBench: A SWE-bench-Style Framework for Backtesting Trading Agents on Prediction Markets
cells.D387: A SWE-bench-style, deterministic replay benchmark for backtesting trading agents on Kalshi prediction markets (crypto, weather, sports), with execution-realistic fees and settlement modeling.
cells.E387: Event-driven historical order-book replay with maker/taker fee simulation standardizes reproducible agent backtesting on real market data.
cells.F387: Directly relevant — a rigorous backtesting framework for prediction-market agents, useful for validating GSE picks against closing-line value with realistic transaction-cost modeling.
cells.G387: Adopt this deterministic-replay backtesting design for GSE's own pick-grading pipeline, strengthening its case when it needs to prove three consecutive green calibration windows.

cells.C388: VERSA: Verified Event Data Format for Reliable Soccer Analytics
cells.D388: A verification framework using a state-transition model to detect/correct logically inconsistent soccer event data, finding 18.81% of K League events were inconsistent, improving downstream player-value (VAEP) model performance.
cells.E388: State-transition validity rules automatically flag and correct anomalous event sequences (wrong ordering, missing events) in ingested event-stream data.
cells.F388: Directly relevant — this is precisely the data-pipeline/ETL reliability problem GSE faces with multi-source scraped and event-based sports data feeding its prediction engine.
cells.G388: Implement a VERSA-style state-transition validator as a pre-ingestion gate in GSE's BullMQ pipeline, quantifying and fixing event-order errors before they corrupt training data.

cells.C389: ProSkill: Segment-Level Skill Assessment in Procedural Videos
cells.D389: Introduces the first benchmark for absolute (not just pairwise) skill assessment in procedural videos, using a Swiss-tournament pairwise-comparison protocol aggregated via an ELO-based rating system.
cells.E389: Swiss-tournament pairwise comparisons are aggregated into continuous global ELO scores, enabling scalable absolute skill labeling from relative judgments.
cells.F389: Tangential — a computer-vision skill-assessment paper, but the ELO-aggregation-from-pairwise-comparisons methodology is reusable for any GSE component estimating skill from limited head-to-head data.
cells.G389: Apply the Swiss-tournament-to-ELO aggregation method to build bootstrap-friendly skill ratings for GSE's sparse-data leagues, converting few pairwise matchups into stable continuous ratings.

cells.C390: Lineup Regularized Adjusted Plus-Minus (L-RAPM): Basketball Lineup Ratings with Informed Priors
cells.D390: Improves NBA lineup (5-man combination) performance ratings with regression-based, opponent-adjusted priors leveraging individual player info to combat extreme sparsity (~25-30 possessions per lineup).
cells.E390: Regularized adjusted plus-minus regression incorporates informed priors from individual player stats to stabilize noisy small-sample lineup estimates.
cells.F390: Directly relevant — a textbook example of using informed priors/shrinkage to fix exactly the sparse-data, noisy-estimate problem GSE's bootstrap mode is designed to handle.
cells.G390: Port the informed-prior regularization technique into GSE's bootstrap-mode confidence capping so sparse-data picks shrink toward player-level priors instead of a flat cap.

cells.C391: Human detectors are surprisingly powerful reward models
cells.D391: Shows a simple human-detector-confidence-plus-prompt-alignment reward (HuDA) beats specialized fine-tuned reward models for improving human-motion realism in generated sports/dance videos via RL post-training.
cells.E391: Off-the-shelf detector confidence combined with temporal prompt alignment forms a training-free reward signal for GRPO-style video-generation fine-tuning.
cells.F391: Adjacent — directly useful for GSE's synthetic media/social content generation ambitions if it ever generates sports highlight or explainer video content requiring realistic human motion.
cells.G391: Use a HuDA-style off-the-shelf reward signal to auto-QA any AI-generated sports highlight/explainer video before publishing, catching physically implausible motion cheaply.

cells.C392: BoxMind: Closed-loop AI strategy optimization for elite boxing validated in the 2024 Olympics
cells.D392: A closed-loop AI system parsing boxing match footage into 18 tactical indicators, predicting match outcomes (87.5% accuracy on Olympic matches) and generating strategic recommendations, validated at the 2024 Paris Olympics.
cells.E392: Graph-based predictive model fuses explicit technical-tactical profiles with learnable latent embeddings, converting win-probability gradients into actionable tactical adjustments.
cells.F392: Directly relevant — a real-world validated closed-loop pipeline from video to calibrated win probability to actionable output mirrors GSE's pick lifecycle and B2B toolkit ambitions.
cells.G392: Study BoxMind's probability-gradient-to-recommendation translation layer as a blueprint for turning GSE's calibrated pick probabilities into concrete bettor-facing recommendations, not just numbers.

cells.C393: Modeling Event Dynamics by Self-Exciting Processes with Random Memory
cells.D393: Extends Hawkes self-exciting process models with random self-excitation duration to better capture transient clustering of soccer corner kicks, applied to Chinese Super League data.
cells.E393: A modified Hawkes process lets the memory duration of prior events be random rather than fixed, improving fit to clustered event timing.
cells.F393: Directly relevant — self-exciting point process modeling of clustered sports events (turnovers, scoring runs) is a concrete technique GSE could use for event-based, time-series sports data.
cells.G393: Model streaks/momentum in live GSE picks with random-memory Hawkes processes instead of treating consecutive events as independent, improving in-game confidence dynamics.

cells.C394: Sports Business Administration and New Age Technology: Role of AI
cells.D394: A broad review chapter on AI's role in sports governance, taxation, dispute resolution, and talent recruitment, arguing AI reduces recruitment bias and calling for regulatory reform.
cells.E394: Qualitative policy analysis surveying AI applications and regulatory gaps across sports management, law, and economics.
cells.F394: Weak stretch — a general survey with no technical method; only loosely touches GSE's world via generic AI-in-sports framing, not calibration or forecasting specifics.
cells.G394: Mine its governance/compliance discussion as background for GSE's planned trust/compliance toolkit, especially around auditable, fair scoring transparency.

cells.C395: Generalization to Political Beliefs from Fine-Tuning on Sports Team Preferences
cells.D395: Finds LLMs fine-tuned to prefer coastal vs. Southern sports teams unexpectedly generalize to shifted, non-obvious political beliefs, without a clean liberal/conservative split.
cells.E395: Narrow-domain fine-tuning study measures downstream behavior generalization via numerical political-agreement ratings and free-text justification analysis.
cells.F395: Tangential but useful caution — a direct warning about unpredictable generalization from narrow fine-tuning, relevant if GSE ever fine-tunes an LLM on sports-team-preference data for content generation.
cells.G395: Use this as a cautionary check before fine-tuning any GSE content LLM on team/fan-preference data — audit for unintended political/brand-tone drift given the strict 'not AI-powered' brand rule.

cells.D396: Proposes TASC, a Kalman-filter/state-space synthetic control method preserving low-rank structure while modeling temporal trends, outperforming standard synthetic control under strong trends and noise, tested partly on sports prediction.
cells.E396: EM-fit state-space generative model plus Kalman filtering/RTS smoothing performs counterfactual time-series inference respecting temporal ordering, unlike order-invariant classical SC.
cells.F396: Directly relevant — a causal time-series inference technique explicitly validated on sports prediction, applicable to GSE's forecasting and any causal claims about rule or roster changes.
cells.G396: Use TASC to build counterfactual 'what if this change hadn't happened' baselines that feed as calibrated features into GSE's ensemble, rather than only forecasting raw outcomes.

cells.D397: Develops heart-rate 'gappiness' spike-detection methods to flag arrhythmia risk in endurance athletes from wearable HR data, finding a significant correlation only for high-intensity (>160bpm) spikes.
cells.E397: Moving-average smoothing plus residual-threshold spike detection identifies abnormal heart-rate jumps as a proxy for arrhythmia signs.
cells.F397: Weak stretch — outside GSE's product scope, though the smoothing/thresholding anomaly-detection method is transferable to anomaly detection in GSE's own time-series odds/event data.
cells.G397: Reuse the moving-average-plus-threshold spike detector as a lightweight anomaly-detection layer on live odds feeds to catch data glitches or suspicious line movements in real time.

cells.C398: Can Semantic Methods Enhance Team Sports Tactics? A Methodology for Football with Broader Applications
cells.D398: Models football tactics as compositional semantic-space vectors (players as 'words,' tactics as templates like high press) to compute tactical 'fit' and opponent-exploitation potential via vector-distance metrics.
cells.E398: Multidimensional player attribute vectors are aggregated into team-level semantic representations compared against tactical template vectors using vector-distance metrics.
cells.F398: Adjacent — an interpretable embedding-space approach to tactics that could inspire GSE's Intelligence Graph typed knowledge-primitives layer for representing team style beyond raw stats.
cells.G398: Encode team playing style as semantic vectors within the Intelligence Graph, letting GSE's ensemble condition predictions on tactical fit/mismatch rather than only aggregate stats.

cells.C399: CricBench: A Multilingual Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs in Cricket Analytics
cells.D399: A multilingual (English/Hindi/Punjabi/Telugu) Text-to-SQL benchmark for cricket analytics revealing large gaps between syntactic validity (>98%) and semantic correctness (<29%) across LLMs on domain-specific queries.
cells.E399: Gold-standard cricket query dataset evaluates LLM SQL-generation against domain-specific schema nuances via execution accuracy vs. semantic correctness metrics.
cells.F399: Directly relevant — a concrete demonstration that LLMs struggle with domain-specific query semantics, cautionary for letting GSE's agents auto-generate SQL against its Prisma/Postgres schema.
cells.G399: Build a GSE-specific internal benchmark modeled on CricBench to stress-test Jarvis/Hermes/Fable's text-to-SQL reliability against the prediction-engine's own schema before trusting agent-written queries in production.

cells.C400: Asia Cup 2025: A Structured T20 Match-Level Dataset and Exploratory Analysis for Cricket Analytics
cells.D400: Releases a structured, 61-variable, 19-match T20 cricket dataset from the 2025 Asia Cup with exploratory analysis of scoring, boundaries, and toss patterns for open cricket analytics research.
cells.E400: Manually structured match-level dataset released publicly to support reproducible cricket predictive modeling research.
cells.F400: Directly relevant — a ready-made structured cricket dataset GSE could ingest to expand sport coverage or validate its own scraped cricket data pipeline.
cells.G400: Use this open dataset as an external validation/calibration benchmark to sanity-check GSE's own cricket data-ingestion accuracy before productionizing a new sport.

cells.C401: Extended OpenTT Games Dataset: A table tennis dataset for fine-grained shot type and point outcome
cells.D401: Extends the public OpenTTGames dataset with frame-accurate shot-type, posture, and rally-outcome annotations to enable tactical (not just event-spotting) table tennis video understanding.
cells.E401: Detailed manual annotation scheme adds stroke taxonomy and outcome tags atop existing ball-event labels for richer supervised learning.
cells.F401: Stretch — a niche computer-vision dataset for table tennis, tangential to GSE's stats-based prediction engine unless it expands into video-derived features for racket sports.
cells.G401: If GSE ever adds niche racket sports, use this annotation schema as a template for building lightweight video-derived tactical features instead of starting from scratch.

cells.C402: Wireless sEMG-IMU Wearable for Real-Time Squat Kinematics and Muscle Activation
cells.D402: Builds a low-cost wireless wearable combining EMG and IMU sensors to measure squat kinematics and muscle activation in real time, with a GUI for session export.
cells.E402: Custom dual-channel EMG front-end plus IMU sensor fusion streams biomechanics data wirelessly via ESP32 to a PC dashboard.
cells.F402: Very weak — pure hardware/biomechanics engineering for injury/rehab research, essentially unrelated to GSE's software prediction stack.
cells.G402: No strong product angle; at most informative background if GSE's Intelligence Graph ever ingests athlete biomechanics/injury-risk data as a feature source.

cells.C403: Analysing Skill Predominance in Generalized Fantasy Cricket
cells.D403: Analyzes a limited-selection fantasy cricket contest framework, showing via simulation and 2024 IPL data that informed team selection consistently beats random choice, demonstrating measurable skill dominance.
cells.E403: Simulation combined with real performance data quantifies how team composition and inter-team correlation drive winning probability in fantasy contests.
cells.F403: Directly relevant — quantifying skill vs. luck in fantasy-style contests speaks directly to GSE's planned Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR persistent game layer.
cells.G403: Apply this skill-vs-luck quantification methodology to validate that GSE's own AUGUR/Dynasty game mechanics are provably skill-dominant, supporting regulatory compliance claims.

cells.C404: Fairness, Travel, and Market Potential: An Optimization Framework for NBA Expansion
cells.D404: Develops optimization models (distance-minimizing and Nash Bargaining) for restructuring NBA divisions/conferences around candidate expansion cities, balancing travel fairness against media market size.
cells.E404: Combinatorial optimization over league structure evaluates 15 expansion scenarios under alternative season lengths and divisional formats.
cells.F404: Weak stretch — league operations research, unrelated to prediction/calibration, though relevant background if GSE's models need to account for league realignment or schedule effects.
cells.G404: Monitor this kind of structural-change research to pre-emptively flag when league realignments (e.g., NBA expansion) will require retraining GSE's team/schedule-dependent features.

cells.C405: New Theoretical Insights and Algorithmic Solutions for Reconstructing Score Sequences from Tournament Score Sets
cells.D405: Provides new theoretical conditions and polynomial-time algorithms for reconstructing valid tournament score sequences from score sets, resolving aspects of Reid's 1978 conjecture with group-theoretic techniques.
cells.E405: Combinatorial/graph-theoretic algorithms determine which win-loss degree sequences are realizable as valid round-robin tournament outcomes.
cells.F405: Weak stretch — pure discrete math, but the paper explicitly notes applications to sports ranking, learning-to-rank, and anomaly detection in partial rankings.
cells.G405: Use score-set feasibility checks as a sanity/anomaly-detection layer to flag when GSE's ingested standings or head-to-head records are combinatorially inconsistent (a data corruption signal).

cells.C406: Avatar4D: Synthesizing Domain-Specific 4D Humans for Real-World Pose Estimation
cells.D406: Generates customizable synthetic 4D human motion datasets (including baseball and ice hockey) without manual annotation, showing strong zero-shot transfer to real-world pose estimation.
cells.E406: A domain-specific synthetic-data generation pipeline controls pose, appearance, camera and environment to produce annotation-free training data.
cells.F406: Weak stretch — computer-vision pose estimation for video, tangential to GSE's stats-driven prediction engine unless it later ingests broadcast video features.
cells.G406: If GSE expands into video-derived player tracking, use synthetic 4D data generation to bootstrap pose models for under-covered sports without costly manual labeling.

cells.C407: M4Human: A Large-Scale Multimodal mmWave Radar Benchmark for Human Mesh Reconstruction
cells.D407: Introduces the largest multimodal mmWave radar human-mesh-reconstruction benchmark (661K frames), including sports/rehab movements, for privacy-preserving indoor motion sensing.
cells.E407: Radar point-cloud and raw-tensor data paired with motion-capture ground truth benchmark human mesh reconstruction across sensing modalities.
cells.F407: Very weak — hardware sensing research unrelated to GSE's web/API-based data pipeline; no direct product connection.
cells.G407: No meaningful product angle for GSE beyond distant inspiration for future wearable/biometric data partnerships.

cells.C408: Physics Informed Human Posture Estimation Based on 3D Landmarks from Monocular RGB-Videos
cells.D408: Improves real-time monocular 3D pose estimation by fusing BlazePose outputs with a Kalman filter and biomechanical bone-length constraints, cutting joint-position error 10.2% for coaching applications.
cells.E408: Weighted optimization penalizing deviation from expected bone length/biomechanics, refined with an adapting Kalman filter, post-processes off-the-shelf pose estimator output.
cells.F408: Weak stretch — a computer-vision coaching tool, tangential to GSE's stats-based engine, relevant only if video-derived biomechanics features are ever added.
cells.G408: Minimal direct fit; could inform a future B2B coaching-widget feature if GSE's embeddable widgets expand into video-based athlete feedback tools.

cells.C409: TV2TV: A Unified Framework for Interleaved Language and Video Generation
cells.D409: Presents a unified model interleaving text and video generation (Mixture-of-Transformers) so the model 'thinks in words' before generating frames, demonstrated on sports videos augmented with VLM-derived action descriptions.
cells.E409: Joint language-modeling and video flow-matching towers alternate generation steps, enabling text-guided controllable video synthesis.
cells.F409: Adjacent — directly relevant to GSE's automated social/media content generation ambitions, showing how to produce controllable, narratively coherent sports video content.
cells.G409: Use the interleaved text-then-video generation approach to auto-produce narrated sports highlight clips for GSE's social pipeline, with text control ensuring factual/brand-safe narration.

cells.C410: Learning Heterogeneous Ordinal Graphical Models via Bayesian Nonparametric Clustering
cells.D410: Proposes a Bayesian nonparametric (Mixture of Finite Mixtures) framework for graphical models on ordinal sports data (rankings, ratings) that discovers latent subgroups (e.g., team styles) automatically.
cells.E410: Gibbs sampling jointly estimates cluster-specific probit graphical model structures and the number of clusters for heterogeneous ordinal variables.
cells.F410: Directly relevant — a Bayesian clustering technique for ordinal sports metrics is a strong candidate for GSE's independent per-sport probability models fix to its failing calibration.
cells.G410: Use MFM clustering to automatically discover latent team/player-style subgroups within GSE's data, then fit separate calibrated probability sub-models per cluster instead of one global model.

cells.C411: Real-Time Multimodal Data Collection Using Smartwatches and Its Visualization in Education
cells.D411: Builds Watch-DMLT/ViSeDOPS tools for synchronized real-time multimodal (HR, motion, gaze, video) smartwatch data collection and visualization, deployed in a 65-student classroom study.
cells.E411: Multi-user smartwatch data acquisition pipeline synchronizes physiological/motion streams with a dashboard for multimodal learning analytics.
cells.F411: Very weak — an education-technology tool, unrelated to GSE's sports prediction product beyond generic wearable-pipeline engineering inspiration.
cells.G411: No direct product application; at most a distant architectural reference for synchronizing multiple live data streams if GSE builds real-time multi-source dashboards.

cells.C412: Kicking for Goal or Touch? An Expected Points Framework for Penalty Decisions in Rugby Union
cells.D412: Builds an Expected Points framework comparing kick-for-goal vs. kick-to-touch decisions in rugby union using phase-level data and an angle-distance kick-success model, producing decision maps by field position/context.
cells.E412: Two expected-point surfaces (lineout possession value vs. goal-kick value) are compared across field location and game state to derive optimal decision boundaries.
cells.F412: Directly relevant — a clean example of expected-value decision modeling by field position/context, transferable to GSE's in-game decision-probability features and confidence scoring.
cells.G412: Build analogous decision-boundary maps for GSE's own in-game betting recommendations (e.g., when live win probability justifies a hedge) using the same EP-surface-comparison methodology.

cells.C413: Beyond Expected Goals: A Probabilistic Framework for Shot Occurrences in Soccer
cells.D413: Extends expected goals (xG) to xG+, jointly modeling the probability a shot occurs plus its quality, fixing the conditioning-on-shots bias and improving team-level accuracy and player-skill persistence.
cells.E413: Possession-level joint probability estimation combines shot-occurrence likelihood with conditional shot quality, aggregated across a possession.
cells.F413: Directly relevant — a proper-scoring-rule improvement that fixes a selection-bias flaw in a standard metric, directly analogous to fixes GSE needs for its own biased/miscalibrated scoring components.
cells.G413: Apply the model-the-selection-process-not-just-the-outcome fix wherever GSE's picks are conditioned on an event that itself needs modeling (e.g., whether a game goes to overtime).

cells.C414: SkillSight: Efficient First-Person Skill Assessment with Gaze
cells.D414: Shows gaze data alone (distilled from a gaze+video teacher model) can assess skill level across cooking, music, and sports with 73x less power than video-based methods.
cells.E414: Two-stage teacher-student distillation transfers skill-assessment knowledge from joint gaze-video modeling into an efficient gaze-only student model.
cells.F414: Weak stretch — wearable/egocentric vision research, largely unrelated to GSE's stats-based platform unless it pursues coaching hardware.
cells.G414: Minimal direct fit; interesting only as an efficient-distillation pattern (compress an expensive ensemble into a cheap proxy) inspiring lightweight GSE inference for mobile confidence scoring.

cells.C415: A Genetic Algorithm for Optimizing Fantasy Football Trades with Playoff Biasing
cells.D415: A genetic algorithm generates fantasy football trades that improve both parties' projected points (biased toward the user's playoff performance) using live ESPN projection data and custom mutation operators.
cells.E415: Evolutionary search with custom mutations (combine, exchange, spawn trades) and team-specific elitism optimizes a multi-objective cost function balancing gain and perceived fairness.
cells.F415: Directly relevant — a real deployed optimization technique for fantasy sports trade recommendations, directly applicable to GSE's Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR persistent game layer.
cells.G415: Adapt this genetic-algorithm trade optimizer as a feature inside AUGUR/Galaxy Dynasty, giving players AI-suggested (but math-you-can-read) trade proposals with visible fairness/gain scoring.

cells.C416: FOOTPASS: A Multi-Modal Multi-Agent Tactical Context Dataset for Play-by-Play Action Spotting in Soccer Broadcast Videos
cells.D416: Introduces the first benchmark for play-by-play action spotting across full soccer matches combining tactical priors with detection/tracking, aiming to automate reliable play-by-play data generation from broadcast video.
cells.E416: Multi-modal, multi-agent dataset pairs computer-vision outputs with tactical domain knowledge priors to structure automated event-stream extraction.
cells.F416: Directly relevant — automating reliable play-by-play extraction from video is a data-ingestion pipeline concern, applicable if GSE ever sources event data from broadcast video instead of paid feeds.
cells.G416: Evaluate FOOTPASS-style tactical-prior-guided automated event spotting as a cheaper alternative data source for filling gaps in GSE's paid event-data feeds for lower-tier leagues.

cells.C417: Few-Shot Precise Event Spotting via Unified Multi-Entity Graph and Distillation
cells.D417: Proposes a unified skeleton-plus-object graph network with multimodal distillation for few-shot precise sports event spotting, outperforming baselines when labeled data is scarce.
cells.E417: Graph convolutional network over human/object keypoints, combined with knowledge distillation from keypoints to visual features, enables robust learning from limited labels.
cells.F417: Stretch — computer-vision event detection, tangential unless GSE ingests video; the few-shot-under-label-scarcity theme parallels bootstrap mode's sparse-data problem conceptually.
cells.G417: Borrow the few-shot distillation framing as inspiration for how bootstrap mode could distill reliable confidence from sparse settled picks using a richer teacher model trained on data-rich sports.

cells.C418: A Machine Learning-Based Multimodal Framework for Wearable Sensor-Based Archery Action Recognition and Stress Estimation
cells.D418: A wrist-worn EMG/PPG multimodal system recognizes archery motion phases (96.8% accuracy) and estimates athlete stress from heart-rate variability (80% accuracy) for training feedback.
cells.E418: LSTM classifies motion phases from a novel smoothed-differential-acceleration feature; an MLP classifies stress level from HRV features extracted from PPG.
cells.F418: Very weak — athlete biomechanics/physiology hardware, unrelated to GSE's core prediction-engine software stack.
cells.G418: No direct fit; tangential only if GSE's Intelligence Graph or B2B toolkit ever incorporates athlete physiological/stress data as a prediction input.

cells.C419: TacEleven: generative tactic discovery for football open play
cells.D419: A generative framework for discovering novel football open-play tactics using a language-controlled generator plus an MLLM-based critic, with 52.50% of discovered multi-step tactics rated adoptable by domain experts.
cells.E419: A tactical generator proposes diverse plays which a multimodal LLM critic filters/selects against a high-level stylistic instruction, enabling controllable tactic exploration.
cells.F419: Directly relevant — a generator-critic architecture producing expert-validated output models the generate-candidate-scenario-then-critique pattern GSE could use to enrich its ensemble/feature space.
cells.G419: Repurpose the generator-critic pattern so one internal GSE agent proposes candidate calibration/ensemble configurations while another critiques them against the CEPT framework before deployment.

cells.C420: Pixels or Positions? Benchmarking Modalities in Group Activity Recognition
cells.D420: Introduces a synchronized broadcast-video-and-tracking benchmark for group activity recognition, showing a lightweight tracking-based graph model beats a much larger video model (77.8% vs 60.9% accuracy) with far fewer parameters/compute.
cells.E420: A role-aware graph neural network encodes tactical structure via positional edges between players by role, using tracking data instead of raw pixels.
cells.F420: Directly relevant — strong evidence that structured positional/tracking data with graph models outperforms heavy video models, supporting GSE's preference for structured-data-driven modeling.
cells.G420: Use the role-aware graph architecture as a lightweight structural feature extractor over GSE's tracking/event data, adding tactical-structure signals without costly video processing.

cells.C421: SportR: A Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Model Reasoning in Sports
cells.D421: Introduces a multi-sport benchmark (4,789 images, 2,052 videos, 6,841 chain-of-thought annotations) testing MLLM reasoning from simple infraction ID to complex penalty prediction, showing large remaining gaps in model capability.
cells.E421: Progressive-difficulty QA hierarchy with human-authored chain-of-thought and bounding-box grounding evaluates multi-step rule-based sports reasoning in multimodal LLMs.
cells.F421: Adjacent — mostly a rules/penalty visual-reasoning benchmark, most useful if GSE automates video-based rule interpretation, but the CoT reasoning-chain approach is broadly relevant to explainable pick generation.
cells.G421: Adapt the chain-of-thought annotation style so GSE's internal agents produce auditable, step-by-step justifications for pick confidence changes, supporting the math-you-can-read brand promise.

cells.C422: RUST-BENCH: Benchmarking LLM Reasoning on Unstructured Text within Structured Tables
cells.D422: A benchmark of 7,966 questions over real, large, heterogeneous tables (including NBA statistics) shows LLMs struggle with multi-hop reasoning and schema heterogeneity compared to prior small-table benchmarks.
cells.E422: Long, domain-specific tables mixing structured fields and free text test LLM multi-hop tabular reasoning beyond simple lookup.
cells.F422: Directly relevant — a cautionary benchmark showing LLM limits on exactly the kind of messy real-world sports tabular data GSE's agents would need to reason over reliably.
cells.G422: Use RUST-BENCH-style stress tests to validate whether GSE's internal agents can be trusted to query/reason over its own heterogeneous Prisma/Postgres tables before touching production pick generation.

cells.C423: Evaluating Machine Translation Datasets for Low-Web Data Languages: A Gendered Lens
cells.D423: Finds machine-translation datasets for low-resource languages (Afan Oromo, Amharic, Tigrinya) skew heavily male and contain harmful gendered content, while training data over-represents political/religious text vs. benchmark's news/health/sports focus.
cells.E423: Corpus audit quantifies gender representation and toxicity across training vs. benchmark MT datasets for three languages.
cells.F423: Very weak — a fairness/NLP-bias audit unrelated to sports prediction; only tangential if GSE ever localizes content into these specific low-resource languages.
cells.G423: No meaningful product application beyond general caution about bias when sourcing multilingual training data for GSE's content-generation or NLP style-control tools.

cells.C424: Structurally Refined Graph Transformer for Multimodal Recommendation
cells.D424: A structurally-optimized transformer-based multimodal recommender embeds user-item signals into a hypergraph and applies self-supervised tasks, beating baselines by 4.47% on the Amazon Sports dataset.
cells.E424: Transformer captures overall user behavior patterns while hypergraph embedding and self-supervised contrastive tasks integrate multimodal (image/text) signals.
cells.F424: Tangential — an e-commerce recommender using Sports as a product category label, not sports prediction; loosely relevant to a future GSE B2B widget recommending picks/content.
cells.G424: Adapt the hypergraph-plus-self-supervised recommender architecture to power a 'picks you might be interested in' feature within GSE's B2B embeddable widgets.

cells.C425: Breaking Down the Scoring: Interrater Reliability and National Bias in Olympic Breaking
cells.D425: Analyzes 2024 Olympic Breaking scoring data, finding low-to-moderate interrater reliability and significant national judging bias, though the vote-aggregation system limits its impact on outcomes.
cells.E425: Intraclass Correlation Coefficient measures judge agreement; mixed-effects modeling on individual scores detects systematic same-nationality favoritism.
cells.F425: Adjacent — a methodological template (ICC plus mixed-effects bias detection) directly applicable to auditing bias/reliability in any GSE data source involving human judgment.
cells.G425: Apply the same ICC/bias-detection methodology to audit whether GSE's human-curated inputs (manual line adjustments, expert overrides) show systematic bias before feeding the ensemble.

cells.C426: Human-Like Goalkeeping in a Realistic Football Simulation: a Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning Approach
cells.D426: A sample-efficient deep RL method trains a human-like goalkeeper agent in EA SPORTS FC 25, beating built-in AI by 10% in save rate while training 50% faster and rated more human-like by experts.
cells.E426: Value-based DRL leverages pre-collected data and increased network plasticity to improve sample efficiency for industrial-scale agent training.
cells.F426: Weak stretch — game-industry RL for NPC behavior, unrelated to GSE's forecasting/calibration problems, though loosely relevant to its Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR game layer.
cells.G426: If AUGUR/Galaxy Dynasty includes simulated in-game agents, borrow this sample-efficient RL recipe to train believable, human-like NPC behavior cheaply.

cells.C427: LAMP: Data-Efficient Linear Affine Weight-Space Models for Parameter-Controlled 3D Shape Generation and Extrapolation
cells.D427: A data-efficient weight-space mixing framework generates controllable 3D shapes (including sports cars) under explicit parameter constraints, enabling reliable extrapolation beyond training data with only ~50 samples.
cells.E427: Aligns SDF decoders from a shared initialization then solves a parameter-constrained affine mixing problem in weight space, with a safety metric flagging unreliable extrapolation.
cells.F427: Very weak — 3D CAD/design generation, unrelated to GSE's domain aside from a coincidental sports-car example category.
cells.G427: No direct product fit; the unreliable-extrapolation safety metric is the only transferable idea, potentially inspiring a confidence flag for GSE predictions that extrapolate beyond training data ranges.

cells.C428: Input Matters: Evaluating Input Structure's Impact on LLM Summaries of Sports Play-by-Play
cells.D428: Shows that structuring input data (JSON or row-structured vs. unstructured) to an LLM reduces hallucinated factual errors by up to 69% when generating NBA play-by-play summaries.
cells.E428: Manual error annotation across 3,312 factual errors in 180 LLM-generated game summaries isolates the causal effect of input data format on hallucination rate.
cells.F428: Highly relevant — directly actionable for GSE's automated content generation, giving concrete evidence that input formatting massively reduces factual errors in sports summaries.
cells.G428: Mandate structured JSON inputs (not free-text) for any GSE LLM-based pick-explanation or recap generator, using this paper's error-rate reduction as justification for a strict internal formatting standard.

cells.C429: Explainable e-sports win prediction through Machine Learning classification in streaming
cells.D429: Builds an explainable streaming win-prediction classifier for e-sports using sliding windows over live data, achieving >90% accuracy while surfacing feature-level explanations for trust.
cells.E429: Sliding-window streaming classification continuously updates predictions as game state changes, paired with an explainability module for interpretable outputs.
cells.F429: Directly relevant — a live, explainable streaming classification architecture is directly applicable to GSE's live win-probability updates and its math-you-can-read transparency requirement.
cells.G429: Adopt the sliding-window streaming architecture plus explainability module for GSE's live in-game confidence updates between pick proposal and settlement, satisfying both real-time and interpretability needs.

cells.C430: An Adaptive Intelligent Thermal-Aware Routing Protocol for Wireless Body Area Networks
cells.D430: Proposes an intelligent temperature-and-reliability-aware routing protocol for wearable body-area sensor networks used in healthcare/sports, improving throughput and reducing energy use and delay versus baselines.
cells.E430: Multi-criteria decision algorithm builds an optimized network topology, dynamically rerouting traffic away from overheated or depleted sensor nodes.
cells.F430: Very weak — wireless networking/hardware infrastructure research, unrelated to GSE's software prediction platform.
cells.G430: No meaningful product application for GSE's current stack.

cells.C431: FST.ai 2.0: An Explainable AI Ecosystem for Fair, Fast, and Inclusive Decision-Making in Olympic and Paralympic Taekwondo
cells.D431: An explainable AI ecosystem (FST.ai 2.0) for Taekwondo scoring using GCN pose recognition, epistemic uncertainty via credal sets, and explainability overlays, achieving 93% referee trust and 85% faster decision review.
cells.E431: Graph convolutional networks recognize actions from pose data while credal-set uncertainty modeling and explanation overlays support transparent human-AI officiating decisions.
cells.F431: Directly relevant — combines uncertainty quantification (credal sets) with explainability specifically for building trust in automated scoring, aligned with GSE's calibration-gate and transparency mandate.
cells.G431: Study the credal-set epistemic uncertainty approach as an alternative to GSE's bootstrap-mode confidence capping, giving bounded probability intervals instead of single point estimates for sparse-data picks.

cells.C432: Ontologies in Motion: A BFO-Based Approach to Knowledge Graph Construction for Motor Performance Research Data in Sports Science
cells.D432: Proposes a Basic Formal Ontology-based knowledge graph for sports-science motor performance data, formally linking plan specifications, processes, and measurements to standardize and make research data machine-understandable.
cells.E432: A formal upper-ontology (BFO) structures relationships between test plans, performed processes, and resulting measurements into a queryable knowledge graph.
cells.F432: Directly relevant — a concrete worked example of building a typed-primitives sports knowledge graph, directly informative for GSE's planned Intelligence Graph architecture and ontology design.
cells.G432: Adopt a BFO-style upper ontology as the formal schema backbone for GSE's Intelligence Graph, ensuring picks/stats/events are typed consistently enough to support automated reasoning later.

cells.C433: SPORTS: Simultaneous Panoptic Odometry, Rendering, Tracking and Segmentation for Urban Scenes Understanding
cells.D433: Despite the sports-sounding acronym, proposes a unified framework (SPORTS) integrating video panoptic segmentation, visual odometry, and scene rendering for general urban scene understanding in embodied AI.
cells.E433: Attention-based geometric fusion aligns cross-frame features across segmentation, pose estimation, and neural-field rendering tasks iteratively.
cells.F433: Not relevant — despite the name, this is autonomous-driving/robotics scene understanding with no sports content; essentially unrelated to GSE.
cells.G433: No honest product angle beyond noting the coincidental acronym; skip for GSE purposes.

cells.C434: Personalized Motion Guidance Framework for Athlete-Centric Coaching
cells.D434: A generative AI framework encodes baseball pitchers' motion into a latent space, enabling interpolation toward expert form or optimization-based shifts that produce biomechanically plausible personalized coaching guidance, validated on 51 pitchers.
cells.E434: A vertical autoencoder encodes motion sequences into athlete-specific latent representations manipulable via interpolation or local optimization to generate improved motion guides.
cells.F434: Adjacent — generative latent-space athlete modeling is conceptually similar to GSE's need for personalized, per-player probability adjustments, though this is biomechanics coaching, not win prediction.
cells.G434: Borrow the latent-space interpolation concept to generate what-if player performance trajectories (e.g., toward healthier/prime form) as counterfactual features for injury-return or form-regression modeling.

cells.C435: Model-free Rank Aggregation in the Presence of Rater Heterogeneity: A Maximum Score Approach
cells.D435: Proposes a model-free rank aggregation method for heterogeneous rater preferences, proving near-minimax-optimal consistency via Kendall's tau convergence, applied to sports player rankings and survey aggregation.
cells.E435: A maximum-score estimator aggregates multi-way pairwise comparisons without assuming Bradley-Terry/Plackett-Luce parametric structure, accommodating rater heterogeneity.
cells.F435: Directly relevant — a theoretically grounded alternative to parametric ranking models, applicable to GSE's rating systems, especially for a robust ranking layer independent of one calibrator's assumptions.
cells.G435: Use this model-free rank aggregator as a non-parametric cross-check on GSE's parametric probability models, flagging cases where parametric assumptions driving the failing Brier/ECE diverge from a distribution-free ranking.

cells.C436: Economic Entropy and Sectoral Dynamics: A Thermodynamic Approach to Market Analysis
cells.D436: Applies geometrothermodynamics to Bogotá's sports economy, finding gambling/betting has lower economic entropy (more organized/regulated) than recreational sports, with curvature scalars flagging potential crisis points.
cells.E436: Thermodynamic analogy (entropy, temperature, heat capacity, curvature scalars) is mapped onto monetary flow data to detect structural phase transitions in economic sectors.
cells.F436: Weak stretch — an econophysics macro-analysis of the gambling sector, not predictive modeling; only loosely relevant as market-context background for GSE's betting-market positioning.
cells.G436: Treat this as macro market-structure context — could inform GSE's messaging about how organized/regulated the sports-betting market is when discussing closing-line-value benchmarks.

cells.C437: Talking Tennis: Language Feedback from 3D Biomechanical Action Recognition
cells.D437: Combines CNN-LSTM biomechanical feature extraction (joint angles, kinetic chains) from tennis stroke video with LLMs to generate technically grounded, actionable natural-language coaching feedback.
cells.E437: Extracted biomechanical features are analyzed for relationships to stroke effectiveness/injury risk, then translated into feedback text via an LLM grounded in those features.
cells.F437: Adjacent — directly relevant to GSE's ambitions for automated, explainable content generation, showing a pattern for grounding LLM text output in quantitative features rather than free hallucination.
cells.G437: Apply the quantitative-feature-grounded LLM text pattern to generate pick rationale strictly derived from the prediction engine's actual feature values, reinforcing math-you-can-read and reducing hallucination risk.

cells.C438: LEAML: Label-Efficient Adaptation to Out-of-Distribution Visual Tasks for Multimodal Large Language Models
cells.D438: A label-efficient adaptation framework for multimodal LLMs on out-of-distribution tasks (medical imaging and sports VQA) using pseudo-QA generation from unlabeled data plus targeted neuron updates.
cells.E438: A QA generator regularized by caption distillation creates pseudo-labels from unlabeled images; only task-relevant neurons are fine-tuned for efficient domain adaptation.
cells.F438: Adjacent — a label-efficient domain-adaptation technique broadly relevant if GSE needs to adapt pretrained vision/NLP models to sparse-labeled niche-sport data cheaply.
cells.G438: Use the pseudo-QA-generation-plus-targeted-neuron-update recipe to cheaply adapt a general LLM to GSE's brand-language lint rules using only a small labeled set of banned/approved phrasing examples.

cells.C439: Paving the Way Towards Kinematic Assessment Using Monocular Video: A Preclinical Benchmark of State-of-the-Art Deep-Learning-Based 3D Human Pose Estimators Against Inertial Sensors in Daily Living Activities
cells.D439: Benchmarks monocular-video 3D pose estimators against IMU sensors for daily-activity kinematic assessment, finding MotionAGFormer performs best but trade-offs remain between video- and sensor-based approaches.
cells.E439: Joint angles from deep-learning pose models are compared against OpenSim inverse-kinematics-derived IMU ground truth using RMSE, MAE, correlation, and R2.
cells.F439: Very weak — clinical/biomechanics benchmarking, unrelated to GSE's stats-driven sports prediction product.
cells.G439: No meaningful application beyond distant inspiration if GSE ever validates video-derived player-tracking data against a sensor ground truth.

cells.C440: Expandable Decision-Making States for Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning in Soccer Tactical Analysis
cells.D440: Proposes Expandable Decision-Making States, a semantically enriched multi-agent RL state representation (marking pressure, passing lanes, ball accessibility) for interpretable soccer tactical analysis, outperforming baselines across datasets.
cells.E440: Relational state variables plus action masking align learned agent value functions/policies with human-interpretable tactical concepts instead of raw coordinates.
cells.F440: Directly relevant — an interpretable multi-agent RL feature-representation design directly applicable to enriching GSE's tactical feature space with human-readable concepts.
cells.G440: Incorporate EDMS-style relational features (marking pressure, passing lanes) into GSE's soccer model as interpretable inputs, satisfying math-you-can-read while improving on raw box-score features.

cells.C441: Aging Decline in Basketball Career Trend Prediction Based on Machine Learning and LSTM Model
cells.D441: Uses autoencoder+K-means clustering to classify NBA player career trend types and LSTM to predict individual performance trajectories, generalizing across career-decline patterns.
cells.E441: Unsupervised clustering groups similar career trajectories while a sequential LSTM forecasts future performance from historical game data.
cells.F441: Directly relevant — an age/career-trajectory forecasting technique directly applicable to improving GSE's player-level features and long-horizon forecasting accuracy for NBA picks.
cells.G441: Feed LSTM-predicted age-adjusted performance trajectories as a forward-looking feature into GSE's ensemble, helping correct for aging-curve effects the current MAE-losing model may miss.

cells.C442: Biomechanical-phase based Temporal Segmentation in Sports Videos: a Demonstration on Javelin-Throw
cells.D442: Uses unsupervised structured optimal transport augmenting a graph convolutional network to automatically segment biomechanical phases (approach, drive, throw, recovery) in javelin-throw video without manual labeling.
cells.E442: Structured optimal transport regularizes an attention-based spatio-temporal GCN to detect motion-phase transitions unsupervised, validated against a newly released annotated dataset.
cells.F442: Weak stretch — niche computer-vision biomechanics segmentation, tangential to GSE's stats-based core unless it expands into video-derived athletics features.
cells.G442: Minimal direct fit; the unsupervised phase-segmentation technique could inspire unsupervised regime/phase detection in GSE's own time-series game-state data (e.g., detecting momentum shifts automatically).

cells.C443: 3DPCNet: Pose Canonicalization for Robust Viewpoint-Invariant 3D Kinematic Analysis from Monocular RGB cameras
cells.D443: A pose-canonicalization module rectifies viewpoint-dependent monocular 3D pose estimates into a consistent body-centered frame using a graph-transformer hybrid, cutting rotation error from 20 degrees to 3.4 degrees.
cells.E443: Self-supervised training on synthetically rotated poses teaches a 6D-rotation predictor to align any input skeleton to a canonical reference frame.
cells.F443: Very weak — a computer-vision pose-normalization technique for kinematic analysis, unrelated to GSE's stats/odds-driven product.
cells.G443: No meaningful product fit for GSE's current stack.

cells.C444: Impact of Environmental Factors on LoRa 2.4 GHz Time of Flight Ranging Outdoors
cells.D444: Collects LoRa 2.4GHz time-of-flight ranging data on a sports field to study how temperature/humidity affect outdoor localization accuracy, finding environmental factors significantly degrade meter-level positioning.
cells.E444: A deep neural network models the relationship between environmental conditions and RF ranging error using field-collected calibration data.
cells.F444: Very weak — a wireless-networking/IoT localization study that merely used a sports field as its test location; no connection to GSE's prediction product.
cells.G444: No meaningful product application for GSE.

cells.C445: JointDiff: Bridging Continuous and Discrete in Multi-Agent Trajectory Generation
cells.D445: A diffusion framework (JointDiff) jointly generates continuous multi-agent trajectories and synchronous discrete possession events in soccer/football, with text- and possessor-guided controllable generation, achieving state-of-the-art results.
cells.E445: A unified diffusion process models continuous spatio-temporal motion and discrete event occurrence together via a novel CrossGuid conditioning mechanism for controllable generation.
cells.F445: Directly relevant — joint continuous/discrete generative modeling of player movement and events is a sophisticated technique for synthetic scenario generation, useful for GSE's sparse-data augmentation and ensemble training.
cells.G445: Use JointDiff-style controllable generation to synthesize realistic what-would-happen-if play scenarios for data augmentation where GSE has too few settled picks for the calibration gate.

cells.C446: Modeling Psychological Profiles in Volleyball via Mixed-Type Bayesian Networks
cells.D446: Learns mixed-type Bayesian network structures (latent MMHC) modeling psychological trait relationships in 164 female volleyball players, revealing how skills, confidence, and Big-Five traits interconnect and propagate through scenario analysis.
cells.E446: A hybrid latent-Gaussian-copula and constraint/score-based structure learner returns a single interpretable DAG over ordinal, categorical, and continuous variables.
cells.F446: Directly relevant — a Bayesian network structure-learning method for mixed-type sports data is directly applicable to GSE's probabilistic modeling toolkit, especially for interpretable causal-style feature relationships.
cells.G446: Apply latent MMHC structure learning to discover interpretable relationships among GSE's own heterogeneous features (injury reports, momentum, market odds), feeding structure-aware priors into the CEPT ensemble.

cells.C447: Outlier Detection in Plantar Pressure: Human-Centered Comparison of Statistical Parametric Mapping and Explainable Machine Learning
cells.D447: Compares Statistical Parametric Mapping vs. explainable CNN+SHAP for detecting outliers in plantar-pressure clinical/sports datasets, finding the ML approach more accurate while both are trusted by domain experts.
cells.E447: A CNN classifier explained via SHAP is benchmarked against non-parametric SPM for automated quality-control outlier detection, validated with expert trust surveys.
cells.F447: Directly relevant — a concrete comparison of explainable ML vs. classical statistical methods for anomaly/outlier detection, applicable to GSE's data-pipeline QA and its need for explainable anomaly flags.
cells.G447: Adopt the SHAP-explained CNN QC pattern as GSE's automated data-quality gate for scraped/live odds data, giving human-readable explanations for why a data point was flagged anomalous.

cells.C448: SlotFM: A Motion Foundation Model with Slot Attention for Diverse Downstream Tasks
cells.D448: A wearable-accelerometer foundation model using Time-Frequency Slot Attention generalizes across 16 diverse classification/regression tasks beyond standard activity recognition, outperforming prior self-supervised approaches on 13 of them.
cells.E448: Slot Attention decomposes raw time/frequency accelerometer signals into multiple small task-relevant embeddings, with regularizers preserving fine-grained local and frequency structure.
cells.F448: Weak stretch — a wearable-sensor foundation model unrelated to GSE's odds/stats data, though the multi-slot embedding pattern generalizing across many downstream tasks is architecturally interesting.
cells.G448: Borrow the multi-slot embedding design for GSE's own prediction-engine backbone, letting one shared representation serve multiple downstream markets (win probability, spread, props) instead of separate models per market.

cells.C449: The Impact of the UEFA Women's EURO on Hotel Overnight Stays: Evidence from a Causal Analysis
cells.D449: Uses Synthetic Difference-in-Differences to estimate the 2025 UEFA Women's EURO's causal impact on host-city hotel stays, finding a modest but statistically supported 1.6% increase in main venues.
cells.E449: Synthetic DiD compares host cities to a weighted synthetic control of non-host cities to isolate the event's causal tourism effect.
cells.F449: Adjacent — a rigorous applied causal-inference method (synthetic control) directly relevant to GSE's causal-inference toolkit ambitions (CEPT) and any future event-impact analytics products.
cells.G449: Apply Synthetic DiD to estimate causal effects of roster changes, coaching changes, or rule changes on team performance, feeding validated causal effect sizes into GSE's ensemble as features.

cells.C450: Probing Gender Bias in Multilingual LLMs: A Case Study of Stereotypes in Persian
cells.D450: Introduces a Domain-Specific Gender Skew Index and template-based probing to quantify LLM gender stereotypes across four domains (including sports) in Persian, finding sports shows the most rigid biases.
cells.E450: Template-based probing validated against real-world data computes a quantitative bias metric across LLM outputs by domain and language.
cells.F450: Tangential — a bias-auditing methodology relevant to GSE's NLP style-control/brand-lint enforcement, ensuring AI-generated sports commentary doesn't encode gender bias if localized to other languages.
cells.G450: Adapt the Domain-Specific Gender Skew Index as an automated bias-audit metric within GSE's brand-lint pipeline, screening AI-drafted sports content for skewed language before publication.

cells.C451: Rethinking player evaluation in sports: Goals above expectation and beyond
cells.D451: Develops a double-machine-learning framework giving statistically valid inference for goals-above-expectation-style player metrics, applying it to soccer, basketball shooting, NFL QB passing, and injury-proneness.
cells.E451: Residualized versions of ML-derived performance metrics, motivated by Rao's score test and double ML, correct finite-sample bias to enable valid frequentist inference on flexible nonlinear models.
cells.F451: Highly relevant — directly addresses making flexible ML-derived sports metrics statistically valid and inferentially sound, a core technical fix applicable to GSE's own miscalibrated Brier/ECE scoring pipeline.
cells.G451: Apply the double-ML residualization technique to GSE's own pick-quality metrics, converting flexible-but-biased ML outputs into statistically valid, properly calibrated confidence scores that could help pass the launch gate.

cells.C452: CoachMe: Decoding Sport Elements with a Reference-Based Coaching Instruction Generation Model
cells.D452: CoachMe compares a learner's motion to a reference athlete's motion and generates natural-language coaching feedback, beating GPT-4o on figure skating and boxing critique quality.
cells.E452: A reference-based multimodal model that diffs temporal/physical motion features against an expert reference and converts the delta into explanatory coaching text.
cells.F452: Tangential to GSE's core scoring engine, but the reference-vs-actual diffing pattern parallels how GSE could explain model disagreement or closing-line-value gaps to users.
cells.G452: Repurpose the diff-and-explain architecture to auto-generate 'why the model moved' narratives when GSE picks shift after new odds/injury data lands, feeding the content-automation roadmap.

cells.C453: PersonaX: Multimodal Datasets with LLM-Inferred Behavior Traits
cells.D453: Introduces PersonaX, datasets pairing LLM-inferred behavior traits with facial/biographical data for public figures and 4,181 pro athletes, plus a causal representation learning framework with identifiability guarantees.
cells.E453: Uses LLMs to infer trait scores from text, then applies a novel multimodal causal representation learning (CRL) method with statistical independence tests to relate traits across modalities.
cells.F453: The AthlePersona athlete trait dataset and identifiable CRL framework are a direct, if unconventional, source of athlete-level features and causal-inference tooling relevant to CEPT-style modeling.
cells.G453: Mine AthlePersona-style LLM-inferred athlete traits (composure, leadership) as auxiliary features in the ensemble, testing whether personality signals improve calibration for close-margin games.

cells.C454: Using LLMs for Late Multimodal Sensor Fusion for Activity Recognition
cells.D454: Shows LLMs can zero/one-shot fuse audio and motion time-series to classify 12 household/sports activities without task-specific training, using text descriptions from modality-specific models.
cells.E454: Late fusion via LLM prompting: each modality's classifier outputs are converted to text and an LLM reasons over them jointly to pick the final activity label.
cells.F454: A stretch for GSE's core pick pipeline, but demonstrates LLM-based late fusion of heterogeneous signals, a pattern usable for combining disparate free-data-pipeline sources without joint training.
cells.G454: Use LLM-based late fusion to merge scraped play-by-play text, odds movement, and injury-report signals into a single feature without building a custom joint embedding model, useful when data sources arrive with different schemas.

cells.C455: Measuring football fever through wearable technology: A case study on the German cup final
cells.D455: Analyzes smartwatch heart rate/stress data from 229 fans during the 2025 DFB cup final, showing pronounced physiological arousal beginning hours before kickoff and peaking at kickoff.
cells.E455: Combines wearable biometric time-series with survey data to quantify emotional engagement dynamics around match events versus non-matchday baselines.
cells.F455: Pure fan-psychology research, not model-relevant, but a legitimate stretch angle for GSE's planned social/content and Galaxy Dynasty game layers around fan engagement timing.
cells.G455: Use the finding that fan arousal peaks at kickoff to time push notifications/content drops for the AUGUR game and social content generation for maximum engagement.

cells.C456: Measuring Implicit Spatial Coordination in Teams: Effects on Collective Intelligence and Performance
cells.D456: Studies how spatial specialization and adaptive proximity among 4-person teams in a search-and-rescue task predict performance, finding specialization helps and moderate adaptation is optimal.
cells.E456: Defines and measures exploration diversity, movement specialization, and adaptive spatial proximity metrics from team movement trajectories to explain performance variance.
cells.F456: Not sports-prediction relevant directly, but the team-coordination metrics echo the kind of spatial-tracking features (pitch control, positioning) sports analytics uses to value team play.
cells.G456: Adapt the 'adaptive spatial proximity' metric as a new feature class for team-sport props (e.g., NFL/soccer positioning coherence) that could feed the prediction-engine's per-sport models.

cells.C457: Wireless Low-Latency Synchronization for Body-Worn Multi-Node Systems in Sports
cells.D457: Characterizes Nordic Semiconductor's Enhanced ShockBurst protocol, achieving sub-millisecond device-to-device latency for synchronizing wearable sensor networks, outperforming Bluetooth Low Energy.
cells.E457: Engineering/protocol benchmarking of wireless synchronization for high-frequency (500Hz-1000Hz) biosignal sensor networks used in athlete monitoring.
cells.F457: Hardware/wearables infrastructure, essentially irrelevant to GSE's software-only stats platform; no data ingestion or modeling application.
cells.G457: If GSE ever partners with wearable-data vendors for real-time biometric feeds (fatigue/injury signals), this protocol informs evaluating vendor data-freshness claims rather than something GSE builds.

cells.C458: A fine-grained attention and geometric correspondence model for musculoskeletal risk classification in athletes
cells.D458: ViSK-GAT fuses visual and skeletal-coordinate features via attention and geometric-correspondence modules to classify athlete musculoskeletal injury risk into REBA categories with over 93% accuracy.
cells.E458: Multimodal deep learning combining a Fine-Grained Attention Module for intra-modal refinement and a Multimodal Geometric Correspondence Module for cross-modal image-skeleton alignment.
cells.F458: Injury-risk classification is adjacent to GSE's need for injury-aware feature inputs into picks, but this is a vision/biomechanics model far from the statistical scoring engine's scope.
cells.G458: Long-shot: license or approximate injury-risk scores as a categorical input signal (not visual) feeding the bootstrap-mode confidence cap when key players show elevated musculoskeletal risk.

cells.C459: Predicting Multi-Type Talented Students in Secondary School Using Semi-Supervised Machine Learning
cells.D459: TalentPredictor, a semi-supervised Transformer/LSTM/ANN hybrid, predicts seven talent types (including sport) in secondary students from behavioral records, reaching 0.908 accuracy.
cells.E459: Semi-supervised multimodal neural network that clusters award records into talent categories and learns from limited labeled data plus abundant unlabeled behavioral features.
cells.F459: Not sports-prediction relevant; it's an education talent-ID system where 'sport' is just one of seven output classes, no transferable modeling technique for GSE's pick engine.
cells.G459: The semi-supervised label-scarcity technique could inspire handling GSE's sparse-label problem for minor sports/leagues where settled-pick data is scarce (echoing bootstrap mode's data-sparsity handling).

cells.C460: Hierarchy and ranking in fencing and tennis
cells.D460: Analyzes win-loss networks in fencing and tennis, showing elimination tournaments create strong structural hierarchy but weaker competing hierarchy (more result cycles) than round-robin formats, with rankings predicting outcomes comparably to Elo.
cells.E460: Network-science approach building directed win-loss graphs and measuring structural vs. competing hierarchy to predict match outcomes, benchmarked against official rankings and Elo.
cells.F460: Directly relevant to GSE's core rating/ranking problem: offers an alternative network-hierarchy signal to blend with or validate against Elo-style rankings in the ensemble.
cells.G460: Add a 'cycle density' network feature (how often circular win-loss situations occur in a sport's recent graph) as an uncertainty signal that could feed bootstrap mode's confidence capping for volatile sports.

cells.C461: CVBench: Benchmarking Cross-Video Synergies for Complex Multimodal Reasoning
cells.D461: Introduces CVBench, a 1,000-QA benchmark testing whether multimodal LLMs can reason across multiple videos (including sports clusters), finding even GPT-4o lags far behind human accuracy on causal cross-video reasoning.
cells.E461: Diagnostic benchmark with three reasoning tiers (object association, event association, complex reasoning) evaluated via zero-shot and chain-of-thought prompting on leading MLLMs.
cells.F461: Not directly about prediction/calibration; relevant only as a caution about current MLLM reasoning limits if GSE ever tries video-based scouting or highlight analysis.
cells.G461: Use CVBench's methodology as a template for internally benchmarking GSE's own agents (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) on cross-source reasoning tasks like reconciling conflicting odds feeds.

cells.C462: Beyond Competitive Gaming: How Casual Players Evaluate and Respond to Teammate Performance
cells.D462: An HCI study finds casual co-op gamers (Overcooked 2) evaluate teammates relatively rather than by absolute metrics, and self-reports miss frustration behaviors that observation captures.
cells.E462: Controlled between-subjects experiment manipulating confederate performance, combining behavioral observation, NASA TLX self-report, and interviews.
cells.F462: Not relevant to GSE's prediction engine; it's UX research about casual gaming teammates, unrelated to sports forecasting or calibration.
cells.G462: Tangential inspiration for Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR game design: use relative-comparison performance framing (vs. absolute stats) when showing players their fantasy-team results to boost engagement.

cells.C463: Evaluating Movement Initiation Timing in Ultimate Frisbee via Temporal Counterfactuals
cells.D463: Proposes a counterfactual method that shifts the timing of off-disc player movements in Ultimate Frisbee to quantify how movement-initiation timing affects space-control value, validated on a new tracking dataset.
cells.E463: Generates rule-based temporal counterfactual scenarios and scores them with a pitch-control-style spatial evaluation metric adapted to Ultimate's rules.
cells.F463: A niche-sport analytics method; relevant as a template for counterfactual 'what if timing were different' evaluation, which echoes the kind of what-if reasoning CEPT's e-process framework could formalize.
cells.G463: Apply the temporal-counterfactual framework to backtest GSE's pick-timing: quantify how much closing-line value is lost/gained by publishing a pick earlier or later relative to information arrival.

cells.C464: SPORTSQL: An Interactive System for Real-Time Sports Reasoning and Visualization
cells.D464: SPORTSQL lets users query live Fantasy Premier League data in natural language, translating questions to SQL via LLMs, evaluated on a new 1,700-query benchmark (DSQABENCH).
cells.E464: LLM-based NL-to-SQL pipeline with schema linking and visualization selection over a temporally indexed live sports database.
cells.F464: Directly applicable pattern for a GSE internal or B2B natural-language analytics interface over their Postgres/Prisma pick and odds data, supporting the trust/toolkit and widget roadmap.
cells.G464: Build a 'talk to your picks' internal tool for Jarvis/Hermes agents using this NL-to-SQL approach so non-technical staff can query calibration metrics (Brier/ECE by sport) without writing SQL.

cells.C465: BasketLiDAR: The First LiDAR-Camera Multimodal Dataset for Professional Basketball MOT
cells.D465: Introduces a synchronized LiDAR+multi-camera dataset from professional basketball games and a real-time multi-object tracking framework that improves accuracy and speed over camera-only methods, especially under occlusion.
cells.E465: Fuses LiDAR point clouds with multi-view video for 3D player tracking, using a novel MOT algorithm exploiting LiDAR's precise spatial data.
cells.F465: Pure computer-vision infrastructure for player tracking, outside GSE's stats/odds-driven modeling scope since GSE doesn't operate cameras or LiDAR.
cells.G465: If GSE later licenses tracking-data feeds (rather than building sensors), this paper's occlusion-robust MOT benchmarks help evaluate vendor data quality claims for positional features.

cells.C466: Bridging the Gap: Doubles Badminton Analysis with Singles-Trained Models
cells.D466: Transfers pose-based shot-recognition models trained on singles badminton to doubles by combining contrastive embeddings, custom multi-object tracking, and a Transformer classifier.
cells.E466: Domain-transfer pipeline: ViT-Pose keypoints, ST-GCN contrastive embeddings, custom ID-switch-resistant tracking, and Transformer-based shot classification.
cells.F466: Illustrates a general domain-transfer pattern (train on data-rich variant, transfer to data-poor variant) analogous to GSE's need for per-sport models when some sports/leagues have thin historical data.
cells.G466: Apply the 'train on the data-rich format, transfer to the data-poor format' recipe to bootstrap minor-league or new-sport prediction models from NFL/MLB-trained architectures rather than starting cold.

cells.C467: Neural Rendering for Sensor Adaptation in 3D Object Detection
cells.D467: Introduces CamShift, a simulated dataset showing cross-sensor domain gap between vehicle camera setups degrades 3D object detection, and proposes neural-rendering-based data adaptation to mitigate it.
cells.E467: Neural rendering pipeline transforms training datasets to simulate different camera sensor configurations, improving detector robustness across vehicle types.
cells.F467: Autonomous-vehicle perception research with no sports content ('sport' here means SUVs); essentially irrelevant to GSE's product.
cells.G467: Only a very indirect analogy: the general idea of synthetically adapting data to a new 'sensor' configuration parallels adapting a model trained on one sport's data distribution to a related sport via synthetic augmentation.

cells.C468: TrajSV: A Trajectory-based Model for Sports Video Representations and Applications
cells.D468: TrajSV learns unsupervised video representations from player/ball trajectories extracted from soccer, basketball, and volleyball broadcasts, achieving state-of-the-art on retrieval, action spotting, and captioning.
cells.E468: Trajectory-enhanced Transformer clip encoder plus an encoder-decoder video-level network trained with triple contrastive loss, requiring no supervision labels.
cells.F468: A video-analytics tool for broadcast content, not the statistical/probability modeling GSE needs, but relevant to the planned automated content-generation and B2B widget features.
cells.G468: Use trajectory-based unsupervised representations to auto-generate short highlight clips or explainer visuals tied to specific GSE picks for the social/media content-automation pipeline.

cells.C469: VIFSS: View-Invariant and Figure Skating-Specific Pose Representation Learning for Temporal Action Segmentation
cells.D469: Proposes a view-invariant, sport-specific pose representation (pretrained via contrastive learning) for detecting figure skating jump types and phases, achieving 92%+ F1 with limited fine-tuning data.
cells.E469: Contrastive pre-training on a new 3D figure-skating pose dataset (FS-Jump3D) followed by fine-tuned temporal action segmentation with entry/landing phase annotations.
cells.F469: Computer-vision technique for a niche sport, no direct bearing on GSE's probabilistic/statistical scoring, calibration, or ensemble problems.
cells.G469: Minimal but real thread: the 'pretrain on general motion, fine-tune with limited sport-specific labeled data' recipe mirrors what GSE would need for per-sport probability models with sparse settled-pick history.

cells.C470: Feature Impact Analysis on Top Long-Jump Performances with Quantile Random Forest and Explainable AI Techniques
cells.D470: Uses quantile regression forests plus SHAP/PDP/ICE to identify which biomechanical features (e.g., support-leg knee angle, landing pose) drive top-decile long-jump performance, differentiated by sex.
cells.E470: Quantile Random Forest models elite-tail performance conditional on features, interpreted via SHAP values and partial dependence to isolate key technical drivers.
cells.F470: Directly relevant as a methodology template: quantile regression + SHAP interpretability could be applied to GSE's own feature-importance and calibration-diagnostic work for identifying which inputs drive miscalibration.
cells.G470: Use quantile random forests to model tail outcomes (blowouts/upsets) rather than mean outcomes, since GSE's baseline-beating problem may stem from mean-focused models missing tail behavior that MAE/Brier penalize.

cells.C471: TOTNet: Occlusion-Aware Temporal Tracking for Robust Ball Detection in Sports Videos
cells.D471: TOTNet uses 3D convolutions and visibility-weighted loss to track balls through occlusion in tennis, badminton, and table tennis video, cutting RMSE from 37.3 to 7.19 and improving fully-occluded-frame accuracy from 0.63 to 0.80.
cells.E471: Temporal occlusion-aware tracking network combining 3D conv features, occlusion augmentation during training, and a visibility-weighted loss function.
cells.F471: Pure computer-vision tracking work; not applicable to GSE's odds/stats-driven prediction engine which doesn't ingest raw video.
cells.G471: The 'visibility-weighted loss that degrades gracefully under missing data' concept could inspire a loss-function tweak for GSE's models when input features (e.g., injury reports) are themselves partially missing/occluded.

cells.C472: ELASTIC: Event-Tracking Data Synchronization in Soccer Without Annotated Event Locations
cells.D472: ELASTIC synchronizes manually-recorded soccer event timestamps with tracking data using only tracking-derived features, avoiding error-prone annotated event locations, and outperforms prior synchronizers.
cells.E472: A synchronization framework that detects pass-like event end times and separates major/minor event detection to reduce error cascades between event and tracking data streams.
cells.F472: Directly relevant to GSE's data-pipeline reliability problem: a concrete technique for aligning noisy multi-source sports event/timestamp data, which is exactly the kind of ETL robustness issue GSE's ingestion pipelines face.
cells.G472: Adapt ELASTIC's location-agnostic synchronization logic to reconcile timestamp drift between scraped play-by-play feeds and live odds-feed timestamps, reducing lookahead-bias bugs in the pick pipeline.

cells.C473: Bringing Everyone to the Table: An Experimental Study of LLM-Facilitated Group Decision Making
cells.D473: A 1,475-participant experiment finds an LLM facilitator increases information-sharing in group decisions (choosing a city for a sporting event) but doesn't significantly change final decision quality versus no facilitation.
cells.E473: Pre-registered randomized experiment comparing no facilitation, prompted sharing, human facilitator, and GPT-4o facilitator on a hidden-profile group task, measuring information exchange and outcomes.
cells.F473: HCI/group-decision research, not directly about prediction modeling; the sporting-event task is incidental context rather than substance.
cells.G473: Relevant to GSE's internal agent tooling: informs designing Jarvis/Hermes/Fable as facilitators that surface withheld or under-weighted information during model/ensemble design reviews, not just as autonomous coders.

cells.C474: PP-Motion: Physical-Perceptual Fidelity Evaluation for Human Motion Generation
cells.D474: Introduces a fine-grained, continuous metric for evaluating whether generated human motion is both physically plausible and perceptually convincing, outperforming binary human-labeled metrics.
cells.E474: Physical labeling computes minimal physics-law-respecting corrections to a motion as ground truth; a model trained with Pearson-correlation loss combines physical and perceptual fidelity signals.
cells.F474: Computer-graphics/motion-generation evaluation metric, largely irrelevant to GSE's statistical prediction pipeline.
cells.G474: If GSE's synthetic media/content generation later animates highlight recreations or avatars for Galaxy Dynasty, this fine-grained fidelity metric could QA-check generated motion quality before publishing.

cells.C475: Determining the acceleration field of a rigid body using three accelerometers and one gyroscope, with applications in mild traumatic brain injury
cells.D475: Presents a linear-algebra algorithm to reconstruct a rigid body's full acceleration field from three accelerometers and a gyroscope, validated in soccer heading experiments for brain-injury research.
cells.E475: Solves rigid-body kinematics equations linearly to recover angular and translational acceleration without differentiating noisy gyroscope data or requiring restrictive sensor placement.
cells.F475: Biomechanics/instrumentation engineering with no direct link to GSE's statistical scoring engine or data pipelines.
cells.G475: No strong product angle; at most, a distant inspiration for injury-risk flags (concussion history) as a categorical confidence-dampening input in bootstrap mode for player-prop picks.

cells.C476: Leveraging Minute-by-Minute Soccer Match Event Data to Adjust Team's Offensive Production for Game Context
cells.D476: Uses Generalized Additive Models on minute-by-minute event data across 15 seasons/5 leagues to adjust offensive stats (shots, corners) for score/red-card context, projecting a standardized 'common denominator' scenario.
cells.E476: Count-response GAM with interaction terms for score differential, home/away status, win probability, and game minute, used to normalize raw offensive statistics.
cells.F476: Directly relevant: a context-adjustment methodology for raw sports statistics that could improve GSE's feature engineering, reducing noise in inputs feeding the core prediction model that currently loses to baseline.
cells.G476: Apply the 'common denominator' context-adjustment to normalize GSE's own training features (e.g., garbage-time stats) before backtesting, potentially closing the MAE gap versus the naive baseline.

cells.C477: Forecasting NCAA Basketball Outcomes with Deep Learning: A Comparative Study of LSTM and Transformer Models
