cells.D477: Compares LSTM and Transformer models for NCAA tournament forecasting, finding Transformer+BCE gives best AUC (0.847) while LSTM+Brier loss gives best calibration (Brier 0.159), highlighting an accuracy-calibration tradeoff.
cells.E477: Sequence models trained with either binary cross-entropy or Brier loss, using GLM team-quality metrics, Elo, seed differences, and box-score features as inputs.
cells.F477: Extremely on-target: directly demonstrates that loss-function choice (Brier vs BCE) changes calibration outcomes, exactly the kind of experiment GSE needs to fix its 0.2563 Brier score gate failure.
cells.G477: Run a controlled ablation like this paper's within GSE's own backtest harness — swap the core model's loss function to Brier-optimized training and measure whether calibration improves without sacrificing MAE.

cells.C478: Canoe Paddling Quality Assessment Using Smart Devices: Preliminary Machine Learning Study
cells.D478: Trains classical ML models (Extremely Randomized Trees best, F1=0.95) on smartwatch motion data to classify paddling stroke quality, delivering LLM-generated coaching feedback via a web interface.
cells.E478: Stroke segmentation and feature extraction from wrist-worn IMU data feeding classical classifiers, paired with an LLM that translates predictions into natural-language feedback.
cells.F478: Niche consumer-fitness ML study with no direct connection to sports outcome prediction or calibration; small-sample proof of concept.
cells.G478: The pattern of 'ML classifier output translated into LLM natural-language explanation' is reusable for GSE's content automation, turning model confidence/feature contributions into readable pick rationales.

cells.C479: ThermoCycleNet: Stereo-based Thermogram Labeling for Model Transition to Cycling
cells.D479: Transfers a stereo/multimodal automatic-labeling method for thermal imaging from treadmill running to cycling, showing fine-tuning on small manually-labeled data sets substantially improves segmentation transfer.
cells.E479: Semantic segmentation network trained on automatically-generated labels then fine-tuned with a small manually annotated subset to adapt across exercise modalities.
cells.F479: Sports-medicine thermal imaging pipeline, unrelated to GSE's statistical prediction stack.
cells.G479: The core lesson — auto-label at scale, fine-tune on a small hand-checked subset — is a transferable pattern for validating GSE's own scraped/free data sources against a small manually-verified gold set.

cells.C480: Silent Impact: Tracking Tennis Shots from the Passive Arm
cells.D480: Shows tennis shot detection/classification can be done accurately (88.2% accuracy) using a wrist sensor on the passive (non-dominant) arm instead of the racket arm, improving comfort without sacrificing accuracy.
cells.E480: Neural networks trained on passive-arm IMU data classify six tennis shot types and detect shot events, deployed via smartwatch and mobile app.
cells.F480: Wearable sports-tech UX research, no direct application to GSE's odds/stats prediction engine.
cells.G480: Minimal thread: illustrates that a proxy/indirect signal can substitute for the 'obvious' direct signal — analogous inspiration for finding proxy features (e.g., betting-market movement) when a direct stat (e.g., player fatigue) is unavailable.

cells.C481: From Sharp to Blur: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for 2D Human Pose Estimation Under Extreme Motion Blur Using Event Cameras
cells.D481: Uses event cameras and a student-teacher framework to adapt pose-estimation models from sharp images to motion-blurred conditions without needing labeled blurred-domain data.
cells.E481: Event-based augmentation generates motion-aware blurred training images; a student-teacher setup with mutual uncertainty masking refines pseudo-labels for domain adaptation.
cells.F481: Computer-vision domain-adaptation research with no direct bearing on GSE's statistical/odds-based modeling.
cells.G481: The uncertainty-masking student-teacher pattern for filtering unreliable pseudo-labels is conceptually reusable for filtering noisy scraped data before it enters GSE's training pipeline.

cells.C482: Beyond the Broadcast: Enhancing VR Tennis Broadcasting through Embedded Visualizations and Camera Techniques
cells.D482: Develops a VR tennis broadcast system combining cinematic camera techniques with embedded tactical visualizations, shown in a user study to outperform traditional VR broadcasting for engagement and comprehension.
cells.E482: Reconstructs simulated tennis matches from broadcast video and overlays adaptive camera motion plus dynamic tactical visualizations in a VR viewing system.
cells.F482: Media/broadcast UX research, unrelated to GSE's prediction/calibration engine, though adjacent to eventual B2B content or fan-facing visualization products.
cells.G482: Borrow the 'embedded tactical visualization over reconstructed play' concept for a lightweight web widget that overlays GSE's model reasoning (win-probability shifts) onto match replays for B2B partners.

cells.C483: Convergence Rate of Efficient MCMC with Ancillarity-Sufficiency Interweaving Strategy for Panel Data Models
cells.D483: Provides the first rigorous theoretical justification for the ASIS MCMC technique in Bayesian hierarchical panel models, proving near-optimal geometric convergence for large cross-sectional panels, with sports-data applications noted.
cells.E483: Theoretical convergence analysis interweaving sufficient and ancillary data-augmentation MCMC schemes, validated by Monte Carlo experiments on panel data.
cells.F483: Directly relevant methodological tool: ASIS-accelerated MCMC could speed up Bayesian hierarchical estimation for GSE's per-sport/per-team hierarchical calibration or ensemble models.
cells.G483: Use ASIS-accelerated MCMC to make Bayesian hierarchical per-sport probability models (individually calibrated per sport, as the founder suspects is needed) computationally tractable at GSE's data scale.

cells.C484: DUSTrack: Semi-automated point tracking in ultrasound videos
cells.D484: DUSTrack combines deep learning and optical flow to robustly track arbitrary points in noisy ultrasound video, demonstrated on cardiac, muscle, and ankle tissue motion tracking.
cells.E484: Semi-automated GUI-assisted point-tracking toolkit with a novel optical-flow-based noise filter that preserves rapid motion while suppressing frame-to-frame jitter.
cells.F484: Medical imaging tool, no connection to GSE's sports-prediction stack.
cells.G484: No credible direct product tie; at best, the noise-preserving-signal-while-filtering-jitter filter design is a loose analogy for smoothing noisy live-odds tick data without lagging real market moves.

cells.C485: AthleticsPose: Authentic Sports Motion Dataset on Athletic Field and Evaluation of Monocular 3D Pose Estimation Ability
cells.D485: Introduces a real athletic-field motion dataset from 23 athletes and shows models trained on authentic sports motion reduce 3D pose error by ~75% versus models trained on imitated motion data.
cells.E485: Public 3D pose dataset plus evaluation of a representative pose-estimation model's sensitivity to camera view, subject scale, and motion speed.
cells.F485: Reinforces a general data-science principle relevant to GSE: models trained on imitated/proxy data transfer poorly to real conditions, a caution for any synthetic-data augmentation in the prediction engine.
cells.G485: Use this 'authentic beats imitated data' finding as evidence when deciding whether to invest in scraping more genuine historical game data versus relying on simulated/synthetic backtests to fix the baseline-losing model.

cells.C486: Transforming Football Data into Object-centric Event Logs with Spatial Context Information
cells.D486: Presents a framework converting soccer match data into object-centric event logs enriched with spatial context, enabling process-mining analysis of football matches for the first time.
cells.E486: Transformation pipeline mapping multi-object (players, ball, teams) soccer event data into OCEL format augmented with pitch-location context for process discovery.
cells.F486: Directly relevant to GSE's data-ingestion/ETL layer: a concrete data-modeling pattern for representing multi-entity sports events that could improve pipeline structure and downstream feature extraction.
cells.G486: Adopt object-centric event logs internally so GSE's pipeline can run process-mining diagnostics on its own pick lifecycle (proposed→modeled→published→graded), surfacing bottlenecks or anomalous state transitions.

cells.C487: Posture-Driven Action Intent Inference for Playing style and Fatigue Assessment
cells.D487: Uses posture-based video analysis to infer cricket batters' aggressive vs. defensive shot intent (75%+ F1, 80%+ AUC-ROC), using match statistics as weak supervision.
cells.E487: Computer-vision posture analysis combined with weak supervision from existing game statistics to infer psychological/tactical intent without labeled mental-state data.
cells.F487: The weak-supervision-from-existing-stats trick is a reusable idea for GSE, which could use settled-pick outcomes as weak labels for otherwise unlabeled intermediate model signals.
cells.G487: Apply weak supervision from historical odds movement (as a proxy label for 'market-perceived momentum') to train an intermediate feature detector without needing hand-labeled momentum data.

cells.C488: Women Sport Actions Dataset for Visual Classification Using Small Scale Training Data
cells.D488: Introduces WomenSports, a new image dataset for classifying women's sports actions, and a CNN with channel attention achieving 89.15% top-1 accuracy with small training data.
cells.E488: Channel-attention CNN trained on a newly curated small-scale, diverse action-image dataset for sports action classification.
cells.F488: Vision-classification dataset paper with no bearing on GSE's statistical/probability modeling.
cells.G488: No strong product application beyond general inspiration that small, well-curated datasets can still yield strong performance — a reminder to prioritize data quality over volume when expanding minor-sport coverage.

cells.C489: MoCap-Impute: A Comprehensive Benchmark and Comparative Analysis of Imputation Methods for IMU-based Motion Capture Data
cells.D489: Benchmarks statistical, ML, and deep-learning imputation methods on a new IMU motion-capture dataset with simulated missingness patterns, finding multivariate deep methods (GAIN, Iterative Imputer) cut MAE by up to 50%.
cells.E489: Systematic comparison of imputation techniques across univariate, cross-subject, and cross-kinematic missingness scenarios using controlled MCAR/block/transition-point missingness simulations.
cells.F489: Directly relevant technique for GSE's data pipeline: robust missing-data imputation is exactly what's needed when free/scraped sports data sources have gaps, affecting feature completeness for the prediction engine.
cells.G489: Adopt the paper's benchmarking methodology to systematically choose an imputation strategy for GSE's own gappy scraped data (e.g., missing play-by-play events), rather than ad hoc forward-fill or drop-row handling.

cells.C490: Portable Biomechanics Laboratory: Clinically Accessible Movement Analysis from a Handheld Smartphone
cells.D490: Introduces PBL, a platform that fits biomechanical models to handheld smartphone video, validated against motion capture with sub-3-degree joint-angle error and clinically reliable gait metrics.
cells.E490: Fits parametric biomechanical body models to monocular smartphone video, validated across clinical populations including sports-medicine patients.
cells.F490: Clinical biomechanics tool, no direct relevance to GSE's odds/stats-based prediction engine.
cells.G490: No credible direct product application; at most a distant idea for a future consumer-facing 'form checker' feature unrelated to GSE's core pick-prediction business.

cells.C491: Enhancing Sports Strategy with Video Analytics and Data Mining: Automated Video-Based Analytics Framework for Tennis Doubles
cells.D491: Builds an automated annotation and ML framework for tennis doubles video, showing CNN-based transfer learning substantially outperforms pose-based methods for predicting shot type, positioning, and formation.
cells.E491: Combines GroundingDINO player localization and YOLO-Pose estimation with CNN transfer-learning classifiers for doubles-tennis tactical analysis.
cells.F491: Video-analytics tooling for tactical prediction; only loosely relevant as a demonstration that transfer-learned CNNs can outperform pose-only features for tactical prediction tasks.
cells.G491: Not directly applicable to GSE's stats pipeline, but the finding that contextual/visual features beat pose-only features supports prioritizing richer contextual odds/market features over minimal structured stats in the ensemble.

cells.C492: Enhancing Sports Strategy with Video Analytics and Data Mining: Assessing the effectiveness of Multimodal LLMs in tennis video analysis
cells.D492: Evaluates multimodal LLMs' ability to classify and sequence tennis rally actions, finding gaps in event-sequence understanding and testing fine-tuning and hybrid approaches with traditional models to close them.
cells.E492: Benchmarks MLLMs on tennis action classification/sequencing and explores training methods plus ensembling with traditional CV models to improve performance.
cells.F492: Not directly relevant to GSE's statistical scoring engine; a video-understanding benchmark rather than a probability/calibration methodology.
cells.G492: The hybrid 'MLLM + traditional model ensemble' pattern for closing MLLM gaps parallels how GSE could combine CEPT-based e-process signals with conventional ML in its ensemble to shore up individual model weaknesses.

cells.C493: USAD: End-to-End Human Activity Recognition via Diffusion Model with Spatiotemporal Attention
cells.D493: USAD uses a diffusion model for data augmentation plus a multi-branch spatiotemporal attention network to improve human activity recognition, achieving strong accuracy on public benchmarks with lightweight deployment.
cells.E493: Unsupervised statistics-guided diffusion augmentation combined with multi-scale convolutional branches, temporal/spatial attention, and adaptive multi-loss fusion.
cells.F493: General HAR sensor-classification architecture, adjacent to but not squarely within GSE's odds/stats prediction domain (no sports outcome modeling).
cells.G493: The diffusion-based data augmentation technique for rare/imbalanced classes could inspire synthetic augmentation for GSE's rare event classes (e.g., upsets) where settled-pick history is thin, aiding calibration in the tails.

cells.C494: Physics-informed Ground Reaction Dynamics from Human Motion Capture
cells.D494: Estimates ground reaction forces directly from motion capture (without force plates) using Euler integration and PD control as physics constraints, outperforming baselines on the GroundLink dataset.
cells.E494: Physics-informed learning model where simulated reactive forces from rigid-body dynamics inform and constrain a deep model estimating ground reaction forces.
cells.F494: Biomechanics simulation technique; the physics-informed-constraint idea is conceptually close to CEPT's likelihood-ratio e-process approach of constraining model outputs with theoretical structure rather than pure black-box fitting.
cells.G494: Borrow the 'physics-as-constraint' pattern to build a domain-knowledge-informed regularizer for GSE's prediction models (e.g., enforcing win-probability monotonicity in score differential) to improve calibration without more data.

cells.C495: VirtualFencer: Generating Fencing Bouts based on Strategies Extracted from In-the-Wild Videos
cells.D495: VirtualFencer extracts 3D fencing motion and two-player strategy from unlabeled in-the-wild video and generates realistic fencing behavior, including self-play and interactive play against real fencers.
cells.E495: Unsupervised extraction of motion and strategic policy from video, used to drive a data-driven generative agent capable of self-play and human interaction.
cells.F495: Motion-generation/game-AI research, not directly applicable to GSE's statistical prediction pipeline, though conceptually related to strategic agent modeling.
cells.G495: The self-play strategy-extraction concept could inspire a simulation module for the Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR game, generating realistic opposing-team AI strategies learned from real historical game data.

cells.C496: Ranking dynamics in movies and music
cells.D496: Introduces system-level indices to quantify how ranking lists (Netflix, Spotify charts) change composition over time, finding new releases drive most turnover and top ranks correlate with list lifetime.
cells.E496: Defines temporal ranking-trajectory metrics analyzing compositional churn and individual item rank dynamics across streaming charts, referencing sports rankings as a comparable domain.
cells.F496: Ranking-dynamics methodology is conceptually transferable to sports power-rankings/Elo evolution, though the paper's actual domain (streaming charts) is not sports.
cells.G496: Apply the compositional-churn indices to GSE's own team/player power rankings to detect when the ranking system is unstable or overly sensitive to recent news, informing ensemble weighting decisions.

cells.C497: FedFitTech: A Baseline in Federated Learning for Fitness Tracking
cells.D497: Presents an open-source federated learning baseline for fitness-activity recognition on wearables, reducing communication by 13% via client-side early stopping while maintaining recognition performance.
cells.E497: Federated learning framework (built on Flower) that trains fitness-activity models across decentralized wearable devices without centralizing raw sensor data.
cells.F497: Not directly relevant to GSE's centralized stats/odds pipeline, since GSE doesn't operate consumer wearables or need privacy-preserving federated training.
cells.G497: If GSE ever builds a consumer app collecting user prediction behavior, federated learning could let them personalize confidence/bootstrap-mode thresholds per user without centralizing sensitive behavioral data.

cells.C498: Quantifying Flow State Dynamics: A Prefrontal Cortex EEG-Based Model Validation Study
cells.D498: Validates a proprietary Flow State Index using prefrontal-cortex EEG correlated with athletes' subjective flow-state reports, primarily in golf but tested across other sports.
cells.E498: Combines portable EEG measurement with a predictive Flow State Index model and self-report questionnaires to validate the neural correlates of athletic flow.
cells.F498: Sports psychology/neuroscience, unrelated to GSE's odds/stats-driven prediction pipeline or calibration problem.
cells.G498: A distant stretch: 'flow state' as a psychological construct could be a narrative angle for content generation (athlete performance storylines) but has no direct modeling application.

cells.C499: SSPINNpose: A Self-Supervised PINN for Inertial Pose and Dynamics Estimation
cells.D499: SSPINNpose estimates joint kinematics and kinetics from IMU data without ground-truth labels, using a physics model to generate virtual training targets, achieving real-time performance at low latency.
cells.E499: Self-supervised physics-informed neural network where a body-dynamics physics model substitutes for motion-capture ground truth during training.
cells.F499: A strong methodological analogy for GSE: self-supervision using a physics/domain model instead of labeled ground truth mirrors how CEPT's e-process theory could substitute for scarce settled-pick labels in calibration.
cells.G499: Explore a 'self-supervised via domain constraints' approach for GSE's calibration model, using known probabilistic consistency constraints (e.g., probabilities summing to 1 across markets) as a training signal when labeled settled picks are scarce.

cells.C500: Time-Varying Home Field Advantage in Football: Learning from a Non-Stationary Causal Process
cells.D500: Proposes DYNAMO, a causal discovery method for non-stationary processes, revealing time-varying, team-specific home-field advantage driven by referee bias in EPL data, and shows it improves goal prediction accuracy over existing methods.
cells.E500: Local M-estimator-based causal discovery that learns time-varying causal structures without stationarity assumptions, with theoretical identifiability guarantees.
cells.F500: Highly relevant: a causal-discovery method directly applied to soccer with proven goal-prediction accuracy gains — squarely in the causal-inference space the founder's CEPT theory wants to leverage for the prediction engine.
cells.G500: Evaluate whether DYNAMO-style non-stationary causal discovery on GSE's own settled-pick data uncovers hidden time-varying biases (e.g., changing referee/venue effects) that could explain part of the current baseline-losing gap.

cells.C501: Large Language Models for Toxic Language Detection in Low-Resource Balkan Languages
cells.D501: Evaluates four LLMs on detecting toxic comments in Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian across topics including sports, finding context-augmented prompting and Gemini in context mode perform best (F1 0.82).
cells.E501: Zero-shot vs. context-augmented LLM prompting compared on a manually labeled multilingual toxic-comment dataset, measuring precision, recall, and false-positive rates.
cells.F501: Sports content is just one topic category in a toxicity-detection dataset; no direct connection to GSE's prediction/calibration engine, though marginally relevant to social/comment moderation if GSE builds community features.
cells.G501: The context-augmented prompting technique for improving classifier recall could be reused for GSE's own brand-language lint rule enforcement, catching subtle 'AI-powered' phrasing violations that simple keyword filters miss.

cells.C502: Question Answering under Temporal Conflict: Evaluating and Organizing Evolving Knowledge with LLMs
cells.D502: Shows LLMs struggle to reconcile conflicting/outdated facts (e.g., sports biographies where 'current team' changes yearly) and proposes an agentic framework building structured external memory to outperform ICL/RAG baselines.
cells.E502: Introduces temporal benchmarks (Temporal Wiki, Unified Clark) and a lightweight agent that incrementally builds structured, timestamped external memory for temporally-filtered retrieval without retraining.
cells.F502: Directly relevant to GSE's Intelligence Graph ambitions: a concrete technique for keeping typed knowledge primitives (player-team, injury status) temporally consistent as facts evolve during a season.
cells.G502: Adopt this agentic temporal-memory framework as the backbone of GSE's planned Intelligence Graph, ensuring facts like 'current roster' or 'active injury' stay correctly time-scoped rather than stale in LLM context.

cells.C503: Analysis of points outcome in ATP Grand Slam Tennis using big data and machine learning
cells.D503: Models point-level outcomes in ATP Grand Slam tennis matches using logistic regression, Random Forest, AdaBoost, and XGBoost, finding only marginal improvement over a simple average baseline given available public data.
cells.E503: Trains classical ML classifiers on historical rally/point data plus player rankings to predict point winners, comparing against an average-based statistical baseline.
cells.F503: Highly relevant cautionary case study: shows that with limited public data, sophisticated ML barely beats a naive baseline — directly parallel to GSE's own MAE 5.31 vs 4.91 baseline-losing problem.
cells.G503: Use this paper's negative result as a diagnostic checklist: audit whether GSE's baseline-losing model suffers the same root cause (data granularity/quality ceiling) rather than assuming the fix is purely architectural.

cells.C504: Where Is The Ball: 3D Ball Trajectory Estimation From 2D Monocular Tracking
cells.D504: An LSTM-based pipeline reconstructs 3D ball trajectories from single-camera 2D tracking using a camera-independent canonical representation, achieving state-of-the-art results trained only on synthetic data.
cells.E504: Sequence model with intermediate representations enforcing reprojection consistency and view-invariance, trained entirely on simulated data yet generalizing to real footage.
cells.F504: Computer-vision trajectory reconstruction, not applicable to GSE's odds-driven statistical pipeline which has no video ingestion.
cells.G504: The core lesson — train entirely on well-designed synthetic data and generalize to reality — supports using synthetic backtests to stress-test GSE's ensemble under rare scenarios missing from real settled-pick history.

cells.C505: Gen4D: Synthesizing Humans and Scenes in the Wild
cells.D505: Gen4D is an automated pipeline generating diverse, photorealistic 4D human animations via diffusion-based Gaussian splatting, used to build SportPAL, a synthetic dataset spanning baseball, ice hockey, and soccer.
cells.E505: Combines expert-driven motion encoding, prompt-guided avatar generation, and human-aware background synthesis to produce synthetic human-sports video data without manual 3D modeling.
cells.F505: Synthetic media generation for sports scenes directly relates to GSE's planned automated content-generation ambitions, even though it's a vision/graphics tool rather than a stats method.
cells.G505: Use Gen4D-style synthetic athlete animation to generate branded, non-copyrighted highlight-style visuals for GSE's social content pipeline, sidestepping licensing issues with real broadcast footage.

cells.C506: TextVidBench: A Benchmark for Long Video Scene Text Understanding
cells.D506: Introduces the first long-video (3+ minute) text-understanding benchmark spanning categories including sports, with a three-stage evaluation framework and techniques improving MLLM performance on scene-text tasks.
cells.E506: Benchmark with 5,000+ QA pairs plus proposed improvements (IT-Rope temporal mechanism, non-uniform positional encoding, lightweight fine-tuning) for long-video comprehension.
cells.F506: A video-understanding benchmark where sports is one of nine categories; no direct connection to GSE's statistical prediction or calibration work.
cells.G506: If GSE automates scraping of broadcast graphics/on-screen stats via video, this benchmark's scene-text techniques could improve extraction accuracy from long game broadcasts as an alternative data source.

cells.C507: EdgeVidSum: Real-Time Personalized Video Summarization at the Edge
cells.D507: EdgeVidSum generates personalized fast-forward video summaries of long-form content (including sports events) locally on edge devices like Jetson Nano, preserving privacy while cutting computation.
cells.E507: Thumbnail-container-based hierarchical analysis with a lightweight 2D CNN identifying user-preferred content, avoiding frame-by-frame processing.
cells.F507: Edge video summarization technology, not applicable to GSE's server-side statistical prediction pipeline.
cells.G507: Conceptually reusable for a future mobile GSE app that generates personalized 'why this pick' summary clips on-device for privacy-conscious users, rather than server-rendered content.

cells.C508: TestAgent: An Adaptive and Intelligent Expert for Human Assessment
cells.D508: TestAgent is an LLM-powered adaptive testing agent applied across education, healthcare, sports, and sociology domains, achieving accurate assessments with 20% fewer questions than prior adaptive-testing baselines.
cells.E508: LLM agent dynamically selects personalized assessment questions, interprets open-ended responses, and detects anomalies through conversational interaction rather than mechanized item selection.
cells.F508: Adaptive-testing methodology is tangential to GSE's prediction engine but conceptually related to efficient information-gathering, which parallels efficiently querying sparse data sources under bootstrap mode.
cells.G508: Adapt the adaptive-testing logic to build a smarter data-collection agent that decides which additional data points (injury reports, weather) are most informative to fetch next, reducing scraping load while maximizing model information gain.

cells.C509: Towards Scalable Video Anomaly Retrieval: A Synthetic Video-Text Benchmark
cells.D509: SVTA is a large-scale synthetic video-text dataset (41K videos, 68 anomaly types) generated via LLM-guided video generation, created to overcome privacy and data-scarcity limits in real-world anomaly retrieval.
cells.E509: LLM-generated captions guide a video generative model to synthesize diverse anomaly scenarios, avoiding real-world privacy risks while covering long-tail events.
cells.F509: Video anomaly detection for public safety, not directly relevant to GSE's statistical prediction domain, though anomaly-detection concepts generally apply to data pipeline QA.
cells.G509: The synthetic-data-for-rare-events strategy could be adapted (in non-video form) to generate synthetic rare game scenarios (e.g., unusual blowouts, overtime patterns) to stress-test GSE's calibration on the sparse tail of outcomes.

cells.C510: Spending Behavior and Economic Impacts of Urban Digital Consumption Vouchers
cells.D510: Evaluates Taipei's digital consumption voucher program, finding sports vouchers mostly substitute existing spending while accommodation vouchers induce genuinely new consumption.
cells.E510: Regional input-output modeling combined with user-level survey data to estimate expenditure substitution, induced consumption, and fiscal multipliers by voucher category.
cells.F510: Economic policy evaluation with 'sports vouchers' as one spending category; no connection to GSE's prediction engine or sports analytics methodology.
cells.G510: No credible product application; at most a loose analogy that GSE should be cautious that promotional credits/free-pick incentives may substitute rather than add incremental engagement, mirroring the voucher substitution effect.

cells.C511: Agent-X: Evaluating Deep Multimodal Reasoning in Vision-Centric Agentic Tasks
cells.D511: Agent-X is a 828-task benchmark for multi-step vision-centric agentic reasoning across six domains including sports, finding even top models like GPT-4/Gemini/Qwen succeed on fewer than 50% of full task chains.
cells.E511: Fine-grained step-level evaluation framework assessing both stepwise reasoning correctness and tool-use effectiveness across multimodal agentic tasks.
cells.F511: Relevant to GSE's internal agentic tooling (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable): a benchmark methodology for rigorously evaluating multi-step agent reasoning quality, not just final-answer accuracy.
cells.G511: Adopt Agent-X's step-level evaluation framework to audit GSE's own autonomous coding/research agents, scoring each reasoning step's correctness rather than only whether the final PR/output looks right.

cells.C512: Paired comparison models with strength-dependent ties and order effects
cells.D512: Extends Bradley-Terry-style paired comparison models so tie probability and order (e.g., home-field) effects both scale with competitor strength, fitting chess tournament data better than standard models.
cells.E512: Novel parametric paired-comparison model allowing tie probability and order effects to vary with the combined strength of the two competitors, fit via maximum likelihood to tournament outcomes.
cells.F512: Directly relevant to GSE's core rating engine: a refined Bradley-Terry/Elo-family model that could improve GSE's win-probability estimates, particularly for sports with meaningful tie/draw outcomes (soccer, MLS).
cells.G512: Swap in this strength-dependent tie/order-effect model as an alternative or component of GSE's ensemble for draw-prone sports, potentially reducing calibration error in tie-heavy leagues where standard Elo underperforms.

cells.C513: Boosting Automatic Exercise Evaluation Through Musculoskeletal Simulation-Based IMU Data Augmentation
cells.D513: Generates synthetic IMU training data via musculoskeletal simulation with anatomically plausible kinematic constraints, improving classification accuracy and generalization for physiotherapy exercise evaluation.
cells.E513: Simulation-based data augmentation combining inverse-kinematic parameter modification with knowledge-based automatic labeling to expand limited labeled datasets.
cells.F513: Not directly relevant to GSE's stats-based prediction engine; it's a wearable-sensor exercise-evaluation method, though the augmentation-for-scarce-labels pattern is broadly reusable.
cells.G513: The domain-constrained synthetic augmentation idea could inspire generating physically/statistically plausible synthetic settled-pick outcomes to enlarge GSE's ~1164-pick calibration training set for sparse sports/markets.

cells.C514: Learning coordinated badminton skills for legged manipulators
cells.D514: Trains a legged mobile robot via reinforcement learning to play badminton against humans, coordinating perception, locomotion, and arm-swing control using a shuttlecock prediction model and noise-aware perception.
cells.E514: Unified RL policy across all robot degrees of freedom, informed by a real-world camera noise model and constrained RL for robust motion control, validated with system identification.
cells.F514: Robotics/RL research entirely outside GSE's statistical prediction and data-pipeline scope; no meaningful connection.
cells.G514: No credible direct application; at most, the constrained-RL-for-robustness idea is a distant conceptual parallel to constraining GSE's models with domain rules (e.g., probability bounds) during training.

cells.D515: Assigns hypothetical energy levels to outcomes using a Boltzmann-distribution framework to derive improved win probabilities from betting odds, which outperform market-implied probabilities when used in Kelly criterion sports betting on 5 EPL seasons.
cells.E515: Maps betting-market outcomes to an energy-based probability transformation inspired by statistical mechanics, then evaluates it via realized Kelly-criterion betting returns.
cells.F515: Extremely on-target: directly proposes an alternative probability-derivation method that beats market-implied odds on closing-line-value-adjacent metrics (Kelly performance) — exactly GSE's calibration and CLV problem space.
cells.G515: Backtest the Boltzmann-informed probability transform as an additional ensemble member or de-vigging technique for GSE's odds-derived implied probabilities, potentially improving both Brier score and CLV simultaneously.

cells.C516: LifeIR at the NTCIR-18 Lifelog-6 Task
cells.D516: Proposes a multi-stage retrieval pipeline (filtering, query rewriting, event-based candidate extension, MLLM reranking) for searching personal lifelog images from wearables like sports watches and GoPros.
cells.E516: Multi-stage image retrieval system combining blur filtering, LLM query rewriting, temporal candidate extension, and multimodal LLM reranking for text-to-image lifelog search.
cells.F516: Personal lifelog retrieval, essentially unrelated to GSE's sports-outcome prediction and calibration work; sports watches are only the data source, not the analytical focus.
cells.G516: No meaningful product tie for GSE's core business; at most, the multi-stage retrieval pipeline pattern (filter, rewrite, extend, rerank) is generically reusable for any internal search tool over GSE's own documentation/data corpus.

cells.C517: SoccerChat: Integrating Multimodal Data for Enhanced Soccer Game Understanding
cells.D517: SoccerChat is a multimodal conversational AI fine-tuned on SoccerNet video plus ASR transcripts, benchmarked on action classification and referee decision-making with competitive accuracy.
cells.E517: Fine-tunes a video-language model on instruction-formatted soccer data enriched with jersey-color annotations and speech transcripts for conversational match understanding.
cells.F517: A conversational sports-video AI system relevant to GSE's B2B widget and content ambitions, though it doesn't touch the core statistical calibration/prediction problem.
cells.G517: Adapt the fine-tuning recipe (domain instruction data from structured match data + ASR) to build a GSE-branded conversational assistant that explains picks and stats to users in natural language, reinforcing the 'math you can read' positioning.

cells.C518: Velocity Completion Task and Method for Event-based Player Positional Data in Soccer
cells.D518: Proposes a neural method to infer missing player velocities from sparse event-based positional soccer data, outperforming rule-based approaches and improving downstream space-evaluation metrics.
cells.E518: Graph-neural-network-based velocity completion exploiting temporal dependencies and player-to-player/player-to-ball interaction structure from event data alone.
cells.F518: A directly relevant data-completion technique for GSE's pipeline, which likely deals with sparse event-based (rather than full tracking) data where derived features like velocity/momentum are unavailable.
cells.G518: Apply a similar graph-neural velocity/momentum-completion approach to GSE's play-by-play event data to derive pseudo-continuous momentum features without needing costly tracking-data feeds.

cells.C519: AutoData: A Multi-Agent System for Open Web Data Collection
cells.D519: AutoData is a multi-agent system that automatically collects web datasets from a single natural-language instruction, using a hypergraph-coordinated agent architecture and a new benchmark spanning academic, finance, and sports domains.
cells.E519: Multi-agent architecture with a central task manager coordinating research/development agent squads via an oriented message hypergraph, plus a hypergraph cache to reduce LLM token costs.
cells.F519: Directly relevant to GSE's data-ingestion pipeline: an automated, low-effort multi-agent web scraping system explicitly benchmarked on sports data collection, addressing scraping robustness and scalability.
cells.G519: Deploy AutoData's multi-agent, natural-language-instructed scraping architecture as a template for GSE's own agents (Jarvis/Hermes) to autonomously add new free data sources when Pro-Football-Reference-style sites change structure.

cells.C520: Space evaluation at the starting point of soccer transitions
cells.D520: Proposes OBPV, extending scoring-probability-based space evaluation to cover the entire pitch (not just near-goal areas), revealing how teams exploit space at the start of possession transitions.
cells.E520: Combines a field value model covering the whole pitch with a kernel-density-estimated transition model of pass distributions to score positional value beyond scoring-opportunity zones.
cells.F520: A sports-analytics spatial-value methodology relevant as inspiration for feature engineering, though it's soccer-tracking-data specific and GSE may not have full tracking data access.
cells.G520: If GSE later licenses soccer tracking data, adapt OBPV-style whole-pitch space valuation as a novel predictive feature for MLS picks, differentiating GSE's soccer models from odds-only competitors.

cells.C521: Domain Adaptation of VLM for Soccer Video Understanding
cells.D521: Fine-tunes an open-source vision-language model on soccer-specific instruction data via curriculum learning, boosting soccer VQA by 37.5% relatively and action classification accuracy from 11.8% to 63.5%.
cells.E521: Curriculum fine-tuning (concepts first, then QA tasks) of a general VLM on 20K curated soccer video clips with LLM-generated instruction data.
cells.F521: Domain-adaptation recipe for building sport-specific AI tools, relevant to GSE's internal tooling and content generation but not to the core probabilistic prediction engine.
cells.G521: Use the curriculum fine-tuning recipe to build an internal soccer-domain assistant for GSE's data/content teams that understands match footage well enough to auto-caption or tag scraped highlight clips.

cells.C522: Framing Causal Questions in Sports Analytics: A Tutorial on Estimand Choice Illustrated Through Crossing in Soccer
cells.D522: A tutorial using propensity score matching on 2019 Chinese Super League data to show when ATE and ATT estimands for a soccer action (crossing) diverge, illustrated with real data and constructed low-overlap simulations.
cells.E522: Propensity score matching estimating causal effects of an in-game action, with simulation scenarios engineered to show when treatment-effect estimands coincide versus diverge under confounding/overlap conditions.
cells.F522: Extremely relevant: a direct, practical tutorial on rigorous causal-effect estimation in sports analytics — exactly the estimand-choice rigor GSE's CEPT-based causal framework needs to get right before deploying causal features.
cells.G522: Use this tutorial's estimand-choice framework as a checklist when GSE's engineers apply CEPT's e-process/causal methods to specific in-game actions, avoiding the ATE/ATT confusion that could silently bias pick features.

cells.C523: An Improved Algorithm for a Bipartite Traveling Tournament in Interleague Sports Scheduling
cells.D523: Proposes a (3/2+ε)-approximation algorithm for the bipartite traveling tournament problem, improving prior approximation guarantees for interleague sports scheduling that minimizes total team travel distance.
cells.E523: Combinatorial optimization algorithm with a proven approximation ratio for scheduling interleague matches under travel-distance minimization constraints.
cells.F523: Sports scheduling optimization is a different problem domain (logistics, not prediction), with no direct bearing on GSE's calibration, forecasting, or data pipeline issues.
cells.G523: No strong direct application, but the scheduling-optimization angle could inform a future B2B feature offering optimized fantasy-league or betting-market scheduling recommendations to partners.

cells.C524: Debiased inference in error-in-variable problems with non-Gaussian measurement error
cells.D524: Develops a hypercomplex-number-based method to reduce bias in regression and density estimation when covariates are measured with non-Gaussian error, demonstrated in a sports analytics application.
cells.E524: Uses hypercomplex number algebra to correct naive parameter estimates that ignore non-Gaussian measurement error in error-prone covariates, validated via simulation and a real sports dataset.
cells.F524: Directly relevant methodologically: GSE's scraped/free-data features likely have non-Gaussian measurement noise, and this debiasing technique could reduce systematic bias currently degrading the core model's MAE.
cells.G524: Apply this debiasing correction to noisy scraped input features (e.g., imprecise play-by-play-derived stats) before they enter the prediction model, potentially closing part of the gap versus the naive baseline.

cells.C525: Relative Advantage: Quantifying Performance in Noisy Competitive Settings
cells.D525: Develops a mathematical framework showing relative (differential) performance metrics outperform absolute metrics by canceling shared environmental noise, validated on rugby data with up to 28% better classification accuracy.
cells.E525: Signal-to-noise-ratio analysis formalizing when relativized metrics beat absolute metrics, with theoretical bounds and simulation plus real-world rugby validation.
cells.F525: Directly relevant feature-engineering principle for GSE: suggests using opponent-relative or context-relative statistics rather than raw absolute stats as model inputs, which could reduce noise contributing to the baseline-losing MAE problem.
cells.G525: Systematically re-engineer GSE's feature set to use relativized (vs. absolute) team/player metrics per the paper's SNR framework, and A/B test whether this alone narrows the 5.31 vs 4.91 MAE gap against the naive baseline.

cells.C526: FSBench: A Figure Skating Benchmark for Advancing Artistic Sports Understanding
cells.D526: Introduces FSBench, a comprehensive figure skating benchmark with technical and artistic QA/commentary tasks, revealing existing multimodal models significantly underperform on artistic sports understanding.
cells.E526: Multi-task benchmark (FSBench-Text and FSBench-Motion) covering technical analysis and performance commentary, exposing model gaps via multiple-choice and QA evaluation.
cells.F526: Niche sport-specific vision benchmark with no connection to GSE's odds/stats-based prediction and calibration work.
cells.G526: No direct product tie for GSE's current sports (NFL/MLB/MLS); the benchmark's approach could inform how GSE builds internal QA benchmarks to test its own agents' domain understanding before deployment.

cells.C527: Enhancing Tennis Training with Real-Time Swing Data Visualisation in Immersive Virtual Reality
cells.D527: A VR tennis training system with a wearable sensor shows real-time swing-metric visualization improves swing consistency and player engagement in a 10-participant study.
cells.E527: Wearable motion-sensor data streamed into a VR overlay providing real-time swing speed/power feedback during simulated play.
cells.F527: Consumer sports-training UX research, unrelated to GSE's statistical prediction engine or data pipeline.
cells.G527: No credible direct application to GSE's core business beyond general inspiration that real-time visual feedback boosts engagement, relevant only loosely to UI design for GSE's live-pick dashboards.

cells.D528: Reconstructs precise 3D table tennis ball trajectories including spin from single-camera broadcast footage, using physics-based bounce-state estimation without needing pose or racket tracking.
cells.E528: Minimizes reprojection error using ball-flight physics to infer bounce states and spin, combined with automated camera calibration and adapted 3D pose estimation for player tracking.
cells.F528: Computer-vision sports-analysis tool for a niche sport, outside GSE's odds/stats prediction and calibration scope.
cells.G528: No strong direct application; the physics-constrained-inference pattern (using known physical dynamics to disambiguate incomplete visual observations) loosely parallels using domain physics/rules to constrain GSE's probability models.

cells.C529: Evaluation of the phi-3-mini SLM for identification of texts related to medicine, health, and sports injuries
cells.D529: Tests Microsoft's phi-3-mini small language model against 7 human evaluators for scoring topic-relatedness of medicine/health and sports-injury news headlines, finding only low-moderate correlation with human judgment.
cells.E529: Compares SLM-generated topic-relatedness scores to human ratings across ~2,200 filtered text samples, assessing real-world labeling reliability versus benchmark performance.
cells.F529: Directly relevant caution for GSE's content/data pipelines: shows small/cheap LLMs may be unreliable for automatically labeling injury-related text, a risk if GSE uses SLMs to tag scraped injury reports.
cells.G529: Use this paper's human-correlation evaluation methodology to audit whichever LLM GSE uses to auto-tag scraped injury/news text for its feature pipeline, before trusting those labels as model inputs.

cells.C530: Action Valuation in Sports: A Survey
cells.D530: A comprehensive survey introducing a nine-dimension taxonomy of Action Valuation methods across sports, covering data types, methodologies, evaluation techniques, and applications, identifying research gaps.
cells.E530: Systematic literature review and taxonomy synthesizing data-driven approaches for scoring individual in-game actions' contribution to outcomes across multiple sports.
cells.F530: Highly relevant reference work for GSE: directly maps the landscape of action-valuation methods (the core problem of scoring plays/picks) that GSE's prediction-engine team should be benchmarking against.
cells.G530: Use this survey's nine-dimension taxonomy as a structured audit checklist to evaluate whether GSE's current prediction-engine methodology has blind spots (e.g., missing evaluation techniques) relative to the broader field's best practices.

cells.D531: Proposes a joint optimization framework for electric superbike powertrains (force distribution, gearing, motor/battery sizing) that cuts energy consumption up to 22.36% on high-performance driving cycles.
cells.E531: Combines a scalable electric-motor energy-consumption model with propulsive force-blending strategy analysis under vehicle dynamics and adherence constraints.
cells.F531: Automotive/vehicle engineering with 'Sport' referring to a driving cycle mode, entirely unrelated to GSE's sports-prediction product.
cells.G531: No credible application to GSE's business; effectively irrelevant beyond the incidental word 'sport' in the paper's terminology.

cells.C532: Strategies for decentralised UAV-based collisions monitoring in rugby
cells.D532: Simulates a decentralized UAV fleet using custom collision-detection algorithms to capture rugby collision events for traumatic brain injury research, outperforming traditional TV-coverage strategies.
cells.E532: Multi-agent UAV coordination simulated in NetLogo, comparing custom collision-detection-driven camera positioning against standard broadcast coverage strategies.
cells.F532: Drone/robotics infrastructure for injury monitoring, unrelated to GSE's software-only statistical prediction and data pipeline business.
cells.G532: No credible direct application; at most, the decentralized-multi-agent-coordination-for-event-capture concept is a loose structural analogy to how GSE's own distributed agents might prioritize monitoring high-value live game events.

cells.C533: Investigating Experiential Effects in Online Chess using a Hierarchical Bayesian Analysis
cells.D533: Uses hierarchical Bayesian regression on large-scale online chess data to test for winner-loser 'hot hand' effects, finding little consistent evidence across players but some individual-level effects, with careful model validation.
cells.E533: Hierarchical Bayesian model with player-level random effects estimating experiential (momentum) effects, validated through model-checking diagnostics on temporally structured data.
cells.F533: Directly relevant methodology: hierarchical Bayesian modeling with careful validation diagnostics is exactly the class of technique GSE needs for building per-sport/per-player probability models and testing momentum-style features rigorously.
cells.G533: Apply this hierarchical Bayesian framework to rigorously test whether 'hot streak' or momentum features actually improve GSE's picks, rather than assuming they do, using the paper's model-validation diagnostics as a template for GSE's own model QA.

cells.C534: From Annotation to Adaptation: Metrics, Synthetic Data, and Aspect Extraction for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis with Large Language Models
cells.D534: Evaluates open-weight LLMs on implicit aspect-based sentiment extraction using a novel synthetic sports feedback dataset, proposing a new metric for evaluating generative aspect extraction.
cells.E534: Synthetic dataset generation plus a proposed evaluation metric for measuring how well LLMs extract aspect-polarity pairs from implicit sentiment text.
cells.F534: NLP methodology using sports feedback text as its test domain; tangentially relevant to GSE's brand-language enforcement (detecting implicit tone/sentiment) rather than to prediction modeling.
cells.G534: Adapt the aspect-based sentiment extraction approach to automatically audit GSE's own marketing copy for implicit AI-claim violations (e.g., subtle phrasing that implies 'AI-powered' without saying it outright).

cells.C535: Simulating Tracking Data to Advance Sports Analytics Research
cells.D535: Presents a method to generate simulated soccer tracking data from the Google Research Football environment, stored in a schema mimicking real tracking data, to support research where real tracking data is scarce.
cells.E535: Extracts high-level features and events from a football-playing RL simulation environment, packaging outputs in a realistic tracking-data schema for model development and testing.
cells.F535: Directly relevant to GSE's data-scarcity problem: offers a concrete way to generate schema-compatible synthetic tracking-style data for sports where GSE lacks real high-resolution positional data.
cells.G535: Use a similar RL-environment-driven synthetic data generator to stress-test GSE's ensemble/calibration models against synthetic edge-case game scenarios not well represented in the current ~1164 settled picks.

cells.C536: Forward propagation of a push through a row of people
cells.D536: Experimentally studies how a physical push propagates through a row of people at events like concerts/sports tournaments, finding propagation distance/speed depend on push strength and initial arm posture.
cells.E536: Controlled crowd-dynamics experiments recording 2D/3D motion capture to measure force propagation through densely packed pedestrian rows.
cells.F536: Crowd-safety physics research, unrelated to GSE's statistical sports-prediction or data pipeline work.
cells.G536: No credible product application; entirely outside GSE's domain despite the sporting-event context mentioned as a motivating scenario.

cells.C537: Unified Uncertainty-Aware Diffusion for Multi-Agent Trajectory Modeling
cells.D537: U2Diff is a diffusion model providing both trajectory completion/forecasting and state-wise uncertainty estimates for multi-agent sports trajectories, outperforming prior methods on NBA, football, and soccer datasets.
cells.E537: Diffusion model augmented with negative-log-likelihood-based uncertainty estimation and a Rank Neural Network that estimates per-prediction error probability for ranking generated scenarios.
cells.F537: Highly relevant to GSE's uncertainty-quantification needs: directly demonstrates state-wise uncertainty estimation and per-prediction error-probability ranking in a sports context, closely aligned with the bootstrap-mode confidence-capping problem.
cells.G537: Adapt U2Diff's uncertainty-estimation and prediction-ranking mechanism as a template for making GSE's bootstrap mode more principled — assigning calibrated per-pick confidence scores rather than a blanket cap when data is sparse.

cells.C538: Validation of Human Pose Estimation and Human Mesh Recovery for Extracting Clinically Relevant Motion Data from Videos
cells.D538: Validates markerless video-based pose estimation against IMU and marker-based motion capture, finding markerless methods produce clinically comparable kinematics with far less setup time.
cells.E538: Comparative validation study benchmarking human pose estimation/mesh recovery accuracy against gold-standard motion capture across multiple kinematic metrics.
cells.F538: Clinical biomechanics validation study, no direct connection to GSE's statistical/odds prediction engine.
cells.G538: No credible direct application to GSE's core business; only a generic reminder that cheaper/faster methods can sometimes match gold-standard accuracy, worth validating similarly for GSE's cheaper free-data sources versus paid feeds.

cells.C539: SoccerSynth Field: enhancing field detection with synthetic data from virtual soccer simulator
cells.D539: Shows a synthetic soccer-field dataset generated from a virtual simulator improves pretraining for field-detection models, outperforming models trained only on real-world data.
cells.E539: Synthetic dataset with controlled lighting/texture/camera variability used to pretrain field-detection models before optional fine-tuning on real data.
cells.F539: Computer-vision field-detection tool for broadcast analysis, unrelated to GSE's statistical prediction and calibration engine.
cells.G539: The synthetic-pretraining-improves-robustness finding reinforces (as a secondary data point) the general viability of synthetic data augmentation strategies GSE might consider for its own sparse-data sports models.

cells.C540: Improving LLM Video Understanding with 16 Frames Per Second
cells.D540: F-16 is a multimodal LLM using 16fps video sampling (vs. typical 2fps) with token compression, achieving state-of-the-art results on general and high-speed sports video understanding tasks like basketball and diving.
cells.E540: Increases video LLM frame-rate input while compressing visual tokens per clip to preserve dynamic detail, with an efficient low-frame-rate inference decoding method requiring no retraining.
cells.F540: Video-understanding architecture improvement demonstrated on sports, relevant only to GSE's potential future video-based content/scouting tools, not to the core statistical prediction pipeline.
cells.G540: If GSE ever ingests broadcast video for automated event extraction, F-16's high-frame-rate sampling technique would better capture fast sports action (e.g., football plays) than standard low-fps video LLMs.

cells.C541: Towards Energy- and QoS-aware Load Balancing for 5G Advanced: Leveraging O-RAN to Achieve Sustainability and Energy Efficiency
cells.D541: Proposes a hierarchical O-RAN energy-QoS load-balancing framework, validated in a simulated massive sports-event environment, achieving 72% energy savings with sub-second handover delays.
cells.E541: MINLP-based joint optimization of UE-to-cell association and dynamic cell deactivation across Non-RT and Near-RT RAN Intelligent Controllers.
cells.F541: Telecom infrastructure engineering for stadium network capacity, entirely unrelated to GSE's software statistical prediction platform.
cells.G541: No credible direct application to GSE's product; the 'sports event' context here is only the network-load test scenario, not a modeling or data methodology GSE could reuse.

cells.C542: Movement Dynamics in Elite Female Soccer Athletes: The Quantile Cube Approach
cells.D542: Introduces a 3D 'quantile cube' summarizing GPS velocity/acceleration/angle distributions per athlete-half, using PCA and Dirichlet-multinomial regression to explain movement variation.
cells.E542: Discretizes continuous movement time-series into quantile bins across three axes, then models the resulting compositional distributions statistically.
cells.F542: A structured, interpretable feature-engineering pattern for GSE's multi-sport time-series ingestion pipeline, especially if it later ingests player-tracking data beyond odds/box scores.
cells.G542: Use the quantile-cube idea to build a compact 'shape fingerprint' feature for bootstrap-mode confidence: sparse-data situations could be flagged by how atypical a team's quantile cube looks versus its historical baseline.

cells.C543: Stellar Parameters for over Fifty Million Stars from SMSS DR4 and Gaia DR3
cells.D543: Produces a huge catalog of stellar effective temperature, luminosity class, and metallicity from photometric survey data cross-matched with Gaia.
cells.E543: Large-scale automated photometric parameter estimation and cross-survey catalog matching at population scale.
cells.F543: Astronomy catalog work with no domain connection to sports prediction; the 'sports' string only appears in an unrelated data-hosting URL path.
cells.G543: None substantive beyond the general pattern of large-scale automated cross-source catalog matching, which loosely echoes GSE's multi-source data-ingestion pipeline engineering challenges.

cells.D544: Argues generative AI should be regulated like prior algorithmic media (search, social) to preserve public trust rather than treated as a uniquely revolutionary technology.
cells.E544: Policy essay framing generative AI within existing media-regulation theory around trust, gatekeeping, and personalization.
cells.F544: Indirect but real: informs how GSE should think about its 'we're not AI' brand positioning and trust messaging as a data/algorithmic media product facing similar scrutiny.
cells.G544: Use the essay's trust/legitimacy framing to draft GSE's public methodology page, proactively addressing 'algorithmic personalization' concerns before regulators or users raise them, reinforcing the deterministic-math brand.

cells.C545: Artificial Intelligence in Sports: Insights from a Quantitative Survey among Sports Students in Germany
cells.D545: Survey of 262 German sports students on their AI tool usage, expectations, and concerns in academic study contexts.
cells.E545: Quantitative questionnaire study measuring attitudes and behavioral patterns toward generative AI adoption.
cells.F545: Only tangentially relevant via the 'sports' population studied; no methodological or product connection to GSE's prediction engine or calibration work.
cells.G545: Could inform how GSE frames AI-adjacent educational content or FAQ copy for a sports-savvy but AI-skeptical audience, given documented user concerns about trust and preparedness.

cells.C546: Gate-Shift-Pose: Enhancing Action Recognition in Sports with Skeleton Information
cells.D546: Improves figure-skating fall classification by fusing RGB video with pose-keypoint heatmaps in early- and late-fusion network variants.
cells.E546: Multimodal fusion of skeletal pose data and raw video frames within a gated spatiotemporal CNN architecture.
cells.F546: Adjacent to GSE's video/content ambitions (social/media generation) rather than its core calibration or forecasting blockers; more useful if GSE adds video-based feature extraction.
cells.G546: Repurpose the fall/event-classification approach as an automated highlight-detection module for GSE's planned automated social content generation pipeline.

cells.C547: What Influences Field Goal Attempts? Basketball Shot Charts via Log Gaussian Cox Processes
cells.D547: Bayesian spatio-temporal point process model of NBA shot locations and success, with spatially varying covariate effects estimated via MCMC.
cells.E547: Hierarchical log Gaussian Cox process with kernel-convolution MCMC for joint spatial intensity and outcome modeling.
cells.F547: Directly relevant as a sophisticated Bayesian spatial modeling technique that could inspire per-sport, per-context probability models GSE needs to fix its failing calibration gate.
cells.G547: Adapt the spatially-varying-coefficient idea to model per-sport, per-market 'conditions' (venue, opponent, rest) as continuous covariate surfaces feeding GSE's ensemble rather than discrete buckets.

cells.C548: Modelling the non-linear viscoelastic behaviour of brain tissue in torsion
cells.D548: Characterizes brain tissue stress-relaxation under torsion via rheometry and a modified quasi-linear viscoelastic model, validated with finite element simulation.
cells.E548: Ramp-and-hold torsion testing fit to viscoelastic constitutive equations, cross-validated with FEniCS FE simulations.
cells.F548: Pure biomechanics/materials science paper; connects to GSE only through its stated motivation of improving sports headgear design, unrelated to prediction or calibration.
cells.G548: No meaningful product application beyond noting it as background if GSE ever expanded into injury-risk or equipment-safety analytics content.

cells.C549: Precise Event Spotting in Sports Videos: Solving Long-Range Dependency and Class Imbalance
cells.D549: Proposes an end-to-end spatio-temporal network with a refinement module and contrastive loss to precisely timestamp sports events in broadcast video, beating prior SOTA.
cells.E549: Convolutional spatio-temporal feature extractor plus long-range temporal module and a soft instance-contrastive loss addressing class imbalance.
cells.F549: Relevant to GSE's data-ingestion ambitions if it ever moves beyond box-score/odds data into video-derived event features for live in-game modeling.
cells.G549: Use the imbalance-aware contrastive loss as inspiration for weighting rare high-impact events (turnovers, injuries) more heavily when training GSE's per-sport probability models, similarly underrepresented in settled-pick data.

cells.C550: BST: Badminton Stroke-type Transformer for Skeleton-based Action Recognition in Racket Sports
cells.D550: Combines pose, shuttlecock trajectory, and court-position data in a transformer to classify badminton stroke types, generalizing to tennis.
cells.E550: Multi-stream transformer fusing skeletal joints, object trajectory, and court geometry for fine-grained action classification.
cells.F550: Niche computer-vision technique with no direct link to GSE's calibration/forecasting core; only tangential as a video-feature-engineering example.
cells.G550: Could inform a future 'shot-type tagging' feature layer if GSE's Intelligence Graph ever ingests granular play-by-play action types for racket sports markets.

cells.C551: Measuring Interlayer Dependence of Large Degrees in Multilayer Inhomogeneous Random Graphs
cells.D551: Develops an upper-tail dependence estimator for multilayer networks and applies it to Reddit, linking financial and sports-subreddit engagement patterns.
cells.E551: Extremal dependence estimation via multivariate regular variation theory applied to multilayer random graph degree sequences.
cells.F551: Loosely relevant to the Intelligence Graph's typed-primitives layer as a rigorous method for quantifying cross-layer (e.g., market sentiment vs. sports discussion) dependence.
cells.G551: Apply the interlayer tail-dependence estimator to detect when social/media buzz spikes co-move with abnormal odds movement, as an anomaly-detection signal for line-shopping or steam-move alerts.

cells.C552: Exploring K-12 Physical Education Teachers' Perspectives on AI Integration Through Ideation Workshops
cells.D552: Qualitative workshop study capturing PE teachers' envisioned AI roles (assistant, coach, evaluator) and concerns like privacy and over-reliance.
cells.E552: Participatory design ideation workshops analyzed thematically for stakeholder perspectives on AI adoption.
cells.F552: Weak connection; useful only as a reminder of user trust/privacy concerns that echo GSE's own athlete-data and brand-trust considerations, not a technical resource.
cells.G552: Mine the identified teacher personas (assistant, coach, evaluator) as a template for designing GSE's own B2B coaching/analytics widget roles for youth or amateur sports organizations.

cells.C553: Metamorphic Testing for Pose Estimation Systems
cells.D553: Introduces MET-POSE, a metamorphic testing framework that evaluates pose-estimation systems without hand-labeled ground truth by checking consistency under transformations.
cells.E553: Applies metamorphic relations (e.g., rotation, occlusion invariance) to test model robustness using unlabeled data.
cells.F553: Directly useful methodology for GSE's data pipeline reliability: metamorphic testing principles could validate scraping/ETL correctness without needing labeled ground truth for every source.
cells.G553: Build metamorphic tests for GSE's own prediction engine — e.g., checking that swapping team order or adding irrelevant noise features doesn't change win-probability outputs beyond expected bounds, as a pre-launch QA gate.

cells.C554: Sports and Women's Sports: Gender Bias in Text Generation with Olympic Data
cells.D554: Uses parallel men's/women's Olympic events to show LLMs default to men's results and gender bias when prompts are ambiguous.
cells.E554: Constructs paired-event prompts and measures retrieval/generation bias via defined bias metrics on LLM outputs.
cells.F554: Relevant to GSE's brand-language enforcement and any LLM-assisted content generation (commentary, social posts) that could inadvertently embed sports gender bias.
cells.G554: Adapt the paired-event bias-testing methodology as a pre-publish QA check for GSE's automated content generation, auditing whether generated picks/commentary systematically underweight women's leagues.

cells.C555: A Decade of Action Quality Assessment: Largest Systematic Survey of Trends, Challenges, and Future Directions
cells.D555: PRISMA-based systematic review of over 200 papers on computer-vision Action Quality Assessment methods, datasets, and metrics.
cells.E555: Structured literature synthesis categorizing AQA frameworks, datasets, and performance benchmarks.
cells.F555: Survey-level background for any future video-based skill-scoring feature; not directly tied to GSE's current calibration/forecasting blockers.
cells.G555: Use the survey's taxonomy of quality-scoring metrics as a design reference if GSE ever builds a 'player form quality' score feeding into its ensemble models.

cells.C556: Impact of Seismic Activities on the Optical Synchronization System of the European X-ray Free-Electron Laser
cells.D556: Analyzes how earthquakes, ocean microseism, and civilization noise (including sports events) disturb phase-locked-loop optical synchronization at a physics facility.
cells.E556: Signal analysis comparing PLL controller data against external seismic/vibration data sources to isolate disturbance causes.
cells.F556: No substantive connection to GSE beyond a passing mention that the sensor detects vibrations from sporting events; physics instrumentation paper.
cells.G556: None meaningful; at most illustrates general signal-denoising/anomaly-attribution technique transferable to noisy time-series in GSE's odds/data pipelines.

cells.C557: Efficient inference of rankings from multi-body comparisons
cells.D557: Presents a faster algorithm for fitting Plackett-Luce ranking models to multi-way (not just pairwise) comparisons, validated on synthetic and real tournament data.
cells.E557: Accelerated iterative inference for the Plackett-Luce model applied to multi-entity contest outcomes, with cross-validated predictive testing.
cells.F557: Directly relevant: multi-body ranking models are a proven alternative/complement to pairwise Elo-style approaches GSE likely uses, and could feed its ensemble or per-sport probability models.
cells.G557: Use the faster Plackett-Luce solver to build real-time, computationally cheap multi-entity ranking updates (e.g., golf/racing fields) that plug directly into GSE's ensemble alongside CEPT-based components.

cells.C558: A Domain Adaptation Framework for Speech Recognition Systems with Only Synthetic data
cells.D558: Uses LLM-generated text converted to synthetic speech to fine-tune Whisper via LoRA adapters for domain-specific ASR, including a sports domain, without real data.
cells.E558: LLM-driven synthetic text-to-speech data generation paired with LoRA fine-tuning and multi-adapter merged decoding.
cells.F558: Tangential: relevant only if GSE builds voice/audio features (e.g., podcast transcription, voice-driven content) for its media/content automation ambitions.
cells.G558: Apply the synthetic-data-only domain adaptation pattern to bootstrap GSE's automated commentary/content generator for a new sport with sparse real transcript data.

cells.C559: KabaddiPy: A package to enable access to Professional Kabaddi Data
cells.D559: Open-source Python package that web-scrapes and organizes Kabaddi team/player statistics from scattered online sources into usable datasets.
cells.E559: Systematic web scraping and data cleaning pipeline producing structured, season-filterable sports statistics.
cells.F559: Directly relevant as a concrete example of the multi-source web-scraping and data-cleaning architecture GSE's data-ingestion pipeline needs for niche/emerging sports coverage.
cells.G559: Use this as a template for rapidly bootstrapping GSE's data pipeline into new emerging leagues (e.g., international kabaddi, MLS expansion) with minimal engineering overhead before official APIs exist.

cells.C560: From Occasional to Steady: Habit Formation Insights From a Comprehensive Fitness Study
cells.D560: Analyzes gym attendance data via survival analysis and causal inference to identify critical periods and interventions that drive exercise habit formation.
cells.E560: Survival-metric clustering of attendance patterns combined with causal inference on intervention effects (classes, PT sessions).
cells.F560: Tangential to GSE's core prediction engine, but the causal-inference-on-behavioral-data methodology is a reusable pattern for modeling user engagement/retention on the platform.

cells.D570: Presents LLaMo, a multimodal LLM that retains motion data in native form (rather than tokenizing it) for instruction-tuned understanding of human behaviors, including sports analytics scenarios.

cells.G570: Explore native-motion-preserving multimodal fusion for a future 'form scanner' feature that lets GSE's agents reason directly over player movement clips when assessing injury/fatigue risk.

cells.D577: Fine-tunes an object detector to directly read game-clock text from basketball broadcast frames, aligning play-by-play annotations to video without localizing the clock UI.

cells.D578: Introduces 'motion graphs' representing video patches as interconnected graph nodes to predict future frames more efficiently than optical flow or motion-matrix methods, tested on UCF Sports.

cells.D601: Introduces a tennis match simulation environment where agents compete against real-data-driven bot strategies, using MCTS to optimize shot-direction decisions realistically.
