cells.E605: Lexicon-based scoring of geospatial OSM data mapped to defined activity-support categories across a global city dataset.
cells.F605: No meaningful connection to GSE's prediction/calibration platform; an urban public-health geospatial study.
cells.G605: None substantive; at most illustrates a lexicon-driven geospatial scoring pattern that is not applicable to GSE's product domain.

cells.C606: Decoupled Prompt-Adapter Tuning for Continual Activity Recognition
cells.D606: Proposes DPAT, combining adapters and learnable prompts in a decoupled training strategy to continually learn new action-recognition tasks without forgetting prior ones, achieving SOTA on benchmarks.
cells.E606: Decoupled continual-learning framework pairing lightweight adapters for spatiotemporal features with prompts to mitigate catastrophic forgetting.
cells.F606: Tangential but conceptually useful: continual-learning-without-forgetting is relevant to GSE's need to keep updating per-sport models with new season data without destroying prior calibration.
cells.G606: Apply a decoupled adapter/prompt continual-learning strategy to GSE's per-sport probability models, letting them absorb new-season data incrementally without catastrophic recalibration failures each offseason.

cells.C607: WSESeg: A Dataset for the Segmentation of Winter Sports Equipment with a Baseline for Interactive Segmentation
cells.D607: Introduces a winter-sports-equipment instance segmentation dataset and tests SAM/HQ-SAM foundation models with interactive online-adaptation methods to improve labeling efficiency.
cells.E607: Interactive segmentation benchmarking of foundation vision models with online adaptation to reduce annotation effort.
cells.F607: Niche computer-vision dataset/tooling paper with no direct link to GSE's statistical calibration or forecasting core.
cells.G607: No meaningful GSE application beyond general annotation-efficiency lessons if GSE ever needed to label sports video data cheaply.

cells.C608: Empirical Determination of Baseball Eras: Multivariate Changepoint Analysis in Major League Baseball
cells.D608: Uses multivariate changepoint analysis on over a century of MLB statistics to empirically identify known eras (Dead Ball, Steroid, etc.) and detect team dynasty/collapse periods.
cells.E608: Multivariate changepoint detection capturing simultaneous mean and variance shifts across many correlated statistical time series.
cells.F608: Directly relevant: a proven method for detecting structural regime shifts across correlated sports statistics, applicable to GSE's need to identify when historical training data spans a different statistical 'era' than current games.
cells.G608: Run multivariate changepoint detection on GSE's own historical training corpora per sport to automatically segment 'eras' and avoid training the ensemble on stale, regime-inconsistent data that could be dragging down calibration.

cells.D609: Proposes a Bayesian Rank-Clustered Bradley-Terry-Luce model that lets statistically indistinguishable objects share a rank via a spike-and-slab prior, demonstrated on sports analytics data.
cells.E609: Bradley-Terry-Luce ranking model extended with parameter fusion via spike-and-slab priors to identify rank-clusters with quantified uncertainty.
cells.F609: Directly relevant: offers a statistically honest way to represent ranking uncertainty (rather than false precision), which is exactly the kind of principled uncertainty quantification GSE's confidence/calibration system needs.
cells.G609: Use rank-clustering to let GSE explicitly communicate when two teams/players are 'too close to call' rather than forcing an artificially precise probability, directly supporting more honest calibration and ECE improvement.

cells.C610: Do they mean 'us'? Interpreting Referring Expressions in Intergroup Bias
cells.D610: Models intergroup linguistic bias in 6M+ NFL fan comments, grounded in live win-probability data, showing LLMs perform better tagging in-group/out-group references with linguistic (not numeric) probability framing.
cells.E610: LLM-based automated tagging of referring expressions in sports fan text, validated against win-probability-grounded context and expert annotation.
cells.F610: Relevant to GSE's brand-language enforcement work: demonstrates that LLMs respond better to linguistic than numeric probability framing, directly informing how GSE should phrase confidence in generated content.
cells.G610: Apply the finding that LLMs handle linguistic probability framing better than raw numbers to redesign GSE's automated content generator's prompt templates, improving both accuracy and brand-consistent tone when describing pick confidence.

cells.C611: AI for Equitable Tennis Training: Leveraging AI for Accurate Classification of Tennis Skill Levels and Training Phases
cells.D611: Uses IMU motion data and SVMs to classify junior tennis players' skill level and swing phases, aiming for an affordable self-training system on consumer devices.
cells.E611: SVM classification on IMU-derived yaw/roll/pitch features for skill-level and stroke-phase categorization.
cells.F611: Weak relevance; a consumer coaching-tech application unrelated to GSE's calibration/forecasting or data pipeline blockers.
cells.G611: No strong application; at most a distant example of low-cost wearable-sensor classification relevant only to a hypothetical future consumer coaching product.

cells.C612: Language and Multimodal Models in Sports: A Survey of Datasets and Applications
cells.D612: Comprehensive survey categorizing post-2020 language and multimodal sports datasets (language-based, multimodal, convertible) and their applications from fan experience to tactics and diagnostics.
cells.E612: Structured taxonomy and review of NLP/multimodal sports datasets, applications, and open challenges.
cells.F612: Directly relevant as a landscape reference for GSE's content-automation and Intelligence Graph efforts, mapping available sports NLP resources it could leverage.
cells.G612: Use this survey as a sourcing map to identify existing public multimodal sports datasets GSE could fine-tune its brand-language content generator or knowledge-graph extraction pipeline on, rather than building from scratch.

cells.C613: When Reasoning Meets Information Aggregation: A Case Study with Sports Narratives
cells.D613: Tests LLM reasoning by requiring accurate aggregation of NBA scoring events into statistics, finding models like GPT-4o frequently miscalculate scores and hallucinate stats from synthetic narratives.
cells.E613: Synthesizes controllable-complexity game narratives (SportsGen) and evaluates LLM score-aggregation accuracy across narrative length and density.
cells.F613: Directly relevant as a cautionary benchmark: shows LLMs unreliably aggregate sports statistics from narrative text, a critical risk for GSE if it uses LLMs anywhere in its data pipeline or automated content that touches numeric facts.
cells.G613: Adapt the SportsGen synthetic-narrative methodology as an internal stress-test suite for GSE's content-generation LLM, catching numeric hallucination bugs before any auto-generated recap with wrong stats reaches the brand-sensitive public site.

cells.C614: LVBench: An Extreme Long Video Understanding Benchmark
cells.D614: Introduces a benchmark for hours-long video comprehension tasks, explicitly motivated by use cases like live sports commentary that require long-term memory in multimodal models.
cells.E614: Curated long-video benchmark testing multimodal LLMs' extended temporal comprehension and information extraction.
cells.F614: Tangential; relevant only if GSE pursues long-form live-broadcast video understanding for content generation, not to its core calibration/forecasting work.
cells.G614: Could validate a future GSE feature that auto-generates game recaps or highlight commentary from full-length broadcast footage, using this benchmark's evaluation approach as a quality bar.

cells.C615: Demo: Soccer Information Retrieval via Natural Queries using SoccerRAG
cells.D615: Demo of a chatbot-style UI wrapping a retrieval-augmented-generation framework for querying multimodal soccer datasets via natural language.
cells.E615: RAG-based natural language query interface over a multimodal soccer dataset with a Chainlit-based conversational UI.
cells.F615: Relevant as a direct architectural template for a GSE B2B or consumer feature allowing natural-language queries over its own sports data (picks, stats, historical performance).
cells.G615: Build a 'chat with your picks' RAG interface using this template, letting GSE users or B2B partners query historical predictions and outcomes conversationally rather than through fixed dashboards.

cells.C616: SoccerRAG: Multimodal Soccer Information Retrieval via Natural Queries
cells.D616: Full framework paper for SoccerRAG, showing RAG plus LLMs effectively handle complex natural-language soccer queries over multimodal data with better accuracy/engagement than traditional retrieval.
cells.E616: Retrieval-augmented generation architecture combining multimodal data validation with LLM-based query answering for sports archives.
cells.F616: Directly relevant as a proven RAG architecture for structured/multimodal sports data retrieval, applicable to GSE's data-ingestion and Intelligence Graph query layer.
cells.G616: Extend the RAG-over-multimodal-sports-data architecture into GSE's Intelligence Graph as the natural-language query layer, letting internal agents (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) or partners retrieve typed knowledge primitives conversationally.

cells.C617: Multi-Aspect Controllable Text Generation with Disentangled Counterfactual Augmentation
cells.D617: Proposes MAGIC, using disentangled counterfactual augmentation to fix imbalanced attribute-correlation stereotypes in multi-aspect (e.g., sentiment + topic) controllable text generation.
cells.E617: Counterfactual feature-vector augmentation in a disentangled latent space to debias and strengthen multi-attribute control during training and inference.
cells.F617: Directly relevant to GSE's strict brand-language lint rule: this is exactly the kind of controllable-text-generation technique needed to reliably enforce banned phrases/tone (no 'AI-powered') while controlling other content aspects like sentiment or sport topic.
cells.G617: Use disentangled counterfactual augmentation to train GSE's content generator to independently control 'brand-compliance' as one controllable aspect alongside tone/topic, making banned-phrase avoidance a first-class trainable attribute rather than a post-hoc filter.

cells.C618: Computer-Vision-Enabled Worker Video Analysis for Motion Amount Quantification
cells.D618: Uses pose estimation and Hotelling's T² statistic to quantify worker motion/ergonomic risk in real time, validated partly against UCF Sports Action benchmark data.
cells.E618: Multivariate statistical process control (Hotelling's T²) applied to joint-position time series for anomaly/workload detection, paired with a Random Forest classifier.
cells.F618: Tangential; the statistical anomaly-detection technique (multivariate control charting) is a reusable pattern for GSE's data pipeline quality monitoring, though the application domain (ergonomics) is unrelated.
cells.G618: Apply Hotelling's T² multivariate control-chart monitoring to GSE's live data-ingestion streams (odds feeds, scraped stats) to statistically flag anomalous data drift in real time before it corrupts model inputs.

cells.C619: A General Framework for Jersey Number Recognition in Sports Video
cells.D619: Adapts scene text recognition models for jersey number identification in hockey and soccer video, aggregating single-frame predictions into tracklet-level labels for player tracking.
cells.E619: Scene-text-recognition adaptation combined with cross-frame aggregation to produce robust player-identity labels from video.
cells.F619: Tangential; relevant only if GSE ingests broadcast video and needs automated player identification for its data pipeline or content generation, not to its calibration blockers.
cells.G619: Could enable automated player-level tagging of scraped highlight clips for GSE's social content pipeline, linking specific players to generated commentary without manual annotation.

cells.C620: AutoSoccerPose: Automated 3D posture Analysis of Soccer Shot Movements
cells.D620: Introduces the largest annotated soccer pose dataset and a graph recurrent autoencoder to embed shot-posture sequences non-linearly, semi-automating 3D posture analysis.
cells.E620: Graph Recurrent AutoEncoder embeds temporal pose sequences nonlinearly, improving on prior linear (PCA/regression) posture analysis approaches.
cells.F620: Tangential computer-vision research; not connected to GSE's core statistical calibration or forecasting challenges.
cells.G620: Minimal application; the nonlinear sequence-embedding idea (graph RAE) is a distant architectural analogy for encoding sequential game-state features in GSE's models rather than a direct fit.

cells.C621: Adolescent sports participation and health in early adulthood: An observational study
cells.D621: Uses matched observational analysis on longitudinal youth data to show teen sports participation, especially collision sports, predicts better self-rated and mental health in early adulthood.
cells.E621: Hierarchical matched-observational-study design with ordered testing to control family-wise error across nested exposure definitions.
cells.F621: No direct connection to GSE's prediction platform; a public-health/sociology study on sports participation outcomes.
cells.G621: None substantive for GSE's core product; at most a content-marketing angle about the documented health benefits of sports participation.

cells.C622: Sports Analysis and VR Viewing System Based on Player Tracking and Pose Estimation with Multimodal and Multiview Sensors
cells.D622: Builds an end-to-end system using multiview LiDAR and cameras for multi-player tracking, pose estimation, and 3D avatar modeling for real-time VR/AR game viewing.
cells.E622: Multimodal sensor fusion (LiDAR + camera) pipeline for player tracking, pose extraction, and 3D avatar reconstruction feeding a VR/AR rendering layer.
cells.F622: Tangential to GSE's core calibration/forecasting work; relevant only to a far-future immersive-viewing feature adjacent to the planned Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR persistent game layer.
cells.G622: Distant inspiration for a VR/AR viewing mode of GSE's Galaxy Dynasty game layer, letting users watch simulated or real games with live prediction overlays in an immersive format.

cells.C623: TeamTrack: A Dataset for Multi-Sport Multi-Object Tracking in Full-pitch Videos
cells.D623: Introduces a large multi-sport (soccer, basketball, handball) full-pitch multi-object tracking benchmark dataset to address gaps in existing MOT resources for team sports.
cells.E623: Benchmark dataset and evaluation suite for multi-object tracking algorithms across diverse team-sport full-pitch video.
cells.F623: Tangential; a computer-vision tracking dataset relevant only if GSE later incorporates video-derived tracking features into its data pipeline, not to current calibration blockers.
cells.G623: Could serve as a benchmark to validate any future in-house or licensed player-tracking feature pipeline GSE builds for its multi-sport Intelligence Graph.

cells.C624: A Multivariate Copula-based Bayesian Framework for Doping Detection
cells.D624: Extends the Athlete Biological Passport's Bayesian doping-detection method (ADAPTIVE) from univariate to multivariate using copulas to jointly model correlated biomarkers.
cells.E624: Copula-coupled hierarchical Bayesian model producing multidimensional predictive reference regions for anomaly detection in correlated biomarker time series.
cells.F624: Directly relevant methodologically: a copula-based multivariate Bayesian reference-region approach is a strong template for GSE's uncertainty-aware anomaly/outlier detection needs, including bootstrap-mode confidence capping.
cells.G624: Adapt the copula-based multivariate reference-region framework to jointly monitor correlated model-output metrics (Brier, ECE, CLV) over time, flagging genuine multivariate calibration anomalies rather than checking each metric in isolation.

cells.C625: A Universal Protocol to Benchmark Camera Calibration for Sports
cells.D625: Proposes ProCC, a camera-model-agnostic benchmarking protocol for sports camera calibration using reprojection of known non-planar 3D objects, exposing limitations of homography-only field-registration metrics.
cells.E625: Defines evaluation criteria and reprojection-based metrics independent of the underlying camera model to fairly benchmark calibration methods.
cells.F625: Not about statistical/probabilistic calibration (GSE's actual blocker) but geometric camera calibration for video; connects only via the shared word 'calibration' and general benchmark-design rigor.
cells.G625: The paper's core lesson — that a benchmark's chosen metric can systematically bias which methods look good — is a useful cautionary parallel for GSE to scrutinize whether its own Brier/ECE evaluation protocol has similar blind spots per sport.

cells.C626: Quantifying fair income distribution in Thailand
cells.D626: Derives 'fairness benchmarks' for income distribution from the distribution of professional athletes' salaries, applying them to assess Thai income inequality data from 1988-2021.
cells.E626: Uses professional-sports salary distributions as a normative fairness reference to evaluate and design national income-distribution policy.
cells.F626: No direct connection to GSE's prediction platform; an economics/policy paper that merely borrows sports-salary data as a fairness benchmark.
cells.G626: None substantive; at most a curiosity noting that sports-salary distributions carry perceived fairness properties, irrelevant to GSE's forecasting or calibration work.

cells.C627: 3D Human Scan With A Moving Event Camera
cells.D627: Uses a moving event camera (not frame-based) to reconstruct 3D human pose and mesh via voxel carving, outperforming conventional frame-based methods including under motion blur.
cells.E627: Event-camera-based 3D voxel carving and statistical body-model fitting from asynchronous event streams rather than RGB frames.
cells.F627: Tangential computer-vision hardware/method paper; relevant only if GSE pursues advanced video capture for sports analysis, not its statistical core.
cells.G627: No strong direct application; a distant possibility for future high-fidelity motion capture if GSE ever builds in-house sports video analytics infrastructure.

cells.C628: Impact of Extensions on Browser Performance: An Empirical Study on Google Chrome
cells.D628: Empirically studies how 72 Chrome extensions (including Sports-category ones) affect energy consumption and page load time, identifying code complexity and data-collection practices as key factors.
cells.E628: Controlled empirical performance measurement (energy, load time) across browser extension categories with statistical factor analysis.
cells.F628: Very tangential; relevant only as generic web-performance engineering guidance for GSE's own Next.js/Vercel frontend, not to its data science blockers.
cells.G628: Apply similar empirical performance-testing discipline to audit any third-party scripts/widgets embedded in GSE's site (analytics, odds widgets) for their real-world load-time and energy impact on users.

cells.C629: Why is soccer so popular: Understanding underdog achievement and randomness in team ball sports
cells.D629: Compares 12 team sports' 'underdog achievement' rates and builds a randomness model via PCA to explain why weaker teams beat stronger ones more often in soccer than other sports.
cells.E629: Cross-sport comparative analysis combining a custom underdog-achievement score with PCA-derived randomness-factor modeling.
cells.F629: Directly relevant: quantifies inherent unpredictability/variance differences across sports, which should directly inform GSE's expectations for achievable Brier score and calibration targets per sport.
cells.G629: Use the cross-sport randomness-factor decomposition to set sport-specific, variance-adjusted calibration targets (rather than one fixed Brier/ECE bar for all sports), since soccer's inherent randomness likely caps achievable calibration lower than less random sports.

cells.C630: Modelling handball outcomes using univariate and bivariate approaches
cells.D630: Proposes Skellam-distribution-based regression models (including zero-inflated and bivariate copula variants) for handball score differences, addressing under-dispersion that breaks standard Poisson models.
cells.E630: Skellam regression on score differences plus copula-based bivariate modeling of first/second-half dependence, fit to Bundesliga handball data.
cells.F630: Directly relevant: a concrete example of choosing a better-fitting scoring-distribution family (Skellam over Poisson) per sport — precisely the kind of per-sport probability-model fix GSE suspects it needs for its calibration gate.
cells.G630: Audit each of GSE's sport-specific scoring models against dispersion diagnostics like this paper's, swapping in Skellam/zero-inflated alternatives wherever the standard Poisson-based approach is mismatched to the sport's actual score-difference distribution.

cells.C631: ChoreoVis: Planning and Assessing Formations in Dance Choreographies
cells.D631: Builds a visual analytics system for planning dance formations and assessing real-world trajectory deviations against planned choreography, developed with dance instructors.
cells.E631: Interactive web-based authoring and trajectory-deviation visualization tools for formation-based movement planning and assessment.
cells.F631: No direct connection to GSE's prediction/calibration platform; a visual-analytics tool for a non-competitive, choreographed movement domain.
cells.G631: None substantive for GSE's core product; at most a distant UI pattern (deviation-from-plan visualization) that could inform a coaching-strategy-adherence dashboard if GSE ever built one.

cells.C632: SalFoM: Dynamic Saliency Prediction with Video Foundation Models
cells.D632: Introduces a video-foundation-model-based encoder-decoder transformer that predicts human visual saliency maps in videos, beating prior state-of-the-art on sports benchmarks.
cells.E632: Uses a pretrained video transformer (UMT) feature extractor plus a heterogeneous local/global spatio-temporal decoder to fuse multi-scale attention cues into a saliency map.
cells.F632: Tangential to GSE — it's about predicting where human eyes look in sports video, not outcome prediction, so the connection is only through shared sports-video data.
cells.G632: Could be repurposed to auto-select the most visually engaging frame/clip from broadcast footage for GSE's automated social/media content generation pipeline.

cells.C633: A Temporal Graph Model to Study the Dynamics of Collective Behavior and Performance in Team Sports
cells.D633: Builds a temporal graph of basketball passing networks and shows entropy measures of network structure correlate positively with team performance.
cells.E633: Constructs time-evolving player-interaction graphs and computes structural entropy as a complexity/self-regulation metric linked to score outcomes.
cells.F633: Directly useful as a feature-engineering idea for GSE's prediction-engine: passing-network entropy could be a per-sport signal feeding the ensemble that's needed to fix the losing backtest.
cells.G633: Feed live in-game entropy trajectories into the pick engine to dynamically flag momentum shifts, tightening in-play confidence bands beyond static box-score features.

cells.C634: Aligning Large Language Models with Recommendation Knowledge
cells.D634: Fine-tunes LLMs with auxiliary tasks mimicking classic recommender techniques (masked item modeling, Bayesian personalized ranking) to inject recommendation-specific knowledge, improving retrieval/ranking.
cells.E634: Generates natural-language auxiliary training samples that encode item-correlation and preference signals, then fine-tunes LLMs on them alongside recommendation data.
cells.F634: Loose fit for GSE — not sports-specific, but the auxiliary-task fine-tuning idea could help their internal agents (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) better reason about structured pick/odds data.
cells.G634: Apply the same auxiliary-task recipe to teach an internal agent to reason over the Intelligence Graph's typed knowledge primitives rather than plain recommendation items.

cells.D635: Proposes a hypergraph-based adjusted plus-minus (APM) method that jointly ranks individual players, sub-lineups, and full lineups in team sports, validated on a decade of NBA data.
cells.E635: Extends regression-based APM using hypergraph representations to capture the full dependency structure between individuals and combinations of players.
cells.F635: Directly relevant to GSE's per-sport modeling ambitions — a more principled player/lineup-value metric could feed features into sport-specific probability models to help close the Brier/ECE gap.
cells.G635: Use hypergraph APM as a structured feature layer inside the Intelligence Graph, letting lineup-combination value propagate into pick confidence scores automatically.

cells.C636: RELI11D: A Comprehensive Multimodal Human Motion Dataset and Method
cells.D636: Releases a multimodal (LiDAR, IMU, RGB, event-camera) human motion dataset across five sports and proposes a cross-attention fusion model for pose estimation.
cells.E636: Combines multiple sensor modalities via cross-attention fusion to improve human pose estimation during fast, complex sports movements.
cells.F636: Off-target for GSE's stats/odds engine — this is sensor-fusion computer vision for biomechanics, not probabilistic forecasting or calibration.
cells.G636: Tangential inspiration only: multimodal motion capture data could someday feed a far-future player-injury-risk feature, but it's a stretch from GSE's current roadmap.

cells.C637: Benchmarking Badminton Action Recognition with a New Fine-Grained Dataset
cells.D637: Introduces VideoBadminton, a fine-grained action-recognition dataset for badminton, and benchmarks CNN/transformer action-recognition methods on it.
cells.E637: Curates labeled badminton footage and evaluates existing video action-recognition architectures for fine-grained shot classification.
cells.F637: Not directly relevant to GSE's calibration/forecasting problems — this is a computer-vision benchmark for a sport (badminton) GSE doesn't currently cover.
cells.G637: Could inform a future action-tagging pipeline if GSE ever expands into granular in-play event detection for content generation.

cells.C638: Augment Before Copy-Paste: Data and Memory Efficiency-Oriented Instance Segmentation Framework for Sport-scenes
cells.D638: Proposes a memory-efficient instance segmentation framework for locating basketball players under limited data and no pretraining, using augmentation-enhanced copy-paste priors.
cells.E638: Incorporates visual inductive priors into data preprocessing/augmentation and inference to improve segmentation without transfer learning.
cells.F638: Not relevant to GSE's core forecasting/calibration blockers — it's a low-data computer-vision segmentation technique unrelated to their stats pipeline.
cells.G638: Minimal thread: the low-data/limited-compute training philosophy could loosely inspire how GSE handles 'bootstrap mode' for sparse-data sports with few historical games.

cells.C639: Gender differences in online communication: A case study of Soccer
cells.D639: Analyzes 9.5M soccer-related tweets in English and Portuguese to find gender differences in emotional expression and network homophily around soccer discourse.
cells.E639: Combines large-scale Twitter data collection with text-level sentiment analysis and network homophily measurement across languages and genders.
cells.F639: Weak connection to GSE — mainly useful as a social-listening methodology if GSE monitors sports Twitter sentiment for content or market signals.
cells.G639: Could inspire a sentiment-differentiated social listening module feeding GSE's automated content generation with audience-segment-aware commentary tone.

cells.D640: Uses neural-network video analysis of badminton matches to extract biomechanical insights (stance, stroke angles) and generate personalized training/nutrition recommendations.
cells.E640: Applies motion analysis and correlation of physical attributes with in-game movement to derive muscle-activation-informed coaching suggestions.
cells.F640: Not relevant to GSE's prediction/calibration stack — this is athlete coaching software, unrelated to their picks lifecycle or scoring engine.
cells.G640: No direct application; at best a distant idea for a future athlete-performance-adjacent feature in the Galaxy Dynasty game layer.

cells.C641: Leveraging Compressed Frame Sizes For Ultra-Fast Video Classification
cells.D641: Classifies video categories (including Sport) directly from compressed bitstream frame sizes without decoding, achieving high accuracy at massive speed over traditional pixel-based methods.
cells.E641: Analyzes post-compression bitstream statistics as classification features, bypassing decompression entirely for ultra-fast inference.
cells.F641: Minimal direct relevance — GSE doesn't do video classification, but the 'cheap proxy signal instead of full processing' philosophy echoes efficient data-pipeline design.
cells.G641: Could inspire a lightweight triage step in GSE's data-ingestion pipeline: quickly classify/tag scraped video/media assets before expensive full processing.

cells.C642: Can Large Language Models do Analytical Reasoning?
cells.D642: Tests LLMs (GPT-4, Claude, etc.) on counting NBA/NFL quarter scores from play-by-play data, finding divide-and-conquer prompting most effective and NBA counting surprisingly harder than NFL.
cells.E642: Compares prompting strategies (chain-of-thought vs. divide-and-conquer) for numerical/analytical reasoning over structured sports play-by-play text.
cells.F642: Directly relevant to GSE's internal agentic tooling (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) — shows concrete failure modes and effective prompting patterns for LLMs reasoning over sports statistics.
cells.G642: Use the divide-and-conquer decomposition technique to have an internal agent audit ingested play-by-play data for consistency errors before it reaches the prediction engine.

cells.C643: ViSTec: Video Modeling for Sports Technique Recognition and Tactical Analysis
cells.D643: Proposes a graph-augmented two-stage model that recognizes stroke techniques and tactics in racket-sport broadcast video, validated with Chinese national table tennis coaches.
cells.E643: Integrates a strategic-knowledge graph over stroke sequences with a two-stage action-perception model to overcome occlusion/blur limitations of prior technique recognizers.
cells.F643: Modest relevance — the technique-sequence graph modeling idea echoes GSE's 'Intelligence Graph' concept of typed knowledge primitives, though applied to video not structured stats.
cells.G643: Adapt the tactic-graph structure as a schema pattern for encoding play-sequence tactics as typed primitives in GSE's Intelligence Graph, independent of video input.

cells.C644: Predicting Outcomes in Video Games with Long Short Term Memory Networks
cells.D644: Uses an LSTM on real-time health-bar time series to predict win/lose outcomes in a fighting game, benchmarked against transformer-based time-series models.
cells.E644: Trains LSTM and transformer forecasters on a single scalar time series (player health) to make live win-probability predictions.
cells.F644: Directly relevant methodologically — a minimal real-time forecasting architecture for live win-probability estimation, comparable to what GSE needs for live/in-play picks.
cells.G644: Benchmark GSE's live win-probability module against a simple LSTM-on-key-signal baseline (e.g., score differential) to sanity-check whether the core model is actually adding value over a cheap baseline.

cells.C645: Large Scale Generative AI Text Applied to Sports and Music
cells.D645: Describes a deployed generative-AI commentary system producing automated highlight narrations and personalized stories for major sports/music events (US Open, Wimbledon, Grammys).
cells.E645: Transforms multimodal event data (video, stats, live feeds) into fluent text via generative models within a scalable production architecture.
cells.F645: Directly relevant to GSE's longer-horizon ambition of automated social/media content generation — a proven production blueprint for turning stats into narrative copy at scale.
cells.G645: Adapt this architecture for GSE's brand-constrained copy: generate pick commentary/narratives programmatically while enforcing the 'math you can read, not AI' lint rule via template-constrained generation.

cells.C646: Effects of term weighting approach with and without stop words removing on Arabic text classification
cells.D646: Compares binary vs. term-frequency weighting with/without stop-word removal for classifying Arabic documents (including a sports category) into topics.
cells.E646: Empirically evaluates classic text-classification feature-weighting schemes across accuracy, recall, precision, and F-measure on an Arabic multi-topic corpus.
cells.F646: Very weak relevance — a classical NLP text-classification study unrelated to GSE's forecasting or calibration problems.
cells.G646: Only tangential use: informs basic feature-weighting choices if GSE ever builds non-English sports-news classification for its data pipeline.

cells.C647: SportsMetrics: Blending Text and Numerical Data to Understand Information Fusion in LLMs
cells.D647: Introduces four benchmark tasks testing LLMs' ability to fuse textual and numerical sports data (NBA/NFL play-by-play) under adversarial conditions like rule changes and scrambled narratives.
cells.E647: Constructs adversarial stress tests combining play-by-play text and statistics to probe LLM numerical reasoning, information fusion, and working-memory limitations.
cells.F647: Directly useful for GSE's internal agentic tooling — a concrete evaluation framework for whether their agents can reliably fuse text and numeric sports data without hallucinating stats.
cells.G647: Adopt SportsMetrics-style adversarial tests as a regression-testing harness for any LLM component touching pick generation or data validation, to catch numeric-fusion errors before they reach production.

cells.C648: Min-Max transformation for the measurement of sports performance through PIR
cells.D648: Proposes a min-max-transformed variant of basketball's Performance Index Rating (PIR) to better measure player performance, illustrated with Bird, Magic, Jordan, and Kobe career data.
cells.E648: Applies min-max normalization to an existing composite performance index to improve its interpretability and comparability for roster decisions and awards.
cells.F648: Directly relevant as a lightweight per-sport player-value feature GSE could add to its NBA modeling inputs, part of the broader push toward independent per-sport probability models.
cells.G648: Use the normalized PIR as a standardized cross-era comparability feature so GSE's ensemble can weight historical player performance consistently despite rule/era changes.

cells.C649: Haris: an Advanced Autonomous Mobile Robot for Smart Parking Assistance
cells.D649: Presents an autonomous SLAM-based robot that tracks vehicle locations via license-plate recognition for managing crowded parking, including at sports stadiums.
cells.E649: Combines simultaneous localization and mapping with computer-vision license-plate recognition and a backend mobile app for real-time vehicle-location tracking.
cells.F649: Not relevant to GSE's prediction/calibration domain — this is stadium infrastructure robotics, unrelated to their stats and picks product.
cells.G649: No meaningful application; at most a stretch idea for a future stadium-experience B2B add-on far outside current roadmap.

cells.C650: Multi-Camera Asynchronous Ball Localization and Trajectory Prediction with Factor Graphs and Human Poses
cells.D650: Uses multi-camera factor graphs plus a temporal convolutional network on human pose to localize tennis balls in 3D and predict spin/trajectory, cutting landing-position error by 63.6%.
cells.E650: Fuses asynchronous multi-camera 3D ball tracking with pose-derived spin priors within a factor-graph state estimator for real-time trajectory prediction.
cells.F650: Tangential — it's a physical trajectory-estimation problem (ball physics), not statistical outcome forecasting, so only loosely related to GSE's core modeling work.
cells.G650: The factor-graph approach to fusing sparse early observations with priors is conceptually similar to how GSE's 'bootstrap mode' could formally blend sparse early-season data with priors via a probabilistic graph rather than an ad hoc cap.

cells.C651: A comprehensive survey of the home advantage in American football
cells.D651: Analyzes two decades of NFL, NCAA, and high-school football data, finding home advantage is declining in the NFL and top college football but not in amateur leagues.
cells.E651: Uses uniform statistical comparison across leagues and decades to quantify and trend home-field advantage effects.
cells.F651: Directly relevant — home-field advantage is a core feature in sports prediction models, and its declining trend is exactly the kind of time-varying effect GSE's per-sport models should capture.
cells.G651: Build a dynamically-updating home-advantage prior per sport/league into GSE's models instead of a static coefficient, informed by this paper's league-specific decay trends.

cells.C652: Individual and team performance in cricket
cells.D652: Comprehensively analyzes One-Day International cricket performance, showing long-term success is predictable from early performance and that winning/losing streaks occur beyond random expectation.
cells.E652: Applies temporal pattern analysis and streak-significance testing to individual and team cricket performance data across specialist roles.
cells.F652: Directly relevant — streakiness beyond random chance and early-performance predictability are exactly the kind of signals a well-calibrated sports model should encode, applicable to any cricket-covering sport module.
cells.G652: Use the streak-significance test as a diagnostic tool to check whether GSE's settled-picks data shows genuine momentum effects the model should capture versus noise the calibrator is currently overfitting to.

cells.C653: In-plane Density Gradation of Shoe Midsoles for Optimized Cushioning Performance
cells.D653: Optimizes zonal foam density in running shoe midsoles using polyurea foams and an interior-point optimization algorithm to maximize cushioning while minimizing weight.
cells.E653: Builds density-dependent material models and solves a constrained optimization problem to allocate optimal foam densities across plantar zones.
cells.F653: Not relevant — pure materials-science/footwear engineering with no connection to GSE's statistical prediction or data platform.
cells.G653: No honest application beyond noting the optimization framework (interior-point method) is a generic technique that also appears in operations-research-flavored sports scheduling, unrelated to this paper's domain.

cells.C654: Early Career Wins and Tournament Prestige Characterize Tennis Players' Trajectories
cells.D654: Uses network science on ATP tournament co-attendance to show that the prestige of a player's first tournament win strongly predicts becoming a top player.
cells.E654: Builds an eigenvector-centrality-based tournament prestige network and correlates early-career milestone events with long-term career trajectories.
cells.F654: Relevant as a feature-engineering idea — tournament prestige and early-milestone signals could enrich GSE's player-level features for individual sports like tennis.
cells.G654: Encode tournament prestige as a typed edge-weight in the Intelligence Graph, letting the ensemble learn how early achievements propagate into longer-term win-probability estimates.

cells.C655: TRACE: A Time-Relational Approximate Cubing Engine for Fast Data Insights
cells.D655: Presents a fast, low-cost time-relational OLAP cube engine that materializes important data slices over time for interactive analytical queries, illustrated with business/sports revenue examples.
cells.E655: Pre-materializes the most important parts of a data cube to enable low-latency interactive slice-and-dice queries on time-relational metrics.
cells.F655: Relevant to GSE's data-pipeline/ETL reliability goals — a lightweight cubing approach could power internal dashboards analyzing pick performance, calibration windows, or CLV across sports/time without expensive full scans.
cells.G655: Use TRACE-style approximate cubing to power a real-time internal dashboard tracking Brier score and ECE trends per sport/time-window, directly supporting the '3 consecutive green windows' launch gate tracking.

cells.C656: Robust CNN-based Respiration Rate Estimation for Smartwatch PPG and IMU
cells.D656: Proposes a CNN with dilated residual inception modules to estimate respiration rate from noisy wrist-worn PPG/IMU signals, outperforming existing methods under free-living conditions.
cells.E656: Extracts temporal features from multimodal wearable sensor signals using dilated convolutions to robustly infer a physiological time series despite noise.
cells.F656: Not directly relevant to GSE's product, but the noise-robust time-series extraction architecture is a generic technique that could inform denoising odds/stats feeds.
cells.G656: Borrow the dilated-residual-inception architecture as a denoising front-end for noisy scraped or live odds time-series before they hit the prediction engine.

cells.C657: Name order and the top elite: Long-term effects of a hidden curriculum
cells.D657: Finds that Japanese students whose surnames fall early in alphabetical class lists are more likely to become part of the ruling elite but less likely to appear in entertainment/sports lists.
cells.E657: Statistically analyzes surname-initial distributions among elite figures across domains to test long-term effects of classroom name-order exposure.
cells.F657: Not relevant to GSE's technical stack — a social-science study on educational hidden curricula with only incidental mention of sports as an outcome category.
cells.G657: No honest strong application; at best a curiosity for understanding demographic biases in athlete/administrator datasets scraped for other purposes.

cells.C658: FightTracker: Real-time predictive analytics for Mixed Martial Arts bouts
cells.D658: Builds real-time UFC fight-outcome prediction models achieving 80% accuracy, deployed as a live app, with a backtested live-betting strategy yielding 90% ROI over 8 weeks.
cells.E658: Uses regression models on in-round fight statistics fed by live ESPN data to predict judges' scores and win probability in real time via a Shiny app.

cells.G658: Study FightTracker's in-round statistical features as a template for building a live, in-play confidence-adjusting layer for GSE's combat-sport or other live-scoring picks.

cells.C659: Hydrodynamic characteristics of sea kayak traditional paddles
cells.D659: Studies drag/lift forces of traditional vs. modern sea kayak paddles using wind-tunnel measurements and stroke-motion modeling.
cells.E659: Measures hydrodynamic force coefficients experimentally and computes stroke-averaged forces to compare paddle efficiency and comfort.
cells.F659: Not relevant — pure fluid-dynamics engineering study with no connection to GSE's statistical prediction platform.
cells.G659: No honest application beyond noting it as an example of niche sports-equipment physics research entirely outside GSE's scope.

cells.C660: EasyVolcap: Accelerating Neural Volumetric Video Research
cells.D660: Releases an open-source Python/PyTorch library unifying multi-view capture, 4D neural scene reconstruction, and rendering for volumetric video applications including sports broadcasting.
cells.E660: Provides a modular pipeline for neural volumetric video capture, reconstruction, and efficient dynamic rendering usable across research and applications.
cells.F660: Not relevant to GSE's statistical engine — this is a broadcast/VR rendering toolkit, unrelated to prediction or calibration work.

cells.C661: On enforcing dyadic-type homogeneous binary function product constraints in MatBase
cells.D661: Describes algorithms within the MatBase system for automatically enforcing 18 types of binary function-product database constraints, applicable to domains including sports data.
cells.E661: Uses the Elementary Mathematical Data Model to declaratively specify and auto-generate enforcement code for complex relational integrity constraints.
cells.F661: Modestly relevant to GSE's Prisma/PostgreSQL data layer — a formal approach to enforcing complex referential constraints could improve data-pipeline reliability for pick lifecycle integrity.

cells.C662: REACT: Recognize Every Action Everywhere All At Once
cells.D662: Presents a transformer-based vision-language architecture for group activity recognition in videos, outperforming prior state-of-the-art on sports and social-scene benchmarks.
cells.E662: Uses a Vision-Language Encoder plus Action Decoder and Actor Fusion blocks to jointly model spatio-temporal and multi-modal actor interactions.
cells.F662: Not directly relevant — a computer-vision group-activity recognition model, unrelated to GSE's statistical calibration and forecasting problems.
cells.G662: No strong application; tangential idea for a future video-based tactical-analysis add-on well beyond current roadmap.

cells.C663: Ego-Exo4D: Understanding Skilled Human Activity from First- and Third-Person Perspectives
cells.D663: Releases a massive multimodal video dataset (audio, gaze, IMU, 3D pose, expert commentary) of skilled activities including sports, with benchmark tasks for proficiency estimation.
cells.E663: Captures synchronized ego- and exocentric multimodal video with expert commentary across many skilled activities to support first-person activity-understanding research.

cells.C664: Multi-agent statistical discriminative sub-trajectory mining and an application to NBA basketball
cells.D664: Proposes a method to statistically identify sub-trajectories of multiple agents (ball, players) that discriminate effective from ineffective NBA plays using SportVU tracking data.
cells.E664: Uses Hausdorff-distance-based discriminative sub-matrix mining over multi-agent trajectory matrices to find statistically significant play patterns.
cells.F664: Directly relevant — a rigorous statistical method for extracting predictive play-level signals from tracking data, useful feature-engineering input for GSE's NBA-specific probability models.

cells.C665: BERT Goes Off-Topic: Investigating the Domain Transfer Challenge using Genre Classification
cells.D665: Shows PLMs like BERT and GPT-3 suffer performance drops under topic-domain shift (e.g., trained on politics, tested on sport) and demonstrates synthetic-data augmentation can partially close the gap.
cells.E665: Quantifies domain-transfer failure in genre/text classifiers and mitigates it via topically-controlled synthetic text augmentation for fine-tuning.

cells.C666: Challenges in Video-Based Infant Action Recognition: A Critical Examination of the State of the Art
cells.D666: Introduces an infant-action dataset and benchmarks skeleton-based action-recognition models, finding a large accuracy gap versus adult action recognition.
cells.E666: Applies existing skeleton-based action-recognition architectures (e.g., PoseC3D) to a novel infant-movement dataset and analyzes failure modes.
cells.F666: Not relevant — infant developmental action recognition has no connection to GSE's sports prediction domain.
cells.G666: No honest application beyond the generic observation that domain-specific data gaps (like GSE's sparse-sport 'bootstrap mode' problem) recur across very different ML fields.

cells.C667: MUDD: A New Re-Identification Dataset with Efficient Annotation for Off-Road Racers in Extreme Conditions
cells.D667: Introduces a large-scale motorcycle-racer re-identification benchmark under mud/motion-blur conditions and shows fine-tuned re-id models greatly outperform out-of-the-box ones.
cells.E667: Provides an efficiently-annotated dataset and benchmarks re-identification models (OSNet, ResNet-50) under extreme visual occlusion for athlete tracking.
cells.F667: Not directly relevant — a computer-vision re-identification benchmark unrelated to GSE's statistical modeling stack.

cells.C668: Surveying Wikipedians: a dataset of users and contributors' practices on Wikipedia in 8 languages
cells.D668: Releases a large multilingual survey dataset on Wikipedia readers' and contributors' demographics, activities, and trust attitudes, including their sports/cultural engagement.
cells.E668: Collects and structures 100k+ survey responses across 8 languages on Wikipedia usage patterns and socioeconomic characteristics.
cells.F668: Not relevant — a social-science dataset on Wikipedia usage with no connection to GSE's sports prediction platform.

cells.C669: The Paradox of Talent: how Chance affects Success in Tennis Tournaments
cells.D669: Uses an agent-based model calibrated on a decade of ATP data to show luck/chance dominates over talent (talent weight ~0.2-0.3) in determining tennis tournament outcomes among elite players.
cells.E669: Simulates tennis matches with a single talent-weighting parameter and calibrates it against real tournament and ranking network data to isolate luck's contribution.
cells.F669: Directly relevant — decomposing outcome variance into skill vs. luck is core to well-calibrated probabilistic forecasting, and this offers a concrete method GSE could apply per sport.
cells.G669: Use the talent-weighting parameter as a sport-specific 'predictability ceiling' diagnostic, helping GSE set realistic Brier-score/ECE targets and communicate honestly about inherent unpredictability in close-talent matchups.

cells.C670: ESPORT: Electronic Sports Professionals Observations and Reflections on Training
cells.D670: Interviews top-tier esports players, coaches, and managers about psychological, physical, and nutritional preparation practices across multiple game titles from 2015-2020.
cells.E670: Conducts and qualitatively codes structured interviews, rating responses via expert-panel consensus to identify key training success factors.
cells.F670: Not relevant to GSE's forecasting/calibration technical stack — a qualitative HCI study of esports athlete preparation.
cells.G670: No strong application; at best distant inspiration for athlete-preparation content within the Galaxy Dynasty game layer's narrative material.

cells.C671: Active Exploration in Iterative Gaussian Process Regression for Uncertainty Modeling in Autonomous Racing
cells.D671: Proposes an active-exploration MPC strategy that purposefully collects high-uncertainty data to iteratively improve Gaussian Process models of vehicle dynamics and opponent behavior in racing.
cells.E671: Balances racing objectives with an exploration criterion in model-predictive control to target data collection where GP model uncertainty is highest, then retrains iteratively.
cells.F671: Relevant as uncertainty-quantification inspiration — GP regression with explicit uncertainty tracking is directly applicable to GSE's need for better ensemble/uncertainty-aware confidence adjustment ('bootstrap mode').
cells.G671: Apply active-exploration logic to GSE's data-ingestion prioritization: dynamically flag which sparse-data sports/matchups need targeted additional scraping to reduce model uncertainty fastest.

cells.C672: Automatic Edge Error Judgment in Figure Skating Using 3D Pose Estimation from a Monocular Camera and IMUs
cells.D672: Uses monocular-camera 3D pose estimation combined with IMU data to automatically detect figure-skating edge errors with 83% accuracy.
cells.E672: Extracts 3D joint positions from smartphone video plus inertial sensors and classifies motion patterns to judge a specific technical scoring criterion.
cells.F672: Not relevant to GSE's product — a computer-vision judging-automation tool for figure skating, unrelated to statistical forecasting.
cells.G672: No honest strong application beyond the generic idea of automated objective scoring, distant from GSE's deterministic math-based positioning.

cells.C673: Maximizing Diver Score by Examining Discrepancies in Diver Competency and Judges' Marks
cells.D673: Analyzes discrepancies between divers' true competency (mean historical score) and judges' actual scores to uncover potential scoring biases in springboard diving.
cells.E673: Defines a competency baseline from historical performance and measures deviation from judges' marks within a given meet as a bias-detection metric.
cells.F673: Modestly relevant — a bias-detection methodology (comparing expected vs. observed scores) is conceptually close to detecting systematic miscalibration in GSE's own settled-pick outcomes.

cells.C674: A Large-Scale Exploratory Study of Android Sports Apps in the Google Play Store
cells.D674: Empirically studies 2000+ sports apps in Google Play, analyzing functionality, user-review topics, and factors driving negative sentiment via topic modeling and sentiment analysis.
cells.E674: Uses manual categorization, topic modeling on reviews, and sentiment/rating analysis to characterize an entire app-store category at scale.
cells.F674: Relevant for competitive/product intelligence — this analysis method could be applied to benchmark GSE against competitor sports-prediction apps to identify common user pain points.
cells.G674: Run the same review-mining methodology against competitor sports-prediction/betting apps to systematically surface UX and trust complaints GSE's product and compliance toolkit should proactively address.

cells.C675: GroundLink: A Dataset Unifying Human Body Movement and Ground Reaction Dynamics
cells.D675: Releases a dataset pairing motion capture with real ground reaction force/center-of-pressure measurements and a benchmark model predicting physics from kinematics for movements including tennis swings.
cells.E675: Uses embedded force platforms to capture synchronized GRF/CoP with kinematic mocap, training a neural network to predict physical forces from movement alone.
cells.F675: Not relevant to GSE's statistical prediction stack — a biomechanics/animation dataset with no direct calibration or forecasting application.
cells.G675: No honest strong application beyond noting physics-informed motion data could theoretically feed a distant future injury-risk feature.

cells.C676: Model-based Clustering for Network Data via a Latent Shrinkage Position Cluster Model
cells.D676: Introduces a Bayesian nonparametric latent-position clustering model that simultaneously infers the latent space dimension and cluster count for network data, applied to sports and political Twitter networks.
cells.E676: Uses a shrinkage prior on latent-position variances combined with a sparse finite Gaussian mixture to jointly infer dimensionality and clustering without model comparison.
cells.F676: Relevant to GSE's Bayesian-methods interest and Intelligence Graph ambitions — a principled way to cluster entities (teams, players, fans) in network data without manually choosing cluster counts.
cells.G676: Use this shrinkage clustering approach to automatically discover latent groupings of teams/players in the Intelligence Graph (e.g., playing-style archetypes) without pre-specifying how many clusters exist.

cells.C677: Selecting the best compositions of a wheelchair basketball team: a data-driven approach
cells.D677: Combines a Bayesian longitudinal performance model with integer linear optimization to select optimal wheelchair basketball lineups, incorporating posterior uncertainty into the optimization.
cells.E677: Propagates uncertainty from a Bayesian longitudinal model's posterior predictive distribution directly into an integer-programming lineup-optimization objective.
cells.F677: Directly relevant — a concrete example of properly propagating Bayesian uncertainty into a downstream decision optimization, exactly the discipline GSE needs for its bootstrap-mode confidence adjustments and ensemble design.
cells.G677: Adapt this Bayesian-uncertainty-into-optimization pipeline for GSE's pick-selection logic, using posterior uncertainty to directly gate which picks get published versus suppressed under bootstrap mode.

cells.C678: Should Sports Professionals Consider Their Adversary's Strategy? A Case Study of Match Play in Golf
cells.D678: Uses PGA Tour data to show that adjusting golf match-play strategy based on an opponent's strategy yields only modest benefit, confirming that stroke-play-optimal strategy is usually sufficient.
cells.E678: Compares strategic outcomes under adversary-aware versus adversary-agnostic optimization to quantify the marginal value of game-theoretic opponent modeling.
cells.F678: Relevant as game-theory methodology for sports strategy modeling — informs whether GSE's models need explicit opponent-strategy terms or can rely on simpler independent-team modeling.
cells.G678: Use this cost-benefit framework to decide whether GSE should invest engineering effort in explicit opponent-interaction modeling for its ensemble versus focusing resources elsewhere, based on expected marginal accuracy gain.

cells.C679: Early Churn Prediction from Large Scale User-Product Interaction Time Series
cells.D679: Treats churn prediction as multivariate time-series classification for a 200M+ user fantasy sports platform, showing deep neural networks on user activity outperform manual feature engineering.

cells.F679: Directly relevant — a production-scale fantasy-sports churn model is a close analog for GSE's own user-retention needs, and the time-series DNN approach parallels their forecasting infrastructure needs.

cells.C680: DROP: Dynamics Responses from Human Motion Prior and Projective Dynamics
cells.D680: Presents a physics-based human motion simulator combining a generative kinematic motion prior with projective dynamics for physically responsive character animation.
cells.E680: Integrates a learned generative motion prior as one of several projective-dynamics energies to produce stable, physically plausible character responses to perturbations.
cells.F680: Not relevant — character animation physics simulation, unrelated to GSE's statistical prediction platform.
cells.G680: No honest strong application; purely off-domain computer graphics research.

cells.C681: Transitioning To The Digital Generation Case Studies (ICT Education in Japan)
cells.D681: Reviews the history of ICT education policy in Japan and analyzes smartphone learning-app usage dynamics among young people during 2020.
cells.E681: Combines historical policy review with usage-dynamics analysis of ICT learning apps to characterize digital-native adoption patterns.
cells.F681: Not relevant — an education-policy and ICT-adoption study with no connection to GSE's sports prediction platform.
cells.G681: No honest application; entirely outside GSE's domain.

cells.C682: Using a quantitative assessment of propulsion biomechanics in wheelchair racing to guide the design of personalized gloves
cells.D682: Combines biomechanical measurement with athlete feedback to design and test personalized rigid wheelchair-racing gloves, finding a 45-degree wrist-extension prototype most effective.
cells.E682: Uses treadmill-based biomechanical testing alongside subjective user experience to iteratively prototype adaptive sports equipment.
cells.F682: Not relevant — adaptive sports equipment biomechanics/design study, unrelated to GSE's data/prediction platform.
cells.G682: No honest strong application; purely equipment-engineering research outside GSE's scope.

cells.C683: Judging a video by its bitstream cover
cells.D683: Classifies videos (including Sport category) directly from compressed bitstream statistics rather than decoded pixels, achieving over 80% accuracy at massive speed.
cells.E683: Extracts classification features purely from post-compression bitstream metadata, avoiding costly video decompression.
cells.F683: Weak relevance — a fast video-classification technique unrelated to GSE's core stats/calibration work, though shares the 'sport' category as one of many labels.

cells.C684: Design of Recognition and Evaluation System for Table Tennis Players' Motor Skills Based on Artificial Intelligence
cells.D684: Builds a wearable-device pipeline that recognizes and evaluates table tennis players' motor skills using feature-engineered BP neural networks, outperforming CNNs on recognition accuracy.
cells.E684: Collects motion data from a custom wearable, segments it via sliding windows into stroke-feature vectors, and classifies motor skills with a feature-based neural network.
cells.F684: Not relevant — wearable motion-recognition system for athlete training, unrelated to GSE's statistical forecasting/calibration stack.

cells.D685: Investigates using dynamic neural radiance fields to reconstruct novel-view soccer replays from multiple static broadcast cameras, showing promise but falling short of broadcast quality.
cells.E685: Composes synthetic soccer environments and tests dynamic NeRF variants to reconstruct large-scale, mostly-static scenes with small fast-moving elements.
cells.F685: Not relevant — a broadcast-replay rendering research project, unrelated to GSE's prediction/calibration technology.
cells.G685: No honest strong application; tangential idea only for a distant future immersive-replay B2B feature.

cells.C686: Text Encoders Lack Knowledge: Leveraging Generative LLMs for Domain-Specific Semantic Textual Similarity
cells.D686: Shows generative LLMs significantly outperform encoder-based models on semantic textual similarity tasks requiring world knowledge, including a new Sports-domain STS challenge set.
cells.E686: Reframes semantic textual similarity as text generation and evaluates it with domain-specific prompting against traditional encoder-based STS baselines.
cells.F686: Relevant to GSE's NLP style-control and content needs — better domain-specific semantic similarity could help detect banned 'AI-powered' phrasing variants or deduplicate/verify scraped sports content.
cells.G686: Use generative-LLM STS scoring to detect near-duplicate or plagiarized sports content scraped from multiple free sources, improving data-pipeline reliability before ingestion.

cells.C687: Jersey Number Recognition using Keyframe Identification from Low-Resolution Broadcast Videos
cells.D687: Proposes a keyframe-identification module plus spatio-temporal network that substantially improves jersey-number recognition accuracy in low-resolution soccer broadcast footage.
cells.E687: Filters video to frames likely to contain visible jersey numbers, then applies a multi-task spatio-temporal model to predict digit probabilities.
cells.F687: Not relevant to GSE's stats/calibration engine — a computer-vision player-identification tool, off their technical stack.
cells.G687: No honest strong application; distant idea for a future broadcast-analytics integration outside current roadmap.

cells.C688: Rethinking Evaluation Metric for Probability Estimation Models Using Esports Data
cells.D688: Proposes a novel 'Balance score' calibration metric that improves on Brier score and ECE (which is imperfectly approximated via binning) for evaluating esports win-probability models.
cells.E688: Analyzes theoretical properties of calibration metrics and derives a new score that more accurately approximates true expected calibration error without binning artifacts.
cells.F688: Highly relevant — directly targets GSE's exact launch-gate problem (Brier 0.2563, ECE 0.0699) with a proposed better calibration metric that avoids ECE's known binning bias.

cells.C689: A compendium of data sources for data science, machine learning, and artificial intelligence
cells.D689: Provides a broad, curated list of publicly known data sources across domains including finance, life sciences, retail, and sports, intended as a reference for ML practitioners.
cells.E689: Compiles and categorizes data-source references across multiple application domains without deep technical methodology.

cells.C690: Improved theoretical guarantee for rank aggregation via spectral method
cells.D690: Derives sharper error bounds for spectral ranking algorithms recovering true scores from noisy pairwise comparisons, improving sample-complexity guarantees over prior work.
cells.E690: Uses leave-one-out perturbation analysis to establish tighter entrywise eigenvector error bounds for normalized/unnormalized spectral ranking under the Erdős-Rényi outliers model.

cells.C691: The Quiet Eye Phenomenon in Minimally Invasive Surgery
cells.D691: Finds that the 'Quiet Eye' gaze behavior, previously studied in sports expertise, also predicts successful task execution and surgeon skill level in minimally invasive surgery.
cells.E691: Analyzes eye-gaze fixation data across two surgical datasets to identify a stable pre-movement fixation pattern correlated with expert performance.
cells.F691: Not relevant to GSE's statistical prediction platform — a gaze-behavior/expertise study transplanted from sports science into surgery, off their technical stack.

cells.C692: Mitigating Motion Blur for Robust 3D Baseball Player Pose Modeling for Pitch Analysis
cells.D692: Proposes a synthetic-data augmentation pipeline to make pose-estimation models robust to motion blur in broadcast-quality baseball pitching videos, cutting pose-estimation loss significantly.

cells.C693: Golf Strategy Optimization and the "Drive for show, putt for dough" adage
cells.D693: Develops a computationally tractable exact Markov Decision Process model for optimal golf stroke-play strategy using PGA Tour and course-imagery data, testing a popular golf adage.
cells.E693: Formulates golf strategy as a stochastic shortest-path MDP and solves it exactly (not via Q-learning heuristics) at full real-world scale through careful engineering.
cells.F693: Relevant methodologically — demonstrates that exact, tractable MDP solutions are feasible at scale for sports strategy, a useful pattern for any sequential-decision aspect of GSE's modeling (e.g., in-play win probability updates).
cells.G693: Apply exact MDP solving (rather than approximate ML heuristics) to model sequential in-game state transitions for a specific GSE sport, potentially yielding more interpretable, deterministic 'math you can read' probability updates aligned with their brand positioning.

cells.D694: Introduces a two-stream video-prediction framework that decouples motion from appearance via motion matrices, outperforming state-of-the-art on datasets including UCF Sports with a smaller model.
cells.E694: Constructs appearance-agnostic motion matrices representing temporal patch similarity as the sole input to a compact motion-prediction module.
cells.F694: Not relevant to GSE's statistical forecasting — this is pixel-level video prediction, unrelated to outcome/probability modeling.

cells.C695: The APX-hardness of the Traveling Tournament Problem
cells.D695: Proves that the Traveling Tournament Problem (TTP-k), a benchmark sports-scheduling optimization problem, is APX-hard for any fixed k≥3.
cells.E695: Provides a theoretical computational-complexity reduction establishing hardness-of-approximation results for round-robin travel-minimizing schedules.
cells.F695: Weak but honest relevance — sports scheduling complexity theory isn't part of GSE's current product, though schedule-aware features (travel distance, rest days) do feed prediction models.
cells.G695: Use TTP research as background for engineering a 'travel fatigue/rest-day' feature pipeline, even without needing to solve the full scheduling optimization themselves.

cells.C696: Towards Real-Time Analysis of Broadcast Badminton Videos
cells.D696: Proposes an end-to-end computer-vision pipeline analyzing live badminton broadcast video to compute real-time player movement distance and heatmaps, deployed during the Premier Badminton League 2019.
cells.E696: Removes replays/redundant footage, tracks players frame-by-frame, and computes on-court distance/speed metrics purely from visual broadcast feeds.
cells.F696: Not directly relevant to GSE's stats-based prediction engine — a live broadcast-video analytics tool, off their data-ingestion approach (stats/odds feeds, not video).
cells.G696: No honest strong application; tangential idea only for a distant future live-broadcast analytics integration.

cells.C697: Graph Encoding and Neural Network Approaches for Volleyball Analytics: From Game Outcome to Individual Play Predictions
cells.D697: Introduces a graph-encoding scheme adding contact-by-contact context to volleyball data, showing GNNs substantially outperform baselines on rally-outcome, set-location, and hit-type prediction.
cells.E697: Encodes volleyball plays as graphs capturing sequential ball-contact context, then applies graph neural networks for multiple prediction tasks compared to non-graph baselines.
cells.F697: Directly relevant — demonstrates graph-based feature encoding meaningfully beats baseline models for sports outcome prediction, directly applicable to fixing GSE's core model that currently loses to a naive baseline.
cells.G697: Apply the same contact-by-contact graph-encoding idea to GSE's Intelligence Graph, representing sequential game events (drives, possessions, at-bats) as graphs fed into GNN-based ensemble members instead of flat box-score features.

cells.C698: Opponents and proponents of the war in Ukraine in Russian social media: who are they?
cells.D698: Compares political identity, values, and interests of pro-war and anti-war Russian social media users, finding shared interest in sport/music groups despite ideological divides.
cells.E698: Analyzes self-reported profile data and group subscriptions on VK to characterize and contrast two opposing political user populations.
cells.F698: Not relevant — a sociopolitical social-media study with only incidental sports mention, unrelated to GSE's prediction platform.
cells.G698: No honest application; entirely outside GSE's scope.

cells.C699: Design Space Exploration on Efficient and Accurate Human Pose Estimation from Sparse IMU-Sensing
cells.D699: Performs a simulative design-space exploration of IMU sensor count/placement to balance human pose estimation accuracy against hardware/energy cost for applications including sports.
cells.E699: Trains deep learning models on synthetic IMU data from varied sensor configurations and proposes a combined accuracy-resource trade-off metric to identify optimal configurations.
cells.F699: Not relevant to GSE's statistical prediction stack — a wearable-sensor hardware/accuracy trade-off study, off their technical domain.
cells.G699: No honest strong application beyond the generic 'accuracy vs. resource cost' trade-off framing, which loosely echoes engineering trade-offs in GSE's own compute-constrained ensemble design.

cells.C700: Miss It Like Messi: Extracting Value from Off-Target Shots in Soccer
cells.D700: Proposes generative-model-based soccer shooting-skill metrics that extract predictive signal from off-target shot trajectories, which prior expected-goals metrics discarded entirely.
cells.E700: Fits a player-specific mixture of truncated bivariate Gaussian distributions to shot trajectories, enabling non-zero valuation of missed shots for more stable, predictive skill metrics.
cells.F700: Highly relevant — directly demonstrates extracting more signal from previously-discarded sparse soccer event data, exactly the kind of technique that could improve GSE's MLS/soccer-specific probability models and combat sparse-data issues.
cells.G700: Apply the same generative trajectory-mixture approach to other 'near-miss' sparse events across GSE's covered sports (e.g., near-interceptions in NFL, near-misses in MLB) to enrich feature signal beyond binary outcome data.

cells.C701: A Virtual Reality Game to Improve Physical and Cognitive Acuity
cells.D701: Presents and iteratively evaluates a VR game (Virtual Human Benchmark) simulating the BATAK lightboard for training reaction time, hand-eye coordination, and visual memory.
cells.E701: Builds a 3D VR simulation with reaction/accumulator/sequence modes and logs performance metrics for coaching/rehabilitation use, validated through two rounds of user studies.
cells.F701: Weak relevance — a VR training-game usability study, but conceptually adjacent to GSE's 'Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR' persistent web game ambitions.
cells.G701: Borrow the game's mode structure (reaction/accumulator/sequence) and iterative usability-testing methodology as a design pattern for building engaging mini-games within Galaxy Dynasty.

cells.C702: Maximizing Success Rate of Payment Routing using Non-stationary Bandits
cells.D702: Deploys non-stationary multi-armed bandit algorithms to optimize payment routing at scale on the fantasy sports platform Dream11, improving transaction success rate by 0.92% over rule-based methods in live experiments.
cells.E702: Uses a Ray-based scalable bandit architecture to continuously select near-optimal payment routes based on recent transaction history, validated via live A/B experiments.
cells.F702: Relevant both as an online-learning/bandits technique and as a real production case study from a major fantasy sports platform, directly transferable to GSE's own infrastructure decisions (e.g., dynamic routing/allocation problems).
cells.G702: Apply non-stationary bandits to dynamically allocate GSE's data-ingestion or job-queue (BullMQ) resources across competing data sources/sports based on recently observed reliability and freshness.

cells.C703: PressureTransferNet: Human Attribute Guided Dynamic Ground Pressure Profile Transfer using 3D simulated Pressure Maps
cells.D703: Proposes an encoder-decoder model that transfers ground-pressure activity profiles across different body attributes using simulated pressure maps, aiding data augmentation for human activity recognition.
cells.E703: Uses simulated sensor data and an encoder-decoder architecture to synthesize body-specific pressure maps conditioned on a target attribute vector.
cells.F703: Not relevant to GSE's statistical prediction platform — a sensor-simulation/data-augmentation technique for activity recognition, off their technical stack.
cells.G703: No honest strong application beyond the generic idea of synthetic data augmentation for sparse-data domains, tangential to GSE's own sparse-sport bootstrap challenges.

cells.C704: Fine-Grained Sports, Yoga, and Dance Postures Recognition: A Benchmark Analysis
cells.D704: Introduces new benchmark image datasets for sports, dance, and yoga posture classification and proposes SYD-Net, a patch-attention CNN achieving state-of-the-art accuracy on Yoga-82.
cells.E704: Uses a patch-based self-attention mechanism atop standard CNN backbones combined with random-erasing augmentation for fine-grained pose classification.
cells.F704: Not relevant to GSE's stats/calibration engine — a computer-vision pose-classification benchmark, off their technical domain.
cells.G704: No honest strong application; distant idea only for a future pose-classification feature unrelated to current roadmap.

cells.C705: DoDo Learning: DOmain-DemOgraphic Transfer in Language Models for Detecting Abuse Targeted at Public Figures
cells.D705: Studies cross-domain (sport vs. politics) and cross-demographic generalization of abuse-detection classifiers, finding small diverse datasets and cross-domain training aid generalizability.
cells.E705: Fine-tunes language models on a novel DODO dataset spanning domain-demographic pairs and analyzes transfer dynamics between groups.
cells.F705: Modestly relevant — abuse/toxicity detection generalization techniques could inform GSE's trust/compliance toolkit for moderating user-generated content or social channels.
cells.G705: Apply the cross-domain generalization findings to build a compact, diverse training set for GSE's own content-moderation classifier, ensuring it generalizes from sports-forum abuse to other channels like the Galaxy Dynasty game community.

cells.C706: A Spectral Approach for the Dynamic Bradley-Terry Model
cells.D706: Introduces Kernel Rank Centrality, a nonparametric spectral ranker for dynamic pairwise-comparison rankings, deriving its asymptotic distribution for predictive inference and outperforming Elo on NBA data.
cells.E706: Applies kernel smoothing within a Markov-chain spectral ranking framework, using a group-inverse technique to derive precise uncertainty bounds for real-time rankings.
cells.F706: Highly relevant — a nonparametric, uncertainty-quantified alternative to Elo-style ranking directly comparable to GSE's core prediction problem, offering both better forecasting and calibrated uncertainty for the launch-gate metrics.
cells.G706: Replace or supplement GSE's static per-sport ranking components with Kernel Rank Centrality to get real-time updated rankings plus rigorous uncertainty bounds usable directly in bootstrap-mode confidence capping.

cells.C707: Automated Hit-frame Detection for Badminton Match Analysis
cells.D707: Builds an automated pipeline detecting hit-frames in badminton broadcast video via rally trimming, player/court keypoint detection, and shuttlecock direction prediction, achieving 99% shot-angle accuracy.
cells.E707: Chains multiple deep-learning detection stages (video trimming, keypoint detection, direction prediction) to automatically extract structured hit-event data from raw match video.
cells.F707: Not directly relevant to GSE's data pipeline (stats/odds feeds rather than video), though conceptually similar to their goal of extracting structured events from raw sources.
cells.G707: The multi-stage 'raw feed to structured event' pipeline pattern could inspire how GSE's data-ingestion team structures a video-to-structured-event extractor if they ever add broadcast video as a data source.

cells.C708: Weakly Supervised Multi-Modal 3D Human Body Pose Estimation for Autonomous Driving
cells.D708: Presents a weakly supervised camera-LiDAR fusion method for 3D human pose estimation targeted at autonomous vehicles, outperforming prior work on the Waymo Open Dataset without full 3D keypoint labels.
cells.E708: Uses pseudo-labels generated from LiDAR-to-image projections combined with an off-the-shelf 2D joint extractor to train pose estimators without expensive manual 3D annotation.
cells.F708: Not relevant to GSE's product domain — an autonomous-driving pose-estimation paper mentioning sports only as a tangential application area for the general technique.
cells.G708: No honest strong application; the weak-supervision-via-pseudo-labels idea is generic but not a natural fit for GSE's structured-stats data pipeline.

cells.C709: CAMP: A Context-Aware Cricket Players Performance Metric
cells.D709: Proposes CAMP, a context-aware cricket player performance metric accounting for opponent strength and match pressure, which matches expert 'Man of the Match' selections 83% of the time, beating the DLS-based baseline.
cells.E709: Uses data-mining methods to weight individual contributions by contextual factors (opponent quality, pressure situations) rather than relying on raw aggregate statistics.
