cells.F709: Directly relevant — a validated, context-aware player-value metric is exactly the kind of feature-engineering improvement GSE needs to strengthen per-sport probability models beyond naive baselines.
cells.G709: Generalize CAMP's context-weighting approach (opponent strength, situational pressure) as a template feature-engineering pattern applied across GSE's other covered sports to boost predictive signal beyond box-score averages.

cells.C710: VIRD: Immersive Match Video Analysis for High-Performance Badminton Coaching
cells.D710: Builds a VR-based immersive badminton match-analysis tool using 3D reconstructed views, computer-vision-derived shot/pose data, and situated visualizations, validated with Olympic-level coaches.
cells.E710: Combines 3D scene reconstruction, computer-vision shot/pose extraction, and VR visualization to let coaches navigate spatial and temporal match data with embodied interaction.
cells.F710: Not relevant to GSE's core forecasting/calibration engine — an immersive coaching visualization tool, off their technical stack.
cells.G710: No honest strong application beyond distant inspiration for a future coach-facing B2B visualization product outside current roadmap.

cells.C711: Beep: Balancing Effectiveness and Efficiency when Finding Multivariate Patterns in Racket Sports
cells.D711: Proposes Beep, a locality-sensitive-hashing-accelerated algorithm for discovering noise-tolerant multivariate patterns across correlated event attributes in racket-sports data, ~5x faster than prior SOTA.
cells.E711: Introduces a novel event-encoding scheme combined with LSH-based acceleration to efficiently mine correlated multi-attribute patterns from sequential sports event data.
cells.F711: Modestly relevant — an efficient pattern-mining technique for multivariate, noisy event-based sports data, applicable to GSE's time-series/event-based data pipeline for feature discovery.
cells.G711: Use Beep-style LSH-accelerated pattern mining to automatically surface recurring multivariate tactical patterns across GSE's ingested event data, feeding candidate features into the per-sport ensemble.

cells.C712: Stop Simulating! Efficient Computation of Tournament Winning Probabilities
cells.D712: Shows that exact computation of tournament winning probabilities (e.g., FIFA World Cup) can be substantially faster than the standard tens-of-thousands-of-simulations Monte Carlo approach, regardless of the underlying match model.
cells.E712: Exploits tournament bracket structure to compute exact winning probabilities algebraically instead of via repeated simulation sampling.
cells.F712: Directly relevant — GSE likely computes tournament/futures win probabilities via simulation; this offers a provably faster, exact alternative applicable regardless of their underlying per-sport match model.
cells.G712: Replace Monte Carlo tournament simulations in GSE's futures/bracket picks with this exact computation method to cut compute cost and eliminate simulation noise from published probabilities, directly supporting the 'math you can read' positioning.

cells.C713: MuLMINet: Multi-Layer Multi-Input Transformer Network with Weighted Loss
cells.D713: Presents a multi-layer, multi-input transformer that predicts future badminton shot types and court coordinates from match sequence data, placing 2nd in the IJCAI CoachAI Badminton Challenge 2023.
cells.E713: Uses a weighted-loss multi-input transformer architecture to jointly predict discrete shot-type and continuous coordinate outputs from sequential shot history.
cells.F713: Modestly relevant — a transformer sequence-forecasting architecture for discrete+continuous joint prediction is a generic pattern transferable to GSE's own sequential-event forecasting (e.g., predicting next scoring play type and field position).
cells.G713: Adapt the multi-input transformer's joint discrete/continuous prediction head to model combined 'outcome type + point spread' predictions in a single GSE ensemble member instead of separate models.

cells.C714: Ranking Handball Teams from Statistical Strength Estimation
cells.D714: Uses a Conway-Maxwell-Poisson distribution to model goal-scoring and derive a cross-championship team-strength ranking for European women's handball, validated against real-season outcomes.
cells.E714: Fits a flexible discrete distribution handling non-equidispersion to goal counts, then derives a closed-form team-strength formula for cross-league comparison.
cells.F714: Directly relevant — a flexible count-distribution approach to team-strength estimation is exactly the kind of statistically rigorous, closed-form ('math you can read') model GSE needs for independent per-sport probability models.
cells.G714: Replace a naive Poisson goal-scoring assumption in GSE's soccer/hockey models with the Conway-Maxwell-Poisson to better capture over/under-dispersion, directly targeting the Brier score gap versus the naive baseline.

cells.C715: A Comprehensive Review of Automated Data Annotation Techniques in Human Activity Recognition
cells.D715: Provides a systematic taxonomy of automated data-annotation techniques used across Human Activity Recognition research, including sports applications, to reduce manual labeling burden.
cells.E715: Surveys and classifies existing automated/semi-automated annotation methodologies (e.g., weak supervision, active learning) applicable to sensor-based activity datasets.
cells.F715: Weak relevance — a survey of annotation automation for sensor-based HAR, tangential to GSE's structured stats data pipeline which doesn't primarily rely on manual video/sensor labeling.
cells.G715: Could loosely inform semi-automated labeling strategies if GSE ever needs to hand-verify scraped play-by-play data for quality control in the ingestion pipeline.

cells.C716: Bayesian taut splines for estimating the number of modes
cells.D716: Introduces a Bayesian method combining flexible kernel estimators and compositional splines to robustly estimate the number of modes in a density, demonstrated in a sports analytics case study.
cells.E716: Blends local and global density properties within a Bayesian inference framework, incorporating expert judgment for soft, uncertainty-aware mode estimation and testing.
cells.F716: Relevant — a Bayesian uncertainty-aware modeling technique with an explicit sports analytics use case, directly aligned with GSE's stated interest in Bayesian methods for calibration/ensemble work.
cells.G716: Use this multimodality-detection technique to check whether GSE's settled-pick outcome distributions are unexpectedly multimodal (e.g., due to distinct game-state regimes), which would explain part of the current calibration failure and suggest a mixture-model fix.

cells.C717: Understanding the power-law nature of participation in community sports organizations
cells.D717: Analyzes 6 years of participation data from 2,956 community sports members, finding activity frequency follows a power law explained by a novel Habit-Formation and Behavioral Inertia (HFBI) model.
cells.E717: Fits a behavioral model combining habit-formation and inertia mechanisms to reproduce observed power-law participation patterns and burst-quiet individual engagement cycles.
cells.F717: Tangential but honest — this models user engagement dynamics in a sports context, loosely relevant to understanding GSE's own user retention/engagement patterns rather than prediction accuracy.
cells.G717: Apply the HFBI behavioral model to GSE's user-engagement data to predict which users are entering a 'quiet' disengagement phase, informing targeted retention nudges within Galaxy Dynasty.

cells.C718: ContextLabeler Dataset: physical and virtual sensors data collected from smartphone usage in-the-wild
cells.D718: Releases a two-week, in-the-wild smartphone sensor dataset (motion, apps, proximity, weather) from three volunteers, labeled with daily activities including sport.
cells.E718: Passively collects heterogeneous physical/virtual sensor features from unconstrained smartphone usage, ground-truthed with activity labels for context-aware research.
cells.F718: Not relevant — a smartphone context-sensing dataset with sport as one incidental activity label, unrelated to GSE's sports-prediction platform.
cells.G718: No honest strong application beyond noting context-aware mobile sensing methodology, irrelevant to GSE's roadmap.

cells.C719: Surge Routing: Event-informed Multiagent Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Rideshare
cells.D719: Proposes a multiagent RL framework that uses internet event data (including sports games) to predict rideshare demand surges and learn cooperative fleet routing policies, tested on NYC data.
cells.E719: Combines textual event-description-based demand prediction with scalable multiagent reinforcement learning (one-agent-at-a-time rollout) to generate intersection-level routing policies.
cells.F719: Tangential — demonstrates using sports-event metadata as an exogenous demand-surge predictor, a pattern loosely relevant to how GSE might model attention/interest surges around major games, but the RL routing application itself is unrelated.
cells.G719: Reuse the event-driven demand-prediction component (not the routing RL) to forecast surges in user traffic/betting volume around major games, informing GSE's infrastructure scaling and content-push timing.

cells.C720: Physics-based Motion Retargeting from Sparse Inputs
cells.D720: Uses reinforcement learning in a physics simulator to retarget sparse VR headset/controller motion data onto avatars of varying skeleton structures in real time, tested on sports-like motions.
cells.E720: Trains an RL policy purely on human motion-capture data to imitate and retarget motion via physics simulation, without per-avatar artist animation.
cells.F720: Not relevant to GSE's statistical prediction platform — a VR avatar-animation technique, off their technical domain.
cells.G720: No honest strong application; distant idea only if Galaxy Dynasty ever adds full-body VR avatar interactions, far outside current scope.

cells.C721: SAHAAYAK 2023 -- the Multi Domain Bilingual Parallel Corpus of Sanskrit to Hindi for Machine Translation
cells.D721: Releases a 1.5M-sentence-pair Sanskrit-Hindi parallel corpus spanning multiple domains including sport, built via mining, cleaning, and alignment for machine translation research.
cells.E721: Combines mining from machine-readable and non-machine-readable sources with a normalization/alignment/cleaning pipeline to build a low-resource-language parallel corpus.
cells.F721: Not relevant — a low-resource machine-translation corpus with sport as one of several incidental content domains, unrelated to GSE's prediction platform.
cells.G721: No honest strong application beyond the generic idea of multi-source corpus-building/cleaning pipelines, distant from GSE's core needs.

cells.C722: FANET Experiment: Real-Time Surveillance Applications Connected to Image Processing System
cells.D722: Proposes a conceptual system combining flying ad-hoc networks (drones) with image enhancement for real-time surveillance including sports and media coverage.
cells.E722: Image enhancement/processing pipeline applied to video streams gathered by a fleet of networked drones (FANET).
cells.F722: Tangential -- GSE doesn't use drones; the image-enhancement-for-live-sports-coverage angle only loosely echoes their data-ingestion pipeline mission, not a direct technical fit.
cells.G722: Could inspire a live-broadcast overlay concept for Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR visuals sourced from camera feeds, though not a near-term priority.

cells.C723: A Badminton Recognition and Tracking System Based on Context Multi-feature Fusion
cells.D723: Presents a two-stage coarse-to-fine ball detection and trajectory-tracking method for badminton using contextual multi-feature fusion.
cells.E723: Combines rule-based trajectory clip trackers with two rounds of coarse-to-fine detection using contextual cues.
cells.F723: Stretch -- relevant only as an example of the raw event-level sports data (tracking/detection) that ultimately feeds odds/analytics providers GSE's ingestion pipeline consumes downstream.
cells.G723: Use the coarse-to-fine detection idea as a pattern for bootstrap mode: cheap coarse signal first, expensive refinement only when data is sparse.

cells.C724: TaiChi Action Capture and Performance Analysis with Multi-view RGB Cameras
cells.D724: Builds a multi-camera motion-capture and analysis pipeline for TaiChi performance using neural radiance fields and 3D skeleton fusion.
cells.E724: Combines classical multi-view geometry with implicit neural radiance fields for 3D pose/surface reconstruction and motion normalization.
cells.F724: Minimal direct tie -- GSE does not do video/motion capture; this is core-sport biomechanics computer vision, outside the prediction engine's scope.
cells.G724: Interesting only as inspiration for a future athlete-avatar 'form analysis' mini-feature within Galaxy Dynasty, far outside current blockers.

cells.C725: Multi-task Item-attribute Graph Pre-training for Strict Cold-start Item Recommendation
cells.D725: Introduces ColdGPT, a pre-trained item-attribute knowledge graph that transfers signal from multiple data sources to solve strict cold-start recommendation.
cells.E725: Multi-task graph pre-training aligning item content, purchase sequences, and reviews via alignment-and-uniformity losses into a shared item-attribute graph.
cells.F725: Directly analogous to GSE's bootstrap-mode problem -- cold-start/sparse-data recommendation mirrors new teams/players/markets with no settled-pick history, mapping onto the planned Intelligence Graph.
cells.G725: Apply the same attribute-graph pre-training trick to seed priors for a new sport/market's probability model before any picks have settled.

cells.D726: Presents VisCommentator, a tool that recommends and inserts data visualizations into sports broadcast videos using ML-based data extraction.
cells.E726: Combines a design-space taxonomy of augmented-video elements with ML-based automatic data extraction and visualization recommendation.
cells.F726: Directly useful for GSE's automated social/media content generation ambitions -- turning picks and stats into shareable augmented video content.
cells.G726: Auto-generate short 'augmented reveal' video clips showing a pick's model reasoning overlaid on live game footage for social distribution.

cells.C727: Human Activity Behavioural Pattern Recognition in Smarthome with Long-hour Data Collection
cells.D727: Combines ambient and wearable sensors with deep learning (GRU, 95% accuracy) to recognize human activities and derive long-term behavioral patterns.
cells.E727: Hybrid sensor fusion (PIR, pressure, accelerometer, gyroscope) feeding a GRU-based activity classifier plus pattern-frequency analysis.
cells.F727: Weak tie -- shares only the general sensor time-series-to-pattern-recognition machinery, not applicable to GSE's odds/pick data.
cells.G727: The behavioral-pattern-over-time framing could inspire modeling anomalous bettor/user engagement patterns in GSE's own product analytics.

cells.C728: Discovering Intrinsic Spatial-Temporal Logic Rules to Explain Human Actions
cells.D728: Learns interpretable spatial-temporal logic rules explaining player movement via an EM algorithm, validated on NBA player trajectories.
cells.E728: Expectation-maximization treats logic-rule content as latent variables, alternating rule-posterior inference and joint rule/parameter optimization.
cells.F728: Directly relevant -- an interpretable rule-discovery method for NBA trajectory data speaks to GSE's 'math you can read' brand and could feed sport-specific feature engineering.
cells.G728: Publish the discovered interpretable logic rules as human-readable justifications alongside a pick, reinforcing the 'not AI, math you can read' positioning.

cells.C729: Shannon Entropy and Herfindahl-Hirschman Index as Team's Performance and Competitive Balance Indicators in Cyclist Multi-Stage Races
cells.D729: Applies Shannon entropy and the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index to quantify team performance and competitive balance in multi-stage cycling races.
cells.E729: Computes entropy/HHI from ranking/time distributions and fits Feller-Pareto distributions to team performance data.
cells.F729: Directly relevant -- competitive-balance and entropy metrics could become new per-sport diagnostic features for GSE's calibration/ensemble work, especially in less-modeled sports.
cells.G729: Use HHI/entropy of a market's odds distribution as a real-time market-efficiency proxy akin to closing-line value, especially in thin/illiquid sports.

cells.C730: Evaluating Superhuman Models with Consistency Checks
cells.D730: Proposes evaluating superhuman ML models via logical consistency checks rather than ground-truth accuracy, applied to chess, forecasting, and legal judgment (including GPT-4 sports-record forecasts).
cells.E730: Surfaces contradictions (e.g., same board valued differently, non-monotonic forecasts) as an evaluation proxy when ground truth is unavailable.
cells.F730: Directly useful for GSE's calibration gate -- consistency checks could supplement Brier/ECE as diagnostics before enough settled picks exist to trust accuracy metrics.
cells.G730: Build automated consistency-check unit tests into the prediction-engine CI (e.g., symmetric matchups get symmetric probabilities) as an early-warning signal for calibration regressions.

cells.C731: Skill-Critic: Refining Learned Skills for Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
cells.D731: Introduces Skill-Critic, a hierarchical RL algorithm that fine-tunes both low- and high-level policies using offline-learned skill latents, tested on Gran Turismo racing.
cells.E731: Joint optimization of a low-level skill policy and high-level skill-selection policy, regularized by an offline latent skill space.
cells.F731: Stretch -- RL policy learning for racing control doesn't map onto GSE's supervised probabilistic forecasting problem.
cells.G731: Tangential inspiration for structuring internal Jarvis/Hermes/Fable coding agents as hierarchical 'skill' policies (high-level task selection, low-level execution fine-tuning).

cells.C732: Ball Trajectory Inference from Multi-Agent Sports Contexts Using Set Transformer and Hierarchical Bi-LSTM
cells.D732: Infers a soccer ball's trajectory from player-only tracking data using a Set Transformer plus hierarchical Bi-LSTM, enabling ball-tracking-free analytics.
cells.E732: Permutation-invariant Set Transformer encodes multi-agent player context; hierarchical Bi-LSTM predicts possession then trajectory with a physical-realism loss.
cells.F732: Directly useful -- a cost-efficient way to reconstruct richer event data from cheaper, freely available player-tracking data, aiding GSE's multi-source free-data ingestion strategy.
cells.G732: Apply the same infer-missing-signal-from-correlated-agents trick to impute missing odds/lines across bookmakers when The Odds API has gaps for a market.

cells.C733: SentiGOLD: A Large Bangla Gold Standard Multi-Domain Sentiment Analysis Dataset and its Evaluation
cells.D733: Introduces SentiGOLD, a 70k-sample multi-domain Bangla sentiment analysis dataset spanning 30 domains including sports, with strong inter-annotator agreement.
cells.E733: Curated and annotated dataset creation plus benchmark classification models achieving macro-F1 around 0.62.
cells.F733: Weak -- a non-English sentiment dataset isn't directly applicable to GSE's English-language brand-tone enforcement, though it exemplifies rigorous domain-specific annotation.
cells.G733: Adapt the annotation protocol's rigor (committee sign-off, IAA scoring) as a template for GSE building its own gold-standard labeled dataset for brand-tone/style compliance checks.

cells.C734: Robust Explainer Recommendation for Time Series Classification
cells.D734: Proposes AMEE, a framework that evaluates and ranks saliency-based explanation methods for time-series classifiers via perturbation-based accuracy-loss scoring.
cells.E734: Perturbs input time series at explanation-flagged points and measures resulting classification accuracy drop, aggregated across classifiers/perturbations to rank explainers.
cells.F734: Directly useful -- GSE could use this to validate which explainability method best surfaces the true drivers behind a pick's prediction, supporting the 'math you can read' claim.
cells.G734: Apply AMEE to rank competing feature-attribution methods for the prediction engine, then auto-select the most trustworthy explainer per sport for public pick rationales.

cells.C735: Unsupervised Statistical Feature-Guided Diffusion Model for Sensor-based Human Activity Recognition
cells.D735: Proposes an unsupervised statistical-feature-guided diffusion model that generates synthetic labeled wearable sensor data for human activity recognition.
cells.E735: Conditions a diffusion model on statistical descriptors (mean, std, Z-score, skewness) to synthesize diverse labeled time series without real annotated data.
cells.F735: Directly relevant technique for combating GSE's bootstrap-mode sparse-data problem -- statistic-conditioned diffusion could generate synthetic settled-pick-like data to stress-test calibration.
cells.G735: Generate synthetic per-sport outcome time series (conditioned on target Brier/ECE statistics) to pressure-test the calibration gate pipeline before enough real data accumulates.

cells.C736: ShuttleSet: A Human-Annotated Stroke-Level Singles Dataset for Badminton Tactical Analysis
cells.D736: Releases ShuttleSet, the largest annotated badminton stroke-level dataset (36k strokes), with benchmarks for stroke/movement forecasting.
cells.E736: Manually annotated stroke-level records (shot type, location, player position) plus baseline forecasting models for tactical analysis.
cells.F736: Stretch -- an example of rich structured sports event data and forecasting benchmarks, useful as a template for what granular in-play data GSE's pipeline should capture per sport.
cells.G736: Model GSE's own internal stroke/play-level schema for niche sports on ShuttleSet's annotation taxonomy to extend beyond NFL/MLB/MLS into racket sports.

cells.C737: Not feeling the buzz: Correction study of mispricing and inefficiency in online sportsbooks
cells.D737: Replicates and corrects a prior 'buzz factor' sports-betting mispricing study, finding most profits vanish once a data error is fixed and markets appear more efficient post-2020.
cells.E737: Backtesting replication methodology exposing how a single outlier bet inflated reported profits, plus out-of-sample robustness testing.
cells.F737: Highly relevant -- a cautionary, directly applicable case study on rigorous backtesting hygiene, exactly the validation GSE needs before trusting its own backtest results or making public accuracy/CLV claims.
cells.G737: Adopt this paper's 'single outlier bet' audit as a pre-launch checklist item -- stress-test GSE's backtest for a few dominating outlier picks before trusting aggregate profitability numbers.

cells.C738: Beyond the Meta: Leveraging Game Design Parameters for Patch-Agnostic Esport Analytics
cells.D738: Uses game-design patch notes and clustering to build a character representation that stays accurate as Dota 2 balance patches change, even after new characters are added.
cells.E738: Clusters characters from patch-note text features to create a representation robust to game-design changes, feeding a neural kill-count predictor.
cells.F738: Directly relevant to model-drift resilience -- GSE's sports (rule/roster changes, season resets) face an analogous regime-change problem that shortens model lifespan.
cells.G738: Build rule/roster-change-aware entity embeddings (e.g., new expansion teams) that keep per-sport probability models valid across season transitions without full retraining.

cells.C739: Assessment of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury Risk Based on Human Key Points Detection Algorithm
cells.D739: Uses OpenPose keypoint detection plus a weighted scoring model (AHP) to assess anterior cruciate ligament injury risk from video.
cells.E739: Extracts biomechanical features (knee flexion, trunk angles) via pose estimation, scores them against LESS thresholds, and combines with AHP weighting.
cells.F739: Not directly relevant to GSE's prediction/calibration stack -- injury-risk computer vision is a different product surface, though injury data could someday feed pick features.
cells.G739: Injury-risk scores like this could become a future input feature (player injury probability) enriching GSE's data pipeline for availability-sensitive predictions.

cells.C740: Run Like a Girl! Sports-Related Gender Bias in Language and Vision
cells.D740: Shows and quantifies gender bias in naming choices for athletes in language-and-vision datasets/models, with sports-name mentions skewed toward men (46% vs 35%).
cells.E740: Corpus analysis of human naming behavior plus a computational model that reproduces the observed gender bias.
cells.F740: Relevant to GSE's brand/content pipeline -- an automated social/media content generator must avoid replicating this sport-naming gender asymmetry.
cells.G740: Add a bias-audit check to the automated content-generation pipeline that specifically screens for gendered sports-naming asymmetry before publishing.

cells.C741: Hang-Time HAR: A Benchmark Dataset for Basketball Activity Recognition using Wrist-Worn Inertial Sensors
cells.D741: Releases a benchmark dataset of wrist-worn IMU data for recognizing basketball training/game activities across two national teams, with baseline deep-learning classifiers.
cells.E741: Wrist-sensor time-series dataset with deep-learning benchmarking for activity classification.
cells.F741: Weak direct tie -- GSE doesn't process wearable sensor streams; relevant only as an example of a possible future data source for the Intelligence Graph.
cells.G741: Could inform a distant B2B widget concept: ingest team-provided wearable data as a premium input for player fatigue/availability signals.

cells.C742: Your smartphone could act as a pulse-oximeter and as a single-lead ECG
cells.D742: Proposes turning a smartphone camera into a pulse-oximeter and single-lead ECG device using CNN/CLIP models on fingertip video (photoplethysmography).
cells.E742: CNN/vision-transformer/CLIP models estimate vitals from smartphone-camera PPG video, plus a DCT+feedforward network reconstructing the ECG waveform.
cells.F742: Not directly relevant to GSE's core stack; a health-monitoring computer-vision application outside sports-prediction scope.
cells.G742: Far-fetched but notable: a consumer-facing 'fan fitness' companion feature for the Galaxy Dynasty game layer, unrelated to core calibration work.

cells.C743: Exploring Few-Shot Adaptation for Activity Recognition on Diverse Domains
cells.D743: Proposes RelaMiX, a few-shot domain adaptation method for activity recognition that adapts models to new domains using very few labeled target examples, benchmarked partly on sports videos.
cells.E743: Temporal relational attention network with relation dropout plus cross-domain feature alignment and few-shot feature mixing.
cells.F743: Directly relevant conceptual analog -- few-shot adaptation to a new domain with minimal labels mirrors GSE launching new sports/markets with almost no settled-pick history.
cells.G743: Adapt RelaMiX's few-shot cross-domain alignment machinery to transfer a well-calibrated sport's probability model into a brand-new sport with only a handful of settled picks.

cells.C744: Double-Iterative Gaussian Process Regression for Modeling Error Compensation in Autonomous Racing
cells.D744: Proposes a double Gaussian Process Regression scheme that compensates modeling errors in both a racing planner and controller, iteratively re-collecting error-rich data.
cells.E744: Two GPR-based error-compensation functions correct planner and controller model mismatch, refined via an iterative data-recollection loop.
cells.F744: Directly transferable idea -- GPR-based error compensation trained on error-rich data is plausible for correcting systematic bias behind GSE's calibration failure (Brier 0.2563, ECE 0.0699).
cells.G744: Use a GPR 'residual corrector' layer atop the core model's outputs, trained on the worst-miscalibrated picks, as a lightweight patch ahead of a full ensemble rebuild.

cells.C745: Anatomically Detailed Simulation of Human Torso
cells.D745: Builds a biomechanically detailed torso simulation (finite-element + rigid body) enabling recovery of spine motion from sparse motion-capture markers.
cells.E745: Couples finite-element modeling of spinal anatomy with rigid-body simulation for physically valid torso kinematics and trajectory optimization.
cells.F745: Not relevant to GSE's statistical prediction stack; a biomechanics/graphics simulation paper.
cells.G745: No meaningful application; at most distant inspiration for a future 'digital athlete' visualization in the Galaxy Dynasty game.

cells.C746: Large Language Models in Sport Science & Medicine: Opportunities, Risks and Considerations
cells.D746: A position paper surveying opportunities and risks of using large language models in sports science and medicine, covering bias, confidentiality, and alignment concerns.
cells.E746: Literature/position discussion of LLM risks and applications, not a novel technical method.
cells.F746: Directly relevant to GSE's internal use of LLM-based coding/research agents (Jarvis, Hermes, Fable) and any LLM-assisted content generation -- the bias/confidentiality/alignment risks apply directly.
cells.G746: Use this paper's risk taxonomy as a checklist when auditing GSE's LLM-driven social/content pipeline for factual and bias risks before publishing.

cells.C747: Human activity recognition using deep learning approaches and single frame cnn and convolutional lstm
cells.D747: Compares single-frame CNN vs Convolutional LSTM for recognizing human actions in video, finding the simpler single-frame CNN more accurate (99.8%) on UCF50.
cells.E747: Benchmarks two standard video-action-recognition architectures on a public dataset.
cells.F747: Minimal -- generic video action-recognition benchmarking, not tied to GSE's tabular/time-series prediction stack.
cells.G747: If GSE ever ingests broadcast video directly, the finding that simple single-frame CNNs beat sequence models is a useful cost-saving prior for a lightweight event classifier.

cells.C748: Profiling the news spreading barriers using news headlines
cells.D748: Classifies news-spreading barriers (cultural, economic, political, linguistic, geographical) from headlines including sports, using commonsense inference and sentiment features.
cells.E748: Combines COMET-based commonsense inference and sentiment scores as features for headline barrier classification.
cells.F748: Weak tie -- relevant only as an NLP feature-engineering example potentially reusable for GSE's brand-language/content NLP tooling.
cells.G748: Reuse the commonsense-inference feature extraction to auto-flag GSE marketing copy likely to be misread across regions before international publishing.

cells.C749: Smart Sports Predictions via Hybrid Simulation: NBA Case Study
cells.D749: Proposes hybrid agent-based simulation for NBA prediction that models teams as rational decision-making agents, studying prediction quality versus data-history length.
cells.E749: Combines predictive variables with agent-based simulation logic representing team/player strategy, tuned via case-study experiments on optimal historical-data window size.
cells.F749: Directly relevant -- the 'how much historical data maximizes prediction accuracy' question is exactly the tuning GSE needs for its own MAE-losing prediction model and calibration windows.
cells.G749: Run GSE's own ablation on training-window length per sport to find an analogous optimal history length, potentially closing part of the MAE gap versus the naive baseline.

cells.D750: A comprehensive survey of IoT-based wearable devices, their sensors, communication tech, and data-processing methods across health, fitness, and sports.
cells.E750: Literature survey, not a novel method.
cells.F750: Weak -- general wearables survey, tangential to GSE's odds/stats-based stack unless they later ingest wearable biometric feeds.
cells.G750: Reference architecture for a hypothetical future B2B data-ingestion module if GSE partners with teams for wearable-derived player-availability signals.

cells.C751: Domain Adaptation for Inertial Measurement Unit-based Human Activity Recognition: A Survey
cells.D751: Surveys domain adaptation techniques for wearable IMU-based human activity recognition, addressing sensor-placement and device heterogeneity.
cells.E751: Literature review of transfer-learning/domain-adaptation methods for sensor data.
cells.F751: Weak direct tie, though the domain-adaptation-for-heterogeneous-sources theme parallels GSE's multi-source (scraped + odds feed) data reconciliation challenge.
cells.G751: Apply domain-adaptation framing to reconcile stat definitions/units across different free scraped sources feeding the same pipeline.

cells.C752: WEAR: An Outdoor Sports Dataset for Wearable and Egocentric Activity Recognition
cells.D752: Introduces WEAR, a synchronized egocentric-video and IMU dataset for 18 outdoor workout activities, benchmarking temporal action localization from both modalities.
cells.E752: Multimodal dataset plus single-stage temporal-action-localization models applied to both raw inertial and visual streams.
cells.F752: Weak -- a wearable/vision HAR benchmark not tied to GSE's odds-and-stats modeling; only tangential as multimodal fusion inspiration.
cells.G752: The finding that vision and IMU offer complementary strengths could inspire fusing scraped play-by-play text with structured stats as multimodal ensemble inputs.

cells.C753: MHfit: Mobile Health Data for Predicting Athletics Fitness Using Machine Learning
cells.D753: Uses mobile-health sensor data and compares five ML algorithms (best: XGBoost, 95.2% accuracy) to predict whether an athlete is a good fit for a sport/team.
cells.E753: Standard supervised classification benchmarking (XGBoost, Naive Bayes, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Logistic Regression) on mobile vital-sign data.
cells.F753: Weak tie -- generic ML benchmarking on health data, not GSE's forecasting problem, though XGBoost is a plausible ensemble component for their prediction engine.
cells.G753: Mainly reinforces XGBoost as a solid baseline candidate within GSE's own ensemble; no especially novel angle otherwise.

cells.C754: Monocular 3D Human Pose Estimation for Sports Broadcasts using Partial Sports Field Registration
cells.D754: Combines 2D human pose estimation with partial sports-field camera calibration to recover valid 3D running kinematics from broadcast close-up footage.
cells.E754: Joint optimization of 3D pose estimation and camera calibration constrained by partial field-line visibility, validated on synthetic Unreal Engine data.
cells.F754: Not directly relevant to GSE's stats-based engine; a computer-vision biomechanics extraction method for broadcast video.
cells.G754: Long-shot: could enable extracting proprietary kinematic features (e.g., sprint form) from broadcast video as a hard-to-replicate data differentiator.

cells.C755: Towards Active Learning for Action Spotting in Association Football Videos
cells.D755: Proposes an active-learning framework using uncertainty sampling to reduce annotation effort for football action-spotting models, matching full-dataset performance with one-third the labels.
cells.E755: Uncertainty-sampling-based active learning selects the most informative video clips to annotate next, accelerating model training.
cells.F755: Directly relevant technique for GSE's data-pipeline efficiency -- active learning could reduce the cost of building labeled event datasets while improving downstream model quality.
cells.G755: Apply uncertainty sampling to prioritize which settled picks/edge cases most need human review before being trusted for the calibration gate, cutting QA effort.

cells.C756: Can the hot hand phenomenon be modelled? A Bayesian hidden Markov approach
cells.D756: Models the 'hot hand' phenomenon in basketball shooting using a Bayesian hidden Markov model with cold/hot latent states and shot-distance covariates.
cells.E756: Bayesian longitudinal HMM estimates latent hot/cold states and state-dependent shot-success probabilities.
cells.F756: Highly relevant -- a Bayesian latent-state model for streaky, time-varying player performance is directly applicable to GSE's per-sport probability models and could improve calibration by capturing momentum effects.
cells.G756: Add a hidden hot/cold-state layer to GSE's player-level features so the ensemble can dynamically adjust confidence based on inferred streakiness.

cells.C757: Who You Play Affects How You Play: Predicting Sports Performance Using Graph Attention Networks With Temporal Convolution
cells.D757: Proposes GATv2-GCN, a graph attention plus temporal convolution model predicting player performance from dynamic player-interaction graphs, explored for sports-betting profitability.
cells.E757: Graph attention network models player-to-player interaction weights; temporal convolution layer captures multivariate stat time series.
cells.F757: Highly relevant -- graph-attention ensembles for performance prediction directly target GSE's core forecasting blocker (MAE losing to baseline) and its interest in better ensembles.
cells.G757: Use the player-interaction attention weights as an interpretable 'who influences whom' explanation layer, feeding GSE's 'math you can read' pick rationales.

cells.C758: Why winning a soccer game is worth 5 points
cells.D758: Introduces a probabilistic model interpreting league-table point systems, showing empirically that a soccer win's true implied value is close to 5 points, not the nominal 3.
cells.E758: Probabilistic ranking model fit to game results that estimates the effective relative value of a win versus draw from data.
cells.F758: Directly relevant -- a rigorous statistical approach to deriving implied probabilities/values from game outcomes maps onto GSE's need for principled, math-transparent scoring rules.
cells.G758: Use this method's implied-point-value estimation as a sanity-check benchmark against GSE's own model-derived win probabilities for soccer.

cells.C759: GOAL: A Challenging Knowledge-grounded Video Captioning Benchmark for Real-time Soccer Commentary Generation
cells.D759: Introduces GOAL, an 8.9k-clip benchmark for knowledge-grounded soccer video captioning to generate automatic real-time commentary with background reasoning.
cells.E759: Pairs video clips with knowledge triples and commentary sentences to train/evaluate knowledge-grounded video captioning models.
cells.F759: Directly relevant to GSE's automated social/media content generation ambitions -- knowledge-grounded captioning is exactly the mechanism needed to auto-generate pick commentary tied to a knowledge base.
cells.G759: Feed GSE's future Intelligence Graph as the knowledge source for a knowledge-grounded commentary generator that narrates why a pick was made, in real time.

cells.C760: Deep Generative Multi-Agent Imitation Model as a Computational Benchmark for Evaluating Human Performance in Complex Interactive Tasks: A Case Study in Football
cells.D760: Trains a Conditional VRNN on player/ball tracking data to imitate football team interactions and uses the model as a data-driven benchmark for evaluating team performance.
cells.E760: Conditional Variational RNN imitates multi-agent team interactions, generating counterfactual performance benchmarks beyond static metrics.
cells.F760: Directly relevant -- a generative multi-agent model used as a dynamic performance benchmark is conceptually close to what GSE needs for evaluating team/player strength beyond static stats.
cells.G760: Use the trained imitation model to simulate 'what an average team would have done here' as a novel explainability baseline for pick confidence.

cells.C761: The Economic Value of User Tracking for Publishers
cells.D761: Empirically quantifies how much ad-impression revenue publishers, including sports-content sites, lose when user tracking is unavailable, using large-scale EU/US datasets.
cells.E761: Large-scale observational/econometric analysis comparing ad prices for trackable vs. untrackable impressions across thousands of publishers.
cells.F761: Tangential -- relevant mainly to GSE's ad/monetization strategy on sports content, not the core prediction engine.
cells.G761: Use the finding that premium/niche publishers suffer less from tracking loss to justify GSE investing in first-party, trust-based data collection over third-party tracking.

cells.C762: Machine learning for sports betting: should model selection be based on accuracy or calibration?
cells.D762: Empirically shows that selecting NBA prediction models by calibration rather than raw accuracy yields much higher betting returns (+34.69% vs -35.17% ROI).
cells.E762: Trains multiple models, compares calibration-based vs accuracy-based model selection, and backtests betting ROI on published odds.
cells.F762: Extremely directly relevant -- this is essentially the exact thesis behind GSE's launch-gate requirement (Brier/ECE calibration over raw accuracy), validated with concrete NBA betting evidence.
cells.G762: Cite this paper directly in GSE's internal case for delaying launch until calibration gates pass, and replicate its calibration-based model-selection protocol as an automated CI step.

cells.C763: Sandpile Universality in Social Inequality: Gini and Kolkata Measures
cells.D763: Reviews Gini and Kolkata inequality indices across social domains, including Olympic sports, showing convergence toward a universal ~0.87 value under unrestricted competition.
cells.E763: Statistical review/synthesis of inequality-index measurements across many competitive domains, framed via self-organized criticality.
cells.F763: Weak/stretch -- an inequality-index framework could be repurposed as a novel competitive-balance metric for GSE, but it's not tied to their current blockers.
cells.G763: Compute a Kolkata-index-style 'competitive balance score' per league/season as a new differentiating analytics feature for GSE's platform.

cells.C764: A Continuous-Time Stochastic Process for High-Resolution Network Data in Sports
cells.D764: Introduces a continuous-time stochastic process model for high-resolution player-interaction network data, applied to Italian Serie A football via Bayesian estimation.
cells.E764: Bayesian continuous-time point-process model captures spatial-temporal player interaction dynamics beyond a simple sum of player strengths.
cells.F764: Directly relevant -- a principled Bayesian stochastic-process framework for team interaction dynamics matches exactly what GSE suspects it needs: independent per-sport probability models.
cells.G764: Prototype this continuous-time interaction model as the per-sport component in GSE's proposed sport-specific ensemble, replacing the current single global calibrator.

cells.C765: Identification of pattern mining algorithm for rugby league players positional groups separation based on movement patterns
cells.D765: Compares three sequential pattern-mining algorithms for classifying rugby league player positions from movement-pattern data, finding one (LCCspm) best separates positions.
cells.E765: Applies and benchmarks pattern-mining algorithms (closed contiguous, longest common subsequence, AprioriClose) plus ML classifiers on positional movement sequences.
cells.F765: Weak-to-moderate -- a feature-engineering methodology from movement sequences, potentially useful if GSE expands into richer positional tracking data for niche sports.
cells.G765: Apply the winning closed-contiguous pattern-mining approach to mine recurring 'market movement patterns' in live odds time series as a new predictive feature.

cells.C766: Impact of a Batter in ODI Cricket Implementing Regression Models from Match Commentary
cells.D766: Proposes an 'Effective Runs' metric for cricket batters derived from regression models trained on match-commentary text (control, pitch, weather) rather than raw box scores.
cells.E766: NLP-extracted contextual features (control, conditions) from commentary text feed multiple regression models (MLR, SVR, Random Forest) predicting player impact.
cells.F766: Directly relevant as a data-pipeline pattern -- extracting structured contextual features from free-text commentary is exactly the enrichment GSE's scraping pipeline could use to beat its baseline MAE.
cells.G766: Mine scraped play-by-play/commentary text for situational context variables (pressure, crowd, weather) as new engineered features for the core forecasting model.

cells.C767: Table Tennis Stroke Detection and Recognition Using Ball Trajectory Data
cells.D767: Detects and classifies table tennis strokes purely from ball trajectory data, achieving 87% stroke-recognition accuracy with a temporal convolutional network.
cells.E767: YOLOv4/TrackNetv2 ball tracking feeds a mathematical stroke-boundary extractor and a TCN classifier trained on trajectory-only features.
cells.F767: Stretch -- a niche computer-vision sports-event-detection method, relevant mainly as another example of extracting structured events from minimal raw signal, echoing GSE's data-scarcity challenges.
cells.G767: Generalize the idea to infer structured 'events' (e.g., momentum shifts) from a sparse odds-line trajectory alone, mirroring stroke-detection-from-ball-trajectory-only.

cells.C768: Transformer-Based Neural Marked Spatio Temporal Point Process Model for Football Match Events Analysis
cells.D768: Proposes a Transformer-based neural marked spatiotemporal point process (NMSTPP) for football event sequences, plus a new 'holistic possession utilization score' metric.
cells.E768: Neural temporal point process models event type, time, and location jointly via a Transformer architecture, validated against team ranking/goal correlations.
cells.F768: Directly relevant -- marked spatiotemporal point processes are a strong candidate architecture for GSE's core prediction model, which currently loses to a naive baseline.
cells.G768: Adopt NMSTPP as an alternative core-architecture experiment to beat the naive baseline (current MAE 5.31 vs 4.91), since point processes natively handle irregular event timing.

cells.C769: Inferring Player Location in Sports Matches: Multi-Agent Spatial Imputation from Limited Observations
cells.D769: Uses LSTM plus GNN to impute all players' locations from sparse event data (95% missing), reducing location error by 62% versus baselines.
cells.E769: Graph neural network plus LSTM jointly model temporal and inter-agent spatial patterns to reconstruct missing multi-agent trajectories.
cells.F769: Directly relevant -- extracting rich spatial features from cheap, freely available event data rather than expensive optical tracking directly supports GSE's free-data ingestion strategy.
cells.G769: Use this imputation approach to synthesize pseudo-tracking-quality features from free box-score/play-by-play data GSE already scrapes, without paying for optical tracking feeds.

cells.C770: InMyFace: Inertial and Mechanomyography-Based Sensor Fusion for Wearable Facial Activity Recognition
cells.D770: Uses inertial, pressure, and acoustic sensors embedded in a sports cap to recognize facial expressions/muscle activity without a camera.
cells.E770: Multimodal wearable sensor fusion (IMU, pressure, mechanomyography) with late fusion classification, achieving about 85% F1.
cells.F770: Not relevant to GSE's stats-prediction stack; a wearable HCI sensing paper.
cells.G770: No meaningful application beyond distant inspiration for a novel wearable fan-engagement gadget, unrelated to core priorities.

cells.C771: Towards Meaningful Anomaly Detection: The Effect of Counterfactual Explanations on the Investigation of Anomalies in Multivariate Time Series
cells.D771: Shows via a behavioral experiment (NYC taxi data, with sporting events as confounders) that counterfactual explanations improve humans' ability to correctly investigate detected anomalies.
cells.E771: Behavioral study comparing anomaly-investigation accuracy with vs. without counterfactual explanation support for explainable anomaly detection.
cells.F771: Directly relevant to GSE's data-pipeline reliability -- counterfactual explanations could help analysts triage whether an odds/stat anomaly is a real event or a scraping glitch.
cells.G771: Build a counterfactual-explanation layer into GSE's pipeline monitoring so on-call engineers can quickly tell real line moves from data-quality bugs.

cells.C772: Fine-Grained Action Detection with RGB and Pose Information using Two Stream Convolutional Networks
cells.D772: Fuses raw RGB and pose data through a two-stream 3D CNN with attention to classify/detect table tennis strokes, reaching 87.3% classification accuracy.
cells.E772: Late-fusion of RGB and pose-rendered-as-image streams through 3D CNN blocks with attention mechanisms.
cells.F772: Weak -- a computer-vision sports action-recognition method not tied to GSE's tabular prediction stack.
cells.G772: No strong application; at most a template if GSE ever adds automated broadcast-clip tagging for its content pipeline.

cells.C773: Conditional expectation with regularization for missing data imputation
cells.D773: Proposes DIMV, a conditional-distribution-based, regularized imputation method for missing data that is explainable, scalable, and provides confidence regions.
cells.E773: Estimates the conditional distribution of a feature with missing values from fully observed features via a regularized regression-like approach.
cells.F773: Directly relevant -- GSE's multi-source scraped/odds pipeline inevitably has missing values, and an explainable, confidence-region-producing imputer aligns with data reliability and the 'math you can read' brand.
cells.G773: Use DIMV's confidence-region output as a signal for bootstrap mode -- treat imputed features with wide confidence regions as evidence of sparse data, automatically capping confidence scores.

cells.C774: Design and Implementation of A Soccer Ball Detection System with Multiple Cameras
cells.D774: Builds a multi-camera 3D ball-detection and tracking system for live soccer broadcasts using bundle adjustment and GPU acceleration.
cells.E774: Combines a learned ball detector, single- and multi-camera triangulation, and bundle adjustment for real-time 3D ball localization.
cells.F774: Not directly relevant to GSE's stats-based engine; a broadcast computer-vision infrastructure paper.
cells.G774: No strong near-term fit; tangential to a hypothetical future live-broadcast integration for Galaxy Dynasty.

cells.C775: A Machine Learning Approach for Player and Position Adjusted Expected Goals in Football (Soccer)
cells.D775: Builds ML Expected Goals (xG) models (logistic regression, gradient boosting) adjusted for player position, showing forwards accumulate more xG efficiency than defenders.
cells.E775: Binary classification of shot outcomes via logistic regression/gradient boosting, stratified by position to create adjusted xG baselines.
cells.F775: Directly relevant -- xG-style probabilistic shot-outcome modeling and position-stratified adjustment is a concrete template for GSE's need for independent per-sport (and per-position) probability models.
cells.G775: Extend GSE's per-sport ensemble idea to per-position sub-models, à la position-adjusted xG, as a finer-grained fix for the failing global calibrator.

cells.C776: A Novel IoT-Based System for Ten Pin Bowling
cells.D776: Presents an IoT/cloud system using two IMUs, DTW-based throw-quality scoring, and SVM skill classification for bowling coaching.
cells.E776: Wearable IMU capture, Dynamic Time Warping comparison to reference throws, and SVM-based skill-level classification.
cells.F776: Not relevant to GSE's core prediction stack; a wearable sports-coaching hardware/software system.
cells.G776: No meaningful application beyond distant inspiration for niche-sport data collection if GSE ever expands into bowling analytics.

cells.C777: Event Detection in Football using Graph Convolutional Networks
cells.D777: A thesis using Graph Convolutional Networks to model players/ball as a per-frame graph for automatic football event detection from tracking data.
cells.E777: Graph convolutional layers plus pooling process per-frame player/ball graphs to classify events, modeling temporal context around actions.
cells.F777: Directly relevant -- GCN-based event detection from tracking-like data is a plausible architecture component for extracting structured features to feed GSE's core forecasting model.
cells.G777: Adapt the graph-based event-detection formulation to detect 'market-moving events' from streaming odds/line-movement graphs rather than player positions.

cells.C778: Building Concise Logical Patterns by Constraining Tsetlin Machine Clause Size
cells.D778: Introduces Clause Size Constrained Tsetlin Machines (CSC-TM), a logic-based ML variant keeping interpretable clauses short with up to 80x fewer literals at similar/better accuracy.
cells.E778: A soft constraint expels literals once a logical clause exceeds a size threshold, tested on tabular, text, image, and board-game data.
cells.F778: Directly relevant to GSE's brand identity -- an inherently interpretable, rule-based (non-neural) ML method is a strong candidate for a 'math you can read' component, and it's hardware-friendly for low-latency scoring.
cells.G778: Use Tsetlin Machines as a genuinely interpretable sub-model whose short logical clauses can be shown verbatim to users as the literal 'math' behind a pick.

cells.C779: A Survey of Advanced Computer Vision Techniques for Sports
cells.D779: Surveys computer-vision techniques (object detection, pose estimation) for sports analytics and demonstrates a shot-speed estimation model from pose data (67% correlation).
cells.E779: Literature survey plus a small applied case study combining pose estimation with regression for shot-speed prediction.
cells.F779: Weak-moderate -- a landscape reference for vision-based data collection, relevant mainly if GSE ever ingests video, not to current calibration/ensemble blockers.
cells.G779: Use the survey as a scouting reference for free/cheap vision-based stats (e.g., shot speed) that could become new proprietary features distinguishing GSE from odds-only competitors.

cells.C780: Your Day in Your Pocket: Complex Activity Recognition from Smartphone Accelerometers
cells.D780: Recognizes complex daily activities including sports from smartphone accelerometer data alone across 600+ users, reaching up to 0.76 AUROC with partial personalization.
cells.E780: Deep-learning binary classifiers trained on raw accelerometer time series, with personalization per user.
cells.F780: Weak -- a personal-sensing HAR paper unrelated to GSE's sports-outcome forecasting, only a loose time-series-classification methodological echo.
cells.G780: The partial-personalization approach could analogously inspire per-bettor or per-team personalized confidence calibration in GSE's product.

cells.C781: On classical and Bayesian inference for bivariate Poisson conditionals distributions: Theory, methods and applications
cells.D781: Develops classical and Bayesian inference methods for a bivariate Poisson conditionals distribution, applied broadly including sports statistics.
cells.E781: Iterative MLE procedure plus Bayesian estimation (conjugate and non-conjugate priors) for a bivariate count model, compared via simulation.
cells.F781: Directly relevant -- bivariate Poisson-type models are the classic workhorse for modeling paired scores, directly applicable to GSE's core probability modeling for score-based sports.
cells.G781: Use the bivariate Poisson-conditionals framework to jointly model correlated team scores in the sport-specific ensemble, potentially improving calibration on scoreline markets.

cells.C782: Big Ideas in Sports Analytics and Statistical Tools for their Investigation
cells.D782: A survey connecting four core sports-analytics ideas across multiple sports: expected value of game state, win probability, team-strength measures, and betting-market data usage.
cells.E782: Comparative review of analytical concepts and statistical/computational methodologies used across different sports' analytics communities.
cells.F782: Extremely directly relevant -- essentially a literature map of exactly the concepts (win probability, team-strength ratings, market-data usage) GSE's prediction engine and calibration work are built on.
cells.G782: Use this survey as a structured checklist to audit which 'big idea' methodologies GSE's current engine is missing versus academic best practice.

cells.C783: Metaverse Communications, Networking, Security, and Applications: Research Issues, State-of-the-Art, and Future Directions
cells.D783: Surveys Metaverse architecture, security, privacy, and applications including sports/socializing for smart-city contexts, covering XR, AI, and blockchain integration.
cells.E783: Broad literature survey of the Metaverse technology stack and threats, no novel prediction/statistical method.
cells.F783: Weak but notable -- a background reference for GSE's long-horizon Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR persistent web-game ambitions and any virtual-world features.
cells.G783: Use the survey's privacy/security threat taxonomy as an early checklist when designing the Galaxy Dynasty persistent game layer's architecture.

cells.C784: Practical Algorithms with Guaranteed Approximation Ratio for TTP with Maximum Tour Length Two
cells.D784: Proposes improved approximation algorithms for the Traveling Tournament Problem (double round-robin scheduling with travel-distance minimization), beating prior benchmarks by 5.66% on average.
cells.E784: Combinatorial approximation algorithms with proven approximation ratios for constrained round-robin tournament scheduling.
cells.F784: Tangential -- sports scheduling optimization is a different problem domain from GSE's probabilistic prediction engine, though schedule structure is a known outcome driver.
cells.G784: Use TTP-style schedule-distance/rest-day features (travel burden, back-to-back games) as engineered inputs to GSE's prediction model, since travel fatigue is a real outcome driver.

cells.C785: Stochastic analysis of the Elo rating algorithm in round-robin tournaments
cells.D785: Provides a rigorous stochastic analysis of the Elo rating algorithm's convergence properties in round-robin tournaments, validated on Italian volleyball data.
cells.E785: Derives analytical expressions for skill/performance-metric evolution under Elo updates and relates the step-size hyperparameter to convergence behavior.
cells.F785: Directly relevant -- Elo-style rating updates are a common team-strength component in sports prediction ensembles; this paper's convergence/step-size guidance could inform tuning GSE's own rating features.
cells.G785: Use the paper's step-size convergence guidance to formally tune an Elo-style component within GSE's multiplicative-weight ensemble tied to the founder's CEPT framework.

cells.C786: Evidence-based policy-making in sports funding using a data-driven optimization approach
cells.D786: Uses a data-driven optimization model to allocate government sports-club funding to maximize children's access, based on Austrian football-club budget/membership data.
cells.E786: Simulation-based optimization exploiting an empirically fitted sub-linear budget-membership relationship, compared against naive allocation.
cells.F786: Not relevant to GSE's prediction engine; a public-policy resource-allocation study.
cells.G786: No meaningful application to GSE's product beyond general optimization-under-constraints methodology awareness.

cells.C787: Commentary Generation from Data Records of Multiplayer Strategy Esports Game
cells.D787: Introduces a data-to-text task and dataset for generating esports commentary from League of Legends structured play logs using Transformer models.
cells.E787: Transformer-based data-to-text generation conditioned on structured esports event records, evaluated with and without pretrained LM initialization.
cells.F787: Directly relevant to GSE's automated content-generation ambitions -- structured-data-to-commentary generation is exactly the mechanism needed for auto-generated pick/game narratives.
cells.G787: Fine-tune a similar data-to-text model on GSE's own structured pick/game data to auto-generate branded, 'math you can read' commentary for social content at scale.

cells.C788: A Bayesian Mixture Model Approach to Expected Possession Values in Rugby League
cells.D788: Proposes a Bayesian mixture-model expected possession value (EPV) approach for rugby league, providing smooth possession-outcome probability surfaces across the pitch under sparse data.
cells.E788: Bayesian estimation at grid centres with linear/bilinear interpolation extrapolates outcome probabilities across pitch locations from sparse observations.
cells.F788: Highly relevant -- a Bayesian approach explicitly designed for low-data-availability sports is a direct blueprint for GSE's bootstrap-mode/sparse-data calibration problem in less-covered sports/markets.
cells.G788: Reuse this Bayesian mixture-and-interpolation pattern as the template for GSE's per-sport probability models in niche or newly added sports/markets with limited historical picks.

cells.C789: Converting College Football Point Spread Differentials to Probabilities
cells.D789: Provides a method to convert NCAA football point-spread differentials into win probabilities using a historically-informed normal-distribution adjustment, released as a public tool.
cells.E789: Modifies a normal-distribution-based spread-to-probability conversion by reweighting for the empirical frequency of common point differentials.
cells.F789: Extremely directly relevant -- this is precisely the closing-line-value/market-efficiency benchmarking and probability-conversion methodology GSE needs for its public accuracy standards.
cells.G789: Directly adapt this spread-to-probability reweighting technique as a sanity-check calibrator baseline for GSE's own model outputs against market-implied probabilities.

cells.C790: Can a face tell us anything about an NBA prospect? -- A Deep Learning approach
cells.D790: Uses CNN image classifiers on prospects' facial photos to predict NBA career trajectory quality, finding a potential (weak) correlation worth further study.
cells.E790: Trains pre-trained image classifiers on a curated dataset of about 1500 draft-class facial photos labeled by career-outcome tier.
cells.F790: Not relevant/questionable -- a speculative, ethically fraught predictor unrelated to GSE's statistical approach; the kind of pseudo-scientific method GSE's brand should explicitly avoid.
cells.G790: Best honest angle: a cautionary example -- GSE should document why it avoids such spurious correlational predictors, reinforcing its 'math you can read' credibility.

cells.D791: Proposes EgoT2, a method that translates outputs across multiple egocentric-video understanding tasks using a shared task-translator module, achieving top results on Ego4D benchmarks.
cells.E791: Task-specific backbones feed a shared translator module that captures cross-task synergies without full multi-task retraining.
cells.F791: Weak direct tie to GSE's tabular/time-series problem, though the shared-translator idea echoes ensemble/multi-task concepts relevant to their multi-sport model architecture.
cells.G791: Borrow the shared-translator-across-task-specific-backbones pattern to let GSE's per-sport models share a common calibration-translation layer instead of one global calibrator.

cells.C792: Progressive Multi-view Human Mesh Recovery with Self-Supervision
cells.D792: Proposes a simulation-based training pipeline for multi-view 3D human mesh recovery that generalizes better to unseen camera setups via 2D intermediate representations.
cells.E792: Learnable calibration/triangulation with progressive multi-view 2D-to-3D aggregation trained on synthetic data to bridge the sim-to-real domain gap.
cells.F792: Not relevant to GSE's core forecasting stack; a computer-vision biomechanics/graphics method.
cells.G792: No meaningful application; at most distant inspiration for future motion-capture-driven Galaxy Dynasty avatars.

cells.C793: Pose Estimation for Human Wearing Loose-Fitting Clothes: Obtaining Ground Truth Posture Using HFR Camera and Blinking LEDs
cells.D793: Develops a method using blinking LEDs and a high-frame-rate camera to obtain accurate 2D pose ground truth for athletes wearing loose clothing.
cells.E793: High-frame-rate capture with LED on/off frame extraction produces annotation-quality ground truth pose data, revealing errors in existing pose estimators.
cells.F793: Not relevant to GSE's core stack; a niche computer-vision ground-truth-collection technique for a different product surface.
cells.G793: No meaningful application to GSE's current priorities.

cells.D794: Develops kinetic data structures to efficiently approximate and track the time-varying density shape of moving groups, such as in sports analysis, via kernel density estimation.
cells.E794: Combines kernel density estimation with kinetic data structures to maintain approximate persistent-maxima tracking as groups move over time.
cells.F794: Weak-moderate -- a computational-geometry technique for tracking group shape over time could be repurposed for detecting evolving clusters in live odds/line movements.
cells.G794: Apply kinetic density tracking to detect emerging clusters of correlated line movement across multiple sportsbooks in real time, as an anomaly/opportunity signal.

cells.D795: Introduces the Muscles in Action dataset (synchronized video plus sEMG) and a bidirectional model linking muscle activation to motion for richer virtual-human modeling.
cells.E795: Learns a bidirectional video-to-muscle-activation and muscle-activation-to-motion representation from paired sEMG/video data.
cells.F795: Not relevant to GSE's statistical stack; a biomechanics/computer-vision dataset paper.
cells.G795: No meaningful near-term application; distant inspiration only for a hypothetical avatar/animation feature in Galaxy Dynasty.

cells.C796: Location analysis of players in UEFA EURO 2020 and 2022 using generalized valuation of defense by estimating probabilities
cells.D796: Proposes a generalized, score-scaled probabilistic method to value defensive play in football using broadcast-derived player location data from men's/women's Euro tournaments.
cells.E796: Predicts probabilities of ball-gain/being-attacked/scoring events from player locations, then rescales by event importance for defense valuation.
cells.F796: Directly relevant -- a probabilistic event-valuation framework using freely obtainable broadcast-derived location data is a strong template for extending GSE's per-sport probability models.
cells.G796: Adapt this score-scaled event-probability framework to create a novel 'defensive value' pick category, differentiating GSE's soccer coverage from win-probability-only competitors.

cells.C797: Where did you tweet from? Inferring the origin locations of tweets based on contextual information
cells.D797: Proposes a model (True Origin Model) using NLP context to infer whether a tweet's mentioned location is its true origin, evaluated across topics including sports.
cells.E797: Uses a contextualizing transformer (locBERT) plus a RoBERTa-based location extractor to classify origin vs. non-origin location mentions in tweets.
cells.F797: Weak -- an NLP geolocation-inference method, tangentially useful only if GSE ever mines social media for sentiment/location-tagged sports discussion.
cells.G797: Could be reused to geo-filter scraped social chatter about games/injuries for regional relevance before feeding it into any future sentiment-based features.

cells.C798: ROC Analysis for Paired Comparison Data
cells.D798: Extends ROC curve analysis to paired-comparison models such as head-to-head sports competitions, proposing two novel methods to construct interpretable ROC curves.
cells.E798: Develops statistical constructions that adapt ROC/AUC methodology to paired binary-comparison data, validated on professional sports competition results.
cells.F798: Directly relevant -- gives GSE a rigorous discrimination-quality metric specifically suited to head-to-head sports outcomes, complementing Brier/ECE in their launch-gate evaluation suite.
cells.G798: Add this paired-comparison ROC/AUC metric as a discrimination-focused companion diagnostic alongside Brier score and ECE in GSE's calibration dashboard.

cells.C799: A Graph-Based Method for Soccer Action Spotting Using Unsupervised Player Classification
cells.D799: Models players/referees/goalkeepers as graph nodes with temporal interaction sequences for soccer action spotting, achieving 97.72% player-classification accuracy.
cells.E799: Unsupervised player classification feeds a graph-based temporal model for detecting key match events, combined with audiovisual modalities.
cells.F799: Moderate -- another graph-based sports-event-detection architecture relevant as a potential feature-extraction component if GSE ever processes broadcast video for event data.
cells.G799: Reuse the unsupervised role-classification idea to auto-label roles in scraped play-by-play text without manual tagging.

cells.C800: Where Will Players Move Next? Dynamic Graphs and Hierarchical Fusion for Movement Forecasting in Badminton
cells.D800: Proposes DyMF, a dynamic-graph and hierarchical-fusion model forecasting badminton players' next stroke type and movement using player-interaction style extractors.
cells.E800: Models within-rally player interactions and tactics evolution via dynamic graphs plus hierarchical fusion of interaction styles over time.
cells.F800: Directly relevant -- a strong example of a dynamic ensemble/interaction architecture for sequential sports forecasting, directly applicable to improving GSE's core model beyond the naive baseline.
cells.G800: Adapt DyMF's interaction-style-extractor concept to model matchup-specific dynamics (e.g., pitcher-batter or QB-defense) as a feature layer in GSE's core prediction model.

cells.C801: The Ball is in Our Court: Conducting Visualization Research with Sports Experts
cells.D801: A reflective paper on lessons learned conducting sports visualization research (AR/XR) with domain experts across athlete, analyst, and fan use cases.
cells.E801: Synthesizes best practices/pitfalls from prior user studies in sports visualization design, not a novel algorithm.
cells.F801: Tangential -- relevant mainly as UX guidance for GSE's B2B embeddable widgets or fan-facing dashboards, not the core prediction stack.
cells.G801: Apply the 'working with domain experts' lessons to GSE's own process for designing analyst-facing calibration dashboards or B2B widget UX.

cells.C802: NeighborTrack: Improving Single Object Tracking by Bipartite Matching with Neighbor Tracklets
cells.D802: Proposes NeighborTrack, a post-processing method that uses neighboring-object confidence to reduce false tracking during occlusion in single-object visual tracking.
cells.E802: Bipartite matching against neighbor tracklets validates/corrects tracking confidence without retraining the base tracker.
cells.F802: Weak -- a general computer-vision object-tracking robustness technique, not directly tied to GSE's tabular/time-series prediction pipeline.
cells.G802: The use-neighbors'-confidence-to-sanity-check pattern could inspire cross-validating one pick's predicted probability against similar contemporaneous picks as an anomaly check.

cells.C803: Sports Camera Pose Refinement Using an Evolution Strategy
cells.D803: Uses an evolution-strategy optimization method to refine sports-broadcast camera extrinsic parameters from a single segmented field image, outperforming prior calibration methods.
cells.E803: A neural field-segmentation network feeds an evolutionary-strategy optimizer that refines camera pose parameters.
cells.F803: Not relevant to GSE's core stack; a broadcast camera-calibration computer-vision method.
cells.G803: No meaningful application to current priorities.

cells.C804: Pre-analysis protocol for an observational study on the effects of adolescent sports participation on health in early adulthood
cells.D804: A pre-registered observational study protocol examining how adolescent sports participation, including contact-sport intensity, affects early-adulthood health outcomes.
cells.E804: Defines a hierarchy of exposure definitions and a matched observational-study/ordered-testing design to estimate causal health effects while controlling family-wise error rate.
cells.F804: Directly relevant methodologically -- the ordered-testing design exploiting a logical hierarchy of related exposure definitions is a rigorous causal-inference pattern the founder's CEPT work could draw on.
cells.G804: Adapt the ordered-hypothesis-testing-across-a-hierarchy design to structure GSE's own multiple calibration-window testing (global model vs. sport-specific sub-models) while controlling false-discovery risk.

cells.C805: Human alignment of neural network representations
cells.D805: Studies which factors (scale, architecture, training data, objective) most affect alignment between neural network and human representations, finding data/objective matter far more than scale, and noting sports-related concepts align poorly.
cells.E805: Compares neural representations against human similarity judgments across datasets/tasks, testing linear transformations to improve alignment.
cells.F805: Directly noteworthy -- the explicit finding that 'sports-related objects' are poorly represented in current vision models is a direct caution if GSE leans on general-purpose models for sports-domain reasoning.
cells.G805: Use this paper's linear-transformation-alignment technique to fine-tune any general-purpose embedding GSE's agents (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) use so sports-domain concepts align better with expert judgment.

cells.C806: Learning to Perform Complex Tasks through Compositional Fine-Tuning of Language Models
cells.D806: Proposes compositional fine-tuning (CFT), decomposing a target task into component sub-tasks for curriculum fine-tuning of small LMs, evaluated partly on a 'sports understanding' task, outperforming chain-of-thought prompting with much smaller models.
cells.E806: Curriculum-based fine-tuning on explicit component sub-tasks instead of end-to-end learning or few-shot chain-of-thought prompting.
cells.F806: Directly relevant to GSE's internal agentic tooling -- a small, cheaply fine-tuned model matching large-LM chain-of-thought performance is highly relevant for cost-efficient internal Jarvis/Hermes/Fable agents doing sports-domain reasoning.
cells.G806: Use compositional fine-tuning to train a small, cheap internal model specialized in decomposed sports-understanding sub-tasks (e.g., parsing box scores) instead of relying on expensive large-LM calls.

cells.C807: Analysis of Smooth Pursuit Assessment in Virtual Reality and Concussion Detection using BiLSTM
cells.D807: Uses a BiLSTM RNN on oculomotor (eye-tracking) data from VR smooth-pursuit tests to detect sport-related concussion more objectively than self-reported symptoms.
cells.E807: BiLSTM sequence model with a custom weighted error metric predicts concussion status from eye-movement time series.
cells.F807: Not directly relevant to GSE's prediction engine; a clinical sports-medicine sequence-modeling application.
cells.G807: Long-shot: injury/concussion-detection signals like this could eventually feed a player-availability probability feature in GSE's Intelligence Graph, if partnered with medical data providers.

cells.C808: Potrika: Raw and Balanced Newspaper Datasets in the Bangla Language with Eight Topics and Five Attributes
cells.D808: Releases Potrika, a large Bangla news-article dataset across 8 categories including sports, with both raw and class-balanced versions for NLP research.
cells.E808: Dataset curation and augmentation-based balancing of a large multi-source news corpus for classification research.
cells.F808: Weak -- non-English NLP dataset unrelated to GSE's English-language brand-tone enforcement; relevant only as a dataset-construction methodology example.
cells.G808: The raw-vs-balanced dataset methodology could inspire GSE building its own balanced corpus of on-brand vs off-brand copy examples for automated style-lint training.

cells.C809: Virtual-Reality based Vestibular Ocular Motor Screening for Concussion Detection using Machine-Learning
cells.D809: Uses VR-generated Vestibular/Ocular Motor Screening (VOMS) data with multiple ML models to standardize and automate sport-related concussion detection, reaching about 99.9% true-positive rate.
cells.E809: Multiple ML classifiers trained on VR-captured smooth-pursuit and visual-motion-sensitivity test data to replace subjective manual VOMS scoring.
cells.F809: Not directly relevant to GSE's core prediction/calibration stack; a clinical concussion-screening application.
cells.G809: A distant future feature: automated concussion-risk flags feeding into a player-availability signal for the Intelligence Graph.

cells.C810: Temporal and Contextual Transformer for Multi-Camera Editing of TV Shows
cells.D810: Proposes a temporal-contextual Transformer model that automatically selects the best camera view across a multi-camera benchmark spanning concerts, sports games, and shows.
cells.E810: A Transformer uses historical shot context and other camera views to predict shot transitions and next-camera selection, trained on an 88-hour multi-camera dataset.
cells.F810: Directly relevant to GSE's automated social/media content generation ambitions -- automatic best-clip-selection logic could power auto-editing of highlight/pick-explainer video content.
cells.G810: Repurpose the shot-selection transformer's logic to auto-select the most relevant stat/graphic 'view' to surface at each moment in an auto-generated pick-explainer video.

cells.C811: Betting the system: Using lineups to predict football scores
cells.D811: Uses machine learning (best: Support Vector Regression) on lineup and player statistics to predict football scores, correctly forecasting all relegated teams and achieving 42% ROI emulating a real betting system.
cells.E811: Compares heuristic and ML models trained on individual player/lineup data to predict match scores, backtested against real-world odds, finding goalkeeper stats matter more than attacker stats.
cells.F811: Extremely directly relevant -- an end-to-end lineup-based score-prediction and real-odds backtesting case study is precisely the forecasting-plus-betting validation GSE needs to close its MAE gap.
cells.G811: Replicate this paper's lineup-level feature-importance analysis (goalkeeper over attacker stats) to check whether GSE's own model under-weights defensive features, a possible source of its baseline-losing MAE.

cells.C812: ASDOT: Any-Shot Data-to-Text Generation with Pretrained Language Models
cells.D812: Proposes a two-stage pipeline (disambiguation + fusion) using GPT-3/T5 to generate fluent text descriptions from structured data with few or no training examples.
cells.E812: Uses prompted LLMs to disambiguate data triples into sentences, then fuses them into coherent paragraphs, working in zero/few/full-shot regimes.
