cells.F919: Relevant as a template for GSE's data-ingestion pipeline design — an end-to-end pipeline of interdependent modules where errors propagate, similar to their ETL reliability concerns.
cells.G919: Adopt the paper's module-interdependency evaluation methodology to audit how errors in GSE's own scraping→cleaning→modeling stages compound into calibration failures.

cells.C920: Computing an Optimal Pitching Strategy in a Baseball At-Bat
cells.D920: Models a baseball at-bat as a zero-sum stochastic game between pitcher and batter, using deep nets for pitch-location and outcome prediction to compute optimal strategies.
cells.E920: Deep neural pitcher/batter representations feed a stochastic zero-sum game solver whose value is on-base percentage.
cells.F920: Directly relevant sports-analytics methodology GSE could use for MLB pick modeling — game-theoretic opponent modeling rather than naive baseline stats.
cells.G920: Use the zero-sum game-solving framework to model pitcher-vs-batter matchups as a genuinely better forecasting method, directly targeting GSE's MAE-vs-baseline problem in MLB picks.

cells.C921: A Markov process approach to untangling intention versus execution in tennis
cells.D921: Builds Markov reward/decision process models on hundreds of millions of simulated tennis shots to separate strategic intention from execution error, showing optimal strategies grow more conservative as execution error rises.
cells.E921: Markov decision/reward processes over shot-location data quantify how execution noise changes optimal value functions and strategies.
cells.F921: Methodologically relevant — a rigorous uncertainty-aware value-function approach that parallels GSE's 'bootstrap mode' need to adjust confidence under noisy/sparse execution data.
cells.G921: Borrow the intention-vs-execution decomposition to separate 'model uncertainty' from 'outcome variance' explicitly in GSE's confidence scores, sharpening bootstrap-mode adjustments per sport.

cells.C922: A review of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and its applications in a wide variety of disciplines
cells.D922: A broad survey of GAN variants and their applications across many fields including finance, marketing, fashion, sports, and music.
cells.E922: Summarizes GAN theory, evaluation metrics, and reviews domain-specific application patterns without new experiments.
cells.F922: Tangential — relevant only as background if GSE explores synthetic data generation for backtesting sparse sports data (e.g., new leagues with little history).
cells.G922: Use GANs to synthesize plausible historical game data for under-covered sports/leagues, giving bootstrap-mode models more synthetic training signal before real data accumulates.

cells.C923: The anatomy of social dynamics in escape rooms
cells.D923: Uses escape rooms as a social laboratory, applying network science to real-time team communication to reveal collaboration patterns and gendered conversational dynamics.
cells.E923: Motif analysis and signed-interaction network models characterize turn-taking and tension in small collaborative teams.
cells.F923: Not relevant to GSE's product; it studies human team collaboration dynamics, unrelated to sports prediction or calibration.
cells.G923: A stretch: could inform internal-agent (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) team-dynamics design if GSE studies how its multi-agent coding agents 'collaborate' analogously.

cells.C924: Three-Stream 3D/1D CNN for Fine-Grained Action Classification and Segmentation in Table Tennis
cells.D924: Fuses RGB, optical flow, and pose streams via attention and bilinear layers to classify and segment table-tennis strokes more accurately and with faster convergence.
cells.E924: A three-branch spatio-temporal CNN with attention fuses modalities at a late stage for fine-grained sports action recognition.
cells.F924: Not directly relevant — GSE's engine works from structured stats/odds, not video, though it echoes their general multi-model ensemble philosophy.
cells.G924: Only a loose methodological parallel: multi-stream late-fusion could inspire combining independent per-sport probability streams before the final ensemble, mirroring GSE's ensemble needs.

cells.C925: Dynamic Ranking with the BTL Model: A Nearest Neighbor based Rank Centrality Method
cells.D925: Extends the Bradley-Terry-Luce ranking model to a time-varying setting, using a locally-averaged Rank Centrality spectral method with proven error bounds for smoothly evolving pairwise comparisons like soccer results.
cells.E925: Local time-window averaging of pairwise comparison graphs feeds a spectral (Rank Centrality) estimator of time-varying latent team strengths.
cells.F925: Highly relevant to GSE's calibration blocker — a theoretically-grounded dynamic per-sport strength/ranking model, exactly the kind of independent per-sport probability model they suspect they need.
cells.G925: Use dynamic Rank Centrality as a candidate lightweight per-sport model in the multiplicative-weight ensemble alongside CEPT, giving a spectral-method alternative with formal error guarantees.

cells.C926: On deploying the Artificial Sport Trainer into practice
cells.D926: Describes a low-cost Raspberry Pi-based bike computer (AST-Monitor) for automatically monitoring realized cycling training sessions to close the loop with computer-generated training plans.
cells.E926: An embedded device with sensors and a custom GUI logs training-session telemetry to validate automatically generated training plans.
cells.F926: Not relevant to GSE, which does not build wearables or training-plan generation; purely a hardware/monitoring device paper.
cells.G926: No direct use; at most inspiration for a future consumer hardware/companion-app idea far outside GSE's current roadmap.

cells.C927: Frame by frame completion probability of an NFL pass
cells.D927: Uses a two-stage random forest model on player/ball tracking data to predict, frame-by-frame while the ball is in the air, the probability an NFL pass will be completed.
cells.E927: A random forest first predicts the intended target receiver, then conditionally predicts completion probability, combined via the law of total probability.
cells.F927: Directly on-target: a proper-scoring-friendly, real-time in-play probability model exactly like GSE would need for NFL live win-probability/pick confidence updates.
cells.G927: Adapt the two-stage conditional random-forest design as a live in-play recalibration signal, feeding real-time completion-probability shifts into GSE's confidence adjustments during a game.

cells.D928: Compares professional vs. beginner FPV drone racing pilots using precise position tracking, finding experts choose more optimal racing lines and post faster times.
cells.E928: High-resolution position tracking and trajectory analysis quantify skill-based differences in racing-line optimality and speed.
cells.F928: Not relevant to GSE's core sports (NFL/MLB/MLS) or its prediction stack; drone racing is a niche, unrelated sport.
cells.G928: No meaningful application beyond noting expertise-quantification techniques could generalize to any 'skill curve' analytics GSE might build for esports markets someday.

cells.C929: Exploring the Long Short-Term Dependencies to Infer Shot Influence in Badminton Matches
cells.D929: Introduces a badminton shot-by-shot language and a deep model with short-term and long-term encoders plus attention to predict rally outcomes and interpret shot influence.
cells.E929: A hierarchical sequence model (short-term extractor + long-term encoder) with attention frames rally analysis as sequence-to-outcome prediction with interpretability.
cells.F929: Adjacent inspiration for GSE's play-by-play/event-based modeling — an interpretable sequence model design pattern for shot/possession-level influence scoring.
cells.G929: Adapt the attention-based shot-influence idea to score which in-game events (turnovers, big plays) most shifted GSE's live win-probability, for transparent 'math you can read' explanations.

cells.C930: 6MapNet: Representing soccer players from tracking data by a triplet network
cells.D930: Uses a triplet network on GPS-derived heatmaps to learn playing-style embeddings that identify soccer players accurately from only a small number of matches, without action annotations.
cells.E930: Triplet-loss embedding learning maps location/velocity heatmap pairs into a feature space where similarity reflects playing-style similarity.
cells.F930: Adjacent — relevant if GSE expands into player-style profiling for MLS/soccer markets using positional data, rather than direct win-probability modeling.
cells.G930: Use triplet embeddings of team/player statistical 'signatures' to detect anomalous performance shifts (e.g., a team playing out of style) as an early-warning input to bootstrap-mode confidence caps.

cells.C931: A truncated mean-parameterised Conway-Maxwell-Poisson model for the analysis of Test match bowlers
cells.D931: Develops a Bayesian truncated Conway-Maxwell-Poisson model to rank cricket Test bowlers across eras, correcting for over/underdispersion in wicket-count data via MCMC.
cells.E931: A mean-parameterised, truncated CMP distribution handles non-Poisson dispersion in count data, fit with Bayesian MCMC to estimate bowler ability.
cells.F931: Directly relevant methodologically — demonstrates a flexible count-distribution alternative to naive Poisson/Gaussian scoring, useful for GSE's per-sport probability modeling of count-based stats.
cells.G931: Apply CMP-based dispersion modeling to GSE's under/over-dispersed sports counting stats (e.g., strikeouts, goals) to get better-calibrated tail probabilities than a plain Poisson baseline.

cells.C932: A Further Improvement on Approximating TTP-2
cells.D932: Improves the approximation ratio for the Traveling Tournament Problem (TTP-2) sports-scheduling optimization from 1+4/n to 1+3/n for even team counts.
cells.E932: A refined combinatorial approximation algorithm produces near-optimal round-robin schedules minimizing total team travel distance.
cells.F932: Not relevant to GSE's prediction/calibration work; this is a scheduling-optimization problem for league organizers, not bettors/analysts.
cells.G932: No direct product use; only a stretch if GSE ever built league-scheduling tools as a B2B adjacent offering.

cells.C933: Bowlership: Examining the Existence of Bowler Synergies in Cricket
cells.D933: Defines and analyzes cricket 'bowlerships' (pairwise bowler synergies) across thousands of matches, building bowlership networks to inform team selection and bowling changes.
cells.E933: Ball-by-ball data is mined for pairwise bowler performance synergy, represented as a network and used in a selection algorithm.
cells.F933: Adjacent inspiration — a synergy/interaction-effect modeling approach that could enrich GSE's per-sport models beyond independent player-level features.
cells.G933: Model 'pick synergy' across correlated same-game props (analogous to bowler pairs) to better price parlays where outcomes aren't independent.

cells.C934: A Unified Taxonomy and Multimodal Dataset for Events in Invasion Games
cells.D934: Proposes a universal event taxonomy for invasion sports (soccer, handball) and releases annotated video+positional datasets, benchmarking an I3D model for automatic event spotting.
cells.E934: A validated hierarchical taxonomy of low/high-level events grounds gold-standard multimodal annotations used to train and evaluate event-spotting models.
cells.F934: Relevant to GSE's data pipeline reliability — emphasizes the importance of consistent, validated event definitions, a discipline directly applicable to their pick/grading lifecycle definitions.
cells.G934: Apply the taxonomy-validation methodology (inter-annotator agreement studies) to audit ambiguity in GSE's own 'pick outcome' grading rules before they contaminate the calibration dataset.

cells.C935: Physics-informed machine learning improves detection of head impacts
cells.D935: Combines finite-element head-impact simulations with mouthguard sensor data to build a physics-informed classifier that detects true head impacts far more accurately than pure ML, cutting false positives.
cells.E935: Synthetic physics-simulation data augments a sparse, imbalanced real dataset to train a more robust impact-detection classifier.
cells.F935: Not directly relevant to GSE's win-probability stack, but methodologically relevant: augmenting sparse real data with simulated data to fix class imbalance parallels their bootstrap-mode/sparse-data problem.
cells.G935: Use simulated (synthetic) game outcomes to augment sparse historical data for newly-added leagues, similar to how physics simulation augments rare true-impact events here.

cells.C936: A comparison of sports-related head accelerations with and without direct head impacts
cells.D936: Finds that indirect impacts (e.g., torso pushes) in college football can produce head accelerations comparable to direct head hits, based on mouthguard sensor and video analysis.
cells.E936: Statistical comparison (Bonferroni-adjusted) of kinematic sensor data between impact-type categories, validated with finite-element brain-strain modeling.
cells.F936: Not relevant to GSE's prediction engine; this is sports-medicine biomechanics research on concussion risk.
cells.G936: No direct product use for GSE beyond noting player-health/injury-risk signals (if licensed) could someday feed player-availability inputs to models.

cells.D937: Presents the first 1+O(1/n) approximation algorithm for the constrained Traveling Tournament Problem TTP(2), improving on prior schedule-optimization bounds.
cells.E937: A combinatorial construction yields near-optimal round-robin sports schedules with proven approximation guarantees.
cells.F937: Not relevant to GSE's prediction/calibration focus; a pure scheduling-optimization result for league organizers.
cells.G937: No direct application; only relevant if GSE ever offers schedule-analysis tools as part of a B2B toolkit.

cells.C938: STAR: Noisy Semi-Supervised Transfer Learning for Visual Classification
cells.D938: Combines transfer learning with noisy-student self-training to classify sports-vs-non-sports images and yoga poses efficiently using only thousands (not billions) of unlabeled images.
cells.E938: A pretrained backbone is fine-tuned via iterative self-training on pseudo-labeled unlabeled images, requiring far less compute and memory than standard SSL.
cells.F938: Adjacent to GSE's data-pipeline concerns — a resource-efficient semi-supervised approach relevant if they ever need to label scraped sports images/video cheaply.
cells.G938: Apply noisy self-training to auto-tag scraped web images (e.g., from Pro-Football-Reference) for content/asset pipelines with minimal manual labeling effort.

cells.C939: TUM-VIE: The TUM Stereo Visual-Inertial Event Dataset
cells.D939: Releases a large stereo event-camera dataset with IMU and motion-capture ground truth, including rapid sports motion sequences, to benchmark visual-inertial SLAM algorithms.
cells.E939: Synchronized event cameras, stereo grayscale frames, and IMU data are hardware-timestamped and paired with motion-capture ground truth for SLAM evaluation.
cells.F939: Not relevant to GSE's software stack; this is a robotics/computer-vision sensor dataset unrelated to sports outcome prediction.
cells.G939: No meaningful application; purely a robotics benchmarking resource outside GSE's scope.

cells.C940: A Longitudinal Analysis on Instagram Characteristics of Olympic Champions
cells.D940: Analyzes four months of Olympic gold medalists' Instagram activity, finding engagement and self-presentation behaviors shift differently by age and gender over time.
cells.E940: Cross-sectional and longitudinal content analysis of social-media post characteristics is correlated with athlete demographics and engagement metrics.
cells.F940: Tangential — relevant only as background for GSE's automated social/media content generation, informing what athlete-related content drives engagement.
cells.G940: Use the engagement-pattern findings to time and format GSE's automated social posts about players/picks for maximum follower engagement.

cells.C941: A hydraulic model outperforms work-balance models for predicting recovery kinetics from intermittent exercise
cells.D941: Shows a three-compartment hydraulic model fits athlete recovery-from-exercise data better than established 'work-balance' models, despite using the same small sample sizes.
cells.E941: A physically-motivated hydraulic (tank/pipe) model with few parameters is fit to sparse exhaustive-exercise-test data and compared via information-criterion penalized metrics.
cells.F941: Methodologically relevant — demonstrates that a small-data, well-chosen structural model beats a simpler baseline, directly parallel to GSE's need for better forecasting methods over naive baselines.
cells.G941: Use the hydraulic-model philosophy (mechanistic small-parameter models beating naive baselines on scarce data) as a template for building a genuinely better MLB/NFL forecasting model instead of just re-tuning.

cells.C942: Implementing the BBE Agent-Based Model of a Sports-Betting Exchange
cells.D942: Describes three implementations (single-threaded, multi-threaded, GPU/OpenCL) of an agent-based simulation of a sports-betting exchange for generating large synthetic in-play betting datasets.
cells.E942: An agent-based model simulates bettors and a betting-exchange order book, with the GPU implementation running ~1000x faster to scale synthetic data generation.
cells.F942: Directly relevant to GSE's core problem — synthetic betting-market data generation is exactly what's needed to backtest calibration and closing-line-value benchmarks when real data is scarce.
cells.G942: Run GSE's prediction engine against synthetic BBE market data to stress-test calibration and CLV performance in scenarios (e.g., new sports) where real settled-pick history is still too thin.

cells.C943: The reaction to news in live betting
cells.D943: Uses high-frequency stake data and a state-space model to show live sports-betting markets systematically overreact to news events like goals, evidencing cognitive bias.
cells.E943: A state-space model separates baseline market activity from event-triggered spikes to quantify market overreaction to in-game news.
cells.F943: Highly relevant to GSE's closing-line-value benchmark — quantifies market inefficiency (overreaction) that a well-calibrated model could exploit for CLV-beating picks.
cells.G943: Build a live in-play signal that flags moments of likely market overreaction (right after big news events) as higher-value pick opportunities relative to the closing line.

cells.D944: Combines program synthesis with variational autoencoders to learn interpretable, symbolic-plus-neural latent representations, evaluated on animal-behavior and sports-analytics trajectory data.
cells.E944: A VAE decoder is paired with programs from a domain-specific language, synthesized to compose neural and symbolic components into factorized, interpretable encodings.
cells.F944: Relevant to GSE's 'math you can read' positioning — an interpretable representation-learning technique well-suited to explainable trajectory/behavior features feeding player or team models.
cells.G944: Use neurosymbolic encoders to turn play-by-play trajectories into human-readable symbolic 'behavior programs' that justify a pick's confidence in plain, non-AI-branded language.

cells.C945: ggViz: Accelerating Large-Scale Esports Game Analysis
cells.D945: Builds a visual analytics system (ggViz) that lets esports (CS:GO) analysts sketch-query tracking data to find similar game states, using win-probability charts and heatmaps.
cells.E945: Sketch-based querying over player-tracking data retrieves similar historical game states, summarized visually via win-probability curves and heatmaps.
cells.F945: Adjacent inspiration for GSE's internal analyst/coach tooling — a visual analytics pattern for surfacing win-probability context, potentially useful for a B2B analyst dashboard.
cells.G945: Build an internal ggViz-style tool letting GSE's own quants sketch-query historical game states to sanity-check model outputs during the calibration-fix effort.

cells.C946: Hierarchical Text Classification of Urdu News using Deep Neural Network
cells.D946: Introduces an Urdu news dataset spanning Sports/Technology/Entertainment and a hierarchical LSTM model (one layer per hierarchy level) that beats baselines at multi-level text classification.
cells.E946: Word2vec embeddings feed a hierarchical stack of LSTM layers, each trained for one level of a genre/topic hierarchy.
cells.F946: Not relevant to GSE's product; it's an Urdu-language NLP classification benchmark unrelated to sports prediction or calibration.
cells.G946: Only a stretch: the hierarchical text-classifier pattern could inspire multilingual auto-tagging of scraped foreign-language sports news for international market coverage.

cells.C947: Poisoning Attack against Estimating from Pairwise Comparisons
cells.D947: Formalizes data-poisoning attacks on pairwise-ranking algorithms (used in elections, sports, recommendations) as distributionally robust optimization, showing malicious comparisons can significantly corrupt rankings.
cells.E947: Integer-programming poisoning problems are relaxed into tractable DRO formulations to construct efficient adversarial ranking-corruption strategies.
cells.F947: Relevant as a security/data-integrity concern for GSE — highlights how manipulated or noisy inputs (scraped data, odds feeds) could corrupt its ranking/rating models if not defended against.
cells.G947: Use the attack framework defensively: stress-test GSE's rating models against adversarially-poisoned or manipulated data feeds to harden the data-ingestion pipeline against corrupted inputs.

cells.C948: Coach2vec: autoencoding the playing style of soccer coaches
cells.D948: Clusters and autoencodes ball-possession sequences from Serie A matches to produce compact 'coach style' embeddings that reveal similarities between prominent soccer coaches.
cells.E948: Ball possessions are clustered by similarity, then compressed into style embeddings via an autoencoder trained on event-stream data.
cells.F948: Adjacent — a style-embedding technique that could enrich GSE's MLS/soccer models with coach/team tendency features beyond raw box-score stats.
cells.G948: Add 'coach-style' embeddings as an ensemble feature for soccer picks, capturing tactical tendencies (possession style) that pure box-score models miss.

cells.C949: Feature Combination Meets Attention: Baidu Soccer Embeddings and Transformer based Temporal Detection
cells.D949: Fine-tunes action-recognition models on soccer footage to extract embeddings, then uses a transformer-based temporal detector to achieve state-of-the-art action spotting and replay grounding on SoccerNet-v2.
cells.E949: Action-recognition backbones produce high-level video embeddings which a transformer temporal-detection head localizes into specific soccer events.
cells.F949: Not directly relevant to GSE's odds/stats-based engine; this is video-understanding for event-spotting, a different data modality than GSE currently ingests.
cells.G949: Only relevant if GSE later scrapes broadcast video for automated highlight clipping to feed its social/content-automation tools.

cells.C950: Human Activity Recognition using Continuous Wavelet Transform and Convolutional Neural Networks
cells.D950: Converts 1D accelerometer signals into 2D wavelet-transform images and classifies them with CNNs, reaching 99.26% accuracy on human activity recognition benchmarks.
cells.E950: Continuous wavelet transform re-represents time-frequency signal features as images, which a CNN then classifies for activity type.
cells.F950: Not relevant to GSE's stack, which processes structured sports/odds data rather than wearable sensor signals.
cells.G950: No direct fit; a stretch only if GSE's Galaxy Dynasty game ever gamifies wearable fitness-tracker inputs.

cells.C951: Public Transit for Special Events: Ridership Prediction and Train Optimization
cells.D951: Uses Atlanta transit fare-collection data around stadium sporting events to build ridership-prediction models (regression, random forest) and optimize train frequency for event-driven demand surges.
cells.E951: Unsupervised clustering identifies boarding patterns, while regression/random-forest models forecast event-driven ridership demand to optimize scheduling.
cells.F951: Not directly relevant to GSE's prediction engine, but tangentially interesting as an example of event-driven time-series demand forecasting around sports events.
cells.G951: Adapt the event-driven demand-forecasting approach to predict spikes in GSE's own platform traffic/betting volume around big games, informing infra scaling (Vercel/BullMQ) decisions.

cells.C952: What Happened Next? Using Deep Learning to Value Defensive Actions in Football Event-Data
cells.D952: Defines a 'Defensive Action Expected Threat' metric using deep learning on Premier League event data to value tackles/interceptions by the danger they prevented, validated across two seasons.
cells.E952: A deep learning threat model estimates the expected-threat trajectory of play sequences, and defensive value is computed as the threat prevented by an action.
cells.F952: Directly relevant methodological pattern — an expected-threat/counterfactual valuation approach analogous to what GSE could use for player-impact features in soccer picks.
cells.G952: Adapt the 'threat prevented' framing to create a defensive-impact feature for MLS player props, differentiating GSE's models from generic offense-only stat lines.

cells.C953: Learning Football Body-Orientation as a Matter of Classification
cells.D953: Frames player body-orientation estimation from video as a classification problem with a cyclic loss, achieving under 12-degree median error using wearable-device ground truth for training.
cells.E953: A CNN classifies discretized orientation bins with a cyclic loss function, trained against EPTS wearable-derived orientation labels.
cells.F953: Not directly relevant — GSE doesn't process video; this is a computer-vision technique for extracting spatial features from broadcast footage.
cells.G953: Only relevant as future-proofing if GSE ever ingests video-derived player-orientation data as a feature for pass-completion or defensive models.

cells.C954: Enhancing Trajectory Prediction using Sparse Outputs: Application to Team Sports
cells.D954: Shows deep trajectory-prediction models for soccer struggle to beat linear extrapolation, but a sparse-prediction-plus-interpolation trick and a new graph+attention architecture (GraN-MA) improve performance.
cells.E954: Models predict sparse waypoints interpolated with constant acceleration, and a graph network with multi-head attention conditions predictions on all players' trajectories.
cells.F954: Directly relevant as a cautionary and instructive parallel — GSE's own model losing to a naive baseline (MAE 5.31 vs 4.91) mirrors this paper's finding that deep models often underperform simple extrapolation without careful design.
cells.G954: Apply the sparse-output-plus-interpolation trick as a concrete architecture change to help GSE's prediction engine finally beat its naive baseline, rather than only re-tuning calibration.

cells.C955: Analysis and classification of main risk factors causing stroke in Shanxi Province
cells.D955: Uses interpretable ML (decision tree, random forest, logistic regression, SHAP) on hospital and community data to rank stroke risk factors, finding physical inactivity ('lack of sports') among the top three.
cells.E955: Random forest and SHAP-value feature importance rank risk factors, with logistic regression estimating stroke probability per risk level.
cells.F955: Not relevant to GSE's product; this is a public-health study where 'sports' appears only as a lifestyle risk factor, unrelated to sports prediction.
cells.G955: No meaningful product application; purely coincidental keyword overlap with 'sports' as physical activity.

cells.C956: The Anatomy of Corner 3s in the NBA: What makes them efficient, how are they generated and how can defenses respond?
cells.D956: Uses player-tracking data and game theory to show NBA corner-three efficiency stems mainly from high assist rates, not shorter distance, and derives Nash-equilibrium defensive responses.
cells.E956: Spatial tracking-data analysis is combined with a simplified offense-defense game to find equilibrium strategies for contesting corner threes.
cells.F956: Directly relevant sports-analytics methodology — a strong example of moving beyond naive shot-distance metrics to game-theoretic, assisted-shot-aware modeling, relevant to any NBA market GSE might add.
cells.G956: Apply the game-theoretic equilibrium-finding approach to model optimal in-game strategic responses (not just outcome probabilities), enriching GSE's win-probability narratives with tactical explanations.

cells.C957: Modeling Collective Anticipation and Response on Wikipedia
cells.D957: Proposes a model of anticipatory growth and decay around Wikipedia page-view peaks (including planned sports events), improving prediction and clustering of attention dynamics versus prior models.
cells.E957: A parametric model captures anticipatory buildup, event-driven peak, decay, and circadian rhythm components to predict future page-view time series.
cells.F957: Adjacent — a time-series forecasting model for anticipatory/decay dynamics around known future events, conceptually similar to modeling betting-market attention/volume around scheduled games.
cells.G957: Adapt the anticipation-decay model to forecast betting volume or public interest spikes around scheduled games, informing GSE's content-automation timing and infra scaling.

cells.C958: Poisson Modeling and Predicting English Premier League Goal Scoring
cells.D958: Validates that EPL goal-scoring follows a Poisson process (goal counts, inter-goal times, timing) and uses Poisson regression simulations to predict season outcomes like relegation and title odds.
cells.E958: Poisson regression fit to historical goal data is used in large-scale season simulations to estimate probabilistic outcomes for teams.
cells.F958: Directly relevant — a textbook baseline soccer forecasting method GSE should benchmark against; also a natural component of a Brier/CLV-focused calibration pipeline for MLS/soccer markets.
cells.G958: Use Poisson-process validation as a diagnostic check: if GSE's soccer picks deviate from the expected Poisson goal-scoring distribution, that's a concrete signal of miscalibration to fix per-sport.

cells.C959: BBE: Simulating the Microstructural Dynamics of an In-Play Betting Exchange via Agent-Based Modelling
cells.D959: Details the design of the open-source Bristol Betting Exchange (BBE), an agent-based simulator of a sports-betting exchange with in-play racetrack betting, intended as a synthetic-data generator for AI/ML strategy research.
cells.E959: Simulated bettors with private odds beliefs place and update in-play bets on a simulated exchange, generating high-resolution synthetic market microstructure data.
cells.F959: Directly relevant to GSE's calibration and backtesting needs — a free, open-source synthetic betting-market generator to test model performance and CLV strategies without needing scarce real data.
cells.G959: Run GSE's calibration pipeline against BBE-simulated markets to pre-validate whether a proposed per-sport model or ensemble change would pass the three-consecutive-green-window gate before touching real picks.

cells.D960: Treats 2D CAD sketches (used in designing everything from mugs to sports cars) as a sequence-modeling problem, generating structured sketches with a language-model architecture.
cells.E960: CAD sketch primitives are serialized and modeled with a general-purpose sequence/language model for unconditional and image-conditioned sketch generation.
cells.F960: Not relevant to GSE's product; 'sports cars' is just an incidental CAD example, unrelated to sports prediction.

cells.C961: Sentiment and Emotion Classification of Epidemic Related Bilingual data from Social Media
cells.D961: Applies ML/DL sentiment and emotion classifiers to bilingual (Urdu/English) social media and news data to detect early signals of a dengue epidemic outbreak.
cells.E961: Sentiment/emotion classifiers trained on bilingual social text are used as an early-warning signal generator for outbreak detection.
cells.F961: Tangential — the underlying NLP sentiment-classification techniques could support GSE's brand-language/lint enforcement or social-listening for content automation, though the domain (epidemiology) is unrelated.
cells.G961: Repurpose the bilingual sentiment-classification pipeline to monitor social sentiment around teams/players as a soft signal input, kept separate from the deterministic scoring engine to preserve brand claims.

cells.C962: Home advantage and crowd attendance: Evidence from rugby during the Covid 19 pandemic
cells.D962: Analyzes 1,027 rugby matches across pandemic-era empty stadiums, finding home teams won fewer matches and had reduced point differentials without crowd support.
cells.E962: A natural-experiment regression design compares home-advantage metrics before and during no-crowd pandemic conditions.
cells.F962: Relevant as a concrete example of a real, quantifiable situational feature (crowd presence) that shifts sports outcomes — directly informative for GSE's per-sport feature engineering and calibration inputs.
cells.G962: Add a dynamic 'crowd/attendance effect' feature (updated in real time from attendance/venue data) to GSE's models, particularly useful during anomalous conditions like weather or travel disruptions.

cells.C963: Simplified Kalman filter for online rating: one-fits-all approach
cells.D963: Proposes a generic Bayesian Kalman-filter-style rating algorithm that unifies Elo, Glicko, and TrueSkill as special cases, applicable to any skills-outcome model in individual or team sports.
cells.E963: An approximate Kalman filter propagates skill estimates and uncertainty after each game using any chosen probabilistic skills-to-outcome model.
cells.F963: Extremely directly relevant — offers a principled, generic online rating/uncertainty-tracking framework that could unify or replace ad-hoc per-sport rating components feeding GSE's ensemble and calibration gate.
cells.G963: Use this unifying Kalman-filter formulation as the backbone for building genuinely independent per-sport probability models with proper uncertainty tracking, directly targeting the suspected calibration fix.

cells.C964: Aerodynamic effects and performance improvements of running in drafting formations
cells.D964: Uses CFD simulations to quantify how drafting formations reduce aerodynamic drag for distance runners, estimating up to 3.5% running-economy gains and meaningful marathon time savings.
cells.E964: Computational fluid dynamics models airflow around runner formations to compute drag reduction and translate it into metabolic/performance gains.
cells.F964: Not relevant to GSE's stack; a physics/biomechanics simulation study with no connection to prediction, calibration, or data pipelines.
cells.G964: No meaningful application; only tangential if GSE ever modeled granular endurance-race outcome factors like drafting effects.

cells.C965: Does home advantage without crowd exist in American football?
cells.D965: Finds NFL home-team performance drops substantially without spectators during COVID, but a home edge returns once even a limited crowd is present.
cells.E965: Historical NFL game data is compared across full-crowd, no-crowd, and limited-crowd conditions to isolate the psychological effect of fan attendance.
cells.F965: Directly relevant — quantifies a specific situational effect (crowd-driven home advantage) that is core domain knowledge for GSE's NFL probability models and feature set.
cells.G965: Incorporate a crowd-attendance-adjusted home-advantage term that dynamically discounts the standard home edge in games with reduced or unusual attendance (e.g., neutral-site games).

cells.C966: SportsCap: Monocular 3D Human Motion Capture and Fine-grained Understanding in Challenging Sports Videos
cells.D966: Introduces a monocular video pipeline that jointly recovers 3D human motion and fine-grained action attributes in sports footage using a motion-embedding module and spatial-temporal graph network.
cells.E966: A learned motion-embedding space with sub-motion classifiers feeds a multi-stream ST-GCN that predicts detailed action attributes for motion scoring/assessment.
cells.F966: Not directly relevant to GSE's odds/stats engine, since it requires video input GSE doesn't currently ingest.
cells.G966: Only relevant if GSE later builds video-derived player-form or technique-quality features for its Intelligence Graph.

cells.C967: Contrastive Learning for Sports Video: Unsupervised Player Classification
cells.D967: Uses contrastive learning to unsupervised-classify hockey players by team affiliation without labeled data, achieving 94% accuracy from a single video frame and 97% within seconds.
cells.E967: An embedding network is trained via contrastive loss to separate same-team from different-team player representations without manual labels.
cells.F967: Not directly relevant to GSE's structured-data engine, but methodologically interesting as an unsupervised approach requiring minimal labeled data.
cells.G967: Only useful if GSE processes scraped video for automated team/player identification within its content-automation pipeline.

cells.C968: Table Tennis Stroke Recognition Using Two-Dimensional Human Pose Estimation
cells.D968: Collects a large table-tennis stroke video dataset and trains a temporal CNN on 2D pose data to classify 11 stroke types with 99%+ accuracy, generalizing to unseen players.
cells.E968: 2D human pose estimation feeds a temporal convolutional network trained for multiclass stroke classification.
cells.F968: Not relevant to GSE's core product; a niche sports-technique-analysis computer-vision paper unrelated to outcome prediction.
cells.G968: No meaningful application to GSE's current roadmap.

cells.C969: Machine-learning-based head impact subtyping based on the spectral densities of the measurable head kinematics
cells.D969: Builds a random-forest classifier on spectral features of head-kinematics sensor data to distinguish impact types (football, MMA, car crash) and improve brain-strain regression via type-specific nearest-neighbor models.
cells.E969: Spectral density features of acceleration/velocity signals feed a random forest classifier, whose output conditions type-specific regression models for injury-risk estimation.
cells.F969: Not directly relevant to GSE's win-probability stack; a biomechanics/injury-classification paper in a different domain.
cells.G969: Only tangential inspiration: the type-specific-conditional-model pattern (classify subtype, then apply specialized regression) parallels the 'independent per-sport probability models' idea GSE is considering for calibration.

cells.C970: On the Linear Ordering Problem and the Rankability of Data
cells.D970: Uses the Linear Ordering Problem to quantify how 'rankable' a dataset is, showing optimal rankings maximize hindsight prediction accuracy and proposing a way to measure diversity among optimal rankings.
cells.E970: Integer/binary programming solves the linear ordering problem to find optimal rankings and computes maximal Kendall-tau distance between alternative optima.
cells.F970: Directly relevant — 'rankability' and hindsight-accuracy-maximizing rankings are foundational concepts for validating any sports rating system GSE builds, including sanity-checking calibration inputs.
cells.G970: Compute a 'rankability score' for each sport's historical results before modeling, flagging sports (or seasons) where outcomes are inherently noisy and thus need wider bootstrap-mode confidence caps.

cells.C971: The Effect of Sport in Online Dating: Evidence from Causal Machine Learning
cells.D971: Uses causal machine learning on online-dating platform data to estimate that weekly sport activity causally increases male users' odds of receiving a first message by 50%.
cells.E971: Causal ML (double/debiased machine learning) estimates heterogeneous treatment effects of sport frequency on dating-platform contact outcomes.
cells.F971: Not relevant to GSE's core prediction/calibration work; the sport reference is incidental to a causal-inference application in social science.
cells.G971: The only transferable thread is the causal-ML methodology itself (double ML for treatment-effect estimation), potentially reusable for isolating true causal drivers (e.g., injuries) in GSE's own feature engineering.

cells.C972: Leaving Goals on the Pitch: Evaluating Decision Making in Soccer
cells.D972: Learns a Markov Decision Process from soccer event-stream data and applies AI verification techniques to counterfactually evaluate whether teams should shoot more from outside the box, finding they should.
cells.E972: An MDP models team offensive behavior from event data, and formal verification/counterfactual reasoning techniques evaluate alternative policies against it.
cells.F972: Directly relevant — a rigorous counterfactual decision-evaluation framework (MDP + verification) that parallels what GSE needs to validate whether specific modeling/strategy choices are actually better than baseline.
cells.G972: Apply the same MDP-plus-counterfactual-verification framework to evaluate whether GSE's own pick-generation policy (e.g., which bets to publish) is leaving value on the table versus alternative policies.

cells.C973: Framework for Inferring Leadership Dynamics of Complex Movement from Time Series
cells.D973: Proposes a generic framework to infer which agents initiate coordinated group activities (sports, animal movement) from time-series data, without assuming leader characteristics.
cells.E973: A model-free inference framework detects 'faction initiators' driving coordinated group-movement changes from multivariate time series.
cells.F973: Adjacent — a general multi-agent time-series inference technique that could inspire novel team-dynamics features (who 'leads' momentum shifts) for GSE's sports models.
cells.G973: Apply the leadership-inference framework to identify which player's actions most often precede momentum swings, creating a novel 'catalyst' feature for in-game win-probability models.

cells.C974: Streaming Social Event Detection and Evolution Discovery in Heterogeneous Information Networks
cells.D974: Builds a heterogeneous information network with a graph convolutional network (PP-GCN) to detect and track evolving social media events (including sports) in real time via streaming clustering.
cells.E974: A meta-path-based heterogeneous graph is processed by a graph convolutional network with similarity search and clustering to detect and evolve event categories in real time.
cells.F974: Adjacent to GSE's Intelligence Graph ambitions — a graph-based, typed-node approach to representing and clustering evolving events, directly analogous to a typed knowledge-primitives layer.
cells.G974: Adapt the heterogeneous-graph event-detection architecture as a technical blueprint for GSE's planned Intelligence Graph, streaming new sports events into typed nodes with evolving clusters.

cells.C975: Autonomous Overtaking in Gran Turismo Sport Using Curriculum Reinforcement Learning
cells.D975: Trains a reinforcement learning controller with curriculum learning to autonomously overtake in the Gran Turismo Sport racing game, matching experienced human driver performance.
cells.E975: Curriculum reinforcement learning progressively increases task difficulty to train a racing-game control policy that outperforms vanilla RL and built-in game AI.
cells.F975: Not relevant to GSE's prediction/calibration work; a robotics/game-AI control paper in a racing-simulation domain.
cells.G975: Only tangential: curriculum-learning technique could inspire how GSE trains its own internal coding/research agents (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) on progressively harder tasks.

cells.C976: Deep Similarity Learning for Sports Team Ranking
cells.D976: Compares LightGBM, XGBoost, and Siamese neural networks with contrastive vs. triplet loss for ranking NBA and Super Rugby teams, finding triplet-loss models achieve state-of-the-art ranking metrics.
cells.E976: Gradient-boosted trees and Siamese networks are trained with pairwise/triplet ranking losses to predict match importance and produce team rankings.
cells.F976: Directly relevant — a comparative benchmark of ensemble (LightGBM/XGBoost) vs. deep similarity-learning approaches for sports ranking, exactly the kind of model comparison GSE needs to beat its naive baseline.
cells.G976: Benchmark triplet-loss Siamese ranking against GSE's current prediction engine on held-out picks, potentially adopting it as one arm of the multiplicative-weight ensemble if it improves MAE.

cells.C977: Evaluation of soccer team defense based on prediction models of ball recovery and being attacked: A pilot study
cells.D977: Proposes predicting frequent events (ball recovery, being attacked) rather than rare goals to build a more reliable defensive-performance index for soccer teams, validated against season outcomes.
cells.E977: Classifiers trained on positional/event data predict frequent intermediate events, whose predicted probabilities are aggregated into a defense-quality index correlated with season results.
cells.F977: Directly relevant methodological insight — favoring frequent proxy-event prediction over rare-event (goal) prediction is a concrete way to build more data-efficient, better-calibrated per-sport sub-models.
cells.G977: Apply the 'predict frequent proxy events instead of rare outcomes' principle to build auxiliary sub-models (e.g., predicting turnovers/possession) that feed into and stabilize GSE's sparse-data win-probability models.

cells.C978: Multi-view data capture for dynamic object reconstruction using handheld augmented reality mobiles
cells.D978: Builds a decentralized multi-mobile synchronization system for capturing nearly-synchronous multi-view video, releasing a new outdoor sports-action dataset (4DM) for 3D reconstruction.
cells.E978: On-device SLAM plus a wireless triggering/data-relay architecture achieves flexible frame synchronization across multiple moving handheld cameras.
cells.F978: Not relevant to GSE's odds/stats-based product; a multi-camera 3D-reconstruction systems paper.
cells.G978: No meaningful application within GSE's current scope.

cells.D979: Proposes a multivariate functional additive mixed model with functional PCA to jointly model correlated functional data streams, demonstrated on snooker-player movement trajectories.
cells.E979: Functional principal component analysis captures cross-dimensional dependency in multivariate functional responses within an additive mixed-model framework, including functional random intercepts.
cells.F979: Methodologically relevant — a rigorous statistical framework for correlated time-series/functional sports data with proper uncertainty bands, applicable to GSE's time-series sports data modeling.
cells.G979: Use multivariate functional mixed models to jointly model correlated time-series signals (e.g., pace, scoring rate) across a game, producing calibrated confidence bands rather than point estimates.

cells.C980: Deep Transfer Learning for WiFi Localization
cells.D980: Trains a CNN on WiFi CSI data for indoor localization and shows feature-extraction layers transfer across environments (including a sports hall), cutting training data and time needs substantially.
cells.E980: A CNN localizes devices from WiFi channel-state-information fingerprints, with transfer learning reusing early layers across different physical environments.
cells.F980: Not relevant to GSE's product; this is indoor-positioning infrastructure research with only incidental sports-hall test venue.
cells.G980: No meaningful application to GSE's roadmap.

cells.C981: Data-driven Analysis for Understanding Team Sports Behaviors
cells.D981: A survey of data-driven methods for understanding invasion-sport (basketball, soccer) team behaviors, covering interpretable feature extraction and generative/controllable behavior simulation approaches.
cells.E981: Reviews techniques for visualizing learned representations, extracting mathematical structure, and simulating counterfactual team behaviors from multi-agent sports data.
cells.F981: Directly relevant as a survey of the exact modeling techniques (interpretable multi-agent behavior models, counterfactual simulation) GSE would draw on for building better, explainable per-sport models.
cells.G981: Use the survey's counterfactual-simulation techniques to generate 'what-if' game outcome distributions as a transparent way to communicate pick confidence without invoking 'AI' branding.

cells.C982: Predictive Factors of Kinematics in Traumatic Brain Injury from Head Impacts Based on Statistical Interpretation
cells.D982: Uses commonality and dominance analysis across multiple head-impact datasets (football, MMA, car crashes) to identify which kinematic factors (angular acceleration, direction) best predict brain strain.
cells.E982: Structure coefficients, commonality analysis, and dominance analysis decompose regression predictive power among correlated kinematic predictors.
cells.F982: Not directly relevant to GSE's stack; a biomechanics feature-importance study in an unrelated injury-risk domain.
cells.G982: Only a loose methodological parallel: dominance/commonality analysis could be reused to decompose which GSE model features actually drive predictive power, aiding interpretability.

cells.C983: Collision Prediction and Prevention in Contact Sports Using RFID tags and Haptic Feedback
cells.D983: Builds an RFID proximity-sensing system that gives athletes haptic warnings of impending player-to-player collisions, validated with pilot tests and simulated NFL data, achieving under 14% false alarms.
cells.E983: RFID-based proximity sensing triggers real-time haptic alerts using a contact-prediction algorithm validated against simulated game data.
cells.F983: Not relevant to GSE's software product; this is athlete-safety wearable hardware, unrelated to prediction/calibration.
cells.G983: No meaningful product application within GSE's scope.

cells.C984: TEyeD: Over 20 million real-world eye images with Pupil, Eyelid, and Iris 2D and 3D Segmentations
cells.D984: Releases a massive labeled eye-tracking image dataset (including outdoor sports activity recordings) with landmarks, gaze vectors, and eye-movement annotations for VR/AR research.
cells.E984: Multiple head-mounted eye trackers capture and automatically annotate millions of eye images across diverse activities for gaze-estimation model training.
cells.F984: Not relevant to GSE's product; sports activity is just one of several incidental data-collection contexts in an eye-tracking dataset paper.
cells.G984: No meaningful application to GSE's roadmap.

cells.C985: Brain Performance Analysis based on an Electroencephalogram Headset
cells.D985: Uses a consumer EEG headset and web app to track students' focus, stress, and engagement, suggesting neurofeedback could help improve sport and artistic performance.
cells.E985: Consumer EEG hardware streams brainwave-derived metrics (focus, stress, engagement) into a web application correlated with self-reported activities.
cells.F985: Not relevant to GSE's product; sports performance is mentioned only as one speculative future application of neurofeedback for students.
cells.G985: No meaningful product application for GSE.

cells.C986: Bayesian GARCH Modeling of Functional Sports Data
cells.D986: Proposes a hierarchical Bayesian model combining a smooth functional trend with a heteroskedastic-error mixed model to describe and predict shot-put athletes' performance trajectories across seasons.
cells.E986: A functional-data smooth term plus a linear mixed-effects model with GARCH-like heteroskedastic errors jointly captures seasonal trend, athlete-specific variance, and forecasts future performance.
cells.F986: Highly relevant — a Bayesian hierarchical model explicitly handling heteroskedasticity (varying uncertainty) over time is directly applicable to GSE's calibration problem, especially for volatile, sparse-data sports.
cells.G986: Adopt the GARCH-style heteroskedastic-error component as the mechanism behind bootstrap-mode's confidence caps, formally tying uncertainty width to detected volatility regimes rather than an ad-hoc rule.

cells.C987: Evaluating Soccer Player: from Live Camera to Deep Reinforcement Learning
cells.D987: Introduces an 'Expected Discounted Goal' (EDG) metric computed via deep reinforcement learning on simulated soccer, paired with an open-source player-tracking model, requiring no human-labeled outcome data.
cells.E987: A supervised player-tracking model feeds a deep RL agent trained purely on simulated soccer games to produce a discounted-goal-value metric for player evaluation.
cells.F987: Directly relevant methodology — an RL-based, simulation-trained value metric parallels the kind of genuinely improved forecasting model GSE needs to beat its naive baseline, and is extensible to other sports.
cells.G987: Adapt the simulation-trained RL valuation approach (no real labeled outcomes needed) to bootstrap better win-probability models for newly-added sports/leagues where historical settled-pick data is still sparse.

cells.C988: EventAnchor: Reducing Human Interactions in Event Annotation of Racket Sports Videos
cells.D988: Builds an interactive annotation tool that uses computer-vision models to pre-detect key events (serves, bounces) in racket-sports video, significantly speeding up human annotation workflows.
cells.E988: CV models propose candidate event detections which a human annotator refines through an interactive tool, reducing manual annotation effort.
cells.F988: Adjacent to GSE's data pipeline concerns — a human-in-the-loop annotation-acceleration pattern relevant if they ever need to label scraped video/event data more efficiently.
cells.G988: Apply the human-in-the-loop pre-detection pattern to speed up manual QA of ambiguous scraped stats (e.g., disputed play results) before they enter the grading pipeline.

cells.C989: Heatmap-based Object Detection and Tracking with a Fully Convolutional Neural Network
cells.D989: Develops 'CueNet,' a fully convolutional network that tracks a fast-moving cueball on a labyrinth game via heatmap prediction, reaching over 99.6% frame accuracy.
cells.E989: A fully convolutional network converts single or sequential input frames into a probability heatmap localizing a fast-moving object.
cells.F989: Not directly relevant to GSE's odds/stats-based stack, though the heatmap-tracking approach is a generic sports-ball-tracking technique.
cells.G989: Only relevant if GSE ever ingests ball-tracking video data (e.g., for MLB pitch location) as an additional structured-data source.

cells.C990: Estimating the change in soccer's home advantage during the Covid-19 pandemic using bivariate Poisson regression
cells.D990: Argues bivariate Poisson regression reduces bias versus linear models for estimating home-advantage changes, applying it across 17 soccer leagues to find mixed (not uniformly declining) effects of empty stadiums.
cells.E990: Bivariate Poisson regression jointly models home/away goal counts, shown via simulation to have far lower bias than linear regression for estimating soccer effects.
cells.F990: Directly relevant — a concrete demonstration that using the correct outcome distribution (Poisson, not linear/Gaussian) meaningfully reduces bias, directly applicable to fixing GSE's soccer-specific probability models.
cells.G990: Audit GSE's soccer model for the same linear-vs-Poisson bias identified here; switching to bivariate Poisson regression for goal modeling could be a concrete, low-effort calibration improvement for the MLS pipeline.

cells.C991: Estimation of the effective reproduction number for SARS-CoV-2 infection during the first epidemic wave in the metropolitan area of Athens, Greece
cells.D991: Compares two standard methods (Wallinga-Teunis, Cori et al.) for estimating COVID-19's effective reproduction number in Athens, noting sports-facility closures among the interventions that reduced transmission.
cells.E991: Two established epidemiological estimators compute time-varying effective reproduction numbers from case-notification data.
cells.F991: Not relevant to GSE's product; sports facilities are mentioned only as one closed venue type during pandemic interventions, in an unrelated epidemiology paper.
cells.G991: No meaningful product application; only a loose analogy in that 'effective reproduction number' style time-varying-rate estimation resembles time-varying team-strength estimation, a stretch at best.

cells.C992: Relationship between brain injury criteria and brain strain across different types of head impacts can be different
cells.D992: Shows that standard brain injury criteria (BIC) do not transfer accurately across head-impact types (sports vs. car crashes) when predicting actual brain strain.
cells.E992: Linear regression models relate 18 BIC metrics to physiologically measured brain strain across five impact-type datasets, comparing within-domain vs. cross-domain fit.
cells.F992: Directly analogous to GSE's cross-sport calibration failure: a single global metric/model doesn't generalize across domains, supporting the founder's hypothesis that per-sport probability models are needed.
cells.G992: Use their cross-domain generalization-error methodology as a template for quantifying how much GSE's calibration degrades when a model trained on NFL data is applied to MLB or MLS.

cells.C993: Hate Speech detection in the Bengali language: A dataset and its baseline evaluation
cells.D993: Introduces a 30,000-comment Bengali hate speech dataset from YouTube/Facebook and benchmarks classifiers including SVM and deep learning models.
cells.E993: Crowd-sourced annotation plus baseline supervised text classifiers (SVM, deep nets with word embeddings) for hate-speech detection.
cells.F993: Tangential: GSE's brand-language lint rule (banning 'AI-powered' claims) and its social content generation both need robust text classification for compliance moderation.
cells.G993: Adapt the annotation/classifier pipeline to auto-flag banned marketing phrases ('AI-powered') in GSE's own auto-generated social content before publish.

cells.C994: Who is the best coach of all time? A network-based assessment of the career performance of professional sports coaches
cells.D994: Builds head-to-head interaction networks from 60+ years of soccer and basketball games to rank coaches by network centrality.
cells.E994: Constructs pairwise coach-vs-coach networks from game results and applies centrality metrics to produce dynamic, time-resolved rankings.
cells.F994: A direct sports-analytics ranking methodology GSE could mine for building historical strength/skill features feeding its prediction engine.
cells.G994: Use coach-network centrality as a slow-moving prior feature in the ensemble, giving 'coaching quality' a Bayesian prior independent of team roster changes.

cells.C995: Limits of PageRank-based ranking methods in sports data
cells.D995: Finds PageRank only outperforms simple win-count ranking early in a season and proposes a PageRank variant that beats it in all tested settings.
cells.E995: Calibrates a synthetic sports-results generator to real league data, then stress-tests PageRank vs. baseline and a new variant under varying randomness/home-advantage.
cells.F995: Directly warns against naive network-ranking methods for GSE's models — relevant to why their core model currently loses to a naive baseline (MAE 5.31 vs 4.91).
cells.G995: Use their synthetic-results calibration framework as a sandbox to diagnose exactly which randomness sources (home advantage, intrinsic variance) are breaking GSE's model versus the naive baseline.

cells.C996: Combining Machine Learning and Human Experts to Predict Match Outcomes in Football: A Baseline Model
cells.D996: Shows that combining statistical match data with NLP-derived features from journalist match previews improves EPL outcome prediction accuracy by 6.9%.
cells.E996: NLP models extract signal from newspaper match-preview text, fused with statistical features in a classifier for win/draw/loss prediction.
cells.F996: Directly relevant to improving GSE's core model, which currently loses to the naive baseline — suggests unstructured text/expert-opinion features as an untapped signal source.
cells.G996: Feed GSE's own auto-generated pre-game content (or scraped beat-writer previews) back into the model as a text-derived feature, closing the loop between content generation and prediction.

cells.C997: Forecasting the Olympic medal distribution during a pandemic: a socio-economic machine learning model
cells.D997: Uses a two-stage Random Forest on socio-economic variables to forecast Olympic medal counts more accurately than naive baselines.
cells.E997: Two-stage Random Forest ensemble trained on historical socio-economic and Games-level covariates, validated against prior Olympics.
cells.F997: A concrete example of an ensemble method beating a naive forecast baseline — directly useful reference for GSE's core model that currently loses to naive MAE.
cells.G997: Borrow the two-stage RF architecture (macro socio-economic stage + fine-grained stage) as a template for a two-stage per-sport model: league-level base rate, then game-level adjustment.

cells.C998: A New Action Recognition Framework for Video Highlights Summarization in Sporting Events
cells.D998: Combines YOLO-v3 and OpenPose in a three-level prediction pipeline to automatically clip sports video highlights with improved accuracy.
cells.E998: Cascaded object detection plus pose estimation drives an action-recognition classifier that flags highlight-worthy segments in sports video.
cells.F998: Directly supports GSE's automated social/media content generation ambition — auto-clipping highlights from game footage for distribution.
cells.G998: Use auto-detected highlight clips as triggers for real-time 'pick' content generation — automatically publishing graded-pick commentary synced to the exact play that resolved it.

cells.C999: CanonPose: Self-Supervised Monocular 3D Human Pose Estimation in the Wild
cells.D999: Learns single-image 3D human pose estimation without labeled data by exploiting multi-view consistency across unlabeled, even uncalibrated, camera footage.
cells.E999: Self-supervised disentanglement of 2D pose into 3D pose and camera rotation using multi-view reconstruction losses, validated on an in-the-wild ski dataset.
cells.F999: Tangential to GSE's core betting/calibration work, but relevant if GSE ever ingests broadcast video for player-tracking features to enrich its data pipeline.
cells.G999: Use uncalibrated multi-broadcast-camera consistency to auto-derive player positioning features from free public game footage, without needing paid tracking-data feeds.

cells.C1000: Bayesian Nonparametric Estimation for Point Processes with Spatial Homogeneity: A Spatial Analysis of NBA Shot Locations
cells.D1000: Develops a Bayesian nonparametric (Dirichlet process + Markov random field) model to estimate smooth, locally-homogeneous shot intensity surfaces for NBA players.
cells.E1000: Combines Dirichlet process clustering with a Markov random field prior to enforce spatial smoothness in a point-process intensity estimate, fit via MCMC.
cells.F1000: A directly applicable Bayesian nonparametric technique for GSE's per-sport probability modeling effort, illustrating how to build smooth, well-calibrated spatial/contextual probability surfaces.
cells.G1000: Apply the same Dirichlet-process/MRF smoothing to GSE's pick-confidence surface across bet types and lines, reducing calibration noise (helping the ECE/Brier gate) in sparse-data regions.

cells.C1001: Self-Supervised Small Soccer Player Detection and Tracking
cells.D1001: Presents a self-supervised pipeline for detecting and tracking small, similar-looking soccer players in broadcast video without any labeled ground truth.
cells.E1001: Self-supervised detection/tracking that bootstraps training signal from unlabeled video itself, avoiding costly manual annotation for small-object multi-player tracking.
cells.F1001: Relevant to GSE's data pipeline robustness — self-supervised extraction techniques could reduce reliance on paid tracking feeds for MLS/soccer coverage.
cells.G1001: Repurpose the self-supervised bootstrapping idea for GSE's web-scraping pipeline: auto-validate scraped stat tables against unlabeled secondary sources without manual QA.

cells.C1002: Game Plan: What AI can do for Football, and What Football can do for AI
cells.D1002: A DeepMind position paper surveying how statistical learning, game theory, and computer vision combine to advance predictive and prescriptive football analytics.
cells.E1002: Reviews state-of-the-art methods (counterfactual predictive models, game-theoretic penalty-kick analysis) and argues football is a rich testbed for multi-agent AI research.
cells.F1002: Broad strategic relevance to GSE's core mission — a roadmap of techniques (counterfactual analysis, game theory) applicable to improving prediction and understanding market dynamics like closing-line value.
cells.G1002: Adapt their game-theoretic penalty-kick framework to model line-setter/bettor strategic interaction, helping interpret closing-line value as an equilibrium GSE's model can exploit or benchmark against.

cells.C1003: Deep Learning Analysis and Age Prediction from Shoeprints
cells.D1003: Trains a deep CNN (ShoeNet) on 100,000 shoeprints to predict a person's age and gender from gait-related pressure/abrasion patterns.
cells.E1003: Multi-branch CNN with skip connections extracts pressure and asymmetry features from paired shoeprints to regress age and classify gender.
cells.F1003: Minimal direct relevance; the most honest thread is general biomechanical/forensic data-engineering practice for large noisy sensor datasets, not GSE's core product.
cells.G1003: Not directly applicable — best framed as inspiration for handling large noisy multi-source sensor datasets robustly, a data-pipeline reliability parallel rather than a modeling one.

cells.C1004: Analysing Long Short Term Memory Models for Cricket Match Outcome Prediction
cells.D1004: Proposes an LSTM model that ingests ball-by-ball cricket statistics to produce continuously updated in-match win probabilities.
cells.E1004: Recurrent neural network (LSTM) processes sequential ball-level match state to output a live win-probability estimate at any timestamp.
cells.F1004: Directly relevant as a time-series forecasting architecture GSE could use for live in-game win-probability updates as picks move from proposed to graded.
cells.G1004: Use an LSTM win-probability head as a real-time recalibration signal, dynamically adjusting 'bootstrap mode' confidence caps as more in-game data accrues.

cells.C1005: A new robust class of skew elliptical distributions
cells.D1005: Introduces a flexible multivariate skew-distribution family with closed-form density, validated on river-flow and Australian Institute of Sport biomedical athlete data.
cells.E1005: Nested parametric construction generalizes canonical skew distributions to model multivariate skewness without severe curse-of-dimensionality, fit via maximum likelihood.
cells.F1005: Directly useful for GSE's probability-modeling work: sports outcome/performance distributions are often skewed, and this offers a tractable non-Gaussian alternative for per-sport probability models.
cells.G1005: Fit skew-elliptical distributions to per-sport scoring margins instead of assuming symmetric normal errors, potentially closing part of the calibration gap by better matching real outcome skew.

cells.C1006: Visualization of Technical and Tactical Characteristics in Fencing
cells.D1006: Presents FencingVis, an interactive visualization system that reveals tactical patterns and strategies in simultaneous-action fencing bouts using tactical flow graphs.
cells.E1006: Custom bar-chart action sequences plus a graph-based 'tactical flow graph' visualize footwork/bladework patterns and mutual fencer influence.
cells.F1006: Tangential — relevant mainly to GSE's dashboarding/analytics UX for niche sports rather than the core calibration or forecasting problems.
cells.G1006: Adapt the tactical flow graph concept as a B2B embeddable widget showing decision-pattern visualizations for niche sports, differentiating GSE's toolkit beyond mainstream leagues.

cells.C1007: Valuing Player Actions in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive
cells.D1007: Introduces an open-source data model and context-aware valuation framework that scores individual player actions in CS:GO by their effect on win probability.
cells.E1007: A graph-distance state representation feeds a context-aware action-value model (akin to expected-goals-style frameworks) trained on 70M+ in-game events.
cells.F1007: Directly relevant methodology (win-probability-based action valuation) transferable to GSE's pick-grading and player-impact features across traditional sports.
cells.G1007: Extend the framework to esports/Galaxy Dynasty's persistent web game, giving in-game player actions real value scores that feed both the prediction engine and game economy.

cells.D1008: Using Kenyan mobile betting transaction data, finds bettors adjust wagering behavior in a Bayesian-updating-consistent way based on past wins/losses, without increased debt.
cells.E1008: Econometric analysis (instrumental variables, behavioral response modeling) of over 50,000 users' real-money sports betting transaction histories.
cells.F1008: Directly relevant to GSE's target market and behavior model — informs understanding of user response to pick performance and could shape responsible-engagement features.
cells.G1008: Use the Bayesian-updating behavioral model to design GSE's user-facing calibration disclosures, framing pick performance feedback in the same terms bettors intuitively update on.

cells.C1009: Multi-agent Trajectory Prediction with Fuzzy Query Attention
cells.D1009: Presents a relational trajectory-prediction architecture with fuzzy attention that models inertia, relative motion, and interactions, validated on NBA and traffic data.
cells.E1009: A novel continuous-valued 'fuzzy' attention mechanism flexibly models pairwise interactions between agents for multi-agent trajectory forecasting.
cells.F1009: Directly relevant as a state-of-the-art architecture for modeling multi-agent sports dynamics (player trajectories), a building block for richer per-sport predictive features.
cells.G1009: Use the fuzzy-attention interaction model to generate an 'interaction risk' feature capturing how entangled two teams' player movements are, feeding into bootstrap-mode uncertainty scoring.

cells.C1010: A statistical model to assess risk for supporting SARS-CoV-2 quarantine decisions
cells.D1010: Develops a Bayesian model estimating the probability no COVID-19 transmission occurred given a sequence of PCR test results, accounting for time-varying test sensitivity.
cells.E1010: Parametric Bayesian model combines time-dependent test sensitivity/specificity with sequential test results to output a posterior transmission-risk probability.
cells.F1010: Tangential — the methodology (Bayesian sequential evidence updating under noisy measurements) parallels how GSE could update pick confidence as new odds/data arrive.
cells.G1010: Repurpose the sequential Bayesian-evidence framework to model how confidence in a pick should update as multiple odds-movement 'signals' accumulate before lock time.

cells.C1011: Object shape error modelling and simulation during early design stage by morphing Gaussian Random Fields
cells.D1011: Proposes a Morphing Gaussian Random Field method to simulate manufacturing-induced shape deviations in parts (e.g., SUV doors) under limited data.
cells.E1011: Models spatial correlation of manufacturing deviations via Gaussian Random Fields, then generates synthetic non-ideal parts via conditional simulation.
cells.F1011: Minimal direct relevance to GSE; the honest thread is the general technique of generating synthetic data under data scarcity via spatially-correlated random fields.
cells.G1011: Borrow the conditional Gaussian-field synthetic-data-generation idea to stress-test GSE's ingestion pipeline with realistic synthetic 'noisy' sports data variants.

cells.C1012: Contextualized Word Embeddings Encode Aspects of Human-Like Word Sense Knowledge
cells.D1012: Finds BERT embeddings capture human judgments of word-sense relatedness, distinguishing homonymy (e.g., 'bat' as animal vs. sports equipment) from polysemy.
cells.E1012: Compares human relatedness judgments from a spatial-arrangement experiment against distances in BERT's contextual embedding space.
cells.F1012: Tangential — relevant to NLP-based brand-language enforcement (detecting disallowed senses/phrasing like 'AI-powered') via contextual embedding similarity.
cells.G1012: Use embedding-space sense-distance to catch subtle paraphrases of banned marketing claims ('smart predictions', 'intelligent picks') that keyword-based lint rules would miss.

cells.C1013: Beating the market with a bad predictive model
cells.D1013: Proves it's possible to profit systematically even with an inaccurate price-predicting model by explicitly decorrelating predictions from consensus market pricing.
cells.E1013: Alters model training objective to maximize decorrelation from market price, exploiting market-maker pricing biases rather than raw predictive accuracy, tested on stocks and sports betting.
cells.F1013: Extremely directly relevant: speaks to GSE's closing-line-value benchmark and suggests accuracy alone (Brier/MAE) isn't the only lever — decorrelation from market consensus can be profitable even with a currently underperforming model.
cells.G1013: Add a decorrelation-objective term to the model training loss specifically for markets where GSE beats naive MAE the least, potentially yielding positive CLV even before the calibration gate is fully passed.

cells.C1014: G-Elo: Generalization of the Elo algorithm by modelling the discretized margin of victory
cells.D1014: Extends the Elo rating algorithm to incorporate margin of victory (not just win/loss/draw) via a principled probabilistic model, validated on EPL and NFL data.
cells.E1014: Defines a probabilistic model linking team skills to discretized margin-of-victory, derives online stochastic-gradient rating updates analogous to Elo, with closed-form coefficient estimation.
cells.F1014: Directly applicable rating-system upgrade for GSE's prediction engine — margin-aware Elo could feed as a well-calibrated baseline/ensemble component, particularly for NFL where it's validated.
cells.G1014: Use G-Elo ratings as one arm of GSE's ensemble, explicitly as the 'transparent, math you can read' rating baseline that also improves calibration via its principled probabilistic foundation.

cells.C1015: Towards Real-time Drowsiness Detection for Elderly Care
cells.D1015: Proof-of-concept deep learning system detects drowsiness cues (yawning, eyelid, head movement) from video for elderly monitoring, noting sports-rehab applicability.
cells.E1015: CNN classifiers on extracted video frames detect eyelid/mouth open-close states, combined with 3D head-pose tracking for spatiotemporal drowsiness patterns.
cells.F1015: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's prediction engine; the honest thread is computer-vision pipeline technique reusable if GSE ever adds athlete-condition monitoring features.
cells.G1015: Not a strong fit — at most, inspiration for a novel 'player fatigue proxy' feature if GSE ever ingests broadcast facial/video data for in-game fatigue signals.

cells.C1016: A Bayesian Hidden Semi-Markov Model with Covariate-Dependent State Duration Parameters for High-Frequency Data from Wearable Devices
cells.D1016: Extends hidden semi-Markov models so state-duration parameters vary over time as a function of covariates, applied to a soccer referee's wearable physiological data.
cells.E1016: Bayesian HSMM with time-varying, covariate-dependent duration parameters, plus a data-subsampling scheme to handle violated conditional-independence in high-frequency sensor streams.
cells.F1016: Directly relevant modeling technique for GSE's time-series/event-based sports data — HSMMs are a natural fit for modeling game-state transitions (possession, momentum) with duration effects.
cells.G1016: Model a game's 'pick lifecycle' states (proposed→modeled→locked→graded) or in-game momentum states as a covariate-dependent HSMM to better time when confidence should shift.

cells.C1017: SoccerMap: A Deep Learning Architecture for Visually-Interpretable Analysis in Soccer
cells.D1017: A fully convolutional network estimates full probability surfaces for pass success, pass selection, and pass value from spatiotemporal soccer tracking data.
cells.E1017: Multi-scale CNN learns dense pixel-level probability maps from sparse single-pixel ground truth, enabling interpretable, visually-rich soccer analytics.
cells.F1017: Directly relevant as an interpretable deep learning technique that produces calibrated probability surfaces — a template for improving GSE's soccer/MLS probability model interpretability and accuracy.
cells.G1017: Adapt the full-surface probability estimation approach beyond passing to model a live 'win probability field' across all remaining game states, useful for in-game pick repricing.

cells.C1018: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Spatio-Temporal Action Localization
cells.D1018: Proposes an end-to-end unsupervised domain adaptation method for action localization that generalizes trained models to new video domains without labeled target data, tested partly on UCF-Sports.
cells.E1018: Image-level (spatial/temporal) and instance-level domain adaptation modules minimize distribution shift between source and target video domains within an object-detection framework.
cells.F1018: Tangential to GSE's core forecasting work, but the domain-shift-robustness concept directly parallels the cross-sport calibration generalization problem GSE faces.
cells.G1018: Borrow the domain-adaptation module design as a conceptual template for adapting a global calibrator to a new sport with little data, rather than fully retraining a bespoke per-sport model.

cells.C1019: Deep Learning Head Model for Real-time Estimation of Entire Brain Deformation in Concussion
cells.D1019: A deep neural network replaces slow finite-element simulations, predicting brain strain from head-impact kinematics in under 1 millisecond with strong accuracy.
cells.E1019: Five-layer DNN with engineered kinematic features (favoring angular acceleration over velocity) trained on 1,803 simulated and real football/MMA head impacts.
cells.F1019: Tangential to GSE's product, but a strong example of using a fast learned surrogate model to replace a computationally expensive first-principles simulation — a pattern applicable to real-time pick scoring.
cells.G1019: Apply the same 'fast neural surrogate replacing slow simulation' pattern to approximate CEPT's more expensive e-process/multiplicative-weight ensemble computation for real-time confidence scoring.
