cells.C1020: A New Open-Access Platform for Measuring and Sharing mTBI Data
cells.D1020: Describes an open-source platform for sharing head-impact biomechanics data plus a deep learning algorithm (96% accuracy) to filter false-positive impact detections from mouthguard sensors.
cells.E1020: Centralized data-sharing infrastructure integrated with a neural-network-based impact-detection classifier for wearable sensor streams.
cells.F1020: Tangential; the relevant thread is the open data-sharing platform pattern and sensor-noise-filtering classifier, both parallel to GSE's own data-pipeline reliability needs for noisy scraped/odds feeds.
cells.G1020: Adopt the false-positive-filtering classifier pattern to auto-detect and discard corrupted or anomalous scraped stat rows in GSE's Pro-Football-Reference ingestion pipeline.

cells.C1021: Automatic Extraction of Urban Outdoor Perception from Geolocated Free-Texts
cells.D1021: Proposes a generic NLP method to extract spatial-temporal-semantic perceptions of urban areas from free-text social media posts, validated against a controlled human-labeled dataset.
cells.E1021: Combines spatial-temporal filtering with semantic similarity clustering of free-text opinions to extract location-based sentiment/perception signals.
cells.F1021: Tangential — could inform GSE's social/media content pipeline by extracting fan sentiment or venue-context signals from geolocated social posts as auxiliary features.
cells.G1021: Mine geolocated fan chatter near stadiums for real-time sentiment/crowd-mood signals as a novel low-cost feature input to the confidence/bootstrap-mode adjustment.

cells.C1022: LiveQA: A Question Answering Dataset over Sports Live
cells.D1022: Introduces a 117k-question multiple-choice QA dataset built from NBA play-by-play broadcasts, testing timeline reasoning and in-game math computation.
cells.E1022: Human-commentator-written questions paired with live broadcast timelines evaluate QA models' ability to track events and compute statistics over time.
cells.F1022: Directly relevant to GSE's ambitions for automated content generation and B2B widgets — a benchmark for building conversational/QA features over live game and pick data.
cells.G1022: Use a LiveQA-style benchmark internally to validate an in-house 'ask the engine' chat feature that answers user questions about live picks without ever claiming to be 'AI-powered' in copy.

cells.C1023: Regression to the Tail: Why the Olympics Blow Up
cells.D1023: Shows Olympic Games cost overruns follow a heavy power-law distribution with infinite mean/variance, making them fundamentally hard to predict or plan for.
cells.E1023: Fits and tests power-law versus other statistical distributions against decades of Olympic cost-overrun data, identifying causal structural drivers of extreme tail risk.
cells.F1023: Tangential but genuinely useful: a cautionary case study in heavy-tailed, poorly-calibratable domains — relevant to GSE's own tail-risk and uncertainty quantification thinking in bootstrap mode.
cells.G1023: Use their power-law diagnostic tests to check whether GSE's own settlement/loss distributions (e.g., parlay or high-variance prop bets) are heavy-tailed enough to require special tail-risk-aware confidence caps.

cells.C1024: Synthetic Training for Accurate 3D Human Pose and Shape Estimation in the Wild
cells.D1024: Trains a 3D human pose/shape regression network entirely on synthetic data (STRAPS) and introduces the SSP-3D sports-person evaluation benchmark.
cells.E1024: Uses on-the-fly synthetic training data from a statistical body model plus proxy representations (silhouettes, 2D joints) with domain-randomization to close the sim-to-real gap.
cells.F1024: Tangential to GSE's core betting product, but the synthetic-data-generation-for-scarce-labels pattern is directly relevant to how GSE could generate synthetic sports events for sparse-sport bootstrap-mode training.
cells.G1024: Apply the synthetic-data-augmentation pattern to generate plausible synthetic game outcomes for low-data sports/markets, giving bootstrap mode more training signal before real data accumulates.

cells.C1025: Weight Training Analysis of Sportsmen with Kinect Bioinformatics for Form Improvement
cells.D1025: Uses Kinect depth sensing to capture and analyze weightlifting motion parameters (range of motion, speed, balance) to give athletes real-time form feedback.
cells.E1025: Kinect depth-image joint tracking feeds algorithms computing biomechanical parameters for real-time and comparative motion analysis.
cells.F1025: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's forecasting/calibration work; a weak thread is general sports-tech data capture, not GSE's actual product surface.
cells.G1025: Not a strong fit for GSE's core business — best framed as unrelated adjacent sports-tech rather than a genuine product lever.

cells.C1026: Analysis of Models for Decentralized and Collaborative AI on Blockchain
cells.D1026: Evaluates simple ML models (Perceptron, Naive Bayes, Nearest Centroid) hosted on blockchain smart contracts under an incentive mechanism, using a sports-prediction dataset among others.
cells.E1026: Simulates blockchain-hosted model updates with a Self-Assessment incentive scheme, tracking accuracy, participant balances, and gas costs over time.
cells.F1026: Tangential — the incentive-mechanism-for-collaborative-model-updating concept could inform a future decentralized/community-contributed data or model layer for GSE, though blockchain itself isn't core.
cells.G1026: Borrow the incentive-mechanism design (not the blockchain) to structure a crowd-sourced data-correction/validation bounty system for GSE's scraped data quality issues.

cells.C1027: Using Social Networks to Improve Group Transition Prediction in Professional Sports
cells.D1027: Shows that incorporating social-network data substantially improves prediction of how MLB and NBA players move between teams compared to performance/fitness data alone.
cells.E1027: Machine learning models combine individual performance, team-fit, and social-relationship data to predict player team transitions.
cells.F1027: Directly relevant data-source insight for GSE: social-network features materially improve prediction accuracy, suggesting an underused signal category for roster/lineup-dependent picks.
cells.G1027: Add a social-network-derived 'team cohesion' feature (player connectivity/tenure overlap) to GSE's per-sport models as a novel predictor beyond standard box-score stats.

cells.C1028: DeepSOCIAL: Social Distancing Monitoring and Infection Risk Assessment in COVID-19 Pandemic
cells.D1028: Combines YOLOv4 detection, inverse perspective mapping, and SORT tracking to monitor social distancing and estimate infection risk from CCTV footage.
cells.E1028: Hybrid CNN detection plus tracking pipeline computes pairwise distances between detected people and statistically analyzes violation trajectories over time.
cells.F1028: Tangential; explicitly notes applicability to sports/crowd analysis, and the detection+tracking pipeline architecture is reusable for GSE if it ever processes broadcast crowd/player video.
cells.G1028: Repurpose the tracking pipeline for stadium-crowd-density analytics as a novel B2B data product for venues, adjacent to GSE's embeddable-widget ambitions.

cells.C1029: Super-Human Performance in Gran Turismo Sport Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
cells.D1029: A deep RL agent trained in the Gran Turismo Sport simulator outperforms the game's built-in AI and the fastest human driver among 50,000+ players.
cells.E1029: Deep reinforcement learning with a course-progress-proxy reward trains a racing policy in a high-fidelity physics simulator to master minimum-time trajectory control.
cells.F1029: Directly relevant to GSE's Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR persistent game ambitions — a proven RL approach for building competitive game-playing agents within a simulated sports environment.
cells.G1029: Use a similar RL-with-proxy-reward approach to train NPC opponents or difficulty-scaled bots for Galaxy Dynasty, giving the game credible skill-based AI without violating the 'not AI-powered' marketing rule for the prediction product itself.

cells.C1030: ConvGRU in Fine-grained Pitching Action Recognition for Action Outcome Prediction
cells.D1030: Applies a convolutional GRU to RGB video sequences of pitching motions to predict pitch outcomes with 79.17% accuracy, beating prior state of the art.
cells.E1030: ConvGRU processes spatiotemporal video sequences of pitching action, with ablations on sampling, fusion, and pretraining strategies for fine-grained outcome classification.
cells.F1030: Directly relevant if GSE ever incorporates video-derived features (pitcher mechanics) into its MLB models — a concrete architecture for outcome prediction from raw motion.
cells.G1030: Use fine-grained pitching-motion outcome prediction as an early-warning signal feature (e.g., fatigue/mechanics degradation) that adjusts confidence on in-game MLB picks mid-at-bat.

cells.C1031: Using Experts' Opinions in Machine Learning Tasks
cells.D1031: Proposes a framework for incorporating expert opinions/betting odds into ML pipelines, applied to NCAA basketball prediction, beating top Kaggle leaderboard solutions on log loss.
cells.E1031: A three-step framework blends historical data-driven models with external expert signals (polls, betting odds) and evaluates using proper scoring (log loss).
cells.F1031: Highly directly relevant: explicitly uses betting odds and proper scoring rules for sports prediction, offering a concrete blueprint for improving GSE's Brier/log-loss calibration via odds-informed ensembling.
cells.G1031: Formally incorporate The Odds API's market-implied probabilities as an explicit ensemble member (not just a benchmark for CLV), directly targeting the calibration gate via odds-anchored blending.

cells.C1032: NewsTweet: A Dataset of Social Media Embedding in Online Journalism
cells.D1032: Builds a large dataset and pipeline studying how tweets get embedded in Google News stories, finding sports and entertainment news embed tweets most heavily.
cells.E1032: Large-scale automated data collection pipeline links Google News articles to embedded tweets, analyzing source diversity and newsworthiness patterns.
cells.F1032: Tangential — offers a data-pipeline pattern (automated large-scale multi-source collection/linking) relevant to GSE's ingestion of news/social content for automated media generation.
cells.G1032: Adapt the news-tweet linking pipeline to auto-surface which social posts about a game correlate with line movement, feeding a sentiment-based feature into odds/CLV analysis.

cells.C1033: Image Generation for Efficient Neural Network Training in Autonomous Drone Racing
cells.D1033: Proposes semi-synthetic image generation (real backgrounds plus randomized 3D-rendered gates) to train gate-detection CNNs for autonomous drone racing without costly manual data collection.
cells.E1033: Domain-randomized synthetic image compositing generates unlimited labeled training data, paired with a line-of-sight guidance algorithm for autonomous navigation.
cells.F1033: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's core product; the honest thread is the general synthetic-data-generation technique for data-scarce training, echoing bootstrap-mode's sparse-data problem.
cells.G1033: Apply domain-randomized synthetic event generation to augment sparse historical data for newly-added niche sports, helping bootstrap mode converge faster.

cells.C1034: Wisdom of crowds: much ado about nothing
cells.D1034: Using Federal Reserve forecaster survey data, finds the aggregated 'crowd' forecast beats most individual forecasters only ~70% of the time and beats all individuals in under 2% of cases, challenging popular wisdom-of-crowds claims.
cells.E1034: Statistical analysis (variance-diversity correlation, skew analysis) tests competing theoretical explanations of crowd forecasting accuracy against real survey data.
cells.F1034: Directly relevant and cautionary for GSE's ensemble strategy: aggregating multiple models/forecasters doesn't guarantee beating the best individual model, informing realistic expectations for the multiplicative-weight ensemble.
cells.G1034: Use their diversity-vs-error correlation methodology to empirically audit whether GSE's planned ensemble actually reduces Brier/ECE versus just picking the single best-calibrated per-sport model.

cells.C1035: Real-time CNN-based Segmentation Architecture for Ball Detection in a Single View Setup
cells.D1035: Proposes an efficient CNN segmentation architecture for detecting a poorly-contrasted, fast-moving ball from a single camera view in real time, with a public dataset release.
cells.E1035: A pair of consecutive frames feeds a segmentation CNN with test-time augmentation to localize the ball without requiring temporal-delay analysis.
cells.F1035: Tangential — relevant only if GSE expands into video-derived real-time event features; otherwise a stretch from core calibration/forecasting work.
cells.G1035: Not a strong fit for the core product — best framed as inspiration for low-latency real-time video feature extraction if GSE builds live in-game repricing from broadcast feeds.

cells.C1036: Contact and Human Dynamics from Monocular Video
cells.D1036: Presents a physics-based trajectory optimization method that corrects unrealistic artifacts (foot penetration, extreme leaning) in kinematic 3D pose estimates from video, including sports motions.
cells.E1036: A contact-timing prediction network combined with physics-based trajectory optimization refines noisy kinematic pose estimates into physically plausible motion.
cells.F1036: Tangential — a data-cleaning pattern (physics-constrained correction of noisy estimates) conceptually similar to how GSE might apply domain constraints to clean noisy scraped/ingested data.
cells.G1036: Borrow the 'apply known physical/domain constraints to clean noisy estimates' pattern to sanity-check scraped box-score data against known game-logic constraints (e.g., score monotonicity) in the ETL pipeline.

cells.C1037: An Autoencoder Based Approach to Simulate Sports Games
cells.D1037: Proposes an autoencoder-based pipeline (UCLData dataset) to simulate how an interrupted UEFA Champions League season might have concluded.
cells.E1037: An autoencoder trained on six years of Champions League game data generates plausible simulated season outcomes and narratives.
cells.F1037: Directly relevant as a season-simulation/what-if forecasting technique, useful for GSE's longer-horizon forecasting and content-generation (narrative 'season outlook') features.
cells.G1037: Use autoencoder-based season simulation to generate probabilistic season-outcome distributions for GSE's automated content ('most likely playoff scenarios'), bridging forecasting and content automation.

cells.C1038: Ordinal Regression with Fenton-Wilkinson Order Statistics: A Case Study of an Orienteering Race
cells.D1038: Introduces a sigmoidal ordinal-regression model based on log-normal leg-time assumptions and Fenton-Wilkinson approximations to accurately predict relay-race finishing places from limited training data.
cells.E1038: Combines Fenton-Wilkinson log-normal sum approximations with a German-tank-problem-style team-count estimator to build an interpretable place-prediction regression function.
cells.F1038: Directly relevant statistical technique — an interpretable, closed-form probabilistic model that outperforms standard regression baselines with little data, aligning with GSE's 'math you can read' positioning and bootstrap-mode needs.
cells.G1038: Adapt the Fenton-Wilkinson order-statistics approach to model finishing-position distributions in individual/racing sports (e.g., golf leaderboards, NASCAR), a currently underexplored bet-type category.

cells.C1039: A metabolomic measure of energy metabolism moderates how an inflammatory miRNA relates to rs-fMRI network and motor control in football athletes
cells.D1039: Integrates fMRI, metabolomic, and VR behavioral measures across a college football season to find biomarkers of subconcussive brain effects from repeated head impacts.
cells.E1039: Permutation-based mediation/moderation analysis links molecular biomarkers to brain-network changes and behavioral (balance) degradation over a season.
cells.F1039: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's forecasting/calibration core; a weak thread is that this is injury-risk research potentially useful for a distant player-availability feature.
cells.G1039: Not a strong fit for GSE's current roadmap — at most, distant inspiration for a future 'injury-risk-adjusted' player-availability feature grounded in biomarker research literature.

cells.C1040: Identifying group contributions in NBA lineups with spectral analysis
cells.D1040: Uses spectral (algebraic signal processing) analysis to decompose NBA team success into orthogonal contributions from individuals, pairs, triples, and full lineups.
cells.E1040: Spectral decomposition of the team-success signal over the lineup-combination space yields pure, non-overlapping group-size contribution components.
cells.F1040: Directly relevant technique for GSE's per-sport modeling — a principled way to attribute predictive signal to lineup combinations rather than only individual player stats, useful for NBA models.
cells.G1040: Use spectral lineup decomposition to build a 'lineup synergy' feature that captures pairwise/triple chemistry effects the naive baseline model is currently missing, directly targeting the MAE gap.

cells.C1041: Two-Sample Testing on Ranked Preference Data and the Role of Modeling Assumptions
cells.D1041: Develops distribution-free and model-based two-sample tests for pairwise-comparison/ranking data, applied to find no significant difference between two seasons of European football team performance.
cells.E1041: Derives sample-complexity bounds for hypothesis testing under various pairwise comparison models (BTL, Thurstone, weak/strong stochastic transitivity) with matching lower bounds.
cells.F1041: Directly relevant statistical toolkit for GSE — rigorous two-sample testing could validate whether a new per-sport model's calibration genuinely differs (improves) from the old one across consecutive windows.
cells.G1041: Use their two-sample testing framework as the formal statistical test underlying GSE's '3 consecutive green calibration windows' launch gate, replacing ad hoc threshold checks with a principled significance test.

cells.C1042: Technical Note: Generating Realistic Fighting Scenes by Game Tree
cells.D1042: Uses a temporal-expansion mapping to apply turn-based game-tree algorithms (Minimax, alpha-beta pruning) to generate realistic, strategically-aware fighting motion sequences.
cells.E1042: Maps continuous-time multi-agent action planning into a discrete causality space enabling classical game-tree search with an offense/defense tactical table.
cells.F1042: Tangential — the game-theoretic strategy-planning approach for continuous sports interactions has conceptual overlap with modeling player decision-making in team sports, though not a core calibration technique.
cells.G1042: Explore using the temporal-expansion game-tree approach to generate synthetic strategic play sequences for Galaxy Dynasty's NPC opponents.

cells.C1043: Evaluating and Rewarding Teamwork Using Cooperative Game Abstractions
cells.D1043: Introduces Cooperative Game Abstractions (CGAs), a parametric model enabling fast, interpretable computation of Shapley values for team contribution from data, tested on RL agents and real sports teams.
cells.E1043: CGAs learn a characteristic function from data that permits linear-time Shapley value computation (avoiding combinatorial blowup), with identification and error-bound guarantees.
cells.F1043: Directly relevant technique for GSE's player/lineup attribution needs — a computationally tractable way to fairly value individual player contributions to team outcomes for feature engineering.
cells.G1043: Use CGA-derived Shapley values as an interpretable per-player 'contribution score' feature, giving GSE's 'math you can read' marketing a literal, auditable attribution metric to showcase publicly.

cells.C1044: Embed2Detect: Temporally Clustered Embedded Words for Event Detection in Social Media
cells.D1044: Combines word embeddings with hierarchical agglomerative clustering to detect real-world events from social media text streams, outperforming baselines on sports and political datasets by 27-29% F-measure.
cells.E1044: Semantic word-embedding features plus temporal hierarchical clustering identify event bursts in social media without relying on purely statistical/syntactic signals.
cells.F1044: Directly relevant to GSE's data pipeline for detecting breaking sports news (injuries, lineup changes, trades) from social/web sources that could move odds or require re-modeling a pick.
cells.G1044: Deploy Embed2Detect-style event detection on team beat-writer/Twitter feeds as an early-warning trigger to auto-flag picks needing re-grading or confidence downgrades before line movement catches up.

cells.C1045: Cracking the Black Box: Distilling Deep Sports Analytics
cells.D1045: Builds an interpretable 'model tree' (linear models + regression-tree structure) that mimics a deep neural network's sports predictions with high fidelity, producing actionable insights for coaches.
cells.E1045: Distills a black-box deep learning sports model into a linear-model-tree surrogate using scalable model-tree learning heuristics for million-row datasets.
cells.F1045: Extremely directly relevant: offers a concrete path for GSE to keep a deep/complex model's accuracy while producing an interpretable surrogate — directly serving the 'math you can read' brand promise while allowing internal use of any technique.
cells.G1045: Distill any future black-box ensemble (including CEPT-based components) into a public-facing linear model tree, letting GSE publish transparent 'why this pick' explanations without violating the no-AI-marketing rule.

cells.C1046: Text Detection and Recognition in the Wild: A Review
cells.D1046: A comprehensive survey and unified benchmark evaluation of scene text detection/recognition methods, noting applications including sports video analysis.
cells.E1046: Reviews deep learning architectures for detecting/recognizing text in natural images and benchmarks pretrained models on shared evaluation criteria across challenge conditions.
cells.F1046: Tangential — relevant only if GSE needs OCR for scraping scoreboard/graphic overlays from broadcast video, a minor potential data-ingestion use case.
cells.G1046: Use scene-text recognition to auto-extract scoreboard/stat-overlay data directly from broadcast video as an alternative or validation source alongside Pro-Football-Reference scraping.

cells.D1047: Studies how leader/follower roles spontaneously emerge in small human walking groups using time-dependent cross-correlation analysis, suggesting extension to team sports.
cells.E1047: Time-dependent cross-correlation of movement data infers leader-follower interaction structure between pairs of group members without designated roles.
cells.F1047: Tangential — the multi-agent leadership-inference methodology could inform identifying which players drive tempo/tactical shifts in team sports, a novel feature category.
cells.G1047: Apply cross-correlation leadership analysis to in-game player movement data to derive an 'on-court leadership' feature that captures tempo-setting influence beyond box-score stats.

cells.C1048: Same-Score Streaks: A Case Study in Probability Modeling
cells.D1048: Analyzes the likelihood of consecutive games with identical scores in MLB history (1901-2019) and fits probability models for run distributions to simulate streak frequencies.
cells.E1048: Historical frequency analysis combined with fitted probability distributions for runs scored, used to simulate and validate streak-length likelihoods.
cells.F1048: Directly relevant to GSE's core scoring/calibration work — a concrete case study in fitting and validating probability models against real MLB scoring distributions.
cells.G1048: Use their same-score-streak validation methodology as an additional out-of-sample calibration sanity check — if GSE's fitted scoring distribution can't reproduce real streak frequencies, that's a red flag for model misspecification beyond Brier/ECE alone.

cells.C1049: Space-Time VON CRAMM: Evaluating Decision-Making in Tennis with Variational generatiON of Complete Resolution Arcs via Mixture Modeling
cells.D1049: Uses an infinite Bayesian Gaussian mixture model on continuous-time tennis tracking data to estimate expected shot value and decompose player performance into shot execution, shot selection, and court coverage metrics.
cells.E1049: A three-step Bayesian generative pipeline (infinite GMM, conditioning on observed trajectories, outcome prediction) produces continuous-time expected value estimates from functional trajectory data.
cells.F1049: Directly relevant: a sophisticated Bayesian mixture-modeling approach for player-level expected value in a specific sport — a strong template for GSE's per-sport probability model / ensemble redesign.
cells.G1049: Adapt the infinite-GMM functional framework to decompose pick-level model error into 'selection' vs. 'execution' components, helping diagnose whether GSE's MAE gap comes from bad situational modeling or bad outcome prediction.

cells.C1050: DAG-Net: Double Attentive Graph Neural Network for Trajectory Forecasting
cells.D1050: Proposes a recurrent generative graph neural network with double attention (goal-aware and interaction-aware) that achieves state-of-the-art multi-agent trajectory forecasting in both urban and sports settings.
cells.E1050: Graph attention network models both agents' individual future goals and mutual interactions to generate multi-modal trajectory forecasts.
cells.F1050: Directly relevant multi-agent forecasting architecture applicable to modeling player/ball movement as a richer feature source for GSE's per-sport models.
cells.G1050: Use goal-aware graph attention to forecast likely game-state trajectories (not just player movement) as a structured feature input for in-game live-pick repricing.

cells.C1051: From Witch's Shot to Music Making Bones -- Resources for Medical Laymen to Technical Language and Vice Versa
cells.D1051: Introduces a German-language dataset and resources mapping laymen medical terminology to technical medical concepts from patient forum text, including sports/lifestyle context.
cells.E1051: Annotated corpus links colloquial health expressions to formal medical terms/synonyms/definitions, with baseline NLP models for term linking.
cells.F1051: Minimal direct relevance to GSE; the honest thread is the general laymen-to-technical language mapping technique, conceptually similar to translating quant model output into plain-language pick explanations.
cells.G1051: Borrow the laymen-to-technical mapping methodology to build the reverse pipeline: translating GSE's statistical model outputs into plain, jargon-free 'math you can read' user-facing explanations.

cells.C1052: Intra- and Inter-Action Understanding via Temporal Action Parsing
cells.D1052: Introduces the TAPOS sports-video dataset with sub-action annotations and shows that parsing actions into constituent sub-actions (even without labels) improves action recognition.
cells.E1052: Temporal parsing method mines latent sub-actions from training data in an unsupervised manner, revealing hierarchical intra-action and inter-action structure.
cells.F1052: Tangential to GSE's core forecasting work; relevant mainly if video-derived fine-grained action features are eventually incorporated into per-sport models.
cells.G1052: Apply unsupervised sub-action parsing to break down complex plays (e.g., a football drive) into latent sub-phases, generating finer-grained situational features than standard box-score data.

cells.C1053: Group Activity Detection from Trajectory and Video Data in Soccer
cells.D1053: Evaluates self-attention models on both trajectory and video data to detect group activities (atomic soccer events) with sub-0.5-second temporal resolution, using a large Sportlogiq dataset.
cells.E1053: Self-attention models learn to extract relevant player-group interaction information from either positional trajectory data or raw video for event detection.
cells.F1053: Directly relevant to GSE's data pipeline — demonstrates event-detection methods from tracking-style data that could enrich soccer/MLS event-level features beyond box scores.
cells.G1053: Use trajectory-based self-attention event detection as a data-quality cross-check, flagging when scraped box-score events disagree with detected on-field activity patterns.

cells.C1054: Do Sports and Politics Mix? Cross-Analysis of Fan Bases of Major League Sports and Presidential Candidates
cells.D1054: Analyzes Twitter data to quantify hidden relationships between NBA/NFL fan bases and political candidate preferences at sport, state, and team levels.
cells.E1054: Proposes a novel 'Congressional Devotedness Score' metric derived from Twitter engagement data to model fan-candidate preference alignment.
cells.F1054: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's core prediction engine; the honest thread is social-media audience-segmentation methodology potentially useful for targeted content/marketing.
cells.G1054: Not a strong technical fit — at most, inspiration for audience-segmentation analytics if GSE builds targeted social content campaigns by fan demographic.

cells.C1055: TTNet: Real-time temporal and spatial video analysis of table tennis
cells.D1055: Presents TTNet, a real-time neural network for spotting events, detecting the ball, and segmenting table tennis video at 120fps with sub-6ms inference, plus a labeled multi-task dataset.
cells.E1055: A multi-task network jointly performs event spotting, ball detection, and semantic segmentation on downscaled video, enabling near-real-time automated game analysis.
cells.F1055: Tangential to GSE's core calibration work; relevant mainly as a real-time video-analytics architecture pattern if GSE expands into live video-derived features for niche sports.
cells.G1055: Not core-relevant — best framed as future-state inspiration for a low-latency auto-referee/event-spotting feature if GSE ever adds live video ingestion for underserved sports like table tennis.

cells.C1056: Decoupling Video and Human Motion: Towards Practical Event Detection in Athlete Recordings
cells.D1056: Uses 2D pose sequences as an intermediate representation (decoupled from raw video) to detect motion events in swimming and athletics with high accuracy and limited data.
cells.E1056: Combines domain-adapted athlete tracking with either rule-based pose-statistic decision rules or a convolutional sequence model to detect stride/start events from pose sequences.
cells.F1056: Tangential to GSE's core sports coverage (NFL/MLB/MLS), but demonstrates a data-efficient event-detection pattern useful if GSE expands into individual/Olympic sports.
cells.G1056: Apply the pose-sequence decoupling idea to build data-efficient event detectors for future niche-sport expansion without needing large labeled video datasets.

cells.C1057: The Impact of Birth Order on Behavior in Contact Team Sports: the Evidence of Rugby Teams in Argentina
cells.D1057: Finds a statistically significant relationship between birth order (second-born males with older brothers) and disciplinary infractions (yellow cards) in Argentine rugby.
cells.E1057: Survey and league-record data analyzed for correlation between birth-order/sibling-sex covariates and in-game disciplinary outcomes.
cells.F1057: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's current sports coverage (rugby isn't a listed sport) and betting-relevant signal; a weak thread is behavioral covariates as niche predictive features.
cells.G1057: Not a strong fit — at most, a reminder that unconventional demographic covariates occasionally carry real predictive signal, worth testing (cheaply) as candidate features in feature-selection sweeps.

cells.C1058: Accumulator Bet Selection Through Stochastic Diffusion Search
cells.D1058: Proposes a binary optimization model using Stochastic Diffusion Search to select the most promising combination of matches for accumulator (parlay) bets, validated on real football league data.
cells.E1058: Formulates combinatorial parlay-selection as a binary optimization problem solved via a swarm-intelligence metaheuristic balancing total payout and win probability.
cells.F1058: Directly relevant to GSE's betting-product domain — a concrete optimization technique for constructing multi-leg parlay recommendations that GSE could offer as a product feature.
cells.G1058: Use the stochastic diffusion search optimizer to auto-generate GSE's own parlay/accumulator picks from its graded single-game probabilities, adding a new product surface built directly on the existing prediction engine.

cells.C1059: Renormalizing individual performance metrics for cultural heritage management of sports records
cells.D1059: Develops a statistical renormalization method to fairly compare player achievement metrics across different sporting eras (e.g., MLB, NBA), correcting for era-specific bias.
cells.E1059: Season-level renormalization technique preserves the functional form of the achievement distribution while enabling era-adjusted cross-comparison and re-ranking of historical records.
cells.F1059: Directly relevant to GSE's historical data-normalization needs — a rigorous method for making cross-era player stats comparable, useful for building consistent historical training features.
cells.G1059: Apply era-renormalization to historical training data before model fitting, preventing rule-change or era-drift artifacts from corrupting GSE's per-sport probability models.

cells.D1060: A position paper identifying key challenges (data collection, real-time decision support, visualization design) for using immersive/XR analytics to support in-game sports decision-making.
cells.E1060: Surveys challenges and proposes user scenarios for augmented/virtual reality analytics tools supporting athletes, coaches, and fans in real time.
cells.F1060: Tangential — mostly relevant to GSE's longer-horizon B2B/embeddable-widget and fan-experience ambitions rather than core calibration work.
cells.G1060: Use the SportsXR challenge framework to scope a future immersive/interactive visualization layer for GSE's B2B widget product, differentiating from static prediction dashboards.

cells.C1061: Multimodal and multiview distillation for real-time player detection on a football field
cells.D1061: Trains a cheap wide-angle fisheye camera student model via knowledge distillation from a narrow-angle thermal camera teacher to detect football-field player occupancy in real time.
cells.E1061: Cross-modal, cross-view knowledge distillation with custom data augmentation and motion detection handles regions uncovered by the teacher sensor, enabling continuous online adaptation.
cells.F1061: Tangential to GSE's core product, but the knowledge-distillation pattern (cheap sensor learns from expensive sensor) parallels using expensive ground-truth data sources to cheaply validate scraped free data.
cells.G1061: Apply cross-source distillation to train a cheap-to-run validator model on free scraped data, using paid odds/tracking data as the 'expensive teacher' only during periodic recalibration.

cells.C1062: Using Player's Body-Orientation to Model Pass Feasibility in Soccer
cells.D1062: Builds a geometric model using player body orientation and spatial configuration from monocular video to estimate the feasibility of soccer passes, improving on Expected Possession Value metrics.
cells.E1062: Body-pose-derived orientation is projected onto a 2D field and combined with a geometric feasibility measure, refining existing expected-possession-value models.
cells.F1062: Directly relevant methodology showing how a novel derived feature (orientation) can meaningfully refine an existing sports probability model — a template for feature engineering to close GSE's MAE gap.
cells.G1062: Use the general pattern (deriving a new geometric feature from cheap video/pose data to refine existing probability models) as a case study for identifying analogous underused features in GSE's NFL/MLB pipelines.

cells.C1063: A parsimonious family of multivariate Poisson-lognormal distributions for clustering multivariate count data
cells.D1063: Proposes a family of multivariate Poisson-lognormal mixture models with covariance decomposition constraints, fit via fast variational-EM, for clustering overdispersed count data such as sports statistics.
cells.E1063: Hierarchical Poisson-lognormal model captures correlated, overdispersed multivariate counts via a latent Gaussian layer, with parsimonious covariance-structure variants for computational efficiency.
cells.F1063: Directly relevant statistical model class for GSE's core scoring problem — sports scores are classic overdispersed count data, and this offers a calibrated, computationally efficient alternative to naive Poisson models.
cells.G1063: Replace or augment GSE's scoring model with a parsimonious Poisson-lognormal variant to explicitly capture score overdispersion and cross-statistic correlation, directly targeting the Brier/ECE calibration gate.

cells.C1064: Implementing multiple imputation for missing data in longitudinal studies when models are not feasible: A tutorial on the random hot deck approach
cells.D1064: A tutorial demonstrating random hot-deck multiple imputation as a model-free alternative for handling missing longitudinal data, illustrated on a children's sports-participation study.
cells.E1064: Matches records with missing data to similar observed records, samples probabilistically among matches to generate multiple plausible complete datasets for standard multiple-imputation analysis.
cells.F1064: Directly relevant to GSE's data pipeline reliability — a practical, model-free technique for handling missing/sparse historical sports data, complementing the bootstrap-mode confidence-capping approach.
cells.G1064: Use hot-deck imputation to fill gaps in sparse historical per-sport data for newly-added leagues, providing more complete training data than dropping incomplete records entirely.

cells.C1065: Challenges and Opportunities for Computer Vision in Real-life Soccer Analytics
cells.D1065: A position paper discussing real-life challenges of applying computer vision to multi-camera soccer analytics for player performance and team-level statistics.
cells.E1065: Frames a multi-camera capture setup to discuss practical machine-learning challenges (calibration, occlusion, scale) in real-world sports video analysis.
cells.F1065: Tangential — mostly a challenges/overview paper relevant to future video-ingestion ambitions rather than GSE's current statistical calibration priorities.
cells.G1065: Use the identified real-world CV challenges as a checklist when evaluating whether to add broadcast video ingestion to the data pipeline versus sticking with structured/scraped stats.

cells.C1066: Event detection in coarsely annotated sports videos via parallel multi receptive field 1D convolutions
cells.D1066: Proposes a multi-tower temporal convolutional network that detects events in sports video despite only coarse (imprecise) frame-level annotations, tested on NHL and SoccerNet data.
cells.E1066: Multiple parallel 1D convolutional towers with different receptive fields process temporal information at various scales to handle annotation uncertainty in event timing.
cells.F1066: Tangential — relevant to video-based data pipelines if GSE incorporates weakly-labeled video event detection, but not core to the current calibration/forecasting blockers.
cells.G1066: Adapt the multi-receptive-field architecture to detect 'signal events' (line-moving news, injury reports) in noisy, imprecisely-timestamped scraped text/social streams.

cells.C1067: Slicing and dicing soccer: automatic detection of complex events from spatio-temporal data
cells.D1067: Presents a two-tier system that detects atomic and complex soccer events (e.g., tackles, filtering passes) from positional data using declarative Interval Temporal Logic, plus a large synthetic dataset.
cells.E1067: Atomic events derived from spatio-temporal object features combine via a declarative Interval Temporal Logic to define and reason about complex, composable in-game events.
cells.F1067: Directly relevant conceptual pattern for GSE's Intelligence Graph ambition — declarative, composable temporal-logic event definitions over structured sports data are a natural fit for typed knowledge primitives.
cells.G1067: Use Interval Temporal Logic-style declarative event composition as the formal specification language underlying GSE's Intelligence Graph, letting typed knowledge primitives be defined and audited transparently.

cells.C1068: Impact of Tactile and Visual Feedback on Breathing Rhythm and User Experience in VR Exergaming
cells.D1068: Compares visual, verbal, and haptic feedback modalities for guiding correct breathing during VR indoor rowing, finding haptic feedback most effective despite user preference for visual.
cells.E1068: Controlled user study measures breathing-movement synchronicity and subjective user-experience ratings across feedback modalities in a VR exergaming context.
cells.F1068: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's prediction engine; the honest thread is UX-feedback-modality research potentially informing the Galaxy Dynasty game's interface design.
cells.G1068: Not a strong fit — at most, a distant UX-design reference if Galaxy Dynasty ever incorporates biometric/haptic feedback mechanics.

cells.C1069: Sorting Big Data by Revealed Preference with Application to College Ranking
cells.D1069: Proposes an endogenous-weighting revealed-preference method to derive consistent linear rankings from heterogeneous consumer choices, explicitly noting applicability to sports team ranking.
cells.E1069: Solves for a steady-state equilibrium ranking that accounts for spillover effects of multi-step interactions among ranked entities, using much less data than exogenous-weighting approaches.
cells.F1069: Directly relevant — explicitly proposed for sports team ranking, offering an alternative, data-efficient ranking methodology GSE could evaluate against or blend into its existing rating systems.
cells.G1069: Blend revealed-preference equilibrium rankings with GSE's existing Elo/CEPT-based ratings as an additional ensemble member, since it requires less data and could stabilize bootstrap-mode confidence for sparse teams.

cells.C1070: Action Localization through Continual Predictive Learning
cells.D1070: Presents a self-supervised, prediction-error-driven continual learning approach for action localization that requires no bounding-box annotations, tested partly on UCF Sports.
cells.E1070: An LSTM+CNN model with attention continuously predicts future high-level features; prediction errors drive ongoing self-supervised parameter updates in a single streaming pass.
cells.F1070: Tangential to GSE's core statistical work, but the continual/online-learning-from-prediction-error pattern is conceptually relevant to how GSE's models could adapt in real time as new game data streams in.
cells.G1070: Borrow the continual prediction-error-driven update pattern as inspiration for an online recalibration loop that continuously nudges GSE's per-sport models between full retraining cycles.

cells.C1071: Cheating in online gaming spreads through observation and victimization
cells.D1071: Analyzes over a million online shooter matches to show antisocial cheating behavior spreads via both observation and direct victimization, especially after repeated exposure.
cells.E1071: Causal-inference-style analysis of event sequences compares observed contagion patterns against alternative gameplay simulations preserving team/interaction structure.
cells.F1071: Tangential to GSE's prediction engine, but directly relevant to any social/multiplayer features in Galaxy Dynasty, where antisocial behavior contagion could affect user retention and community health.
cells.G1071: Use the observation-plus-victimization contagion model to design targeted moderation interventions in Galaxy Dynasty's social features, preventing cheating/toxicity from spreading through the player base.

cells.C1072: Predicting play calls in the National Football League using hidden Markov models
cells.D1072: Uses hidden Markov models on a comprehensive play-by-play NFL dataset to predict play calls, achieving 71.5% out-of-sample accuracy for the 2018 season, beating comparable studies.
cells.E1072: Fits an HMM to sequential play-by-play state transitions to model latent 'play-calling regimes' and predict the next play type out of sample.
cells.F1072: Extremely directly relevant: a proven, interpretable time-series model specifically for NFL play-level prediction — directly applicable to improving GSE's NFL model beyond the naive baseline it currently loses to.
cells.G1072: Add an HMM-based play-calling-regime feature to GSE's NFL model, letting the model condition win-probability/spread predictions on inferred latent offensive tendencies rather than static team averages.

cells.C1073: Unified Image and Video Saliency Modeling
cells.D1073: Proposes UNISAL, a lightweight encoder-RNN-decoder network achieving state-of-the-art saliency prediction jointly across image and video datasets including UCF-Sports, via domain-adaptation techniques.
cells.E1073: Domain-adaptive priors, fusion, and smoothing techniques allow a single compact model to jointly learn from heterogeneous image and video saliency datasets without catastrophic domain shift.
cells.F1073: Tangential to GSE's core calibration/forecasting work; relevant mainly if GSE builds automated highlight/thumbnail generation needing to know where viewers look in sports footage.
cells.G1073: Use saliency prediction to auto-select the most visually compelling frame/moment for auto-generated social media thumbnails from game footage, supporting the content-automation roadmap.

cells.C1074: Pursuing Sources of Heterogeneity in Modeling Clustered Population
cells.D1074: Proposes a regularized finite mixture effects regression that simultaneously identifies clusters and distinguishes which predictors truly drive cluster differences versus having common effects, applied to baseball salary/performance data among other domains.
cells.E1074: An effects-model parameterization decomposes each predictor's influence into a common term and cluster-specific terms, with sparse regularization to identify true sources of heterogeneity with estimation/selection consistency guarantees.
cells.F1074: Directly relevant statistical methodology for GSE's calibration problem: a rigorous way to identify which predictors genuinely need per-sport-specific treatment versus a shared global effect, directly informing the 'independent per-sport probability models' hypothesis.
cells.G1074: Apply this heterogeneity-pursuit regression to formally test and justify which model components should be sport-specific versus shared globally, giving an empirical, statistically-grounded architecture decision for the ensemble redesign.

cells.C1075: MoVi: A Large Multipurpose Motion and Video Dataset
cells.D1075: Introduces a large multi-modal dataset (motion capture, video, IMU) of 90 actors performing everyday and sports movements under multiple recording conditions.
cells.E1075: Combines optical motion capture, multi-view video, and IMU sensors across capture rounds to provide synchronized ground-truth full-body motion and shape data.
cells.F1075: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's core statistical/calibration work; the honest thread is a reusable benchmark dataset if GSE ever develops motion-based player features.
cells.G1075: Not a strong fit for GSE's core roadmap — at most, a benchmark reference if motion-capture-derived athlete features are explored far down the roadmap.

cells.C1076: Always Look on the Bright Side of the Field: Merging Pose and Contextual Data to Estimate Orientation of Soccer Players
cells.D1076: Combines pose estimation (with super-resolution) and ball-position context to estimate soccer player body orientation from monocular broadcast video, validated against wearable tracking devices.
cells.E1076: OpenPose-derived shoulder/hip keypoints are mapped to a 2D field and fused with ball-position context to infer player orientation, visualized via novel orientation maps.
cells.F1076: Tangential but concretely relevant if GSE ingests broadcast video for soccer/MLS features — offers a low-cost way to approximate expensive wearable tracking-device data.
cells.G1076: Use video-derived orientation estimation as a free proxy for expensive EPTS tracking devices, letting GSE extract richer soccer/MLS features from broadcast footage alone.

cells.C1077: Information cartography in association rule mining
cells.D1077: Develops an evolutionary-algorithm-based method to automatically build 'metro map' visual summaries of association rules mined from data, including one sports dataset.
cells.E1077: Formulates metro-map construction from association rules as an optimization problem solved with an evolutionary algorithm, producing structured visual knowledge summaries.
cells.F1077: Tangential — relevant mainly as a visualization/summarization technique for presenting mined patterns, conceptually adjacent to GSE's Intelligence Graph knowledge-primitive layer.
cells.G1077: Use metro-map-style visual summarization to present GSE's Intelligence Graph relationships to B2B customers in an intuitive, non-technical visual format.

cells.C1078: Allotaxonometry and rank-turbulence divergence: A universal instrument for comparing complex systems
cells.D1078: Introduces a tunable rank-based divergence measure and paired visualization ('allotaxonograph') for comparing any two ranked lists, demonstrated across domains including sports performance.
cells.E1078: Rank-turbulence divergence quantifies and visualizes how components shift rank between two ranked lists, generalizing across arbitrarily different system types and scales.
cells.F1078: Directly relevant as a general-purpose tool for comparing GSE's model-generated rankings (team power rankings, player rankings) across time windows or between model versions during calibration testing.
cells.G1078: Use rank-turbulence divergence to visually communicate how GSE's per-sport model rankings shift after a calibration fix, giving stakeholders an intuitive before/after diagnostic beyond raw Brier/ECE numbers.

cells.C1079: Unsupervised Temporal Feature Aggregation for Event Detection in Unstructured Sports Videos
cells.D1079: Proposes unsupervised player re-identification and data augmentation techniques to improve event detection accuracy in unstructured (arbitrary camera angle) sports videos like table tennis.
cells.E1079: Temporal feature aggregation with person re-identification boosts weak heuristic player-retrieval scoring, combined with multi-modal image translation for pose-variation data augmentation.
cells.F1079: Tangential — relevant mainly if GSE ingests unstructured/amateur video sources beyond standard broadcast feeds, a stretch from its core structured-data pipeline.
cells.G1079: Not a strong core fit — at most, useful if GSE's data-scraping ever needs to process inconsistent camera-angle amateur game footage as a supplementary data source.

cells.C1080: What is Trending on Wikipedia? Capturing Trends and Language Biases Across Wikipedia Editions
cells.D1080: Proposes an automated method to extract and compare trending Wikipedia topics across language editions, finding entertainment and sports are consistently popular across cultures.
cells.E1080: Combines Wikipedia's hyperlink graph, pageview statistics, and semi-supervised topic extraction to identify and compare cross-lingual trending topics.
cells.F1080: Tangential — relevant mainly as a trend-detection methodology potentially useful for GSE's automated content generation to identify globally trending sports topics.
cells.G1080: Adapt the cross-lingual trend-extraction pipeline to auto-surface trending sports storylines for GSE's automated social content generation pipeline.

cells.C1081: Multiresolution Tensor Learning for Efficient and Interpretable Spatial Analysis
cells.D1081: Develops a multiresolution tensor learning algorithm (MRTL) that trains interpretable spatial latent-factor models 4-5x faster by progressively refining from coarse to fine resolution.
cells.E1081: Initializes latent factors from an approximate full-rank tensor model then progressively trains from coarse to fine spatial resolution, with proven convergence guarantees, explicitly noted as applicable to sports data.
cells.F1081: Directly relevant technique for GSE's spatial/contextual modeling needs (e.g., shot-location or field-position models) — offers faster, more interpretable tensor factorization explicitly validated as sports-applicable.
cells.G1081: Use multiresolution tensor learning to build an interpretable spatial 'hot zone' model for shot/play-location data that trains fast enough to update within the BullMQ job-queue pipeline in near real time.

cells.C1082: The role of intrinsic dimension in high-resolution player tracking data -- Insights in basketball
cells.D1082: Uses a Bayesian mixture model (Hidalgo) to estimate heterogeneous intrinsic dimension in NBA tracking data, finding higher unpredictability correlates with winning and close-score plays.
cells.E1082: Bayesian mixture modeling estimates local intrinsic dimensionality as a complexity/unpredictability signal within movement and shot-chart data.
cells.F1082: Offers a novel complexity/unpredictability feature GSE could add to its per-sport probability models to help close the Brier/ECE calibration gap tied to game-state variability.
cells.G1082: Use intrinsic-dimension spikes as a real-time 'chaos index' that automatically triggers bootstrap-mode confidence capping when a game enters an unusually unpredictable phase.

cells.C1083: RePose: Learning Deep Kinematic Priors for Fast Human Pose Estimation
cells.D1083: Proposes a lightweight hierarchical CNN that encodes human body kinematic structure to achieve state-of-the-art pose estimation with far fewer parameters.
cells.E1083: Coarse-to-fine convolutional network propagates features along a kinematic skeleton graph to predict keypoints efficiently.
cells.F1083: Tangential — GSE doesn't currently do computer-vision pose work, but this could matter if it builds player-tracking-derived features from broadcast video for sports beyond box-score stats.
cells.G1083: Bolt onto the data-ingestion pipeline as a cheap pose-tracking add-on for injury/fatigue proxy features scraped from public game footage, feeding the confidence/bootstrap-mode system.

cells.C1084: TRAP: A Predictive Framework for Trail Running Assessment of Performance
cells.D1084: Introduces a statistical framework and Python scraper (ScrapITRA) for predicting ultra-trail runners' checkpoint times and giving prediction intervals using ITRA race-history data.
cells.E1084: Combines a runner-ability estimation model with terrain-aware checkpoint-time regression and interval estimation.
cells.F1084: A direct analogue for GSE's data-ingestion pipeline: a working public-data scraper plus a prediction-interval methodology relevant to bootstrap mode and calibration work.
cells.G1084: Adapt the checkpoint prediction-interval technique as a template for live in-game 'time-to-event' markets (e.g., time to next score) with honest uncertainty bands instead of point picks.

cells.C1085: A copula-based multivariate hidden Markov model for modelling momentum in football
cells.D1085: Uses copula-based multivariate HMMs on minute-by-minute Bundesliga stats to detect latent 'momentum shift' states correlated with match control.
cells.E1085: Hidden Markov model with copula-linked state-dependent distributions captures correlated in-game metrics and latent regime switches.
cells.F1085: Directly useful for GSE's core prediction engine — HMM/copula regime-detection could feed sport-specific latent-state features that improve MAE versus the naive baseline it currently loses to.
cells.G1085: Build a 'momentum state' layer into live win-probability picks so confidence scores adjust dynamically as the HMM detects a team entering a high-control regime, distinct from static pre-game features.

cells.C1086: ARAACOM: ARAbic Algerian Corpus for Opinion Mining
cells.D1086: Presents an Arabic Algerian dialect corpus and approach for opinion/sentiment mining from web comments.
cells.E1086: Corpus construction plus standard NLP sentiment classification pipeline for a low-resource dialect.
cells.F1086: Weak tangential link — only useful if GSE expands multilingual social/media content generation or sentiment-driven signal ingestion beyond English.
cells.G1086: Reuse the dialect-corpus construction methodology as a template if GSE ever wants to mine non-English sports betting/fan sentiment as an auxiliary predictive signal.

cells.C1087: augKlimb: Interactive Data-Led Augmentation of Bouldering Training
cells.D1087: Describes a mobile app that records and visualizes climbers' acceleration data alongside video to give feedback on technique.
cells.E1087: Wearable/phone sensor data capture combined with a UI/UX design study for athlete self-coaching and gamified feedback.
cells.F1087: A stretch — bouldering isn't a GSE market — but the gamified data-feedback loop pattern is relevant to the future Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR persistent game layer.
cells.G1087: Borrow the 'record, graph, and score' feedback-loop design pattern for a fantasy/dynasty-game feature that visualizes a user's pick performance over time as a coaching-style dashboard.

cells.C1088: Estimating locomotor demands during team play from broadcast-derived tracking data
cells.D1088: Develops models predicting off-screen player locomotor load (acceleration, high-speed running) in soccer from broadcast-derived tracking data lacking full coverage.
cells.E1088: Statistical models impute missing off-camera load metrics from partial broadcast-derived x-y coordinate tracking data.
cells.F1088: Directly relevant to GSE's data-ingestion pipeline — shows how to derive richer player-load features from cheap broadcast feeds instead of expensive proprietary tracking data, similar to its free/scraped-data strategy.
cells.G1088: Use the broadcast-derived load-imputation technique to build a low-cost fatigue/workload proxy feature for covered sports without paying for licensed optical tracking data.

cells.C1089: Predicting competitions by combining conditional logistic regression and subjective Bayes: An Academy Awards case study
cells.D1089: Combines conditional logistic regression with subjective Bayesian priors to probabilistically predict competition winners, illustrated via the Best Picture Oscar race.
cells.E1089: Conditional logistic regression for baseline probabilities, updated with expert-elicited Bayesian priors to incorporate qualitative judgment.
cells.F1089: Directly on-target for GSE's ensemble/calibration work — a template for blending a statistical baseline model with subjective priors (e.g., CEPT-style expert adjustments) in a principled, auditable way.
cells.G1089: Use this framework to let GSE's human analysts inject calibrated 'expert nudges' into picks during bootstrap mode without breaking the deterministic, auditable-math brand promise.

cells.C1090: From Kinematics To Dynamics: Estimating Center of Pressure and Base of Support from Video Frames of Human Motion
cells.D1090: Trains deep networks (PressNet) to regress foot-pressure heatmaps and stability metrics from 2D pose video, validated on a large synchronized Taiji dataset.
cells.E1090: Cross-modality deep regression maps video-derived kinematic pose to physical foot-pressure dynamics.
cells.F1090: Not directly relevant to GSE's calibration/forecasting blockers; a stretch application only if GSE pursued biomechanical injury-risk modeling from broadcast video.
cells.G1090: Could inspire a novel 'stability index' proxy feature extracted from broadcast pose data as an early injury/fatigue signal feeding confidence adjustments.

cells.C1091: Feature engineering workflow for activity recognition from synchronized inertial measurement units
cells.D1091: Proposes an automated time-series feature-extraction workflow (based on the FRESH algorithm) for classifying human activity from wearable IMU sensor data.
cells.E1091: Automated, statistically significant feature extraction and selection from multivariate time series, feeding a downstream classifier.
cells.F1091: Directly relevant as a general-purpose automated feature-engineering method GSE's data pipeline could apply to any time-series sports data to speed up model iteration.
cells.G1091: Apply the FRESH automated-feature-extraction workflow to live odds and play-by-play time series to mine new candidate signals for the failing prediction model without manual feature crafting.

cells.C1092: Measuring Spatial Allocative Efficiency in Basketball
cells.D1092: Proposes a Bayesian hierarchical model estimating court-location-specific field goal percentages to detect whether basketball lineups allocate shots efficiently among teammates.
cells.E1092: Bayesian hierarchical spatial modeling of shooting efficiency conditioned on location and lineup context.
cells.F1092: A good template for GSE's per-sport probability modeling — spatial Bayesian hierarchies could become part of the 'independent per-sport probability models' fix for the calibration gate.
cells.G1092: Repurpose the allocative-efficiency framework as a content-generation hook: auto-flag 'inefficient shot allocation' storylines for the automated media/content pipeline.

cells.C1093: Event Ticket Price Prediction with Deep Neural Network on Spatial-Temporal Sparse Data
cells.D1093: Proposes a bi-level deep network with coarsening/refining layers to predict sparse spatio-temporal event ticket prices for sports and concerts.
cells.E1093: Hierarchical deep network with a custom bi-level loss handles extreme sparsity in spatio-temporal transaction data.
cells.F1093: Relevant to GSE's sparse-data problem (bootstrap mode): the coarsening/refining architecture is a concrete technique for improving predictions when data is thin, similar to sparse early-season sports data.
cells.G1093: Adapt the bi-level sparse-data architecture for early-season/new-market sports (e.g., MLS) where GSE has few historical picks, reducing reliance on blunt confidence capping.

cells.C1094: Bayesian Hierarchical Models for the Prediction of Volleyball Results
cells.D1094: Develops Bayesian hierarchical models to predict volleyball match outcomes and national league rankings, validated on Italian Serie A1 data.
cells.E1094: Hierarchical Bayesian rating model estimates team strength and predicts match results with partial pooling across teams.
cells.F1094: Directly relevant — a template sport-specific Bayesian model exactly matching GSE's stated need for independent per-sport probability models rather than one global calibrator.
cells.G1094: Use the hierarchical partial-pooling structure to let GSE's under-covered sports (e.g., MLS) borrow statistical strength from related leagues, easing the bootstrap-mode confidence cap.

cells.C1095: A regularized hidden Markov model for analyzing the 'hot shoe' in football
cells.D1095: Applies a LASSO-regularized hidden Markov model to Bundesliga penalty data to find evidence of a 'hot shoe' (hot-hand) effect in penalty takers and goalkeepers.
cells.E1095: HMM with player-specific covariates and LASSO penalty models latent 'form' states affecting performance.
cells.F1095: Directly useful for the core prediction model — regularized latent-state modeling of player 'form' is a concrete technique to improve forecasting accuracy beyond the failing naive baseline.
cells.G1095: Build a per-player 'hot/cold form' latent state feeding pick confidence, giving GSE's brand-safe 'math you can read' story a legible, explainable form indicator instead of an opaque AI label.

cells.C1096: Bayesian models for prediction of the set-difference in volleyball
cells.D1096: Compares an ordered multinomial logistic model and a truncated Skellam-distribution model for predicting volleyball set-difference outcomes, fit within a Bayesian framework.
cells.E1096: Two competing likelihood specifications tailored to the discrete, bounded nature of volleyball scoring, compared via Bayesian model fitting.
cells.F1096: Directly relevant as an example of choosing outcome-appropriate probability distributions per sport — exactly the 'independent per-sport probability models' direction GSE suspects will fix calibration.
cells.G1096: Use the truncated-Skellam-vs-multinomial comparison methodology as a checklist for auditing each GSE sport model to ensure its likelihood matches the scoring structure before ensembling.

cells.C1097: A Bayesian Quest for Finding a Unified Model for Predicting Volleyball Games
cells.D1097: Introduces a two-level hierarchical Bayesian model (set outcome via logistic regression, points via truncated negative binomial) achieving strong predictive fit on Italian Superlega data.
cells.E1097: Nested hierarchical Bayesian model separately captures set-winner probability and point-margin distribution, linked through the sport's rules.
cells.F1097: Directly relevant — a worked example of a rules-aware, multi-layer sport-specific probability model, which is exactly the ensemble architecture GSE is considering to fix Brier/ECE.
cells.G1097: Mirror this two-level structure (win/loss layer + margin layer) as a reusable pattern GSE's prediction-engine package could apply across sports to standardize model architecture while keeping per-sport calibration.

cells.C1098: Trouble with the Curve: Predicting Future MLB Players Using Scouting Reports
cells.D1098: Builds a dataset of ~10,000 MLB scouting reports and trains deep NLP models to predict which minor-league prospects will reach the majors from written text plus grades.
cells.E1098: Deep neural text classifiers combine structured skill grades with free-text scouting language to predict career outcomes.
cells.F1098: Relevant to data-ingestion breadth — shows how to fuse scraped unstructured text (scouting reports) with structured data, useful for GSE's multi-source free-data pipeline beyond box scores.
cells.G1098: Feed scraped scouting-report language into GSE's models as a soft prior for prospect/rookie picks where box-score history is thin, complementing bootstrap-mode confidence capping.

cells.D1099: Uses a Bayesian non-parametric catch-probability model on NFL tracking data to evaluate whether quarterbacks threw to the receiver most likely to catch, imputing unobserved hypothetical inputs.
cells.E1099: Bayesian non-parametric regression plus imputation-based counterfactual averaging over unobserved play states.
cells.F1099: Directly relevant — a rigorous uncertainty-aware method for reasoning about counterfactual/unobserved game states, a technique that could sharpen NFL-specific probability models and confidence estimates.
cells.G1099: Adapt the imputation-and-average approach to generate 'what if the pick had been different' explainer content for the brand's transparent, math-you-can-read positioning.

cells.C1100: Context-Driven Data Mining through Bias Removal and Data Incompleteness Mitigation
cells.D1100: Proposes a Context-driven Data Science Lifecycle (C-DSL) that folds domain context into each pipeline stage to reduce bias and incompleteness, tested on sports-event datasets.
cells.E1100: Lifecycle framework injects contextual metadata at each ETL/modeling stage to correct for hidden biases and missing data.
cells.F1100: Directly relevant to GSE's data-ingestion and calibration reliability — a structured methodology for auditing bias/incompleteness in scraped multi-source sports data before it hits the prediction engine.
cells.G1100: Adopt C-DSL as an internal checklist/gate the Jarvis/Hermes/Fable agents run automatically before any new scraped data source is admitted into the prediction pipeline.

cells.C1101: Rugby-Bot: Utilizing Multi-Task Learning & Fine-Grained Features for Rugby League Analysis
cells.D1101: Presents a multi-task, wide-and-deep neural network that predicts multiple rugby league outcomes and full distributions from one shared fine-grained spatial representation.
cells.E1101: Multi-task learning with wide-and-deep architecture outputs distributional predictions rather than single point estimates from a single feature source.
cells.F1101: Directly relevant: a multi-task, distribution-output architecture is exactly the kind of ensemble/probabilistic upgrade GSE needs to beat its naive-baseline MAE and improve calibrated confidence.
cells.G1101: Use the multi-task shared-representation trick to jointly train GSE's per-sport probability models, letting sports with sparse data (bootstrap mode) borrow statistical strength from data-rich sports.

cells.C1102: Inequalities, chance and success in sport competitions: simulations vs empirical data
cells.D1102: Compares 100m sprint results to an agent-based luck-vs-talent simulation, finding a small but nonzero role for random luck among top performers.
cells.E1102: Agent-based modeling decomposes observed competitive outcomes into talent and stochastic luck components, benchmarked against empirical data.
cells.F1102: Conceptually relevant to calibration: quantifying an irreducible 'luck floor' helps explain why Brier/ECE can't reach zero and supports realistic target-setting for the launch gate.
cells.G1102: Use the luck-decomposition method to communicate to stakeholders why a model can be well-calibrated yet still 'lose' individual bets — reframing variance as expected, not a bug.

cells.C1103: Random forest model identifies serve strength as a key predictor of tennis match outcome
cells.D1103: Trains random forest and other ML models on the largest tennis match dataset to date, achieving ~80% outcome accuracy and finding serve strength most predictive; results approximate betting-market odds.
cells.E1103: Ensemble tree-based classifiers on curated historical match features, benchmarked against market betting odds.
cells.F1103: Highly relevant — directly addresses GSE's core forecasting blocker and its closing-line-value benchmark, showing simple ensembles can approximate market efficiency in an under-modeled sport.
cells.G1103: Use the finding that combined model probabilities 'recreate' market odds as a diagnostic: if GSE's ensemble can't match this convergence, that's a red flag the calibration gate should catch pre-launch.

cells.C1104: Template-free Data-to-Text Generation of Finnish Sports News
cells.D1104: Builds a corpus of edited Finnish ice hockey news and trains an end-to-end data-to-text system judged by journalists as relatively close to publishable quality.
cells.E1104: End-to-end neural data-to-text generation trained on real (not templated) sports journalism paired with game statistics.
cells.F1104: Directly relevant to GSE's automated social/media content-generation ambitions — a working template for generating readable game recaps from structured stats.
cells.G1104: Fine-tune a similar data-to-text system specifically on GSE's own deterministic-math brand voice so auto-generated recaps stay compliant with the 'no AI-powered' public copy rule by construction.

cells.C1105: Fast and Fair Simultaneous Confidence Bands for Functional Parameters
cells.D1105: Develops a fast, resampling-free method for simultaneous confidence bands over functional data with balanced false-positive rates, demonstrated on sports biomechanics data.
cells.E1105: Analytic (non-bootstrap) construction of simultaneous confidence bands for function-valued estimates, without needing the full covariance function.
cells.F1105: Directly relevant to calibration/uncertainty quantification — a fast, principled way to generate confidence bands could improve GSE's bootstrap-mode uncertainty estimates without expensive resampling.
cells.G1105: Replace ad-hoc bootstrap-mode confidence capping with these analytic simultaneous bands to get statistically 'fair' (balanced false-positive) uncertainty intervals for sparse-data picks.

cells.C1106: Time Series Modeling for Dream Team in Fantasy Premier League
cells.D1106: Combines ARIMA and RNN time-series forecasts of player fantasy points with linear programming optimization to construct an optimal Fantasy Premier League team.
cells.E1106: ARIMA/RNN ensemble forecasts fed into a linear-programming roster optimizer under budget and position constraints.
cells.F1106: Directly relevant — an ensemble time-series forecasting approach for player performance, plus a template for GSE's planned fantasy/Dynasty game layer.
cells.G1106: Repurpose the ARIMA+RNN ensemble and LP-optimizer combo as the engine behind Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR's roster-building mechanics, reusing GSE's own forecasting stack.

cells.C1107: Bigger data, better questions, and a return to fourth down behavior: an introduction to a special issue on tracking data in the National Football League
cells.D1107: Argues that player tracking data overturns prior conclusions (e.g., about aggressive fourth-down strategy) drawn from coarser play-level data, and surveys a special issue on NFL tracking research.
cells.E1107: Editorial/survey piece contrasting play-level vs. player-tracking-level statistical inference in football analytics.
cells.F1107: Directly relevant methodological caution for GSE: a reminder that models built on coarse public data (like GSE's current pipeline) may embed systematic biases that finer tracking data would correct.
cells.G1107: Use this as justification to prioritize acquiring or scraping richer NFL tracking-adjacent data sources specifically to re-derive features behind the currently underperforming core model.

cells.C1108: Robust Inference for Skewed data in Health Sciences
cells.D1108: Develops minimum density power divergence estimators for robust inference under the skew-normal family, applied to Australian athlete and clinical trial data.
cells.E1108: Robust divergence-based estimation and hypothesis testing that downweights outliers when fitting skewed distributions.
cells.F1108: Relevant to calibration robustness — outlier-resistant estimation could stabilize GSE's per-sport probability models against extreme blowout games or data glitches that distort Brier/ECE.
cells.G1108: Apply the robust divergence estimator to detect and downweight anomalous settled-pick outcomes (e.g., data errors) before they corrupt the 3-consecutive-green calibration window.

cells.C1109: FACE: Feasible and Actionable Counterfactual Explanations
cells.D1109: Proposes generating counterfactual explanations along density-weighted 'feasible paths' through the data manifold rather than the naive closest-point counterfactual.
cells.E1109: Shortest-path search over a density-weighted graph produces realistic, achievable counterfactual explanations for ML decisions.
cells.F1109: A stretch for GSE's core betting product, but relevant to its trust/compliance toolkit ambitions — explaining picks via realistic 'what would have to change' narratives rather than opaque model internals.
cells.G1109: Use feasible-path counterfactuals to power a 'what would flip this pick' explainer widget for the B2B embeddable widgets, reinforcing the transparent-math brand without exposing model internals.

cells.C1110: Optimizing Through Learned Errors for Accurate Sports Field Registration
cells.D1110: Trains a network to regress registration error for sports field template alignment, then optimizes camera parameters against that learned error rather than using feed-forward prediction directly.
cells.E1110: Learned-error-as-objective optimization loop replaces direct feed-forward regression for camera calibration.
cells.F1110: Weak direct relevance to GSE's core stack (no field registration need), but the 'learn-the-error-then-optimize' pattern is conceptually transferable to model calibration workflows.
cells.G1110: Repurpose the learned-error-as-objective idea to train a network that predicts GSE's own calibration error (Brier/ECE) per sport/segment, then optimize ensemble weights against that learned error surface.

cells.C1111: ProtoGAN: Towards Few Shot Learning for Action Recognition
cells.D1111: Proposes a conditional GAN that synthesizes training examples for novel action classes from class-prototype vectors, improving few-shot and generalized few-shot action recognition.
cells.E1111: GAN conditioned on learned class-prototype vectors generates synthetic examples to augment scarce classes.
cells.F1111: A stretch for GSE's tabular prediction engine, but conceptually relevant to bootstrap mode: synthetic data augmentation for sparse classes (e.g., new sports/markets with little history).
cells.G1111: Explore synthetic scenario generation (GAN-style) to augment sparse early-season MLS/new-market data, giving the calibrator more synthetic 'settled picks' to stabilize per-sport models faster.

cells.C1112: User-Controlled Privacy-Preserving User Profile Data Sharing based on Blockchain
cells.D1112: Builds a MultiChain blockchain architecture letting users control which profile data enterprises (travel, hotels, etc.) can access and share.
cells.E1112: Decentralized data-sharing ledger with user-consent controls for cross-enterprise profile data exchange.
cells.F1112: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's core prediction problems; loosely relevant only if GSE's trust/compliance toolkit or B2B data-sharing widgets ever need auditable consent trails.
cells.G1112: Could inspire an auditable, tamper-evident log of pick lifecycle events (proposed→settled) for the trust/compliance toolkit, borrowing the ledger-based provenance idea rather than the blockchain tech itself.

cells.C1113: Home Sweet Home: Quantifying Home Court Advantages For NCAA Basketball Statistics
cells.D1113: Analyzes over 100,000 NCAA basketball games to quantify home-court advantage in box-score stats, finding scorekeeper and referee bias increases with crowd size and team strength.
cells.E1113: Regression analysis controlling for possessions and team strength, leveraging neutral-site games to isolate true home advantage from measurement bias.
cells.F1113: Directly useful for GSE's sport-specific feature engineering — a concrete, quantified home-advantage adjustment and a caution about scorekeeper bias contaminating training data used for calibration.
cells.G1113: Use the scorekeeper/referee-bias findings to build a data-quality filter that flags box-score inputs likely inflated by crowd-driven bias before they feed the prediction engine.

cells.C1114: Running Event Visualization using Videos from Multiple Cameras
cells.D1114: Identifies and tracks marathon runners across multiple unlabeled camera feeds using bib-number text detection and person re-identification, combined weakly-supervised.
cells.E1114: Scene-text spotting plus person re-identification, trained without ground-truth labels via mutual filtering between the two methods.
cells.F1114: Weak direct relevance to GSE's stack, but the multi-source weak-supervision/self-training pattern is relevant to robustly fusing GSE's multi-source scraped sports data without labeled ground truth.
