cells.G1114: Adapt the cross-source mutual-filtering technique to reconcile conflicting player/team IDs scraped from different free data sources (e.g., Pro-Football-Reference vs. odds feeds) without manual mapping.

cells.C1115: Benchmarking Zero-shot Text Classification: Datasets, Evaluation and Entailment Approach
cells.D1115: Provides unified datasets, evaluation protocols, and an entailment-based method for zero-shot text classification across topic, emotion, and situation aspects, including 'sports' as a label.
cells.E1115: Frames zero-shot classification as textual entailment, enabling label prediction without task-specific training data.
cells.F1115: Relevant to GSE's brand-language enforcement and content pipeline — entailment-based zero-shot classifiers could flag banned phrases (e.g., 'AI-powered') or categorize content without retraining per rule.
cells.G1115: Use zero-shot entailment classification as a lightweight, explainable brand-lint checker that flags any new marketing copy entailing 'AI-powered' claims before publish.

cells.C1116: In-bed Pressure-based Pose Estimation using Image Space Representation Learning
cells.D1116: Trains a network to transform ambiguous in-bed pressure-sensor maps into image-like representations so off-the-shelf pose estimators can accurately locate body parts.
cells.E1116: A learned pre-processing network converts one data modality (pressure) into a domain (image-like) compatible with existing pretrained models.
cells.F1116: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's product; a distant analogy for domain-adapting scraped odds/stat data into formats compatible with existing modeling tools.
cells.G1116: Borrow the 'translate ambiguous input into a familiar modality' trick to convert noisy scraped web-table data into a standardized schema pretrained ingestion models expect.

cells.C1117: DeepHuMS: Deep Human Motion Signature for 3D Skeletal Sequences
cells.D1117: Learns a deep embedding for 3D human motion sequences that supports motion retrieval and sub-motion search, outperforming hand-crafted feature approaches, including for sports biomechanics.
cells.E1117: Self-supervised deep embedding trained with trajectory cues enables similarity-based retrieval of motion sequences.
cells.F1117: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's tabular/odds-based prediction stack; mainly a stretch application if GSE ever ingests motion-capture data for biomechanics-based sports features.
cells.G1117: Conceptually reusable: embed teams' or players' game-level statistical 'trajectories' (not motion, but performance time series) into a similarity space for finding comparable historical situations to inform picks.

cells.C1118: Deep Learning-Based Quantification of Pulmonary Hemosiderophages in Cytology Slides
cells.D1118: Applies deep learning object detection to automatically grade hemosiderin-laden macrophages in horse lung cytology slides, matching or exceeding expert concordance.
cells.E1118: CNN-based object detection and classification pipeline replaces manual cell-grading with automated, reproducible scoring.
cells.F1118: Not relevant to GSE — this is veterinary pathology imaging with no meaningful connection to sports prediction, calibration, or the described product stack.
cells.G1118: No honest strong angle beyond the general observation that automated scoring reduces inter-rater variability, which loosely echoes GSE's goal of replacing subjective judgment with deterministic scoring.

cells.C1119: Difficulty Classification of Mountainbike Downhill Trails utilizing Deep Neural Networks
cells.D1119: Uses accelerometer/gyroscope sensor data and a 2D CNN to classify mountain bike downhill trail difficulty into easy/medium/hard categories.
cells.E1119: Sensor time-series reshaped into 2D representations and classified via convolutional neural network.
cells.F1119: A stretch for GSE's core betting stack, but demonstrates converting raw sensor time-series into classification labels, a pattern relevant to any future athlete-condition or terrain-based features.
cells.G1119: Marginal — could inspire a novel data source (course/venue difficulty scoring) as a contextual feature for niche outdoor-adjacent sports markets GSE might expand into.

cells.C1120: A Benchmark of Visual Storytelling in Social Media
cells.D1120: Introduces the SocialStories benchmark and metrics for assessing coherent visual storylines assembled from social media images/videos covering sports and cultural events.
cells.E1120: Curated benchmark dataset plus novel quantitative metrics for evaluating temporal/narrative coherence of automatically assembled visual stories.
cells.F1120: Directly relevant to GSE's automated social/media content-generation ambitions — provides evaluation metrics for coherent story assembly from scraped social content.
cells.G1120: Use the coherence metrics to automatically QA GSE's auto-generated game-recap content or social posts before publishing, catching narrative gaps the brand-lint rules alone wouldn't catch.

cells.D1121: Proposes a least-squares functional rating model producing a continuous point-differential-over-time rating for teams, adjusted for strength of schedule and home-court effects.
cells.E1121: Least-squares functional regression yields a time-varying rating curve usable to predict expected point differential at any game moment.
cells.F1121: Directly relevant — a legible, deterministic rating methodology ('math you can read') well suited to GSE's brand positioning and usable as a component of its ensemble scoring engine.
cells.G1121: Publish the functional-rating curve itself as a transparent, explainable visualization in B2B widgets, letting clients see exactly how a team's rating evolved — reinforcing the non-AI brand promise.

cells.D1122: Presents STEVE, a method for learning real-valued embedding vectors for soccer teams from match-history data, outperforming competitors on team market-value estimation and similarity ranking.
cells.E1122: Embedding model trained solely on historical match outcomes places similar teams close together in vector space for downstream ML tasks.
cells.F1122: Directly relevant — team embeddings from historical results are a lightweight feature-engineering technique GSE's prediction engine could adopt to improve per-sport models without new data sources.
cells.G1122: Use team-similarity vectors to power a 'find comparable historical matchups' explainer feature, adding narrative color to picks that stays within the deterministic-math brand voice.

cells.C1123: CoachAI: A Project for Microscopic Badminton Match Data Collection and Tactical Analysis
cells.D1123: Describes a multi-component research project combining video-based deep learning tracking, tactical ML analysis, AR/VR visualization, and IoT training devices for badminton.
cells.E1123: Integrated pipeline: video object tracking, ML tactical analysis, and connected hardware for granular badminton competition data.
cells.F1123: Tangential — badminton isn't a current GSE sport, but the integrated data-collection-to-tactical-analysis pipeline design pattern is relevant to expanding data ingestion into new niche sports.
cells.G1123: Use the project's modular architecture (collect → analyze → visualize) as a blueprint if GSE expands its data-ingestion pipeline into additional niche sports beyond NFL/MLB/MLS.

cells.C1124: FedHealth: A Federated Transfer Learning Framework for Wearable Healthcare
cells.D1124: Proposes FedHealth, combining federated learning for privacy-preserving data aggregation with transfer learning for personalized wearable activity-recognition models.
cells.E1124: Federated aggregation across devices followed by transfer learning to personalize a shared base model per user.
cells.F1124: Modest relevance — the federated + transfer-learning pattern could inform how GSE builds personalized per-sport or per-user models while keeping raw data siloed for compliance.
cells.G1124: Apply federated-style aggregation across GSE's internal agents (Jarvis, Hermes, Fable) so each specializes per sport locally while contributing to a shared global calibration model.

cells.C1125: A Cost Effective Solution for Road Crack Inspection using Cameras and Deep Neural Networks
cells.D1125: Uses a GoPro-mounted vehicle camera and a GAN-based ConnCrack model with connectivity maps to detect pavement cracks cheaply and accurately.
cells.E1125: Conditional Wasserstein GAN combined with connectivity-map post-processing improves crack segmentation from cheap consumer camera footage.
cells.F1125: Not relevant to GSE's product — this is civil infrastructure inspection with no meaningful connection to sports prediction or the described tech stack.
cells.G1125: No honest strong angle; at most, the 'cheap consumer hardware substituting for expensive sensors' theme loosely parallels GSE's own reliance on free/scraped data instead of paid feeds.

cells.C1126: The acute:chronic workload ratio: challenges and prospects for improvement
cells.D1126: Reviews methodological flaws in the widely used acute:chronic workload ratio for predicting athlete injury risk and proposes directions for improved formulations.
cells.E1126: Critical statistical review of a ratio-based risk metric, identifying issues like discretization, sparse data, and unmeasured confounding.
cells.F1126: Relevant as a cautionary methodological parallel — GSE's own launch-gate thresholds and ratio-based metrics could suffer analogous pitfalls (discretization bias, sparse-data instability) worth auditing.
cells.G1126: Apply this critique's lessons to sanity-check GSE's own calibration-gate metrics (Brier/ECE thresholds) for similar discretization and small-sample bias risks before publishing accuracy claims.

cells.C1127: How should we score athletes and candidates: geometric scoring rules
cells.D1127: Derives a family of 'geometric' and 'optimal' scoring rules for ranking competitors from ordinal position data, validated against real biathlon, golf, and athletics scoring systems.
cells.E1127: Axiomatic derivation of parametric scoring-rule families based on independence principles, compared to empirically observed sport scoring systems.
cells.F1127: Directly relevant to GSE's proper-scoring-rule and Brier-score work — a rigorous framework for designing/choosing scoring rules that matches real competitive structures rather than arbitrary points systems.
cells.G1127: Use the geometric-scoring-rule framework to design GSE's own pick-confidence or leaderboard scoring system for the Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR game layer with provably sound axiomatic properties.

cells.C1128: TrackNet: A Deep Learning Network for Tracking High-speed and Tiny Objects in Sports Applications
cells.D1128: Introduces TrackNet, a heatmap-based deep network that tracks a tennis ball across video frames with high precision even when blurry or occluded.
cells.E1128: Convolutional network trained on consecutive frames learns motion patterns to output a positional heatmap for a fast-moving small object.
cells.F1128: Not directly relevant to GSE's tabular prediction stack, but a stretch application if GSE later ingests broadcast video for in-play features (ball tracking) beyond box-score/odds data.
cells.G1128: Could seed a future 'live ball-tracking feature extraction' module feeding real-time in-game probability updates, distinguishing GSE from purely box-score-driven competitors.

cells.C1129: Gaussian Processes for Analyzing Positioned Trajectories in Sports
cells.D1129: Combines a physics-based kinetic motion model with Gaussian process regression (grey-box modeling) to analyze forces and velocity in cross-country skiing, reducing predictive uncertainty by 30-40% versus black-box models.
cells.E1129: Grey-box modeling fuses domain physics equations with a data-driven Gaussian process residual model to quantify and reduce uncertainty.
cells.F1129: Directly relevant to GSE's calibration and uncertainty problems — Gaussian processes are a well-established uncertainty-quantification tool, and the grey-box (domain-knowledge + ML) approach mirrors combining sports-domain rules with statistical models.
cells.G1129: Use grey-box Gaussian process modeling to combine known sports rules/physics (e.g., scoring constraints) with a residual GP layer, directly targeting the reported 30-40% uncertainty reduction to help pass the ECE gate.

cells.C1130: E-Sports Talent Scouting Based on Multimodal Twitch Stream Data
cells.D1130: Predicts CS:GO player skill rank from multimodal Twitch video, audio, and chat data using neural feature extraction pooled via a hierarchical Bayesian model.
cells.E1130: Modality-specific neural probability estimates are combined via hierarchical Bayesian pooling into an intrinsic-skill estimate.
cells.F1130: Relevant as an ensemble-pooling technique — the hierarchical Bayesian method for combining heterogeneous modality-specific probability estimates parallels GSE's need for a better ensemble/calibrator.
cells.G1130: Use the hierarchical Bayesian pooling scheme to combine GSE's disparate signal sources (scraped stats, odds movement, CEPT e-process outputs) into one coherent skill/probability estimate.

cells.C1131: Visual analytics for team-based invasion sports with significant events and Markov reward process
cells.D1131: Models an entire soccer match as a Markov chain of significant events in continuous parameter space, solving a Markov reward process via fitted-value iteration to value any event location/time/score condition.
cells.E1131: Continuous-state Markov reward process solved with fitted-value iteration regression to estimate event values across a continuous spatiotemporal domain.
cells.F1131: Directly relevant to GSE's core forecasting model — a continuous-state MDP/value-iteration approach is a legitimate alternative to naive baselines that could genuinely beat the current losing MAE.
cells.G1131: Adapt the continuous-state Markov reward process to generate a 'live pick value' surface, letting GSE visually show why a pick's confidence shifts as game state evolves — reinforcing the transparent-math brand.

cells.C1132: Detecting and classifying moments in basketball matches using sensor tracked data
cells.D1132: Uses kinematic thresholds tuned via an ROC-like procedure on player tracking data to automatically identify and classify active offensive/defensive periods in basketball.
cells.E1132: Threshold-based signal segmentation calibrated against video ground truth using ROC-curve-style tuning.
cells.F1132: Modestly relevant — a simple, interpretable data-labeling technique that fits GSE's 'math you can read' philosophy for structuring raw tracking-style time series into modelable game segments.
cells.G1132: Apply similar threshold-tuning segmentation to any future GSE-ingested tracking data to auto-label possession/play segments as new engineered features for sport-specific models.

cells.C1133: Unsupervised Methods for Identifying Pass Coverage Among Defensive Backs with NFL Player Tracking Data
cells.D1133: Uses Gaussian mixture modeling and hierarchical clustering on NFL tracking data to automatically infer man vs. zone pass-coverage labels without manual annotation.
cells.E1133: Unsupervised clustering (GMM + hierarchical) on engineered spatial features assigns soft coverage-type labels to plays.
cells.F1133: Directly relevant to GSE's data pipeline — an unsupervised feature-labeling technique that could enrich NFL-specific models with tactical context features without costly manual annotation.
cells.G1133: Use GMM soft cluster assignments as probabilistic (not hard) tactical features feeding the prediction engine, giving a built-in uncertainty signal consistent with bootstrap-mode philosophy.

cells.C1134: A Bayesian Approach to In-Game Win Probability in Soccer
cells.D1134: Introduces a Bayesian in-game win/tie/loss probability model for soccer that outperforms models borrowed from higher-scoring sports, validated as well-calibrated across eight seasons of top-five league data.
cells.E1134: Bayesian statistical framework leveraging contextual game-state features to jointly estimate running win/tie/loss probabilities, explicitly evaluated for calibration.
cells.F1134: Highly directly relevant — a soccer-specific, well-calibrated win-probability model is precisely the kind of per-sport probabilistic model GSE needs to pass its Brier/ECE calibration gate, especially for MLS.
cells.G1134: Adopt this soccer-specific calibration methodology as the reference architecture for GSE's MLS model, since it explicitly solves the low-scoring-sport calibration failure mode GSE is likely hitting.

cells.C1135: Stretching the Effectiveness of MLE from Accuracy to Bias for Pairwise Comparisons
cells.D1135: Shows the standard MLE for the Bradley-Terry-Luce model is minimax-optimal in accuracy but suboptimal in bias, and proposes a simple 'stretching' modification that improves bias while preserving accuracy.
cells.E1135: Domain-stretching correction to the maximum-likelihood estimator reduces systematic bias in pairwise-comparison parameter estimates.
cells.F1135: Directly relevant to GSE's core ranking/rating models (e.g., team strength via BTL-style comparisons) — a concrete, low-cost fix for bias that could improve calibration without full model redesign.
cells.G1135: Apply the stretching correction to GSE's team-rating estimators as a quick, mathematically justified patch to reduce systematic bias contributing to the current ECE failure, ahead of a full ensemble rebuild.

cells.C1136: Time to Die: Death Prediction in Dota 2 using Deep Learning
cells.D1136: Trains a deep network with shared weights to predict whether any of 10 Dota 2 players will die within a 5-second window, handling the 1% base-rate rarity of death events.
cells.E1136: Deep neural network with shared weights across players, trained on rich telemetry to make short-horizon rare-event probability predictions.
cells.F1136: Relevant as a rare-event/imbalanced-probability forecasting example — techniques for calibrated short-horizon predictions under severe class imbalance are directly applicable to GSE's live in-game event models.
cells.G1136: Adapt the rare-event prediction architecture for live 'next scoring play' or 'upset alert' micro-predictions, a differentiated live-odds feature built on GSE's own deterministic scoring engine.

cells.C1137: Ranking and synchronization from pairwise measurements via SVD
cells.D1137: Proposes an SVD-based algorithm for recovering a global ranking/signal from noisy, sparse pairwise measurements, with theoretical robustness guarantees, applied to sports ranking data.
cells.E1137: Spectral (SVD) method recovers latent rank/offset signal from a sparse pairwise-comparison graph, robust to noise and outliers via matrix perturbation theory.
cells.F1137: Directly relevant to GSE's team-rating/ranking components — a fast, theoretically grounded alternative to iterative rating systems (e.g., Elo) for deriving team strength from sparse historical matchups.
cells.G1137: Use the SVD ranking method as a lightweight, explainable cross-check against GSE's primary rating model, flagging discrepancies as a data-quality/calibration diagnostic signal.

cells.C1138: Going Deep: Models for Continuous-Time Within-Play Valuation of Game Outcomes in American Football with Tracking Data
cells.D1138: Introduces a continuous-time framework using an LSTM ball-carrier model plus conditional density estimation to value NFL plays moment-by-moment from player tracking data.
cells.E1138: Recurrent neural network models yards-gained trajectories conditioned on player positions, combined with conditional density estimation for continuous-time expected-value/win-probability outputs.
cells.F1138: Directly relevant to GSE's core prediction engine — a continuous-time, uncertainty-aware (density estimation) valuation framework is a genuine forecasting upgrade path beyond the current losing MAE baseline.
cells.G1138: Use the conditional density estimation output (not just point predictions) as the native uncertainty source for GSE's confidence scores, replacing the blunt bootstrap-mode cap with model-native uncertainty.

cells.C1139: Spatio-Temporal Action Localization in a Weakly Supervised Setting
cells.D1139: Uses unsupervised video segmentation plus Multiple Instance Learning with continuous labels to localize actions in video without frame-level annotations, tested on UCF-Sports.
cells.E1139: Weakly supervised MIL formulation with continuous (not discrete) segment labels makes the optimization tractable without dense annotation.
cells.F1139: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's tabular prediction stack; a stretch application only if GSE pursues video-based action recognition to feed additional game-event features.
cells.G1139: If GSE ever scrapes broadcast video, this weak-supervision approach could cheaply label in-play events (e.g., turnovers) without manual annotation to enrich the data pipeline.

cells.C1140: Fine-grained Entity Recognition with Reduced False Negatives and Large Type Coverage
cells.D1140: Proposes the HAnDS framework to automatically build high-quality distantly-supervised datasets for fine-grained entity recognition spanning domains including sports, reducing annotation errors.
cells.E1140: Heuristic-augmented distant supervision pipeline using Wikipedia/Freebase links produces cleaner entity-typed training data at scale.
cells.F1140: Directly relevant to GSE's data-ingestion and Intelligence Graph ambitions — a method for automatically building clean, typed entity datasets (players, teams, events) from web text without manual labeling.
cells.G1140: Use the HAnDS-style distant-supervision pipeline to auto-populate GSE's planned Intelligence Graph with typed player/team/event entities mined from scraped sports news and reference sites.

cells.C1141: Identifying cross country skiing techniques using power meters in ski poles
cells.D1141: Uses LSTM networks on ski-pole power-meter sensor data to classify which skiing gear/technique an athlete is using, achieving 95% accuracy within-subject but dropping to 78% cross-subject.
cells.E1141: LSTM time-series classifier trained on labeled sensor streams, with an explicit test of generalization across individuals.
cells.F1141: Modest relevance — the cross-subject generalization drop is a useful cautionary parallel for GSE: models trained on one context (team/era) may generalize poorly, informing per-sport/per-era calibration splits.
cells.G1141: Use the cross-subject generalization-gap finding as a design principle: test GSE's per-sport models explicitly for cross-team/cross-season generalization before declaring a calibration window 'green'.

cells.C1142: Semi-Supervised First-Person Activity Recognition in Body-Worn Video
cells.D1142: Uses motion-based features and semi-supervised classification to label activity in body-worn video with far less training data than supervised/deep methods, tested on real police body-cam footage.
cells.E1142: Motion-feature extraction combined with semi-supervised segmentation achieves competitive accuracy using minimal labeled data.
cells.F1142: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's tabular sports-prediction stack; a distant analogy for label-efficient classification if GSE ever needed to process video with scarce labeled examples.
cells.G1142: The 'competitive with a fraction of labels' semi-supervised pattern could inspire label-efficient training for any future GSE video-derived feature, minimizing costly manual annotation.

cells.C1143: Early Detection of Injuries in MLB Pitchers from Video
cells.D1143: Applies convolutional video-recognition models to TV broadcast footage of MLB pitchers to detect and predict injuries, evaluating generalization across pitchers and injury types.
cells.E1143: CNN-based video classification models trained on broadcast footage to detect/predict pitcher injury from pitching mechanics.
cells.F1143: A stretch for GSE's current stack, but directly relevant in spirit — injury risk is a key uncertainty driver in sports prediction, and this shows a feasible video-based injury signal usable as a model input.
cells.G1143: If GSE later scrapes broadcast video, an injury-detection signal like this could feed directly into bootstrap-mode confidence downgrades for picks involving pitchers showing early injury indicators.

cells.C1144: Searching News Articles Using an Event Knowledge Graph Leveraged by Wikidata
cells.D1144: Builds a semantic search engine over news articles by annotating them with Wikidata-derived event knowledge graphs, supporting structured filtering by event schema properties, including sports competitions.
cells.E1144: Wikidata-grounded semantic annotation pipeline links news text to a typed event knowledge graph enabling structured + keyword search.
cells.F1144: Directly relevant to GSE's planned Intelligence Graph — a concrete architecture for building a typed knowledge-graph layer over scraped sports news and events.
cells.G1144: Use this Wikidata-linked annotation approach as the backbone for GSE's Intelligence Graph, automatically tying scraped news/injury reports to typed event/player/team nodes for richer model context.

cells.D1145: Replaces static parameters in pairwise-comparison models with continuous-time Gaussian processes to capture evolving team/player skill, scaling to millions of sports observations with efficient approximate Bayesian inference.
cells.E1145: Gaussian process priors over time-varying skill parameters combined with an efficient linear-time approximate Bayesian inference algorithm.
cells.F1145: Highly directly relevant — a scalable, uncertainty-aware, time-varying rating model that outperforms static competitors, precisely addressing GSE's need for genuinely better forecasting beyond a naive baseline.
cells.G1145: Replace or complement GSE's static team-rating components with this GP-based time-varying skill model, using its native Bayesian posteriors as the uncertainty source for bootstrap-mode confidence adjustment.

cells.C1146: Multidimensional ground reaction forces and moments from wearable sensor accelerations via deep learning
cells.D1146: Trains CNNs on motion-capture-derived training data to predict multidimensional ground reaction forces/moments from wearable accelerometer data, aiming for field-deployable injury-risk monitoring.
cells.E1146: Supervised CNN regression maps wearable sensor accelerations to biomechanical force/moment estimates validated against force-plate ground truth.
cells.F1146: A stretch for GSE's current tabular stack, but relevant in spirit to injury-risk quantification as an uncertainty-relevant input if GSE ever incorporates athlete biomechanical data.
cells.G1146: Distant inspiration: a future 'injury-risk confidence modifier' could draw on wearable-derived force estimates as a novel bootstrap-mode input if GSE partners with athlete-tracking data providers.

cells.C1147: Does the winning team always cover the point spread? A study in professional basketball since 1990
cells.D1147: Performs regression analysis on NBA betting lines and outcomes since 1990 to study the relationship between winning and covering the spread, embedding results in an expert system.
cells.E1147: Regression analysis linking win percentage and betting-line variables to point-spread-covering outcomes.
cells.F1147: Directly relevant to GSE's public accuracy standards — closing-line value and spread-covering behavior are core to its market-efficiency benchmarking work.
cells.G1147: Use the win-vs-cover decomposition to build a GSE feature that separately communicates 'likely winner' versus 'likely to beat the market line,' making the brand's CLV benchmarking legible to users.

cells.C1148: DeepHoops: Evaluating Micro-Actions in Basketball Using Deep Feature Representations of Spatio-Temporal Data
cells.D1148: Builds an end-to-end deep sequence model (DeepHoops) that predicts terminal-action probabilities moment-by-moment during NBA possessions to estimate expected points and value off-ball actions.
cells.E1148: Multi-class sequence classification over spatio-temporal tracking data, with downsampling to handle class imbalance, explicitly evaluated for calibration.
cells.F1148: Directly relevant — a well-calibrated, continuous-in-time expected-value model handling severe class imbalance mirrors exactly the calibration and forecasting challenges GSE is trying to solve.
cells.G1148: Reuse the downsampling-for-imbalance technique to fix any rare-outcome classes (e.g., upsets, overtime) in GSE's settled-pick training data that may be dragging down its Brier/ECE scores.

cells.C1149: Playing Fast Not Loose: Evaluating team-level pace of play in ice hockey using spatio-temporal possession data
cells.D1149: Uses spatio-temporal possession data to study how pace of play varies by ice zone, period, and manpower situation in hockey, and its relationship to shot quality and turnovers.
cells.E1149: Descriptive spatial-statistical analysis of possession-derived pace metrics correlated with downstream event outcomes.
cells.F1149: Relevant as a sport-specific feature-engineering example — zone/situation-conditioned pace metrics could become engineered features in a per-sport hockey model, if/when GSE expands beyond NFL/MLB/MLS.
cells.G1149: If GSE adds hockey, use zone-conditioned pace as a novel predictive feature and as auto-generated 'why this pick' narrative content for the media pipeline.

cells.D1150: Proposes a neural data-to-text model that imitates the writing style of a given exemplar sentence while faithfully describing structured records, tested in restaurant and sports domains, using weak supervision.
cells.E1150: Hybrid attention-copy neural architecture with a content-coverage constraint learns style transfer from exemplar sentences without parallel training data.
cells.F1150: Directly relevant to GSE's brand-language enforcement and content automation — style-imitation generation could enforce the 'math you can read, never AI-powered' voice consistently in auto-generated copy.
cells.G1150: Use style-imitation generation to auto-draft pick explanations and social content that strictly mimic GSE's approved brand voice exemplars, reducing manual brand-lint review overhead.

cells.C1151: MOROCO: The Moldavian and Romanian Dialectal Corpus
cells.D1151: Introduces a large news-domain corpus (including a 'sports' topic label) for dialect and topic classification between Moldavian and Romanian text, with string-kernel and CNN baselines.
cells.E1151: Corpus construction paired with shallow (string kernel) and deep (CNN with Squeeze-and-Excitation) topic/dialect classifiers.
cells.F1151: Weak tangential relevance — only useful if GSE expands sports-content classification/monitoring into Romanian/Moldavian-language markets or media sources.
cells.G1151: Reuse the multi-label topic-classification baseline setup as a template for building GSE's own 'sports' topic classifier when filtering scraped multilingual news/social content for the pipeline.

cells.C1152: A Customized System to Assess Foot Plantar Pressure: A Case Study on Calloused and Normal Feet
cells.D1152: Develops a low-cost, high-frame-rate plantar pressure monitoring system for biomechanical assessment, validated on diabetic patients with foot calluses, applicable to sports use cases.
cells.E1152: Custom hardware/software system captures high-frequency pressure data for gait and posture analysis.
cells.F1152: Not directly relevant to GSE's prediction/calibration stack; a distant stretch only via general biomechanical-monitoring interest for athlete-condition features.
cells.G1152: No strong honest angle beyond noting the 'low-cost custom system replacing expensive commercial tools' theme, echoing GSE's own reliance on free data sources instead of costly paid feeds.

cells.C1153: Statistical models for short and long term forecasts of snow depth
cells.D1153: Presents zero-inflated gamma regression models for short-term (physics-informed) and long-term snow-depth forecasting, validated on three Norwegian locations, relevant to winter sport and avalanche risk.
cells.E1153: Zero-inflated gamma regression nonlinearly incorporates temperature/precipitation covariates following physical snow accumulation/melt principles.
cells.F1153: Relevant methodologically — zero-inflated distributions and physics-informed nonlinear covariate structures are directly transferable techniques for modeling sports outcomes with many zero/boundary values (e.g., shutouts, low scores).
cells.G1153: Apply the zero-inflated regression approach to low-scoring sports outcomes (e.g., MLS shutouts, MLB scoreless innings) where standard distributions currently contribute to GSE's calibration failure.

cells.C1154: Six-Day Footraces in the Post-Pedestrianism Era
cells.D1154: Analyzes 37 years of six-day ultra-footrace data and applies a forecasting model to predict the probability that current world records will be broken within the next decade.
cells.E1154: Historical-data regression combined with a probabilistic record-breaking forecast model.
cells.F1154: A minor stretch — niche ultra-endurance sport outside GSE's current NFL/MLB/MLS focus, but the record-breaking probability forecasting technique is conceptually transferable to any GSE market-expansion analysis.
cells.G1154: Repurpose the record-breaking probability model as a novel 'milestone watch' content feature (e.g., probability a season/career record falls this year) for the automated content-generation pipeline.

cells.C1155: Adaptive Feature Processing for Robust Human Activity Recognition on a Novel Multi-Modal Dataset
cells.D1155: Introduces a multimodal (RGB-Depth plus other sensors) indoor activity dataset and an adaptive feature-extraction algorithm, achieving up to 96.8% accuracy, explicitly noting sports analytics as an application.
cells.E1155: Multi-sensor fusion dataset paired with an adaptive preprocessing pipeline that lets different ML algorithms extract compatible features.
cells.F1155: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's tabular sports-betting stack; a distant stretch only if GSE later fuses multiple sensor modalities for athlete-monitoring features.
cells.G1155: The adaptive multi-modal feature-processing pattern could inspire a unified preprocessing layer that normalizes GSE's heterogeneous data sources (scraped stats, odds, text) into model-ready features consistently.

cells.D1156: Connects analogical reasoning to kernel methods, introducing an 'analogy kernel' and applying it to object-ranking preference learning across domains including sports, achieving competitive predictive accuracy.
cells.E1156: A kernel function measuring four-object analogical relationships is embedded into an SVM-based preference-ranking framework.
cells.F1156: Relevant as an alternative ranking-model technique — the analogy kernel offers a novel, interpretable way to rank teams/players by relational similarity, complementing GSE's ensemble approach.
cells.G1156: Use the analogy kernel to power a 'this matchup is like that matchup' explainer feature, giving human-readable analogical reasoning behind picks that fits GSE's transparent-math brand.

cells.C1157: Sentiment Classification of Customer Reviews about Automobiles in Roman Urdu
cells.D1157: Compares classical ML classifiers (finding Multinomial Naive Bayes best) for sentiment classification of Roman Urdu automobile reviews scraped from the web.
cells.E1157: Standard bag-of-features text classification pipeline benchmarked across several classical ML algorithms on scraped review text.
cells.F1157: Weak tangential relevance — only useful as a low-resource-language sentiment-classification template if GSE's content/monitoring pipeline ever needs Urdu-language coverage.
cells.G1157: Could serve as a low-cost baseline template for classifying scraped fan sentiment in additional languages, feeding auxiliary signals into GSE's market/sentiment monitoring.

cells.C1158: A Bayesian Additive Model for Understanding Public Transport Usage in Special Events
cells.D1158: Combines smart-card transit data with web-mined event context (including sports games) in a Bayesian additive Gaussian-process model to predict and disaggregate transit demand around concurrent special events.
cells.E1158: Bayesian additive model with Gaussian process components and expectation-propagation inference disaggregates overlapping event effects on a shared signal.
cells.F1158: Relevant methodologically — the Gaussian-process additive model with efficient approximate Bayesian inference (expectation propagation) is a transferable technique for GSE's calibration/ensemble work, and event-context web-mining parallels its data-ingestion approach.
cells.G1158: Adapt the additive-effects disaggregation technique to separate overlapping influences on betting-market movement (e.g., weather, injury news, public betting) within GSE's odds-ingestion pipeline.

cells.D1159: Proposes a custom data-provenance notation for sport performance analysis workflows, mapped to the W3C PROV standard, finding existing generic provenance tools fail to capture sport-specific automated/manual workflows well.
cells.E1159: Domain-specific provenance notation extends/critiques the W3C PROV standard to better represent sport analytics data lineage.
cells.F1159: Directly relevant to GSE's data pipeline reliability and ETL trustworthiness — a sport-domain-specific provenance framework for tracking exactly how each stat/pick traces back to its raw source, which matters for its trust/compliance toolkit.
cells.G1159: Build GSE's pick lifecycle (proposed→modeled→published→graded→settled) as a domain-specific provenance graph modeled on this notation, giving auditable, sport-native data lineage for compliance and debugging.

cells.C1160: Urban scaling of football followership on Twitter
cells.D1160: Analyzes geolocated Twitter followers of major football clubs to show club follower counts scale with city size, with scaling exponents varying by national income level.
cells.E1160: Urban-scaling-law analysis applied to social media follower geodata using power-law regression.
cells.F1160: Loosely relevant to GSE's B2B/market-expansion strategy — urban scaling patterns could inform where fan engagement and market demand concentrate geographically for widget/content rollout decisions.
cells.G1160: Use the urban-scaling methodology to prioritize which cities/markets to target first for GSE's B2B embeddable widgets based on predicted fan-base scaling, rather than uniform rollout.

cells.C1161: Computational Intelligence in Sports: A Systematic Literature Review
cells.D1161: Systematically reviews 31 sports data-mining studies (2010-2018), summarizing themes, datasets, algorithms, and identifying open research opportunities in the field.
cells.E1161: Systematic literature review synthesizing methods, applications, and gaps across sports computational-intelligence research.
cells.F1161: Directly relevant as a meta-resource — a structured map of the sports-analytics research landscape circa 2018 that GSE's research/agent team could mine for candidate techniques and unexplored gaps to pursue.
cells.G1161: Feed this review's identified 'research opportunities' list directly to GSE's internal research agents (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) as seed prompts for systematically scouting techniques to fix the calibration and forecasting blockers.

cells.C1162: Automated Camera-Based Estimation of Rehabilitation Criteria Following ACL Reconstruction
cells.D1162: Introduces a markerless camera-based method to estimate leg-press displacement, force, and limb symmetry during ACL rehabilitation, validated against encoder/force-plate ground truth over 12 weeks.
cells.E1162: Camera-based pose/force estimation replaces costly lab instrumentation for tracking rehabilitation progress metrics.
cells.F1162: A stretch for GSE's current product, but relevant if GSE ever wants injury-recovery-stage signals (e.g., 'is this player fully healthy') as a probabilistic input feature for player-availability-dependent picks.
cells.G1162: Distant inspiration: partner-sourced or publicly reported rehab-progress signals could become a novel 'player readiness confidence' input feeding bootstrap-mode adjustments for injury-return games.

cells.C1163: Sports Camera Calibration via Synthetic Data
cells.D1163: Uses a synthetic camera-pose engine and a two-GAN model to calibrate broadcast sports cameras from a single image, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy on soccer and volleyball datasets.
cells.E1163: Synthetic data generation plus a feature-pose database and GAN-based field-marking detection enable automatic single-image camera calibration.
cells.F1163: Not directly relevant to GSE's current tabular/odds-based prediction stack; a stretch only if GSE builds broadcast video ingestion for tactical or tracking-derived features.
cells.G1163: If GSE later ingests broadcast video, this synthetic-data calibration approach could be the entry point for automatically registering camera views to extract player-position features cheaply.

cells.C1164: Nonlinear methods to quantify Movement Variability in Human-Humanoid Interaction Activities
cells.D1164: Applies nonlinear time-series methods (recurrence plots, recurrence quantification analysis) to wearable sensor data from human-robot arm-imitation tasks, finding Shannon Entropy with RQA a robust discriminator.
cells.E1164: Nonlinear dynamical-systems analysis (state-space reconstruction, recurrence quantification) characterizes movement variability from time-series sensor data.
cells.F1164: Minimal direct relevance to GSE's core stack; a distant methodological parallel where nonlinear dynamics/entropy measures could be explored as novel volatility features for game or player time series.
cells.G1164: Explore recurrence quantification entropy as an exotic 'game unpredictability' feature computed from play-by-play time series, paralleling the intrinsic-dimension idea from other papers in this batch.

cells.C1165: Illusion of persistence in NBA 1995-2018 regular season data
cells.D1165: Re-examines a prior finding of 'persistence' (hot-hand-like patterns) in NBA teams' win-record time series, showing the effect is consistent with simple random null models rather than true persistence.
cells.E1165: Detrended fluctuation analysis results are compared against multiple random benchmark models to test whether apparent persistence is statistically meaningful.
cells.F1165: Directly relevant as a calibration/methodology caution — a reminder to rigorously benchmark any 'momentum' or 'form' features against random null models before trusting them in GSE's ensemble, avoiding false signal.
cells.G1165: Build a standing internal null-model benchmark (per this paper's method) that any new candidate feature (e.g., CEPT-derived signals) must beat before being trusted in the prediction engine.

cells.C1166: Can high-density human collective motion be forecasted by spatiotemporal fluctuations?
cells.D1166: Uses mode analysis from material science and non-equilibrium physics to forecast emergent crowd density waves at a concert roughly 1 second in advance from video data.
cells.E1166: Physics-inspired mode/fluctuation analysis on positional time-series data forecasts emergent collective patterns shortly before they occur.
cells.F1166: Not directly relevant to GSE's betting/prediction stack; a distant stretch only via the general 'forecast emergent systemic patterns from fluctuation data' theme.
cells.G1166: Conceptual inspiration only: the fluctuation-forecasting approach loosely parallels using early market/odds fluctuation signals to anticipate line movement just before it happens.

cells.C1167: Very Highly Skilled Individuals Do Not Choke Under Pressure: Evidence from Professional Darts
cells.D1167: Analyzes 23,192 professional darts throws and finds strong evidence that elite players perform better, not worse, under pressure, contradicting the common 'choking' hypothesis.
cells.E1167: Large-sample within-individual statistical analysis of performance under varying pressure conditions in a controlled, non-interactive sport setting.
cells.F1167: Relevant as a sports-psychology finding that could inform feature engineering — a 'pressure situation' indicator might behave counterintuitively, which is directly useful for correctly signed features in GSE's models.
cells.G1167: Encode a 'clutch performance' feature using this paper's methodology per player/team, testing whether elite performers in GSE's covered sports also outperform under pressure rather than assuming a choke effect.

cells.C1168: Learning Sports Camera Selection from Internet Videos
cells.D1168: Predicts which broadcast camera should be 'on air' for soccer using a random survival forest to impute missing candidate-view data and a spatial-appearance heatmap of players/ball.
cells.E1168: Random survival forest imputes incomplete multi-camera training data; spatial-appearance heatmaps describe foreground objects for camera-selection prediction.
cells.F1168: Not directly relevant to GSE's tabular prediction stack; a stretch application relevant only if GSE pursues broadcast/content automation involving video camera selection.
cells.G1168: The survival-forest imputation technique for handling structurally missing data (only 'selected' views observed) is conceptually reusable for GSE's own missing-data problems in incomplete odds/stat feeds.

cells.C1169: Operations Guided Neural Networks for High Fidelity Data-To-Text Generation
cells.D1169: Improves neural data-to-text generation fidelity by incorporating pre-executed symbolic operations (calculations) via a gating and quantization mechanism, tested on two sports datasets.
cells.E1169: A gated attention-based seq2seq network conditions generation on results of pre-computed symbolic operations to avoid hallucinated numbers.
cells.F1169: Directly relevant to GSE's automated content-generation ambitions — ensures generated pick summaries/recaps stay numerically faithful to the underlying deterministic math, reinforcing the 'not AI, math you can read' brand claim.
cells.G1169: Use operation-guided generation so any auto-written pick explanation is provably grounded in the exact computed numbers (e.g., actual Brier/CLV values), making brand-lint compliance structurally enforced rather than post-hoc checked.

cells.C1170: Sentimental Content Analysis and Knowledge Extraction from News Articles
cells.D1170: Extracts noise-robust sentiment and hot-topic knowledge from cross-country news articles across five categories including sports, using Word2Vec and topic extraction.
cells.E1170: Sentiment scoring pipeline combined with topic/keyword extraction and Word2Vec embeddings applied to multi-country news corpora.
cells.F1170: Modest relevance to GSE's data-ingestion — a template for mining sentiment/topic signals from scraped sports news as an auxiliary predictive or content-monitoring feature.
cells.G1170: Use the cross-country sentiment comparison technique to monitor regional media narrative differences around teams/events, feeding a novel sentiment-based context feature into GSE's ensemble.

cells.C1171: Towards Machine Learning on data from Professional Cyclists
cells.D1171: Trains an LSTM to predict elite cyclists' heart-rate response during training sessions from power-meter and sensor time-series data, as a first step toward broader athlete performance modeling.
cells.E1171: LSTM sequence model predicts a physiological response variable from time-series training-session sensor data.
cells.F1171: A stretch for GSE's current sports coverage (no cycling), but the LSTM physiological-response-forecasting pattern is a directly transferable time-series technique for any athlete-condition modeling GSE might add.
cells.G1171: Repurpose the LSTM approach as a template for forecasting in-game fatigue/performance decline curves for covered sports, feeding a fatigue-adjusted confidence signal into late-game picks.

cells.C1172: Improving pairwise comparison models using Empirical Bayes shrinkage
cells.D1172: Derives Empirical Bayes shrinkage estimators for pairwise comparison models (e.g. sports outcomes) that outperform max-likelihood on sparse data.
cells.E1172: Models uncertainty in who-plays-whom vs who-wins, then shrinks parameter estimates toward a prior using estimated pairwise uncertainty.
cells.F1172: Directly attacks GSE's bootstrap-mode problem (confidence capping under sparse data) and the calibration gate, since shrinkage is a principled alternative to ad hoc confidence caps.
cells.G1172: Replace GSE's hard bootstrap-mode cap with a per-sport Empirical Bayes shrinkage layer that smoothly degrades confidence as sample size shrinks, rather than a binary flag.

cells.C1173: A Skellam Regression Model for Quantifying Positional Value in Soccer
cells.D1173: Uses a Skellam (goal-difference) regression on 20,000 games plus FIFA ratings to estimate each soccer position line's contribution to win probability.
cells.E1173: Regression on the difference of two Poisson-like goal counts, converted into expected league points added above replacement (eLPAR).
cells.F1173: A concrete template for building an MLS-specific probability sub-model using free/public data, feeding GSE's push toward per-sport probability models.
cells.G1173: Use eLPAR-style positional decomposition to generate 'why this pick' explainer content for GSE's automated media generation, tying picks to specific tactical factors.

cells.C1174: Discovery of causal paths in cardiorespiratory parameters in elite athletes
cells.D1174: Applies multiple causal discovery algorithms (CAM, FGES, GFCI, Bayesian network learning) to find causal links between heart and respiratory signals in athletes at rest.
cells.E1174: Compares several time-independent causal discovery frameworks on physiological time-series to infer directed causal graphs.
cells.F1174: Tangential — its rigorous, non-founder causal-discovery methodology is a useful contrast/benchmark for evaluating the founder's CEPT framework's causal claims.
cells.G1174: Borrow the multi-algorithm cross-validation approach (running CAM/FGES/Bayesian-network learners side by side) as a sanity-check harness for CEPT's causal assumptions before trusting it in the calibration gate.

cells.C1175: Filtering Procedures for Sensor Data in Basketball
cells.D1175: Proposes an automatic algorithm to clean basketball player-tracking data by dropping inactive moments and labeling offensive/defensive game segments.
cells.E1175: Rule-based filtering and segmentation of spatio-temporal trajectory data validated via robustness checks.
cells.F1175: Directly useful for GSE's data-ingestion pipeline reliability — a template for automated cleaning/segmentation of noisy tracking or scraped sports data.
cells.G1175: Adapt the inactive-moment detection logic as an anomaly filter inside the ETL pipeline to auto-flag corrupted or stale scraped play-by-play feeds before they reach the prediction engine.

cells.C1176: Evaluating Non-Motorized Transport Popularity of Urban Roads by Sports GPS Tracks
cells.D1176: Defines a 'p-index' from crowdsourced running/cycling GPS tracks to rank urban road segment popularity for non-motorized transport.
cells.E1176: Aggregates GPS trace density and frequency across time windows into a popularity index per road segment.
cells.F1176: Weak stretch — the p-index construction pattern is a distant analog for building a 'popularity/engagement index' from user pick activity for the Galaxy Dynasty game layer.
cells.G1176: Repurpose the p-index methodology to score which fictional 'AUGUR' game locations/leagues attract the most player engagement over time.

cells.C1177: Wearable Audio and IMU Based Shot Detection in Racquet Sports
cells.D1177: Fuses accelerometer and audio sensor data from a wrist wearable to detect table tennis shots in real time with 95.6% accuracy.
cells.E1177: Sensor fusion (IMU + audio) with synchronized timestamps feeding a lightweight real-time event classifier.
cells.F1177: Tangential — relevant only as a data-ingestion source concept if GSE ever ingests wearable/IoT event streams beyond scraped box scores and odds feeds.
cells.G1177: Use the fusion architecture as inspiration for combining multiple noisy free-data sources (scrapes + odds feeds + social signals) into one robust event-detection layer for live game state changes.

cells.C1178: Deep Decision Trees for Discriminative Dictionary Learning with Adversarial Multi-Agent Trajectories
cells.D1178: Builds an interpretable decision-tree architecture that learns a dictionary of multi-agent (soccer) group interaction patterns from tracking data.
cells.E1178: Hierarchical clustering-based tree construction fine-tuned via backprop to produce interpretable 'team strategy' dictionary entries.
cells.F1178: Relevant to GSE's ensemble/interpretability goals — an interpretable structure-learning approach could inform building auditable per-sport sub-models rather than black-box ensembles.
cells.G1178: Use the learned interaction dictionary as a feature layer feeding the Intelligence Graph, turning discovered team-strategy patterns into typed knowledge primitives.

cells.C1179: Players Movements and Team Shooting Performance: a Data Mining approach for Basketball
cells.D1179: Uses cluster analysis and multidimensional scaling on player GPS data to find movement patterns linked to shooting performance in professional basketball.
cells.E1179: Clustering (defensive vs transition patterns) plus MDS visualization to link spatial player configurations to shot outcomes.
cells.F1179: Modest — an example of turning positional tracking data into predictive features, relevant if GSE ever ingests player-tracking data beyond box scores/odds.
cells.G1179: Apply the clustering approach to bettor/market 'formations' (line movement clusters across books) rather than player positions, as a market-microstructure feature for closing-line-value modeling.

cells.C1180: Mining Automatically Estimated Poses from Video Recordings of Top Athletes
cells.D1180: Develops unsupervised algorithms to mine cycle speed, stability, and phase segmentation from noisy pose-estimation data in swimming and long jump videos.
cells.E1180: Unsupervised time-series segmentation and cycle-stability analysis applied to noisy DNN pose outputs.
cells.F1180: Weak — only tangentially relevant as an example of extracting reliable structured metrics from noisy, automatically-collected sports video/pose data.
cells.G1180: Use the unsupervised cycle-stability metric as a template for detecting 'rhythm/consistency' signals in team performance time-series that feed into confidence scoring.

cells.C1181: On Finding Stable and Efficient Solutions for the Team Formation Problem
cells.D1181: Formulates team/lineup assignment as a bi-level optimization balancing social welfare and game-theoretic (core) stability, solved via branch-cut-and-price.
cells.E1181: Bi-level binary integer program transformed into a single-level exponential IP solved with a custom exact algorithm.
cells.F1181: Tangential — the optimization machinery (not the sports application) could inform resource allocation problems like job-queue prioritization in BullMQ, not the core prediction pipeline.
cells.G1181: Adapt the stability/efficiency trade-off framing to design fair matchmaking or league-balancing rules inside the Galaxy Dynasty persistent game.

cells.C1182: Flow From Motion: A Deep Learning Approach
cells.D1182: Trains deep neural nets on wearable sensor data to detect a tennis player's psychological 'flow state' as labeled by a professional coach, achieving ~98% accuracy.
cells.E1182: Supervised deep learning classifier mapping wrist-worn IMU signals to coach-annotated mental-state labels.
cells.F1182: Weak stretch — illustrates using proxy sensor signals to infer a latent unobservable state, conceptually similar to inferring latent team/player form for GSE's models.
cells.G1182: Borrow the 'coach-labeled latent state' framing to build a proxy 'momentum state' classifier from in-game event sequences, feeding it as a feature into the prediction engine.

cells.C1183: Stance Detection on Tweets: An SVM-based Approach
cells.D1183: Builds SVM classifiers to detect Favor/Against/Neither stance in sports-related tweets using n-gram, hashtag, and named-entity features.
cells.E1183: Feature-engineered SVM text classification with a released annotated sports-tweet dataset.
cells.F1183: Adjacent to GSE's brand-language enforcement and social/media content pipeline — stance detection could help gauge public sentiment feeding confidence or content generation.
cells.G1183: Use stance-detection features as an automated pre-screen for outbound social content, flagging any generated post that reads as taking a partisan 'stance' rather than neutral analysis, protecting the 'math you can read' brand tone.

cells.C1184: The Advantage of Doubling: Deep RL for the Double Team in the NBA
cells.D1184: Uses deep reinforcement learning on 643,000 NBA possessions to evaluate the risk/reward trade-off of double-teaming defensive strategies.
cells.E1184: Learns a value function over defensive actions via RL on player trajectory data, validated against points-per-possession outcomes.
cells.F1184: Directly relevant as a rigorous sports-specific probabilistic modeling example; shows how RL-derived policy values can be validated against real outcome metrics, a template for backtesting rigor GSE needs.
cells.G1184: Apply the same policy-value validation methodology (checking that learned values predict points-per-possession) as a template for validating GSE's own pick confidence scores against realized CLV.

cells.C1185: On the Complexity of Opinions and Online Discussions
cells.D1185: Builds a latent-space model of opinions in online discussions (including Yahoo Sports) validated against human voting, linking it to matrix sign-rank theory.
cells.E1185: Learns low-dimensional opinion embeddings from voting data, using sign-rank to estimate the true dimensionality of opinion space.
cells.F1185: Tangential — relevant only as a technique for quantifying user/community sentiment around sports content, useful for community engagement features rather than core prediction.
cells.G1185: Use the opinion-embedding technique to map fan sentiment/discussion polarization around a given pick, surfacing it as a 'crowd disagreement' signal alongside GSE's own probability.

cells.C1186: Neural Relational Inference for Interacting Systems
cells.D1186: Introduces an unsupervised VAE-based model (NRI) that jointly infers a latent interaction graph and dynamics from observed trajectories, demonstrated on sports tracking data.
cells.E1186: Graph-neural-network variational autoencoder where the latent code is an interaction graph, learned purely from observational multi-agent trajectories.
cells.F1186: Strong architectural fit for GSE's longer-term Intelligence Graph ambition — a way to infer typed relational structure directly from raw tracking/event data rather than hand-coding it.
cells.G1186: Use NRI-style unsupervised interaction-graph inference to auto-populate parts of the Intelligence Graph's typed relationships (e.g. which players/teams interact and how) directly from ingested play-by-play data.

cells.C1187: nflWAR: A Reproducible Method for Offensive Player Evaluation in Football
cells.D1187: Introduces nflscrapR and a multilevel-model WAR (wins above replacement) framework for NFL players built entirely on public play-by-play data, with resampling-based uncertainty estimates.
cells.E1187: Multinomial logistic regression for expected points, GAM for win probability, then multilevel models isolating player contributions with bootstrap uncertainty.
cells.F1187: Extremely relevant — an open, reproducible, free-data pipeline (like Pro-Football-Reference scraping) for building calibrated per-player value/uncertainty estimates in exactly GSE's NFL domain.
cells.G1187: Fork nflscrapR's public play-by-play pipeline as a second, independent NFL data source to cross-validate GSE's own scraped feeds and catch pipeline drift or missing plays.

cells.C1188: Which Football Player Bears Most Resemblance to Messi? A Statistical Analysis
cells.D1188: Uses normalized WhoScored performance metrics and a distance metric to rank which footballers are statistically most similar to Lionel Messi.
cells.E1188: Multi-criteria similarity scoring via data normalization and a chosen distance/metric function over player statistics.
cells.F1188: Weak — a lightweight similarity-metric exercise, only tangentially useful for player-comparison features in GSE's content or B2B widget layer.
cells.G1188: Repackage the similarity-scoring method as a 'find your team's closest historical comparable' feature for automated social content generation.

cells.C1189: DxNAT: Deep Neural Networks for Explaining Non-Recurring Traffic Congestion
cells.D1189: Trains a deep network on 900M+ traffic records to classify non-recurring congestion (e.g., caused by football games) with 98.7% accuracy using image-encoded traffic data fused with event data.
cells.E1189: Encodes regional traffic as scaled images, fuses with event/time data, augments via crossover, and tunes sensitivity via ROC analysis.
cells.F1189: Tangential — its event-driven anomaly classification pattern (detecting disruption from sports games) is conceptually adjacent to anomaly detection in GSE's data pipeline for odds/line anomalies.
cells.G1189: Adapt the image-encoding + event-fusion trick to detect anomalous odds-market disruptions (e.g. sudden line moves correlated with breaking news events) as an anomaly-detection layer.

cells.C1190: A Two-point Method for PTZ Camera Calibration in Sports
cells.D1190: Proposes a two-point calibration method for pan-tilt-zoom soccer broadcast cameras using minimal correspondences plus a random forest for fast new-image calibration.
cells.E1190: Geometric calibration algorithm combined with a random-forest regressor predicting pan-tilt angles without feature matching.
cells.F1190: Low relevance — purely computer-vision broadcast tooling, not applicable to GSE's statistical/data pipeline unless they build video-based scouting tools later.
cells.G1190: If GSE ever builds video-based automated highlight/content generation, this calibration approach could let it auto-track camera framing to synchronize broadcast footage with play-by-play event timestamps.

cells.C1191: Conversational AI: The Science Behind the Alexa Prize
cells.D1191: Describes the Alexa Prize competition and the NLU/dialog/response-generation techniques university teams built for open-domain socialbots covering topics including sports.
cells.E1191: Survey of conversational AI system components: NLU, context modeling, dialog management, response generation, evaluated via live user interaction at scale.
cells.F1191: Relevant to GSE's internal agentic tooling (Jarvis/Hermes/Fable) and any future conversational pick-explainer or customer-facing chat features, though the product itself can't be marketed as 'AI'.
cells.G1191: Use the Alexa Prize's dialog-evaluation and traffic-management engineering lessons to architect a conversational 'ask about this pick' assistant that stays internally agentic without ever surfacing 'AI-powered' branding.

cells.C1192: A method for Bayesian regression modelling of composition data
cells.D1192: Proposes a new simulation-based Bayesian fitting approach for Dirichlet regression on compositional (proportion) data, illustrated with a sport science application.
cells.E1192: Bayesian simulation-based estimation for Dirichlet-distributed outcome vectors, improving accuracy and inference power over existing methods.
cells.F1192: Directly useful — compositional/proportion modeling (e.g. how win/loss/draw or possession shares split) is exactly the kind of Bayesian regression that could feed GSE's per-sport probability models.
cells.G1192: Use Dirichlet regression to jointly model multi-outcome markets (win/draw/loss, or player prop distributions) as compositions, rather than separate binary models, tightening calibration across correlated outcomes.

cells.C1193: Mapping to Declarative Knowledge for Word Problem Solving
cells.D1193: Learns a latent mapping from math word-problem text (including sports examples) to declarative arithmetic knowledge for solving quantitative reasoning problems.
cells.E1193: Latent-variable model selecting relevant declarative rules per arithmetic operation, trained without expensive annotation.
cells.F1193: Weak stretch — the underlying NLP-to-structured-reasoning mapping is a distant analog for turning natural-language sports questions into structured queries against GSE's data.
cells.G1193: Adapt the declarative-knowledge-mapping idea to auto-translate user natural-language betting questions ('who covers the spread if X') into structured prediction-engine queries.

cells.C1194: Towards Structured Analysis of Broadcast Badminton Videos
cells.D1194: Builds an end-to-end pipeline segmenting badminton broadcast points, tracking/identifying players, and annotating strokes with high accuracy, enabling automated gameplay metrics.
cells.E1194: Multi-stage CV pipeline: point segmentation, player detection/re-identification, then stroke-level action segmentation.
cells.F1194: Tangential — a template for turning raw broadcast video into structured event data, relevant only if GSE expands data ingestion beyond text-based scraping into video analytics.
cells.G1194: Could inform an automated highlight-clip generator for GSE's content-automation roadmap, auto-tagging key moments from broadcast footage to pair with generated commentary.

cells.D1195: Trains an ML 'artificial judge' to reproduce human evaluators' soccer performance ratings, revealing that humans rate players using a 'noticeability heuristic' biased toward extreme feature values.
cells.E1195: Supervised ML model reproducing human judge scores, then interpreted to reveal systematic human evaluation biases.
cells.F1195: Highly relevant to calibration — shows how human 'ground truth' labels can be systematically biased, a caution for any GSE model trained against subjective ratings, and a case study in interpretable model-of-a-judge design.
cells.G1195: Build an analogous 'artificial judge' model of sportsbook line-setters' biases (rather than fan judges) to systematically detect and exploit oddsmaker biases, extending the closing-line-value benchmark work.

cells.C1196: Coupling Story to Visualization: Textual Analysis as a Bridge Between Data and Interpretation
cells.D1196: Automatically extracts narrative components (who/what/when/where) from sports journalism text and links them bidirectionally to data visualizations.
cells.E1196: NLP-based narrative extraction combined with quantitative narrative analysis to auto-generate linked text+visualization stories.
cells.F1196: Directly relevant to GSE's automated social/media content generation ambitions — a concrete method for pairing generated text with data visualizations for sports content.
cells.G1196: Use this bidirectional text-visualization coupling to auto-generate 'explainer' pages per pick, where clicking a stat in the narrative highlights the corresponding chart, reinforcing the 'math you can read' brand.

cells.C1197: tHoops: A Multi-Aspect Analytical Framework for Spatio-Temporal Basketball Data
cells.D1197: Uses tensor decomposition (PARAFAC) on a 3D team/location/time tensor to extract interpretable prototype spatiotemporal shot-selection and offensive patterns.
cells.E1197: Tensor factorization of spatio-temporal-contextual basketball data into a small set of interpretable components, expressing entities as weighted mixtures.
cells.F1197: Relevant to GSE's ensemble/interpretability goals — tensor decomposition offers an interpretable alternative to opaque ensembling for capturing per-sport, per-team latent tendencies.
cells.G1197: Apply tensor decomposition across sport/team/time to auto-discover interpretable 'style archetypes' that could feed both the Intelligence Graph and explainable ensemble weighting.

cells.C1198: Hint of a Universal Law for the Financial Gains of Competitive Sport Teams
cells.D1198: Finds a simple scaling law describing how prize money/gains scale with team ranking in the Tour de France and Formula 1.
cells.E1198: Empirical scaling-law fitting on rare-event financial/ranking data using physics-style power-law analysis.
cells.F1198: Weak — a niche econophysics curiosity, only tangentially useful as inspiration for modeling reward/payout distributions in the Galaxy Dynasty game economy.
cells.G1198: Use the scaling-law framing to design in-game reward curves for Galaxy Dynasty's competitive tiers so payouts feel statistically grounded rather than arbitrary.

cells.C1199: Learning to Rank based on Analogical Reasoning
cells.D1199: Proposes an object-ranking method using analogical proportions (A:B::C:D) combined with instance-based learning, tested on sports and other ranking domains.
cells.E1199: Analogy-based inference pattern combined with rank aggregation and instance-based learning for predicting linear orders of new objects.
cells.F1199: Relevant to GSE's ranking/calibration problem — an alternative ranking paradigm to standard regression-based approaches, potentially useful when transferring models across sports with sparse data.
cells.G1199: Use analogical reasoning to bootstrap a new sport's ranking model by transferring learned proportional relationships from a data-rich sport (e.g. NFL) to a sparse one, addressing bootstrap-mode cold starts.

cells.C1200: TweetIT: Analyzing Topics for Twitter Users to Garner Maximum Attention
cells.D1200: Computes an 'attention factor' from likes/retweets to select top tweets per user, then applies topic modeling (including a sports category) to determine intent and popularity drivers.
cells.E1200: Attention-weighted tweet selection followed by topic modeling and similarity comparison against a news corpus.
cells.F1200: Adjacent to GSE's content-automation goals — a template for identifying which topics/phrasings drive social engagement, useful for tuning automated content generation.
cells.G1200: Use the attention-factor methodology to A/B test and optimize which pick-explainer phrasings or formats get the most social engagement before scaling automated posting.

cells.C1201: Open Set Logo Detection and Retrieval
cells.D1201: Introduces a large open-set logo dataset and a two-stage CNN detector/comparator for finding previously unseen logos in images/video, demonstrated on sports broadcast advertisement assessment.
cells.E1201: Separate CNN-based detection and comparison modules enabling single-query logo retrieval without retraining for new logos.
cells.F1201: Low — a computer-vision advertising-effectiveness tool, not connected to GSE's statistical prediction core.
cells.G1201: Could be repurposed for a B2B sponsor-analytics add-on measuring brand exposure in embedded sports content widgets, if GSE expands into media analytics.

cells.C1202: Exploiting oddsmaker bias to improve the prediction of NFL outcomes
cells.D1202: Shows that models exploiting systematic biases in bookmaker-set point spreads outperform other approaches for predicting NFL game outcomes.
cells.E1202: Trains predictive models on real gambling data, comparing 'exploit oddsmaker bias' strategies against direct outcome-prediction baselines.
cells.F1202: Extremely relevant — directly informs GSE's closing-line-value benchmark and the core forecasting problem, since it's about beating a market baseline using bias exploitation rather than better outcome modeling.
cells.G1202: Build a dedicated 'oddsmaker bias' sub-model that runs alongside GSE's primary prediction engine specifically to generate CLV-beating signal, decoupled from the calibration-gated outcome model.

cells.C1203: Asymptotically Optimal Sequential Design for Rank Aggregation
cells.D1203: Develops a Bayesian sequential design (with mirror-descent computation) for adaptively choosing which pairwise comparisons to collect to rank K items efficiently, applicable to sports.
cells.E1203: Bayesian decision framework balancing exploration/exploitation in sequential pairwise comparison collection, with asymptotic optimality proofs.
cells.F1203: Relevant to online learning/bandit methods GSE could use for efficiently allocating scarce labeled data (e.g. deciding which matchups most reduce model uncertainty) during bootstrap mode.
cells.G1203: Use this sequential design theory to prioritize which upcoming sparse-data matchups the ingestion pipeline should scrape more deeply first, maximizing calibration-relevant information gain per compute dollar.

cells.C1204: Beating the bookies with their own numbers - and how the online sports betting market is rigged
cells.D1204: Designs a profitable strategy exploiting mispriced odds implicit in bookmaker-published probabilities rather than building an independent forecast, validated over 10 years and live betting.
cells.E1204: Extracts implied probabilities from published odds, finds inconsistencies/mispricing across bookmakers, and bets accordingly; documents bookmaker retaliation against winners.
cells.F1204: Directly relevant — validates that market-implied probability comparison (not raw forecasting) can beat bookmakers, a close analog to GSE's closing-line-value standard and a caution about how betting markets react to consistently accurate models.
cells.G1204: Build a live cross-book odds-consistency scanner as a standalone GSE feature that flags mispriced lines directly, sidestepping the need to beat the naive baseline with a standalone forecast model.

cells.C1205: An Aerodynamic Analysis of Recent FIFA World Cup Balls
cells.D1205: Fits novel drag/lift coefficient models to different FIFA World Cup ball designs and simulates how surface texture changes affect flight trajectories under varying conditions.
cells.E1205: Physics-based curve fitting of aerodynamic coefficients plus numerical trajectory simulation.
cells.F1205: Very low — pure sports physics with no connection to GSE's statistical/data platform.
cells.G1205: No meaningful product application; at most a fun trivia-style content piece for automated social media generation about World Cup ball physics.

cells.C1206: Fine-Grained Retrieval of Sports Plays using Tree-Based Alignment of Trajectories
cells.D1206: Proposes a hierarchical tree-based method to retrieve similar multi-agent sports plays from tracking data, solving the permutation/alignment problem across players.
cells.E1206: Coarse-to-fine hierarchical alignment and partitioning of multi-agent trajectory data for similarity-based retrieval.
cells.F1206: Relevant if GSE ingests player-tracking data — a solid method for building a 'similar historical plays/games' feature for context-aware forecasting or content.
cells.G1206: Use trajectory-alignment retrieval to find historically similar game situations as comparables for a given upcoming matchup, feeding an explainable 'this reminds us of...' feature into pick explanations.

cells.C1207: A physical model for efficient ranking in networks
cells.D1207: Presents a physically-inspired, scalable algorithm (SpringRank) that infers real-valued hierarchical rankings from directed interaction networks, validated on sports tournaments among other domains.
cells.E1207: Solves a sparse linear system to assign continuous ranks that best explain observed win/lose interactions, with a built-in significance test.
cells.F1207: Directly relevant to GSE's core ranking/probability engine — an efficient, statistically-principled ranking method that could feed or replace parts of a per-sport probability sub-model, especially given its significance-test and speed advantages.
cells.G1207: Use SpringRank's significance test to automatically detect which sports/leagues currently have genuinely learnable hierarchy versus near-random competitiveness, informing where GSE should trust its models most.

cells.C1208: Speech Recognition Challenge in the Wild: Arabic MGB-3
cells.D1208: Describes an Arabic dialect speech-recognition and dialect-ID challenge using multi-genre YouTube videos, one genre being sports.
cells.E1208: Benchmark challenge comparing ASR and dialect-identification systems on noisy multi-genre audio.
cells.F1208: Very low — an Arabic ASR benchmark; sports is just one of seven incidental content genres, no direct connection to GSE.
cells.G1208: No strong application; only tangential if GSE ever needs multilingual transcription of sports commentary for international content localization.

cells.C1209: Towards a Dedicated Computer Vision Tool set for Crowd Simulation Models
cells.D1209: Builds a computer-vision toolkit for crowd flow segmentation, counting, and group detection to calibrate/validate crowd simulation models at events like sports games.
cells.E1209: CV pipeline combining flow segmentation, source/sink identification, and group tracking from video.
cells.F1209: Very low — safety/crowd-management tooling for physical venues, unrelated to GSE's statistical prediction platform.
cells.G1209: No direct fit; at most tangential inspiration if GSE ever builds live-attendance/venue-analytics features for stadium partnerships.

cells.C1210: Generating Video Descriptions with Topic Guidance
cells.D1210: Proposes a topic-guided video captioning model that mines data-driven topics (including sports) to generate more topic-appropriate video descriptions.
cells.E1210: Topic mining model teaches a student topic-prediction model using multi-modal video features, which then guides a caption decoder.
cells.F1210: Relevant to GSE's automated content generation ambitions — a template for generating topic-consistent natural-language descriptions, applicable to auto-captioning highlight clips or picks.
cells.G1210: Adapt the topic-guided decoder architecture to keep GSE's automated social copy consistently in its 'math you can read' register by treating brand voice as an explicit topic/style guidance signal.

cells.C1211: Self-supervised Learning of Pose Embeddings from Spatiotemporal Relations in Videos
cells.D1211: Learns pose similarity embeddings from unlabeled video using temporal ordering and spatial placement as self-supervised auxiliary tasks, evaluated on Olympic Sports datasets.
cells.E1211: Siamese CNN trained via curriculum learning on self-supervised temporal/spatial pretext tasks, refined by mining repetitive poses.
cells.F1211: Low-moderate — a self-supervised learning template useful only if GSE expands into video-based pose/motion analytics beyond box-score data.
cells.G1211: The curriculum-learning idea (start with reliable samples, gradually add harder ones) could be repurposed for training GSE's calibration models: start calibrating on data-rich sports/seasons before extending to sparse ones.

cells.C1212: Automatic Curation of Golf Highlights using Multimodal Excitement Features
cells.D1212: Fuses player reactions, crowd cheering, and commentator tone/word analysis to automatically identify and curate the most exciting moments in golf broadcasts.
cells.E1212: Multi-modal excitement scoring combining action recognition, audio crowd analysis, and NLP-based commentary analysis, deployed live at a major tournament.
cells.F1212: Directly relevant to GSE's automated content/social generation ambitions — a proven real-world system for turning raw sports broadcasts into curated highlight content with reduced manual annotation.
cells.G1212: Adapt the multimodal excitement-scoring approach to automatically rank which settled picks/games are most 'story-worthy' for GSE's automated content pipeline to write up first.
