cells.C1213: LinNet: Probabilistic Lineup Evaluation Through Network Embedding
cells.D1213: Uses a directed network of NBA lineup matchups plus node2vec embeddings to predict which lineup beats which with well-calibrated, sport-agnostic probabilities (69% accuracy, outperforming plus-minus).
cells.E1213: Builds a matchup-performance-margin network, learns latent lineup embeddings via node2vec, then models beat-probability from embedding distances, explicitly validated with calibration curves.
cells.F1213: Highly relevant — a directly analogous, already-validated calibrated probability model (with reported calibration curves) in exactly GSE's domain, and explicitly sport-agnostic, matching the push toward per-sport probability models.
cells.G1213: Adopt LinNet's network-embedding-plus-calibration-curve validation approach as a concrete methodology for GSE's calibration gate, since it's a proven precedent for achieving well-calibrated sports win probabilities from matchup data alone.

cells.D1214: Reviews state-of-the-art methods for analyzing player positioning/movement data and presents preliminary convex-hull-based findings linking spatial patterns to team performance.
cells.E1214: Literature review plus a convex-hull geometric analysis of player trajectory data.
cells.F1214: Moderate — a survey of techniques for turning tracking data into performance features, useful background if GSE expands beyond box-score/odds data into positional analytics.
cells.G1214: Use convex-hull 'team shape' metrics as a lightweight, interpretable feature to add to per-sport probability models when richer tracking data becomes available.

cells.D1215: Presents a Turkish-language stance-detection tweet dataset targeting two sports clubs, with SVM baseline classifiers using n-gram/hashtag features.
cells.E1215: Annotated dataset creation plus SVM classification baselines for stance (Favor/Against/Neither) toward sports club targets.
cells.F1215: Weak — only relevant as another data point for sentiment/stance detection techniques applicable to social monitoring around GSE content, in a non-English market.
cells.G1215: Could inform international expansion of GSE's brand-monitoring tooling to detect stance/sentiment about GSE picks in non-English social media.

cells.C1216: Learning to Learn from Noisy Web Videos
cells.D1216: Uses reinforcement learning (Q-learning) to learn a policy for selecting good training examples from noisy web-search video results, evaluated on the Sports-1M benchmark.
cells.E1216: RL-based data-labeling policy trained on a small clean dataset, then applied to automatically curate noisy web-sourced training data.
cells.F1216: Relevant to GSE's data pipeline reliability — an RL approach for automatically filtering noisy, web-scraped data (directly analogous to cleaning free multi-source scraped sports data).
cells.G1216: Train an analogous RL-based data-quality policy to automatically triage and down-weight unreliable scraped data sources (e.g. inconsistent Pro-Football-Reference pages) before they enter the modeling pipeline.

cells.C1217: Luck is Hard to Beat: The Difficulty of Sports Prediction
cells.D1217: Quantifies luck vs skill across 198 leagues/1503 seasons in 4 sports, showing sophisticated models 'hardly beat simple models' at forecasting outcomes, and estimates underdog win probability with home-advantage effects.
cells.E1217: Probabilistic graphical model decomposing game outcomes into skill and luck components, benchmarked against feature-rich models across many leagues.
cells.F1217: Directly and centrally relevant — this is essentially an academic explanation for why GSE's core model currently loses to the naive baseline, suggesting the ceiling on beatable signal may be structurally low and simple models may be near-optimal in many sports.
cells.G1217: Use this paper's luck/skill decomposition framework to set sport-specific, honest 'ceiling' expectations for GSE's MAE targets, reframing the backtest-vs-naive-baseline problem as partly a fundamental luck constraint rather than pure modeling failure.

cells.C1218: Extraction and Classification of Diving Clips from Continuous Video Footage
cells.D1218: Provides an end-to-end pipeline to temporally crop, track, and classify diving actions from continuous broadcast footage despite the diver occupying <1% of pixels.
cells.E1218: Combines temporal event cropping, small-object tracking, and fine-grained pose-based action classification.
cells.F1218: Low — a niche computer-vision pipeline, only tangentially relevant if GSE later ingests video for automated highlight generation.
cells.G1218: Not a strong fit for GSE's current text/odds-centric stack; best left as background technique for a future video-content feature.

cells.C1219: TwiInsight: Discovering Topics and Sentiments from Social Media Datasets
cells.D1219: Presents a system extracting popular topics (including sports) and sentiments from Twitter via topic modeling, comparing six popular topic-modeling and sentiment algorithms.
cells.E1219: Compares LDA-style topic models and sentiment classifiers, visualized through an interactive dashboard.
cells.F1219: Adjacent — a benchmark comparison of topic-modeling/sentiment tools GSE could use for monitoring public discourse around its picks or sports events feeding content generation.
cells.G1219: Use the multi-algorithm comparison as a starting toolkit to build a lightweight 'what's trending in sports discourse' feed that surfaces topics for GSE's automated content team to write about.

cells.C1220: Learning Spatiotemporal Features for Infrared Action Recognition with 3D CNNs
cells.D1220: Proposes a two-stream 3D CNN for infrared video action recognition, pretraining on the visible-spectrum Sports-1M dataset before fine-tuning on infrared data.
cells.E1220: Two-stream 3D CNN with a discriminative code layer, using transfer learning from Sports-1M to a smaller infrared dataset.
cells.F1220: Very low — a niche computer-vision domain-transfer study; Sports-1M is used only as a generic pretraining corpus, unrelated to GSE's statistical modeling needs.
cells.G1220: No meaningful GSE application; at most illustrates transfer-learning-from-large-corpus patterns applicable to unrelated future CV projects.

cells.C1221: Spatiotemporal Rate Adaptive Tiled Scheme for 360 Sports Events
cells.D1221: Proposes a bandwidth-efficient tiled streaming scheme for 360-degree VR sports video that reduces storage overhead while preserving perceived quality in low-bandwidth conditions.
cells.E1221: Degrading-quality tiled video representation optimized for head-mounted-display field-of-view streaming.
cells.F1221: Very low — video-streaming infrastructure, unrelated to GSE's prediction/data platform.
cells.G1221: No meaningful fit unless GSE builds an immersive VR viewing product; not a near-term application.

cells.C1222: Analysing Human Mobility Patterns of Hiking Activities through Complex Network Theory
cells.D1222: Analyzes GPS trajectories from hiking/tracking apps using complex weighted network theory to identify trail crossing/trailhead network structure across seasons.
cells.E1222: Constructs a trail network from overlapping trajectories and analyzes its topology with network-science metrics.
cells.F1222: Very low — outdoor recreation network analysis, no meaningful connection to GSE's competitive-sports prediction domain.
cells.G1222: No strong application; tangential at best as an example of extracting network structure from geolocated activity-tracking data.

cells.D1223: Compares statistical signatures of record-progression across sports, games, biological evolution, and technology, finding sports/games improve slowest and show 'bursty' record-breaking, with a deep-dive on marathon running.
cells.E1223: Cross-domain statistical comparison of improvement rate, burstiness, and acceleration in record-setting time series.
cells.F1223: Moderate — directly informs how GSE should model 'ceiling' improvement rates and expect bursty rather than smooth performance trends in sports time-series forecasting.
cells.G1223: Use the 'burstiness' metric from this paper to flag when a team/player's recent performance surge is statistically consistent with a genuine step-change versus a normal bursty fluctuation, informing confidence adjustments.

cells.C1224: Cross-label Suppression: A Discriminative and Fast Dictionary Learning with Group Regularization
cells.D1224: Proposes an efficient dictionary-learning method for image classification using cross-label suppression, tested across six datasets including a sport action categorization dataset.
cells.E1224: Structured dictionary learning with group regularization avoiding costly ℓ0/ℓ1 sparse coding, improving speed and discriminative power.
cells.F1224: Very low — a general-purpose image classification method; sports data is just one of many incidental benchmark datasets.
cells.G1224: No direct application to GSE's core stack; only a generic ML-efficiency technique of possible use in unrelated future CV work.

cells.C1225: Deep 360 Pilot: Learning a Deep Agent for Piloting through 360 Sports Video
cells.D1225: Trains a policy-gradient RL agent to automatically select the best viewing angle when watching 360-degree sports videos, evaluated on a new 5-domain 360-sports dataset.
cells.E1225: Policy-gradient RL jointly optimizing viewing-angle accuracy, transition smoothness, and foreground-object focus.
cells.F1225: Very low — 360-video viewing automation, unrelated to GSE's prediction/data core; only conceivably relevant to a future immersive content product.
cells.G1225: No strong near-term fit; tangential inspiration only if GSE later builds automated video content curation tools.

cells.C1226: Quantifying the relation between performance and success in soccer
cells.D1226: Analyzes 6,000+ games/10M events across six European leagues to show a team's final ranking correlates strongly with in-game technical performance, and simulates season outcomes from performance data alone (excluding goals).
cells.E1226: Extracts technical performance features from event data, trains an ML model on past seasons, then simulates whole-season rankings and compares to actual standings.
cells.F1226: Directly relevant — a strong precedent showing performance-based features (not just outcomes) can simulate accurate standings, useful validation methodology for GSE's own backtesting against real season outcomes.
cells.G1226: Adopt this paper's 'simulate an entire season from features, excluding realized outcomes' methodology as an additional backtest layer to stress-test GSE's model beyond single-game MAE, closer to a full-season calibration check.

cells.C1227: Audio-based performance evaluation of squash players
cells.D1227: Builds a framework that uses characteristic sound patterns in a squash court to classify shot type, localize position, and estimate ball speed/precision.
cells.E1227: Acoustic event classification and localization from court-installed audio sensors, feeding derived shot-quality metrics.
cells.F1227: Low — a niche sensor-based sport-specific system; only tangential if GSE expands into wearable/IoT sports data ingestion beyond public feeds.
cells.G1227: Not a strong fit for GSE's current free-data-driven stack; at most inspiration for future proprietary sensor-data partnerships.

cells.C1228: Distant Supervision for Topic Classification of Tweets in Curated Streams
cells.D1228: Uses topically-focused curated Twitter streams (including sports) as a distant-supervision signal to train topic classifiers that generalize to noisier, topically-diffuse streams.
cells.E1228: Semi-automatic identification of topically pure curated streams provides free labels for training classifiers that adapt to topic drift.
cells.F1228: Adjacent — a low-cost method for building sports-topic classifiers from existing curated content, useful for GSE's social-media monitoring/content pipeline without manual labeling.
cells.G1228: Use curated sports-news Twitter accounts as free distant-supervision labels to train a classifier that automatically routes scraped social content into GSE's brand-safe content categories.

cells.C1229: Boosting with Structural Sparsity: A Differential Inclusion Approach
cells.D1229: Proposes Split LBI, a boosting-type algorithm with structural sparsity control that outperforms generalized Lasso, demonstrated on partial-order ranking of sport teams.
cells.E1229: Variable-splitting Linearized Bregman Iteration producing a regularization path with theoretical model-selection consistency guarantees.
cells.F1229: Relevant to GSE's ensemble/calibration modeling — a rigorous sparse regression method applicable to ranking sport teams from noisy crowdsourced or model data, with stronger theoretical guarantees than standard Lasso.
cells.G1229: Apply Split LBI to sparsely regularize GSE's ensemble weights across many candidate sub-models, automatically pruning weak per-sport models while retaining path-consistency guarantees during calibration.

cells.C1230: A Hierarchical Bayesian Model of Pitch Framing
cells.D1230: Introduces a Bayesian hierarchical model estimating each MLB umpire's strike-call probability adjusted for pitch context, isolating catcher framing effects and translating them into runs saved.
cells.E1230: Bayesian hierarchical logistic model with player/umpire/context random effects, followed by a spatial run-value translation metric.
cells.F1230: Directly relevant — a rigorous, calibrated Bayesian hierarchical modeling template exactly matching GSE's need for independent per-sport probability models with proper uncertainty quantification.
cells.G1230: Adapt this hierarchical Bayesian framing-effect methodology to isolate and quantify hidden 'referee/officiating bias' effects across GSE's covered sports, adding a bias-correction layer to the prediction engine.

cells.C1231: A PageRank Model for Player Performance Assessment in Basketball, Soccer and Hockey
cells.D1231: Adapts Google's PageRank to rate individual player contributions to successful plays across three sports using a node/arc graph of in-game events.
cells.E1231: Builds a per-game player-node graph with sport-specific event arcs (passes, turnovers, goals) and computes a PageRank vector for player ranking.
cells.F1231: Relevant — a cross-sport, generalizable graph-based ranking method that fits GSE's need for per-sport probability/ranking models and could feed the Intelligence Graph's typed relational structure.
cells.G1231: Use the PageRank-on-event-graph approach as a generic 'flow value' metric applied consistently across GSE's covered sports, providing a uniform interpretable feature for the ensemble regardless of sport-specific data availability.

cells.C1232: Combining Lexical and Syntactic Features for Detecting Content-dense Texts in News
cells.D1232: Trains a classifier to detect whether news articles (including sports) are 'content-dense' (factual/succinct) versus not, finding about half of news text isn't content-dense.
cells.E1232: Two-layer classifier combining lexical and unlexicalized syntactic features, trained on heuristically labeled data and evaluated against human annotations.
cells.F1232: Adjacent to GSE's brand-language enforcement — a content-density classifier could help enforce the 'math you can read' concise, factual tone in automated content generation.
cells.G1232: Repurpose the content-density classifier as an automated style-lint check ensuring GSE's generated pick summaries stay information-dense rather than padded, reinforcing brand voice at scale.

cells.C1233: Learning from Noisy Labels with Distillation
cells.D1233: Proposes a distillation framework using a small clean dataset and knowledge-graph label relations to robustly learn from noisy labels, introducing new benchmark datasets including a Sports domain.
cells.E1233: Combines a clean 'teacher' subset with knowledge-graph relations to distill robust classifiers from large noisily-labeled datasets.
cells.F1233: Relevant to GSE's data pipeline — since scraped/free sports data is inherently noisy, this distillation framework offers a principled way to combine small trusted data with large noisy scraped data.
cells.G1233: Use knowledge-graph label relations (analogous to GSE's future Intelligence Graph) plus a small verified dataset to distill cleaner labels out of noisy multi-source scraped sports data automatically.

cells.C1234: A Survey on Content-Aware Video Analysis for Sports
cells.D1234: Surveys a decade of content-aware sports video analysis techniques, organizing them by object-, event-, and context-oriented approaches and identifying trends/challenges.
cells.E1234: Structured literature survey with a content-hierarchy model for categorizing sports video analysis research.
cells.F1234: Low-moderate — useful background survey only if GSE expands into video-based content analysis; not directly applicable to its current statistical/text/odds pipeline.
cells.G1234: Use the survey's content hierarchy taxonomy as a planning reference if GSE later builds automated video highlight or broadcast-analysis features.

cells.C1235: Progress Estimation and Phase Detection for Sequential Processes
cells.D1235: Introduces a multimodal deep-learning system estimating process completeness and phase in real time, validated on both medical trauma resuscitation and Olympic swimming events.
cells.E1235: Multimodal deep regression with a novel rectified-tanh activation and conditional loss, combined with Gaussian mixture phase prediction.
cells.F1235: Moderate — the underlying real-time progress/phase-estimation technique could inform live in-game state tracking (e.g. estimating 'how far along' a game is for live-odds features).
cells.G1235: Adapt the completeness-estimation approach to build a live 'time-remaining-adjusted win probability' feature for in-play picks, updating confidence as the game phase progresses.

cells.C1236: Sports stars: analyzing the performance of astronomers at visualization-based discovery
cells.D1236: Applies sports performance-analysis software (SportsCode) to study how expert astronomers visually distinguish real signals from noise in spectral data cubes.
cells.E1236: Repurposes timeline-based sports coaching/annotation software as a visual notebook for cross-domain expert behavior analysis.
cells.F1236: Weak stretch — a cross-domain borrowing of sports analytics tooling for an unrelated science use case, only tangentially useful as an example of sports-analytics software's general applicability.
cells.G1236: Flip the direction: use expert-annotation/coaching workflows like this to build an internal 'coach the model' interface where domain experts annotate GSE's mispredicted picks for retraining, borrowing SportsCode's timeline UX pattern.

cells.C1237: Similarities between GSH, Hypoplasticity and KCR
cells.D1237: Compares three constitutive models (GSH, hypoplasticity, KCR) for granular media elasto-plastic and flow behavior, showing GSH provides a physics-grounded foundation for the others.
cells.E1237: Theoretical derivation showing correspondences between a hydrodynamic theory and empirically-derived granular material models.
cells.F1237: None substantive — pure granular-media physics; 'sporting' in the abstract is incidental wordplay, not a sports-analytics connection.
cells.G1237: No honest application to GSE beyond noting the coincidental keyword match; not worth pursuing.

cells.C1238: How often does the best team win? A unified approach to understanding randomness in North American sport
cells.D1238: Builds Bayesian state-space models using betting-market data, applied uniformly across NFL/NHL/NBA/MLB, to estimate team strength, variability, and home advantage, and to compare cross-sport randomness/competitiveness.
cells.E1238: Bayesian state-space modeling of latent team strength dynamics inferred from historical betting odds across multiple sports and seasons.
cells.F1238: Extremely relevant — a near-exact precedent for GSE's stated goal of independent per-sport probability models using betting-market data, directly informing both the calibration gate and closing-line-value benchmarking.
cells.G1238: Adopt this paper's cross-sport Bayesian state-space architecture as the backbone for GSE's per-sport ensemble, using its home-advantage and strength-variance parameters as built-in, principled components of the calibration fix.

cells.C1239: The Medial Axis of a Multi-Layered Environment and its Application as a Navigation Mesh
cells.D1239: Extends medial-axis navigation mesh computation to 3D multi-layered walkable environments like sports stadiums, enabling efficient real-time pathfinding for crowd simulation.
cells.E1239: Geometric algorithm computing a navigation mesh over projected distances in multi-storey environments, enabling millisecond-scale path planning.
cells.F1239: Very low — a computational geometry / game-pathfinding paper; sports stadiums are just an example environment type, unrelated to GSE's prediction platform.
cells.G1239: Could be repurposed if Galaxy Dynasty ever includes navigable 3D venue environments for its persistent web game, providing efficient pathfinding for in-game characters.

cells.C1240: Uncovering the Spatiotemporal Patterns of Collective Social Activity
cells.D1240: Proposes a Spatial Dirichlet Hawkes Process to automatically cluster streaming geolocated social media posts (including sporting events) into distinctive spatiotemporal activity patterns.
cells.E1240: Online sequential Monte Carlo inference for a spatiotemporal point-process clustering model, scaling to millions of posts.
cells.F1240: Adjacent — the underlying Hawkes-process clustering technique is a plausible tool for detecting emergent social buzz/event clusters around sports games in real time, feeding social-content automation.
cells.G1240: Use a Spatial Dirichlet Hawkes Process to auto-detect when social chatter around a specific game/team is spiking in a distinctive pattern, triggering GSE's automated content generation to react in near real time.

cells.C1241: ActionFlowNet: Learning Motion Representation for Action Recognition
cells.D1241: Proposes a multitask CNN jointly estimating optical flow and recognizing actions from raw video, improving accuracy over hand-crafted flow features, evaluated partly on Sport-1M-scale data.
cells.E1241: Single-stream CNN trained end-to-end on a joint optical-flow-estimation and action-classification objective.
cells.F1241: Very low — a generic video action-recognition architecture using sports video merely as a large training corpus, not connected to GSE's statistical modeling needs.
cells.G1241: No meaningful GSE application; only relevant background if GSE later pursues video-based automated highlight tagging.

cells.D1242: Introduces a probabilistic theory of 'selection' processes showing selected extreme values converge to universal limiting distributions, supported by data from biology, agriculture, and sport.
cells.E1242: Derives universality classes and scaling exponents for selected (not just extreme) values based on the tail thickness of the underlying distribution.
cells.F1242: Moderate stretch — offers rigorous statistical theory for how 'selected' outcomes (e.g. only published/notable picks) can differ systematically from the underlying population, relevant to survivorship-bias concerns in evaluating settled picks.
cells.G1242: Apply this selection theory to check whether GSE's published/highlighted picks suffer from a selection-bias skew relative to the full population of scored predictions, which would distort perceived calibration.

cells.C1243: Domain Adaptation for Named Entity Recognition in Online Media with Word Embeddings
cells.D1243: Proposes methods to adapt NER models trained on news to other domains like Sports and Finance using distributed word representations, capturing domain-specific semantics.
cells.E1243: Word-embedding-based domain adaptation techniques combining global and domain-specific semantic representations for NER transfer.
cells.F1243: Relevant to GSE's data-ingestion pipeline — improved entity recognition (player/team names) in scraped, noisy sports text sources directly supports data extraction reliability.
cells.G1243: Use domain-adapted NER to more reliably parse player/team entities out of messy scraped sources like Pro-Football-Reference or news feeds, reducing pipeline breakage from naming variants and abbreviations.

cells.C1244: Spatio-Temporal Movements in Team Sports: A Visualization approach using Motion Charts
cells.D1244: Proposes using GoogleVis motion charts to visualize player trajectory data for basketball, aiding preliminary exploratory analysis of team movement patterns.
cells.E1244: Applies an existing R visualization tool (motion charts) to spatio-temporal trajectory data as an exploratory analysis aid.
cells.F1244: Low — a visualization convenience tool, tangential unless GSE builds internal analyst dashboards for exploring tracking data.
cells.G1244: Could inspire an internal analyst-facing 'replay explorer' dashboard for visually auditing why a given pick's model inputs behaved unexpectedly.

cells.D1245: Uses 3D CNN spatiotemporal features (C3D) with SVR/LSTM regression to automatically score Olympic diving, vault, and figure-skating performances from video, on a small dataset.
cells.E1245: C3D feature extraction followed by SVR and/or LSTM regression to predict a continuous judged 'action quality' score.
cells.F1245: Low-moderate — a specialized video-based scoring system for individual/artistic sports, only tangential to GSE's team-sport-focused, odds-driven prediction engine.
cells.G1245: Could be adapted to automatically pre-score gymnastics/figure-skating-style events if GSE ever expands its coverage beyond traditional team sports into judged individual sports.

cells.D1246: Generalizes topic modeling theory to complex document distributions (using sports as an illustrative topic), directly learning document classifiers with provable guarantees rather than explicit topic distributions.
cells.E1246: Theoretical framework generalizing standard topic models to non-i.i.d. word generation, learning classifiers with sample-complexity and noise-tolerance guarantees.
cells.F1246: Low — primarily theoretical NLP/learning-theory work using sports only as an illustrative topic example, tangential to GSE's applied needs.
cells.G1246: Could inform building a more theoretically robust sports-vs-other-topic content classifier for GSE's brand-safety content filtering, leveraging its noise-tolerance guarantees.

cells.C1247: Analysis of Tourism Dynamics and Special Events through Mobile Phone Metadata
cells.D1247: Uses anonymized call detail records to evaluate tourism strategies and the impact of special events, including sports competitions, on visitor flows and revenue in Andorra.
cells.E1247: Extracts spatial/temporal tourist-flow indicators from telecom metadata to evaluate event impact and marketing effectiveness.
cells.F1247: Low — an economic-impact analytics application unrelated to GSE's prediction/calibration problems.
cells.G1247: Tangential inspiration only for a hypothetical B2B analytics product measuring economic impact of sporting events, outside GSE's current scope.

cells.C1248: Exercise Motion Classification from Large-Scale Wearable Sensor Data Using Convolutional Neural Networks
cells.D1248: Classifies 50 gym exercises from forearm-worn wearable sensor data by formatting time-series as images and applying CNNs, achieving 92.1% accuracy.
cells.E1248: Converts accelerometer/orientation time-series into image representations for CNN-based classification, comparing architectures.
cells.F1248: Low — a wearable fitness-classification study unrelated to GSE's data-driven forecasting/odds platform.
cells.G1248: Not a strong fit; only tangential if GSE later ingests personal fitness wearable data for a health/fantasy-sports crossover feature.

cells.C1249: Edge Based Grid Super-Imposition for Crowd Emotion Recognition
cells.D1249: Detects spontaneous group emotion from video using edge detection and grid superimposition, tested on crowds watching sports events, achieving 70.9% accuracy.
cells.E1249: Edge-based feature extraction with grid overlay tracking, feeding a crowd emotion classifier robust to occlusion.
cells.F1249: Low — crowd emotion recognition from video, unrelated to GSE's statistical data pipeline.
cells.G1249: Tangential only; could inspire a future 'fan sentiment from broadcast crowd shots' feature for content generation, not a near-term priority.

cells.C1250: Measuring and Modelling Crowd Flows - Fusing Stationary and Tracking Data
cells.D1250: Fuses RFID split-time data and smartphone GPS traces using a macroscopic traffic-flow model to detect congestion and estimate crowd density/speed at marathons in real time.
cells.E1250: First-order macroscopic flow model with a triangular fundamental diagram, fusing two heterogeneous real-time data sources, validated via simulation.
cells.F1250: Moderate — a strong methodological template for GSE's data pipeline: fusing multiple heterogeneous, imperfect real-time data sources (like odds feeds + scraped stats) into one coherent state estimate.
cells.G1250: Apply the multi-source data-fusion methodology (combining sparse 'stationary' checkpoints with continuous 'floating' traces) as a design pattern for reconciling GSE's odds-feed data with scraped play-by-play data into one unified live game-state model.

cells.C1251: A Rotation Invariant Latent Factor Model for Moveme Discovery from Static Poses
cells.D1251: Learns rotation-invariant 3D pose basis 'movemes' from 2D projected poses in sports images (Leeds Sports Dataset), enabling activity classification and motion synthesis from a single frame.
cells.E1251: Data-driven latent factor model recovering 3D basis poses from multiple 2D viewing angles without hand-designed features.
cells.F1251: Low — a computer-vision pose-representation study, tangential unless GSE processes sports imagery directly.
cells.G1251: Not a strong near-term fit for GSE's odds/stats-centric stack; only relevant background if a future video/image analytics feature emerges.

cells.C1252: The Inverse Gamma Distribution and Benford's Law
cells.D1252: Studies how closely the inverse gamma distribution follows Benford's Law as its parameters vary, noting Benford's Law's use in detecting match-fixing in competitive sports.
cells.E1252: Analytical/numerical study of leading-digit distribution conformance to Benford's Law under parameter variation.
cells.F1252: Relevant to GSE's anomaly-detection needs — Benford's Law is a concrete, cheap statistical test for detecting suspicious/manipulated data patterns, directly applicable to spotting match-fixing or data-integrity anomalies.
cells.G1252: Add a Benford's-Law leading-digit check as a lightweight automated anomaly detector on incoming odds/line-movement data to flag potential match-fixing or data-corruption signals before they reach the prediction engine.

cells.C1253: A short review and primer on multimodal psychophysiological applications in HCI
cells.D1253: Reviews methods for aggregating multiple physiological signals (e.g. heart rate, skin conductance) into classifiers of cognitive/affective states for human-computer interaction, distinguishing work applications from sports/clinical uses.
cells.E1253: Survey of multimodal physiological signal classification pipelines and machine learning techniques for state inference.
cells.F1253: Very low — a general HCI physiology survey; sports is mentioned only to be excluded as the focus, no direct GSE relevance.
cells.G1253: No meaningful application to GSE's platform; not worth pursuing.

cells.C1254: Transferring Object-Scene Convolutional Neural Networks for Event Recognition in Still Images
cells.D1254: Proposes a CNN combining object and scene recognition knowledge to classify events in images, achieving state-of-the-art results including on the UIUC Sports Event dataset.
cells.E1254: Multi-task transfer learning combining object- and scene-recognition CNNs with an iterative class-selection method to reduce overfitting.
cells.F1254: Low — a generic image event-classification method using a sports dataset as one of several benchmarks, not directly tied to GSE's statistical modeling.
cells.G1254: Could be useful only if GSE processes sports photography for automated content tagging, not a current priority.

cells.C1255: A short review and primer on electromyography in HCI applications
cells.D1255: Reviews how electromyography (EMG) signals are used in human-computer interaction to infer emotional valence and stress, distinguishing everyday HCI use from clinical/sports applications.
cells.E1255: Survey of EMG signal recording, processing, and interpretation techniques for affective computing.
cells.F1255: Very low — sports is mentioned only as an excluded use case in this general HCI survey; no direct GSE connection.
cells.G1255: No meaningful application to GSE's platform; not worth pursuing.

cells.C1256: Applying Deep Learning to Basketball Trajectories
cells.D1256: Uses recurrent neural networks on raw 3-point-shot trajectory sequences (20,000+ shots from NBA SportVu data) to predict shot success, outperforming a feature-rich static ML baseline.
cells.E1256: Sequence model (RNN) learning shot success directly from positional trajectory data, without hand-engineered physics features.
cells.F1256: Directly relevant — a concrete precedent that sequence-based deep learning can beat feature-engineered baselines on real sports tracking data, informing GSE's search for genuinely better forecasting methods beyond its underperforming core model.
cells.G1256: Apply the 'let the sequence model learn dynamics directly from raw data' philosophy to GSE's core forecasting model, replacing some hand-engineered features with sequence-learned representations from raw play-by-play event streams.

cells.C1257: Keep it SMPL: Automatic Estimation of 3D Human Pose and Shape from a Single Image
cells.D1257: Fits a statistical 3D body shape model (SMPL) to 2D detected joints from a single image, evaluated on the Leeds Sports dataset among others, achieving state-of-the-art pose accuracy.
cells.E1257: Bottom-up 2D joint detection (DeepCut) combined with top-down fitting of a population-informed statistical body-shape model via objective minimization.
cells.F1257: Very low — a computer-vision pose-estimation method, using Leeds Sports only as one evaluation dataset, unrelated to GSE's statistical prediction pipeline.
cells.G1257: Not a strong fit for GSE's current stack; only tangential if a future video-based scouting/analysis feature is built.

cells.C1258: Tie-breaker: Using language models to quantify gender bias in sports journalism
cells.D1258: Uses a language-model-based method to quantify differences in question framing between male and female tennis players in post-match interviews, finding male players get more game-focused questions.
cells.E1258: Language-model-based comparative analysis of question style/content, with fine-grained breakdowns by question type, outcome, and player rank.
cells.F1258: Directly relevant to GSE's NLP style-control and brand-language enforcement needs — a proven quantitative method for auditing systematic bias/tone patterns in sports-related generated or curated text.
cells.G1258: Repurpose this bias-quantification methodology as an internal audit tool checking GSE's own automated content/commentary for unintended systematic framing bias across teams, players, or demographics before publishing.

cells.C1259: Protocol for an Observational Study on the Effects of Playing High School Football on Later Life Cognitive Functioning and Mental Health
cells.D1259: Proposes a retrospective observational study design comparing 1,153 former high school football players to non-players on later-life cognitive and mental health outcomes, with sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding.
cells.E1259: Matching and model-based covariate adjustment plus an ordered testing procedure with formal sensitivity analysis for causal inference from observational data.
cells.F1259: Relevant methodologically — a rigorous template for causal inference under confounding using observational sports data, directly applicable to strengthening the causal-inference rigor behind GSE's CEPT-based claims.
cells.G1259: Adopt this paper's sensitivity-analysis-for-unmeasured-confounding framework as a check on any causal claims GSE's CEPT-based ensemble makes about factors driving pick outcomes, guarding against overconfident causal interpretations.

cells.D1260: Introduces a Bayesian hierarchical model built in PyMC3 to estimate team strengths and predict scores for the 2014 Six Nations rugby tournament, as a probabilistic-programming tutorial.
cells.E1260: Hierarchical Bayesian model (implemented via probabilistic programming) estimating latent team attack/defense strength parameters to predict match scores.
cells.F1260: Directly relevant — a hands-on precedent for exactly the kind of Bayesian hierarchical, per-sport probabilistic model GSE needs for its calibration fix, implementable with existing open-source tooling.
cells.G1260: Use PyMC3-style hierarchical Bayesian models as rapid-prototyping scaffolding to test candidate per-sport probability models before committing engineering resources to a production TypeScript/Prisma implementation.

cells.C1261: Leveraging Contextual Cues for Generating Basketball Highlights
cells.D1261: Automatically generates basketball highlight reels by ranking plays using contextual excitement cues from play-by-play stats alongside audio-visual signals, matching ESPN-quality highlights in user studies.
cells.E1261: Combines video/audio cues with contextual play-by-play excitement data to rank and select highlight-worthy moments, validated with a new 25-game NCAA dataset.
cells.F1261: Directly relevant to GSE's automated content generation ambitions — a validated method for turning structured play-by-play data (which GSE already ingests) into automatically ranked highlight-worthy content.
cells.G1261: Reuse the play-by-play excitement-ranking logic (without needing video) to auto-select which of GSE's graded picks are most 'highlight-worthy' for automated social posts, prioritizing content generation around the most compelling outcomes.

cells.C1262: Generative Models for Global Collaboration Relationships
cells.D1262: Proposes GeneSCs, a generative algorithm building simplicial complexes for collaboration networks (co-authorship, movie crews, teams) via preferential attachment on facet degree rather than node degree.
cells.E1262: Grows a hypergraph/simplicial-complex model facet-by-facet using data-driven facet-size distributions and preferential attachment to reproduce real-world collaboration structures.
cells.F1262: A stretch, but the facet-based network-growth mechanism is a plausible primitive for GSE's planned Intelligence Graph, which needs typed multi-entity (team/player/game) relationships beyond simple pairwise graphs.
cells.G1262: Use the facet-degree preferential-attachment idea to model which player/coach/team combinations co-occur in winning contexts, surfacing 'collaboration clusters' as a novel feature for the ensemble model.

cells.C1263: Universal temporal features of rankings in competitive sports and games
cells.D1263: Finds that 'rank diversity' over time follows the same universal functional form across many sports, games, and even languages, suggesting shared mechanisms of hierarchy formation.
cells.E1263: Statistical analysis of how often entities occupy a given rank over time, comparing rank-diversity curves across systems to find a universal law.
cells.F1263: Directly useful for GSE's ranking/rating components across NFL/MLB/MLS: a universal rank-turnover model could inform how quickly team/player rankings should be expected to shift, aiding calibration windows.
cells.G1263: Use rank-diversity as a diagnostic: if a sport's rank turnover deviates from the universal curve, flag it as needing its own per-sport probability model rather than the shared ensemble.

cells.C1264: Fairly Random: The Impact of Winning the Toss on the Probability of Winning
cells.D1264: Analyzing 44,224 cricket matches, finds winning the coin toss raises win probability by ~2.8%, varying by team parity and playing conditions.
cells.E1264: Large-sample empirical regression estimating a small causal covariate's effect on match outcome probability.
cells.F1264: A close analog for GSE: shows how to quantify small but real edge factors (like coin tosses) that could be folded into sport-specific probability models to close the Brier/ECE calibration gap.
cells.G1264: Build a 'micro-edge' catalog (weather, home-field, rest days, toss-equivalents per sport) each individually weak but summable, then feed as engineered features into the per-sport ensemble.

cells.D1265: Develops a Bayesian nonparametric method for estimating quantiles directly, extended hierarchically to subpopulations, validated on sports statistics data.
cells.E1265: Uses Hausdorff base measures within a Bayesian framework to place priors directly on quantiles rather than the full distribution, enabling hierarchical pooling across subgroups.
cells.F1265: Directly applicable to GSE's push for independent per-sport probability models: a hierarchical quantile model could let each sport share statistical strength while retaining sport-specific tails, improving calibration.
cells.G1265: Apply hierarchical quantile pooling to 'bootstrap mode' — instead of blanket confidence caps under sparse data, borrow quantile strength from related leagues/seasons to right-size uncertainty per bucket.

cells.C1266: A Supervised Learning Algorithm for Binary Domain Classification of Web Queries using SERPs
cells.D1266: Classifies web search queries as 'scholar' vs 'non-scholar' domain by examining search-engine result page features, achieving 0.809 precision.
cells.E1266: Trains a classifier on SERP-derived features (using Google as an oracle) to route queries to specialized vs general sources.
cells.F1266: A stretch, but the query-routing/classification technique is loosely relevant to GSE's data-ingestion pipeline, e.g. classifying scraped web content by sport/domain before ingestion.
cells.G1266: Repurpose the SERP-feature classifier idea to auto-tag scraped free sports data sources by reliability/domain before they enter the pipeline, reducing manual curation.

cells.C1267: The Market for English Premier League (EPL) Odds
cells.D1267: Uses a Skellam process on real-time betting odds to estimate teams' scoring rates and derive an implied volatility measure that updates dynamically during EPL matches.
cells.E1267: Fits scoring-rate parameters from market odds matrices and re-estimates them in real time as in-game events (goals, cards) occur, producing a live 'implied volatility' signal.
cells.F1267: Directly relevant to GSE's closing-line-value benchmark and live-odds ingestion — offers a concrete method to back out market-implied probabilities dynamically from The Odds API feeds.
cells.G1267: Use the Skellam-process implied-volatility signal as a real-time trigger for GSE's bootstrap-mode confidence caps, tightening or loosening confidence as market volatility spikes mid-game.

cells.C1268: Semi-supervised and Unsupervised Methods for Categorizing Posts in Web Discussion Forums
cells.D1268: Proposes HMM-based unsupervised/semi-supervised methods to classify forum posts (problem, solution, feedback, spam) across domains including sports, without heavy labeled data.
cells.E1268: Models post categories via Hidden Markov Models over word and part-of-speech sequences, requiring minimal or no labeled training data.
cells.F1268: A stretch for GSE's core engine, but directly useful for their planned automated social/media content generation and brand-language enforcement — could classify/filter user or generated posts cheaply.
cells.G1268: Adapt the low-label HMM classifier to auto-flag generated marketing copy that drifts into banned 'AI-powered' language, as a lightweight pre-publish lint check.

cells.C1269: Analyzing In-Game Movements of Soccer Players at Scale
cells.D1269: Derives player movement/physical-performance profiles from event-based (not tracking-camera) soccer data across 50+ leagues, enabling player similarity and consistency metrics at scale.
cells.E1269: Reconstructs movement characteristics from cheap event logs instead of expensive tracking systems, then computes similarity scores between players.
cells.F1269: Directly relevant to GSE's data-ingestion pipeline: shows how to extract rich physical/performance features from freely available event data (like Pro-Football-Reference-style sources) without costly tracking feeds.
cells.G1269: Build a 'replacement player' similarity index from event-derived movement profiles to power a B2B widget answering 'who plays like X' for fantasy/DFS audiences.

cells.C1270: Adjusting for Scorekeeper Bias in NBA Box Scores
cells.D1270: Quantifies systematic bias and generosity of individual NBA scorekeepers in recording subjective stats (assists, blocks), then corrects season totals using contextual tracking data.
cells.E1270: Fits statistical models isolating scorekeeper identity effects from true player performance, then debiases box-score totals.
cells.F1270: Directly relevant to GSE's data pipeline reliability: subjective/noisy labels in scraped box scores are exactly the kind of systematic bias that could be silently corrupting features feeding the prediction engine, worsening calibration.
cells.G1270: Build an automated 'source bias' detector across GSE's multi-source scraped data (comparing the same event as reported by different providers) to flag and correct systematic recording biases before ingestion.

cells.C1271: Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Team Sports -- A Survey
cells.D1271: Surveys computational research extracting insight from high-frequency spatio-temporal player-tracking data across invasion sports (football, basketball, hockey).
cells.E1271: Categorizes existing techniques (trajectory clustering, formation detection, event recognition) applied to player/ball tracking data into a coherent taxonomy.
cells.F1271: A useful reference map for GSE's longer-horizon ambitions (Intelligence Graph, richer sport features) even though GSE currently uses free/event data rather than tracking feeds.
cells.G1271: Use the survey's taxonomy of spatio-temporal features as a roadmap for which cheap event-based proxies (from item 1603.05583) could approximate expensive tracking-derived signals.

cells.C1272: Compact Flow Diagrams for State Sequences
cells.D1272: Introduces algorithms to compactly summarize large sets of state sequences as a small flow diagram, proving hardness results and heuristics, applied to football tactical analysis.
cells.E1272: Formulates minimal flow-diagram construction as a combinatorial optimization problem (W[1]-hard in general) and provides heuristics that scale to real datasets.
cells.F1272: A stretch for core calibration work, but the sequence-summarization technique could help GSE visualize/compress pick lifecycle state transitions (proposed→modeled→published→graded→settled) for debugging pipeline issues.
cells.G1272: Apply flow-diagram summarization to visualize how picks move through GSE's BullMQ job-queue lifecycle, spotting bottlenecks or anomalous state loops at a glance.

cells.C1273: Footballonomics: The Anatomy of American Football; Evidence from 7 years of NFL game data
cells.D1273: Analyzes 7 seasons of NFL data to reject 'rational coaching' hypotheses (PAT/4th-down decisions) and builds a logistic-regression-based NFL game prediction engine achieving ~63% accuracy.
cells.E1273: Uses logistic regression on game-level factors (turnovers, possession time, penalties) plus bootstrap resampling to build a lightweight prediction model, benchmarked against expert analysts.
cells.F1273: Highly relevant: a directly comparable NFL prediction engine and evaluation methodology GSE can benchmark its own MAE-losing model against, and a source of concrete features to test.
cells.G1273: Use this paper's specific factor set (turnovers, possession time, penalty yards) as a minimal 'naive-plus' baseline stronger than GSE's current naive baseline, to diagnose exactly where their model underperforms.

cells.C1274: Determining Tournament Payout Structures for Daily Fantasy Sports
cells.D1274: Formalizes and solves the problem of algorithmically generating appealing, succinct DFS tournament payout structures at scale (100,000+ winners) using DP, integer programming, and heuristics.
cells.E1274: Treats payout-structure design as a constrained optimization problem and evaluates dynamic programming, integer programming, and heuristic algorithms for scalability.
cells.F1274: A stretch relative to GSE's calibration/prediction blockers, but directly relevant to the persistent web game (Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR) ambition, which will need fair, scalable prize/payout structures.
cells.G1274: Apply the heuristic payout-structure algorithm to design tiered reward structures for Galaxy Dynasty's leaderboard payouts, balancing appeal against structural complexity.

cells.C1275: Hot Hands, Streaks and Coin-flips: Numerical Nonsense in the New York Times
cells.D1275: A critique showing how New York Times coverage misrepresented statistical work on 'hot hand'/streak phenomena in sports and gambling, clarifying the actual probability concepts involved.
cells.E1275: Pedagogical statistical debunking, contrasting naive streak intuitions with correct probability calculations (e.g. conditional probability in coin-flip sequences).
cells.F1275: Directly relevant as a cautionary reference for GSE's public accuracy communications — a reminder to avoid overclaiming 'hot streak' effects that aren't statistically real, tying into their strict brand/lint accuracy rules.
cells.G1275: Use this paper's examples as internal training material for GSE's content-generation system, teaching it to avoid manufacturing false 'hot streak' narratives in auto-generated commentary.

cells.D1276: Reviews principles of optimal basketball strategy: allocative efficiency, dynamic (shot-clock) efficiency, and risk/reward tradeoffs in shot selection, with analytical models for each.
cells.E1276: Surveys game-theoretic and statistical models formalizing basketball decision problems (e.g. optimal shot allocation, variance-seeking under adversity) with worked analytical examples.
cells.F1276: Directly relevant to sports-specific probability modeling GSE needs (per-sport models for basketball), providing domain theory that could inform NBA-specific feature engineering distinct from a global model.
cells.G1276: Encode the risk/reward tradeoff framework as an underdog-detection feature: teams facing unfavorable win probability should show measurably higher-variance play calling, useful as a leading indicator in live win-probability updates.

cells.C1277: How the medium shapes the message: Printing and the rise of the arts and sciences
cells.D1277: Uses a city's distance to Mainz as an instrument to show early printing-press adoption predicts higher rates of producing famous scientists/artists, and later media (radio/TV) correlate with sports/performing fame.
cells.E1277: Causal-inference instrumental-variable design linking communication-technology adoption to downstream fame/output records across history.
cells.F1277: A real stretch for GSE's technical blockers, but tangentially relevant to their planned automated media/content generation — illustrates how media technology shapes what gets recorded and celebrated.
cells.G1277: Use the paper's framing to design GSE's content strategy: media format itself (short video vs. long article) will shape which 'stars' the automated content system elevates, suggesting deliberate format diversification.

cells.C1278: TennisVid2Text: Fine-grained Descriptions for Domain Specific Videos
cells.D1278: Generates rich, human-like textual commentary for tennis broadcast video clips by combining low-level video action analysis with a large corpus of scraped human-written descriptions.
cells.E1278: Domain-specific video captioning pipeline combining computer vision action recognition with retrieval/adaptation from human-authored sports commentary corpora.
cells.F1278: Directly relevant to GSE's automated social/media content generation ambition — a template for generating readable, sport-specific commentary text rather than generic captions.
cells.G1278: Adapt the domain-specific commentary generation approach to auto-narrate GSE picks ('why the model favors X') in natural sports-commentary style, reinforcing the 'math you can read' brand voice.

cells.C1279: Seasonal Linear Predictivity in National Football Championships
cells.D1279: Shows that despite many confounders, football (soccer) team results across a season follow a roughly linear trend useful for prediction, tested on 707 teams across 22 divisions and 20 seasons.
cells.E1279: Applies linear regression to longitudinal team performance data across leagues, evaluating predictive power of simple linear trend models.
cells.F1279: Directly relevant as a simple, testable baseline for GSE's MLS/soccer prediction models — a linear in-season trend model could be a stronger baseline than their current naive one for that sport.
cells.G1279: Use seasonal linear predictivity as a diagnostic per-sport: sports/leagues where linear trend already predicts well may need less complex per-sport models, focusing ensemble effort elsewhere.

cells.C1280: Latent Dirichlet Allocation Based Organisation of Broadcast Media Archives for Deep Neural Network Adaptation
cells.D1280: Discovers latent 'genre' domains (including sports) within diverse broadcast media using LDA, then uses these to adapt DNN acoustic models for speech recognition, cutting error up to 13%.
cells.E1280: Unsupervised topic modeling (LDA) over broadcast content to find latent domains, encoded via unique binary codes to condition/adapt neural acoustic models.
cells.F1280: A stretch for GSE's core calibration work, but relevant to any future automated commentary/transcription features (e.g. transcribing broadcast audio as an additional free data source).
cells.G1280: Apply LDA-based latent-domain discovery to auto-cluster scraped sports articles/transcripts by sub-genre (recap, injury report, analysis) to route them to different NLP pipelines in content automation.

cells.C1281: A Scalable Framework for NBA Player and Team Comparisons Using Player Tracking Data
cells.D1281: Uses PCA to reduce high-dimensional NBA player tracking stats to four interpretable components explaining 68% of variance, then builds a similarity index (SDI) for player/team comparison.
cells.E1281: Dimensionality reduction (PCA) on player tracking data followed by a distance-based similarity metric for comparing statistical profiles.
cells.F1281: Directly relevant to GSE's ensemble/feature engineering: PCA-based dimensionality reduction could tame high-dimensional per-sport feature sets before feeding sport-specific probability models.
cells.G1281: Use the Statistical Diversity Index concept to power a B2B embeddable widget letting clients explore 'similar player/team' comparisons as a lightweight product beyond core picks.

cells.C1282: Mining Interesting Trivia for Entities from Wikipedia
cells.D1282: Builds a system that extracts and ranks 'interesting' trivia sentences about entities (movies, celebrities, sports) from Wikipedia to boost user engagement.
cells.E1282: Trains an interestingness ranker using domain-independent linguistic and entity-based features, leveraging existing user-generated trivia as weak supervision.
cells.F1282: A stretch for the prediction engine, but directly useful for GSE's automated content generation — auto-surfacing engaging trivia/context to accompany picks or the Intelligence Graph's entity pages.
cells.G1282: Feed GSE's Intelligence Graph typed entities (players, teams) through a similar interestingness ranker to auto-generate 'fun fact' sidebars alongside picks, boosting engagement without AI-marketing claims.

cells.C1283: Quality-Aware Coding and Relaying for 60 GHz Real-Time Wireless Video Broadcasting
cells.D1283: Designs an optimal video coding/relaying scheme for 60GHz wireless links broadcasting multi-camera sports stadium video feeds, formulated as convex programming.
cells.E1283: Splits a video source's data stream across multiple relays and jointly optimizes compression/routing via convex optimization to maximize overall video quality.
cells.F1283: Essentially unrelated to GSE's prediction/calibration stack; the sports-stadium setting is coincidental (broadcast engineering, not analytics).
cells.G1283: No direct product tie; at most, its convex multi-path optimization framing is a generic pattern that could inspire load-balancing logic in GSE's data-ingestion job queues.

cells.C1284: Environmental structure and competitive scoring advantages in team competitions
cells.D1284: Analyzes ~10 million online-game team competitions to show scoring dynamics/tempo follow a universal three-phase pattern also seen in real sports, driven by environmental structure rather than skill.
cells.E1284: Applies a generative scoring-dynamics model to large-scale online game data, quantifying how map/environment heterogeneity predicts tempo and balance.
cells.F1284: Tangentially relevant: suggests that structural/contextual features (venue, schedule) rather than only team skill drive scoring dynamics, reinforcing the case for per-sport/per-context probability models.
cells.G1284: Test whether GSE's picks systematically mis-calibrate in specific 'environmental' contexts (dome vs outdoor, back-to-back games) the way this paper finds environment-driven scoring advantages, as a calibration diagnostic.

cells.C1285: Robust Image Segmentation in Low Depth Of Field Images
cells.D1285: Proposes a parameterless algorithm to automatically segment the in-focus 'object of interest' in low-depth-of-field photos, applicable to macro/portrait/sports photography.
cells.E1285: Uses image sharpness cues to robustly separate foreground focus regions from blurred backgrounds without manual parameter tuning.
cells.F1285: A genuine stretch — pure computer-vision image segmentation with no connection to GSE's statistical/calibration stack.
cells.G1285: Only tangential: could help auto-crop scraped sports photos for social/media content generation, isolating the athlete for graphics without manual editing.

cells.C1286: Joint Scalable Coding and Routing for 60 GHz Real-Time Live HD Video Streaming Applications
cells.D1286: Extends prior 60GHz video-relay work by jointly optimizing route selection and compression rate across multiple relay scenarios for stadium video broadcasting, via mixed-integer convex programming.
cells.E1286: Formulates joint routing+coding as convex mixed-integer optimization across three relay-aggregation scenarios, solved for guaranteed-optimal video quality.
cells.F1286: Unrelated to GSE's analytics stack; another broadcast-engineering paper coincidentally set in a sports stadium.
cells.G1286: No meaningful product application beyond generic inspiration for optimizing GSE's own data pipeline resource allocation via similar convex formulations.

cells.C1287: TwitterPaul: Extracting and Aggregating Twitter Predictions
cells.D1287: Extracts and classifies football-game predictions from Twitter mentions during the 2010 World Cup, aggregates them, and shows resulting forecasts approach betting-line accuracy.
cells.E1287: NLP classification pipeline extracts prediction-type tweets, identifies accurate forecasters, and aggregates crowd predictions, benchmarked against prediction markets.
cells.F1287: Directly relevant to GSE's closing-line-value benchmark and could supplement sport-specific ensembles with a social-sentiment signal as an additional weak predictor to test against Brier/ECE targets.
cells.G1287: Build a 'crowd wisdom' auxiliary signal from social media predictions as one member of GSE's multiplicative-weight ensemble (CEPT), weighted dynamically based on historical forecaster accuracy.

cells.C1288: Records in stochastic processes -- Theory and applications
cells.D1288: Reviews the mathematical theory of record-breaking events (extremes) in both uncorrelated and correlated stochastic processes, including applications to sports and climate records.
cells.E1288: Surveys statistical distributions governing the rate and magnitude of new records in random walks and independent sequences, and their real-world validation.
cells.F1288: Tangentially relevant: record-statistics theory could inform how GSE's models should treat rare extreme outcomes (upsets, record performances) that stress-test calibration in the tails.
cells.G1288: Use record-statistics theory to build an 'extreme event' guardrail flagging picks involving statistically improbable record-breaking performances, routing them to bootstrap-mode confidence capping.

cells.C1289: EMMIX-uskew: An R Package for Fitting Mixtures of Multivariate Skew t-distributions via the EM Algorithm
cells.D1289: Describes an R package implementing closed-form EM algorithms for fitting unrestricted multivariate skew-t mixture models, validated partly on Australian Institute of Sport athlete data.
cells.E1289: Provides a closed-form EM algorithm for mixtures of multivariate skew t-distributions, handling heavy-tailed, asymmetric multivariate data better than restricted alternatives.
cells.F1289: Directly relevant to GSE's ensemble/calibration work: skew-t mixture models could better capture heavy-tailed, asymmetric prediction-error distributions than Gaussian assumptions, potentially improving Brier/ECE.
cells.G1289: Fit skew-t mixtures per sport to model residual error distributions, using divergence from a well-fit mixture as an automated trigger for flagging when a sport needs its own dedicated probability model.

cells.D1290: Detects geographically-localized emerging topics (including sports events) on Twitter using a neural-network-based time-series outlier detection method over location-tagged message volumes.
cells.E1290: Builds per-location time series of topic-word frequency and applies a neural network to flag statistical outliers signaling emergent local events.
cells.F1290: Relevant to GSE's data pipeline: an anomaly-detection technique applicable to monitoring live odds/data feeds for unusual spikes (e.g. breaking injury news) that should trigger re-modeling.
cells.G1290: Repurpose the location-based event detector to auto-flag social-media spikes around specific teams/players as an early-warning signal feeding into bootstrap-mode confidence adjustments.

cells.C1291: Optimal Weighting of Multi-View Data with Low Dimensional Hidden States
cells.D1291: Proposes an unsupervised algorithm to optimally weight noisy multi-view features (e.g. title/text/references) sharing a common low-dimensional latent state, for NLP tasks like topic classification.
cells.E1291: Derives closed-form optimal weights for combining multiple noisy 'views' of data generated from a shared low-dimensional hidden state (applicable to HMM/LDA-style models).
cells.F1291: Directly relevant to GSE's ensemble design: multiple noisy data sources (scraped stats, live odds, social signals) could be optimally weighted using this shared-latent-state framework before combination.
cells.G1291: Apply the multi-view weighting method to fuse GSE's disparate data sources (Odds API, scraped box scores, social sentiment) into a single denoised feature per pick, rather than naive concatenation.

cells.D1292: Models how a fixed upset probability propagates through single-elimination tournaments vs. round-robin leagues, showing tournaments are efficient-but-unfair and leagues fair-but-inefficient, then proposes a hybrid gradual-elimination format.
cells.E1292: Uses an elementary random-upset process to derive analytic scaling laws for how the probability of the weakest team winning depends on competition format (tournament vs league), validated against empirical sports data.
cells.F1292: Directly relevant to GSE's calibration and market-efficiency goals: quantifies exactly how much noise/upset-probability format structure injects into outcomes, which bears on interpreting Brier scores and closing-line value differently per competition format (playoff bracket vs regular season).
cells.G1292: Use the tournament-vs-league fairness/efficiency tradeoff model to explain to users why playoff-bracket picks are inherently noisier than regular-season picks, turning a calibration limitation into transparent brand messaging ('math you can read').

cells.C1293: Mining Statistically Significant Substrings using the Chi-Square Statistic
cells.D1293: Presents an O(n^1.5) algorithm to find the most statistically anomalous substring in a sequence relative to a Bernoulli baseline, with applications including finance and sports data.
cells.E1293: Uses a chi-square deviation measure and an efficient search algorithm to identify substrings deviating most from an expected letter-frequency baseline.
cells.F1293: A stretch, but the general anomaly-detection-in-sequences technique is applicable to GSE's data pipeline for finding statistically anomalous stretches in time-series sports/odds data (e.g. scoring streak anomalies).
cells.G1293: Adapt the chi-square substring-mining algorithm to auto-detect anomalous 'runs' in scraped play-by-play data that might indicate scraping errors or genuine hot/cold streaks worth flagging.

cells.C1294: A network theory analysis of football strategies
cells.D1294: Builds weighted directed passing networks for World Cup football teams from FIFA data, using centrality measures to identify play patterns, key players, and team weaknesses.
cells.E1294: Constructs graph representations of team play (nodes=players, edges=passes) and applies network centrality metrics to quantify player importance and strategic patterns.
cells.F1294: Relevant to GSE's Intelligence Graph ambitions: a template for representing typed sports entities (players, passes, formations) as a graph with derived centrality features usable in prediction models.
cells.G1294: Feed passing-network centrality scores into GSE's per-sport soccer model as engineered features (e.g. 'network fragility if key playmaker removed') to improve MLS forecast accuracy.

cells.C1295: Efficient Video Indexing on the Web: A System that Leverages User Interactions with a Video Player
cells.D1295: Proposes VideoSkip, which auto-generates thumbnails of important video scenes by analyzing user interactions (pause, skip) with a web video player, tested informally on sports-like content.
cells.E1295: Mines implicit user behavior signals (play/pause/skip timestamps) to infer which video segments are most engaging and select representative thumbnails.
cells.F1295: A stretch for the prediction engine, but relevant to GSE's automated content generation — using viewer engagement signals to auto-select the best highlight clips or thumbnails for generated media.
cells.G1295: Apply implicit-interaction mining to GSE's own web app to detect which pick explanations users linger on, informing which model outputs to surface more prominently in the UI.

cells.C1296: Persistence and Uncertainty in the Academic Career
cells.D1296: Models scientific career productivity growth using longitudinal data, comparing to 21,156 sports careers, finding cumulative-advantage effects and right-skewed career-longevity distributions.
cells.E1296: Applies a proportional-growth stochastic model to explain increasing returns, symmetric 'tent-shaped' production-growth distributions, and skewed career-length distributions.
cells.F1296: Tangential, but the career-longevity modeling using sports-career data is a legitimate analog for GSE modeling player/team performance trajectories and aging curves within per-sport models.
cells.G1296: Adapt the proportional-growth model to forecast player career trajectories (breakout/decline risk) as a feature informing long-horizon prop or season-win-total picks.

cells.C1297: Universality, limits and predictability of gold-medal performances at the Olympic Games
cells.D1297: Shows relative year-over-year improvements of Olympic medal-winning performances are normally distributed, enabling prediction of when performance 'limits' will be approached and records broken.
cells.E1297: Models performance improvement as an exponential approach to an unknown asymptotic limit, using normality-testing to estimate that limit and predict record-breaking years.
cells.F1297: Tangentially relevant to sports forecasting: the exponential-approach-to-limit model is a reusable pattern for modeling any bounded improving metric, applicable to team/league scoring-rate trends over seasons.
cells.G1297: Use the asymptotic-limit model to forecast league-wide scoring-rate ceilings (e.g. NFL offensive efficiency), helping calibrate whether recent scoring surges are transient or a new baseline.

cells.C1298: A network-based dynamical ranking system for competitive sports
cells.D1298: Proposes a dynamic, time-weighted network centrality ranking system for tennis players that outperforms static ranking systems at predicting future match outcomes.
cells.E1298: Derives linear online update equations for player scores based on a directed win/loss network, weighting recent (peak-performance-era) wins more heavily than older ones.
cells.F1298: Directly relevant to GSE's core prediction problem: a proven dynamic ranking update rule that beats static rankings for match prediction — a concrete alternative/complement to their current losing baseline.
cells.G1298: Integrate the dynamic network ranking as one 'expert' in the CEPT multiplicative-weight ensemble, giving the e-process ensemble a forecasting method with documented predictive edge over static Elo-style ratings.

cells.C1299: Adjusted Plus-Minus for NHL Players using Ridge Regression with Goals, Shots, Fenwick, and Corsi
cells.D1299: Uses ridge regression on goals, shots, Fenwick, and Corsi data to estimate NHL player contributions independent of teammates/opponents, reducing the large error bars of ordinary least squares APM.
cells.E1299: Applies ridge regression (regularized regression) to handle collinearity from frequent teammate pairings and sparse scoring, using higher-volume proxy stats (shots) to shrink estimate error.
cells.F1299: Directly relevant to GSE's calibration blocker: ridge regression to combat multicollinearity and reduce variance in player/team effect estimates is a proven technique applicable to their prediction-engine feature set.
cells.G1299: Apply ridge-regularized adjusted plus-minus modeling to all GSE sports as a per-player 'true contribution' feature, using shot/event-volume proxies to stabilize estimates in low-sample-size ('bootstrap mode') situations.

cells.C1300: Recent Trends and Research Issues in Video Association Mining
cells.D1300: Surveys association-rule mining techniques applied to video databases across domains including sports broadcasts, summarizing frameworks and open research issues.
cells.E1300: Reviews methods for discovering frequent co-occurring patterns/events within video content using association rule mining.
cells.F1300: A stretch for GSE's core stack, tangential relevance to any future video-based sports data ingestion the company might pursue for automated content generation.
cells.G1300: If GSE ever ingests broadcast video, use association-rule mining on detected in-game events to surface recurring situational patterns (e.g. certain formations preceding turnovers) as new model features.

cells.D1301: Combines relation extraction with context discovery to improve text document categorization, demonstrated partly on synthetic sports-domain data.
cells.E1301: Learns contextual relations between document features to enrich standard bag-of-words categorization, improving classification accuracy over baseline methods.
cells.F1301: A stretch, tangentially useful for GSE's data-ingestion pipeline in categorizing scraped sports articles/text by topic before extracting structured features.
cells.G1301: Use context-aware categorization to auto-triage scraped news/injury reports by relevance and urgency before they reach the modeling pipeline, reducing noise in feature inputs.

cells.D1302: Finds that score and prize-money distributions in sports ranking systems (e.g. tennis) follow universal power laws, explained by a toy model where win probability depends on rank difference via a sigmoid.
cells.E1302: Empirically fits power-law distributions to ranking data and proposes a simple sigmoidal win-probability-vs-rank-difference model that reproduces the universal scaling in simulation.
cells.F1302: Directly relevant: the sigmoidal rank-difference win-probability model is a simple, interpretable building block GSE could test as a per-sport component model to improve calibration versus their current losing model.
cells.G1302: Fit the sigmoidal rank-difference function per sport as a transparent, math-you-can-read baseline component of the ensemble, directly supporting GSE's brand positioning against opaque 'AI' competitors.

cells.C1303: Scoring Strategies for the Underdog: A general, quantitative method for determining optimal sports strategies
cells.D1303: Develops an analytical framework using the binomial distribution to compute optimal risk-taking strategies for underdogs, covering examples like stalling, run/pass choices, and Hack-a-Shaq.
cells.E1303: Models offensive output as binomial (mean/variance) and calculates optimal variance-increasing strategies that maximize an underdog's win probability given a fixed mean-score sacrifice.
cells.F1303: Directly relevant to per-sport modeling: formalizes how variance/risk should shift with win-probability context, a concept GSE's models should reflect since not all game situations have symmetric prediction uncertainty.
cells.G1303: Use the underdog risk-tradeoff framework to build a 'strategic variance' feature — flagging situations where trailing teams are expected to take high-variance action, adjusting live win-probability updates accordingly.

cells.D1304: Applies archetypal analysis to basketball and soccer statistics to identify 'archetypal' extreme-performance athletes as convex-combination building blocks describing all other athletes.
cells.E1304: Uses archetypal analysis (finding extreme points on the data boundary) rather than clustering means, to characterize athletes as combinations of a small number of archetypes.
cells.F1304: Relevant to GSE's feature engineering: archetype-based player representation could be a compact, interpretable dimensionality-reduction alternative to standard PCA for per-sport models.
cells.G1304: Build player 'archetype scores' (e.g. % playmaker-archetype, % scorer-archetype) as engineered features feeding sport-specific probability models, adding interpretability aligned with the 'math you can read' brand.

cells.C1305: Random Walk Picture of Basketball Scoring
cells.D1305: Shows NBA scoring dynamics across ~6000 games are well described by a weakly-biased continuous-time random walk with exponential inter-scoring-event times, reproducing many statistical scoring features.
cells.E1305: Models scoring events as a memoryless (exponential) random walk process, augmented with team-strength heterogeneity, validated against real play-by-play data.
cells.F1305: Directly relevant to GSE's core prediction-engine blocker: offers a simple, well-validated generative model of in-game scoring dynamics that could serve as a principled component or sanity-check baseline for basketball forecasts.
cells.G1305: Use the random-walk scoring model as a real-time in-game win-probability calculator, cross-checked against GSE's ensemble output as an independent 'physics-based' consistency check.

cells.C1306: Onset of coherent attitude layers in a population of sports fans
cells.D1306: Studies how sports fans' opinions/emotions/actions coalesce into stable 'coherent layers' in response to referee decisions, using a physics-inspired (Brillouin function) social-response model.
cells.E1306: Fits fan response data to a quantum-statistical-physics-inspired model, using correlation and PCA to detect collective phase-transition-like behavior in fan sentiment.
cells.F1306: A real stretch for GSE's core prediction stack, but tangentially relevant to social-sentiment monitoring for content generation or gauging fan reaction to controversial calls/predictions.
cells.G1306: Borrow the 'coherent layering' concept to detect when social sentiment around a pick or controversial call is polarizing sharply, flagging content moments ripe for auto-generated commentary.

cells.C1307: Basketball scoring in NBA games: an example of complexity
cells.D1307: Analyzes 6150 NBA games finding non-uniform scoring-interval dynamics with identifiable 'tipping points' suggesting phase transitions in game dynamics.
cells.E1307: Statistical analysis of point-differential time series across a large game sample, identifying critical score-difference thresholds where scoring dynamics shift qualitatively.
cells.F1307: Relevant to GSE's live win-probability modeling: identifying score-differential 'tipping points' could directly improve in-game calibration, especially for the currently underperforming core model.
cells.G1307: Encode identified tipping-point thresholds as explicit regime-switch features in GSE's live model, letting probability updates react non-linearly near known phase-transition score margins.

cells.C1308: Selecting Attributes for Sport Forecasting using Formal Concept Analysis
cells.D1308: Applies Formal Concept Analysis to detect temporal regularities in sports data and select useful attributes, building a knowledge-based system to increase confidence in sports betting predictions.
cells.E1308: Uses FCA's implication/association-rule reasoning over qualitative attribute data to extract logically-grounded patterns for forecasting confidence.
cells.F1308: Directly relevant to GSE's calibration and bootstrap-mode confidence work: a rule-based, symbolic method for deriving confidence signals that is transparent — well aligned with 'math you can read.'
cells.G1308: Use FCA-derived implication rules as an auxiliary, fully interpretable confidence-adjustment layer that explains in plain language why bootstrap mode capped a given pick's confidence.

cells.C1309: Human as Real-Time Sensors of Social and Physical Events: A Case Study of Twitter and Sports Games
cells.D1309: Detects NFL game events (touchdowns, etc.) in real time from Twitter activity with up to 90% accuracy and ~40 second latency, treating humans as distributed event sensors.
cells.E1309: Builds an efficient Twitter data collection and event-recognition pipeline that infers physical game events from spikes/patterns in tweet volume and content.
cells.F1309: Directly relevant to GSE's data pipeline: a low-latency, free alternative/supplement signal for detecting live game events, useful for triggering re-modeling or confidence updates faster than some official feeds.
cells.G1309: Use Twitter-based event detection as a redundant, near-real-time cross-check against GSE's official live-odds feed, flagging discrepancies that might indicate feed lag or scraping errors.

cells.C1310: Using Logistic Regression to Analyze the Balance of a Game: The Case of StarCraft II
