cells.D1310: Uses logistic regression on tournament outcome data to statistically assess whether StarCraft II's game design is balanced across factions/strategies, rather than relying on anecdotal debate.
cells.E1310: Fits logistic regression models to competitive match outcomes to test for systematic non-random advantages tied to game-design factors.
cells.F1310: A stretch for core sports prediction, but directly relevant to GSE's Galaxy Dynasty/AUGUR persistent game ambition — a template for statistically validating game balance before launch.
cells.G1310: Apply this balance-testing methodology to audit Galaxy Dynasty's game mechanics for unintended statistical advantages before wide release, avoiding a 'pay-to-win' perception problem.

cells.C1311: A Discrete Evolutionary Model for Chess Players' Ratings
cells.D1311: Proposes a stochastic evolutionary model explaining why chess Elo ratings are approximately normally distributed with variance growing logarithmically over time, validated against real rating data.
cells.E1311: Models player entry, pairwise games, and rating updates as a discrete stochastic process, deriving a continuous approximation predicting the ratings distribution shape over time.
cells.F1311: Directly relevant to GSE's rating/ranking components: provides a principled generative explanation for how rating distributions and their skew evolve, useful for validating or correcting any Elo-like sub-model.
cells.G1311: Use the evolutionary rating model to predict how quickly a newly modeled sport's rating distribution should stabilize, setting data-driven timelines for exiting 'bootstrap mode.'

cells.C1312: Instant Replay: Investigating statistical Analysis in Sports
cells.D1312: Reviews prior sports-analytics work using Markov Chains, Bayesian inference, and MCMC methods, and suggests Neuro-Dynamic Programming/Control Theory could further improve statistical sports analysis.
cells.E1312: Literature review synthesizing probabilistic modeling approaches (Markov chains, Bayesian, MCMC) applied across sports analytics, with a case study using neuro-dynamic programming for football.
cells.F1312: Directly relevant as a broad primer connecting several of GSE's exact tools (Bayesian methods, Markov models) to sports prediction, useful context for prioritizing which techniques to invest in for calibration fixes.
cells.G1312: Use the neuro-dynamic-programming (approximate dynamic programming) angle as inspiration for modeling sequential in-game decisions (e.g. optimal live-bet timing) rather than only static pre-game predictions.

cells.C1313: Let Us Dance Just a Little Bit More --- On the Information Capacity of the Human Motor System
cells.D1313: Generalizes Fitts' Law using information theory to measure motor-skill 'capacity' for complex unconstrained movement like dance, validated with motion-capture data from professional dance.
cells.E1313: Applies information-theoretic movement-reproduction accuracy measures to quantify the bandwidth of human motor control beyond simple point-to-point aimed movements.
cells.F1313: A genuine stretch for GSE's product; at most a distant conceptual link to quantifying athlete skill/consistency if GSE ever ingests motion-capture-derived features.
cells.G1313: If GSE later ingests biomechanical tracking data, borrow this information-capacity framing to quantify athlete movement consistency as a novel skill-rating input.

cells.D1314: Surveys the least-squares graph-ranking framework (matching pairwise comparison edge data to vertex score differences), connecting it to spectral graph theory, Hodge decomposition, and sports team ranking.
cells.E1314: Formulates ranking as a least-squares problem on a graph Laplacian, discussing residual analysis and connections to arbitrage detection and multilevel numerical methods.
cells.F1314: Directly relevant to GSE's ranking/rating infrastructure: a mathematically rigorous, interpretable least-squares ranking method well-suited to their 'math you can read' brand positioning.
cells.G1314: Use the graph Laplacian residual decomposition (per the cited Jiang et al. extension) to detect intransitivity/inconsistency in scraped historical matchup data, flagging noisy or anomalous data sources.

cells.C1315: Match Analysis an undervalued coaching tool
cells.D1315: Reviews biomechanical match-analysis methods for judo competitions, proposing new 'dromogram' (athlete movement path) analysis as an underused coaching data source.
cells.E1315: Surveys technological/methodological advances in extracting physiological, technical, strategic and scouting data from combat-sport match footage.
cells.F1315: A stretch for GSE's core betting-market-facing product, since judo/combat-sport coaching analytics differ from GSE's mainstream league focus, but shares the general theme of turning match data into actionable metrics.
cells.G1315: Borrow the 'four levels of information' framework (physiological, technical, strategic, scouting) as an organizing schema for structuring GSE's Intelligence Graph entity attributes per player.

cells.C1316: Soccer: is scoring goals a predictable Poissonian process?
cells.D1316: Shows soccer goal-scoring is well described by independent Poisson processes with fitness-dependent rates, quantifying the fundamental predictability limits of soccer match outcomes.
cells.E1316: Derives a team-fitness-based finite-size-scaling function predicting expected match outcomes, testing whether goal scoring deviates from a pure Poisson process.
cells.F1316: Highly relevant to GSE's calibration blocker for soccer/MLS: a validated Poisson-process baseline model with quantified predictability limits, directly usable as a per-sport component or sanity benchmark.
cells.G1316: Use this paper's quantified 'limits of predictability' for soccer as an explicit ceiling target for GSE's MLS Brier score, so the team knows how much of the 0.2563→0.22 gap is even theoretically closable.

cells.C1317: Steganography An Art of Hiding Data
cells.D1317: Proposes a private-key steganography/LSB technique for covertly embedding hidden messages on public display screens, mentioning sports-stadium billboards as a use case.
cells.E1317: Uses symmetric-key steganography and least-significant-bit encoding to hide messages within displayed visual content.
cells.F1317: Essentially unrelated to GSE's statistical/product stack; the sports-stadium billboard mention is incidental to a security/cryptography paper.
cells.G1317: No natural product tie; at most a novel (and likely unnecessary) way to watermark GSE-generated graphics/content for provenance tracking.

cells.C1318: Synthesis of supervised classification algorithm using intelligent and statistical tools
cells.D1318: Proposes non-parametric background-subtraction and team-identification algorithms for detecting players and assigning team membership from football match video, tested on Tunisian league footage.
cells.E1318: Combines color-space segmentation with classification to detect players and identify their team affiliation from broadcast video pixels.
cells.F1318: A stretch for GSE's data pipeline today (they use scraped stats, not video), but relevant if they later add computer-vision ingestion of broadcast footage as another 'free data' source.
cells.G1318: If GSE expands to video-derived data, use this team-identification pipeline as a starting point for auto-extracting formation/possession features from freely available broadcast clips.

cells.D1319: Presents polynomial-time algorithms for recovering a true underlying ranking (permutation) from noisy pairwise comparisons or noisy orders, with rankings in sports as a stated application.
cells.E1319: Uses maximum-likelihood estimation under Mallows-model and noisy-comparison models, proving the recovered ranking is provably close to the true order with high probability.
cells.F1319: Directly relevant to GSE's ranking/rating infrastructure: a theoretically grounded method for recovering true team/player strength rankings from noisy game outcomes, applicable across all their sports.
cells.G1319: Use the noisy-sorting MLE framework to build confidence intervals around GSE's internal power rankings, quantifying how much noise in scraped results still permits reliable ranking recovery.

cells.C1320: Statistical Properties of Height of Japanese Schoolchildren
cells.D1320: Analyzes national survey data showing children's height distribution transitions from lognormal to normal during puberty.
cells.E1320: Fits and compares lognormal vs. normal distributions to large-scale anthropometric survey data across age cohorts.
cells.F1320: Essentially unrelated to GSE's product; a pure biometric/demographic statistics paper with no sports-prediction content despite touching 'sports science' ministry data.
cells.G1320: At most, illustrates a general technique (distribution-shape transition detection) that could be repurposed to detect when a sport's outcome-distribution shape shifts (e.g. rule changes altering scoring distributions).

cells.C1321: The price of anarchy in basketball
cells.D1321: Models a basketball offense as a traffic network and applies 'price of anarchy' concepts to show that always taking the highest-percentage shot can be less efficient than optimal team-level shot allocation, suggesting a basketball analog of Braess's Paradox.
cells.E1321: Maps basketball shot-selection pathways to a traffic-network game-theory framework, comparing selfish (locally optimal) vs. globally optimal offensive strategies.
cells.F1321: Relevant to GSE's per-sport basketball modeling: illustrates a subtle, counterintuitive strategic dynamic (removing a player can increase team efficiency) worth encoding as a non-obvious feature in NBA models.
cells.G1321: Encode a 'price of anarchy' feature testing whether a team's shot distribution is closer to selfish-optimal or team-optimal, using deviations as a predictive signal for under/over-performance versus market lines.

cells.C1322: Computational Biomechanics, Stochastic Motion and Team Sports
cells.D1322: Models a single team-sport athlete's on-field trajectory as a biased random walk (viscous/pushing/pedestrian forces plus randomness), matching simulated paths to real match-analysis trajectory data.
cells.E1322: Combines deterministic strategic drift (toward goal) with stochastic tactical perturbations in a random-walk model, validated against Brownian-like empirical player paths.
cells.F1322: A stretch for GSE's current stats-based stack (no tracking data), but conceptually related to the random-walk scoring models (item 1109.2825) that could underpin future physics-inspired sport models.
cells.G1322: If GSE gains access to tracking-like data via a partner, use this biased-random-walk framework to simulate player movement as a generative feature for possession-based sports.

cells.C1323: Quantitative and empirical demonstration of the Matthew effect in a study of career longevity
cells.D1323: Develops a stochastic career-progress model demonstrating the 'rich get richer' Matthew effect, validated on scientists and over 20,000 athletes across four sports leagues.
cells.E1323: Builds an exactly solvable stochastic model linking early-career success/longevity to cumulative future advantage, fit to large real-world career datasets.
cells.F1323: Relevant to GSE's per-player/per-team modeling: cumulative-advantage dynamics could be encoded as a feature capturing how early-career/early-season success compounds, informing longer-horizon prediction models.
cells.G1323: Add a 'Matthew-effect momentum' feature quantifying how much a team/player's recent success is compounding versus regressing, to improve the core model's currently underperforming MAE.

cells.D1324: Improves classical sorting/selection algorithms to the setting of partially ordered sets (posets) where some pairs are incomparable, with sports rankings cited as a motivating application.
cells.E1324: Develops near-information-theoretically-optimal query-complexity algorithms for sorting and finding minimal elements in a poset of given width using pairwise comparison queries.
cells.F1324: Relevant to GSE's ranking infrastructure: models situations where team/player comparisons are genuinely incomparable (different conferences, no common opponents), a real complication in cross-league ranking.
cells.G1324: Use poset-based partial ranking to explicitly represent incomparability between teams from different leagues/conferences, avoiding false-precision cross-league comparisons in GSE's power ratings.

cells.D1325: Develops an efficient algorithm to recover a near-maximum-likelihood total order from one-time noisy pairwise comparisons (no resampling allowed), with proven closeness bounds to the true order, citing sports ranking as an application.
cells.E1325: Solves a weighted feedback-arc-set-like problem under a bounded-error noisy-comparison model using an efficient algorithm with polynomial runtime and sample complexity.
cells.F1325: Directly relevant to GSE's ranking work: models the realistic constraint that each matchup is observed only once (you can't resample a game), directly matching how sports outcome data actually arrives.
cells.G1325: Use the one-shot noisy-sorting algorithm to build power rankings that explicitly account for the fact each head-to-head result is a single noisy sample, rather than assuming resampling as many methods implicitly do.

cells.D1326: Analyzes ball-touch and out-of-play interval statistics across football matches, finding power-law-tailed 'q-gamma' distributions and proposing a model explaining the dynamics.
cells.E1326: Fits generalized (Tsallis q-statistics) distributions to empirical ball-touch and stoppage-time data, proposing a mechanistic model reproducing the observed statistics.
cells.F1326: Relevant to GSE's soccer-specific modeling: a validated heavy-tailed distribution family for in-game event timing, useful for modeling event-based soccer data more accurately than naive Gaussian/exponential assumptions.
cells.G1326: Use q-gamma distribution fits for soccer event timing to better model live in-game time-remaining effects, feeding a more accurate live win-probability curve for MLS picks.

cells.D1327: Uses a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate MLB outfielder/catcher throwing ability from game event data, shrinking small-sample player estimates toward a population mean.
cells.E1327: Attributes run-value contributions to throwing success/failure events, then fits a Bayesian hierarchical model with shrinkage across players and seasons.
cells.F1327: Directly relevant to GSE's bootstrap-mode confidence capping: this is a textbook example of exactly the shrinkage-toward-population-mean technique needed to handle sparse per-player data responsibly.
cells.G1327: Directly port this hierarchical-shrinkage Bayesian approach as the statistical basis for GSE's 'bootstrap mode,' replacing an ad hoc confidence cap with a principled, published methodology.

cells.D1328: Describes Astro-WISE, an astronomical information system providing end-to-end chaining of distributed scientific data acquisition, processing, and archiving, mentioning sports-car-scale storage costs only as an aside.
cells.E1328: Builds a 'scientific information layer' with full backward/forward data lineage chaining, integrating distributed analysis, processing, and federated archiving into one system.
cells.F1328: A real stretch for GSE's sports product specifically, but the underlying data-lineage/chaining architecture is a legitimate inspiration for GSE's own data-ingestion pipeline reliability and provenance tracking.
cells.G1328: Adopt Astro-WISE's full data-lineage chaining concept to give every GSE pick an auditable chain back through its input data sources, supporting transparency claims central to their 'math you can read' brand.

cells.C1329: Predicting Baseball Home Run Records Using Exponential Frequency Distributions
cells.D1329: Models annual home-run-count frequency distributions as exponentials to predict the probability of MLB home run records being broken, estimating an 80% chance Bonds' record falls within 10 years.
cells.E1329: Fits exponential distributions to historical home-run frequency data year by year, using distributional shifts to forecast record-breaking probabilities.
cells.F1329: Directly relevant to GSE's MLB modeling and proper-scoring-rule goals: a simple, transparent distributional forecasting method for record/extreme-event probabilities that fits their brand of readable math.
cells.G1329: Use this exponential record-forecasting approach to generate auto-published 'record watch' probability content for MLB, feeding both prediction accuracy and automated media content simultaneously.

cells.D1330: Analyzes results from five major sports leagues to relate team parity (variance in win fraction) to game predictability (upset frequency), introducing a fixed-upset-probability model linking the two.
cells.E1330: Derives a mathematical model connecting standings-based parity metrics to game-level upset frequency, letting one estimate upset rates directly from standings data.
cells.F1330: Directly relevant to GSE's calibration work across NFL/MLB/MLS: gives a simple, validated cross-league model of how upset probability relates to league parity, directly informing prior probabilities per sport/league.
cells.G1330: Use league-specific parity-upset relationships as a data-driven prior for each sport's per-sport probability model, giving the ensemble a principled starting Brier-score expectation before fitting.

cells.C1331: What is the most competitive sport?
cells.D1331: Extends prior parity/upset analysis across five major leagues to propose 'likelihood of upsets' as a formal competitiveness measure, ranking sports by inherent unpredictability.
cells.E1331: Uses the same upset-probability model as related work to derive and compare a single competitiveness metric across different sports leagues.
cells.F1331: Directly relevant: gives GSE a concrete, comparable competitiveness/upset-rate metric per sport, useful for setting differentiated calibration targets (Brier/ECE) rather than one global threshold across NFL/MLB/MLS.
cells.G1331: Use the derived per-sport competitiveness ranking to justify and calibrate different confidence-cap thresholds per sport in bootstrap mode, rather than a single blanket confidence rule.

cells.C1332: On Minimum Violations Ranking in Paired Comparisons
cells.D1332: Proposes a statistical-physics-based method for finding minimum-violations rankings from paired comparison (e.g. sports) results, overcoming difficulties of earlier combinatorial approaches.
cells.E1332: Reformulates the minimum-violations ranking problem using statistical mechanics techniques to more tractably search the ranking space than prior combinatorial methods.
cells.F1332: Directly relevant to GSE's ranking infrastructure: an alternative optimization approach to build internally consistent, low-inconsistency team/player rankings from win/loss results.
cells.G1332: Use minimum-violations ranking as a diagnostic layer, comparing its rankings to GSE's model outputs to flag matchups where the model's implied ranking is unusually inconsistent with actual results.

cells.C1333: A Derivation of the Pythagorean Won-Loss Formula in Baseball
cells.D1333: Provides a theoretical derivation of Bill James' Pythagorean win-percentage formula by modeling runs scored/allowed as independent Weibull-distributed variables, validated on 2004 AL data.
cells.E1333: Derives the empirical Pythagorean formula and its exponent from first principles using Weibull distribution fitting and maximum-likelihood/least-squares parameter estimation.
cells.F1333: Directly relevant to GSE's MLB modeling: a rigorous theoretical foundation for a widely-used baseball forecasting heuristic, directly usable as a transparent, interpretable per-sport probability component.
cells.G1333: Use the Weibull-based derivation to build confidence intervals around Pythagorean-formula predictions per team, feeding uncertainty estimates into bootstrap-mode confidence capping for MLB picks specifically.

cells.C1334: Complex network study of Brazilian soccer players
cells.D1334: Builds bipartite and projected networks of Brazilian soccer players and clubs across 32 championship editions, finding exponential club/game-count distributions but power-law goal-scoring distributions.
cells.E1334: Constructs player-club bipartite networks and player-player co-employment networks, computing degree distributions, clustering, assortativity, and path-length statistics over time.
cells.F1334: Relevant to GSE's Intelligence Graph ambitions: a concrete methodology for representing player-club relationships as networks with well-characterized statistical properties, applicable to any league's data.
cells.G1334: Track evolving assortativity/clustering metrics of GSE's own player-team graph over time as a meta-signal for league structural changes (e.g. talent consolidation) that might require recalibrating models.

cells.C1335: Effects of Thermal Fluctuations in the SPOrt Experiment
cells.D1335: Analyzes systematic errors from thermal instabilities in the SPOrt cosmic microwave background polarization instrument aboard the ISS, showing they are largely negligible for the science goal.
cells.E1335: Derives instrument transfer functions from temperature to signal fluctuations and estimates resulting contamination maps and power spectra under various thermal-instability scenarios.
cells.F1335: No real connection to GSE — 'SPOrt' here is an astrophysics instrument acronym, not sports; at most a naming coincidence with zero substantive overlap.
cells.G1335: None meaningful; the only transferable idea is the general engineering practice of quantifying systematic-error budgets, loosely analogous to auditing sources of error in GSE's data pipeline.

cells.C1336: Polarization Measures And Nature Of Dark Energy
cells.D1336: Analyzes how CMB polarization measurements from experiments like SPOrt and WMAP can constrain dark energy models, particularly Ratra-Peebles quintessence potentials.
cells.E1336: Uses likelihood analysis of predicted anisotropy-polarization correlations across dark-energy models to determine which models future polarization data could rule out.
cells.F1336: No genuine connection to GSE; 'SPOrt' is again a CMB polarization experiment name, unrelated to sports analytics.
cells.G1336: None meaningful beyond the general pattern of using likelihood analysis to determine which competing models can be statistically distinguished by upcoming data — a generic idea transferable to any model-comparison exercise.

cells.C1337: An iterative destriping technique for diffuse background polarization data
cells.D1337: Describes an iterative algorithm to remove instrumental striping noise from CMB polarization data collected by the SPOrt space experiment, generalizable to other polarization/intensity experiments.
cells.E1337: Iteratively estimates and subtracts correlated 1/f-type noise stripes from scan-based astronomical data using knowledge of instrument scan/orbit periodicity.
cells.F1337: A genuine stretch, but the general iterative-destriping technique for removing correlated systematic noise is conceptually transferable to cleaning correlated noise/bias in GSE's scraped time-series data feeds.
cells.G1337: Adapt the iterative destriping algorithm's logic (exploit known periodicity to isolate correlated noise) to detect and remove recurring scraper artifacts or systematic biases in periodic data pulls (e.g. daily odds refresh cycles).

cells.C1338: Nature of Dark Energy and Polarization Measurements
cells.D1338: Analyzes how CMB polarization data sensitivity (from experiments like SPOrt/WMAP) can distinguish dark energy models, finding WMAP's early results already excluded a class of Ratra-Peebles models.
cells.E1338: Performs likelihood analyses of anisotropy-polarization correlations predicted by competing cosmological models against real and simulated instrument sensitivities.
cells.F1338: No genuine connection to GSE; another SPOrt-acronym cosmology paper, coincidental keyword match only.
cells.G1338: None substantive; at most illustrates using early real data to promptly rule out theoretical models, a generic idea about updating quickly on new evidence applicable to any modeling program including GSE's calibration gate.

cells.F1339: Could not retrieve metadata for this ID (404 from the paper-lookup tool on two attempts); based on the ID's cs/0210021 form (submitted ~Oct 2002 to a computer science category), it likely predates most modern ML/stats work and its relevance cannot be assessed without content.
cells.G1339: Without abstract/title, no specific creative application can be proposed beyond a generic suggestion to re-attempt retrieval via arXiv's listing page directly if this paper is later deemed important.

cells.C1340: Cosmic opacity to CMB photons and polarization measurements
cells.D1340: Performs a likelihood analysis of how low-l CMB polarization measurements (from experiments like SPOrt) can break a degeneracy between spectral index and cosmic reionization opacity.
cells.E1340: Uses likelihood analysis incorporating cosmic variance to assess how well specific instrument noise levels can resolve a parameter degeneracy in CMB analysis.
cells.F1340: No genuine connection to GSE; another SPOrt-acronym cosmology paper unrelated to sports.
cells.G1340: None substantive; only generically illustrates how instrument noise level interacts with cosmic/statistical variance to determine parameter identifiability, a pattern echoed in GSE's own data-sparsity/'bootstrap mode' problem.

cells.C1341: SDAMS: SPOrt Data Archiving and Management System
cells.D1341: Describes SDAMS, a database and software system for archiving, quick-look analysis, and web-accessible distribution of data from the SPOrt cosmic microwave background experiment.
cells.E1341: Combines a database backend with tiered user-access controls and web-based analysis/plotting tools to manage and distribute astronomical experiment data.
cells.F1341: No sports connection (SPOrt is the instrument's name), but the general data-archiving/tiered-access/web-analysis system design is a legitimate loose analog for GSE's own data pipeline and internal analytics tooling.
cells.G1341: Borrow the tiered-access design (public outreach view vs. researcher-level raw access) as a model for GSE's own internal vs. public-facing data/analytics dashboards.

cells.C1342: From Current CMBology to its Polarization and SZ Frontiers circa TAW8
cells.D1342: A conference summary reviewing advances in CMB anisotropy/polarization research and Sunyaev-Zeldovich cluster studies as of a 2001 workshop, surveying many contemporaneous experiments including SPOrt.
cells.E1342: Synthesizes results across numerous CMB and SZ experiments to summarize the state of precision cosmology parameter estimation at the time.
cells.F1342: No genuine connection to GSE; a broad cosmology conference-proceedings summary with only a coincidental SPOrt acronym mention.
cells.G1342: None substantive beyond the generic observation that combining many independent experimental probes narrows parameter uncertainty — loosely mirroring GSE's own multi-source data-ingestion philosophy.

cells.C1343: Large Stock Market Price Drawdowns Are Outliers
cells.D1343: Analyzes major financial indices and stocks to show large market drawdowns are statistical outliers not explained by the same distribution governing typical daily returns, calling for a distinct 'crash' mechanism.
cells.E1343: Fits stretched-exponential distributions to drawdown magnitudes and statistically tests whether the largest drawdowns are consistent with that same fitted distribution or constitute genuine outliers.
cells.F1343: Directly relevant to GSE's data pipeline and modeling: a rigorous method for detecting genuine tail-risk outliers in financial-style time series, directly transferable to detecting anomalous odds-market moves or line-shift outliers.
cells.G1343: Apply the outlier-drawdown detection methodology to live odds/line-movement data to auto-flag anomalous market moves (e.g. sharp money, breaking news) as a distinct event class deserving special handling in the pipeline.

cells.C1344: Correlation Functions of CMB Anisotropy and Polarization
cells.D1344: Derives correlation-function estimators and signal-to-noise calculations for cross-correlating cosmic microwave background anisotropy and polarization, applied to planned experiments including SPOrt/ISS.
cells.E1344: Constructs auto- and cross-correlation function estimators corrected for instrumental noise, computing expected signal-to-noise ratios for various planned CMB polarization experiments.
cells.F1344: No genuine connection to GSE; the earliest of several unrelated SPOrt-acronym cosmology papers in this list, sharing no substantive methodology with sports prediction.
cells.G1344: None substantive beyond the generic idea of designing noise-corrected correlation estimators before committing to a costly measurement campaign — vaguely analogous to piloting a new data source before full pipeline integration.
